maps.area: Links, the Index and the Pages view as they are (89893aa, claude/beta5-features): links.ini/nav.ini models, how a link is made, followed, hit-tested, changed and removed, the Index tab and naming, Go to page, PDF outline and links, backlinks, limits, and what non-ink areas, hotbar rename/delete and a graph view would need
maps.summary:
Today a link is exactly one ink stroke, the lasso. Its seed keys a line in links.ini (`link.<pid>=<seed8hex>,<index|p<pid>>`). The tap area is the axis-aligned box of that stroke's points, made at least 7 mm a side and computed fresh from the page's strokes on every tap. Only a finger follows a link: a tap follows it, and a 600 ms hold opens the Pages view in picking mode to change the target or remove the link. The pen always draws. The Index is a different thing: it is nav.ini's named pages (section starts), listed in notebook order. A link has no name of its own, and the Index never shows links. Nothing keeps a reverse index, but there are at most 4000 links, so a full scan to answer "which pages link here" costs under a millisecond. The one blind spot is whether a link's ink still exists: links.ini can't tell you without reading the page.

All four asks fit the hard rules without touching .qpg:
- (a) Non-ink area: store a rectangle on the link's line in links.ini. The beta.5 format is unreleased, so the line can change. The editor already has a path that takes a just-drawn stroke back off the page, which can capture the area.
- (b) Rename from the hotbar: call nav_set_name on the target page id. This renames the page everywhere and, if the page was unnamed, makes it a section start.
- (c) Delete a link: the link-only half exists (PV_UNLINK). Removing the ink too can reuse the whole-stroke eraser's history step.
- (d) Graph data: all of it is in nb->page_ids, nav names and nav->links. Only the "is the box still there" bit and a layout are missing.

Two existing quirks bear directly on the redesign:
- A ring removed with the precise eraser or white ink keeps working as an invisible link until compaction drops the stroke at notebook close; then the link silently stops working.
- On a page at fit zoom, a two-finger drag is currently consumed by pinch-pan.
facts: DATA MODEL nav.ini: `name.<pid>=<title>` lines; NavName{pid,text[96]} sorted by pid (nav.h:16, nav.c:18-31 binary search). nav_set_name trims, 95-byte UTF-8 cut, controls become spaces, empty removes (nav.c:33-65); at most STORE_MAX_PAGES=2000 names (nav.c:52, store.h:7). nav_save writes the whole file atomically and prunes names of deleted pages only after success (nav.c:225-248). A named page IS a section start: nav_index = named pages in notebook order (nav.c:250-257); nav_section_of walks back to the nearest named page (nav.c:259-263). FORMAT.md:717-732.

DATA MODEL links.ini: `link.<pid>=<seed 1-8 hex>,<target>`; NavLink{pid,seed,target[16]} kept sorted by (pid, seed) (nav.h:21, nav.c:268-298). The parser takes the target as the rest of the line, 1-15 bytes from '!' to '~' (nav.c:157-181), so a line can't hold spaces or UTF-8: no labels. Known targets are "index" and "p<pid>" (nav.c:301-310, 312-313). Unknown targets are carried and do nothing. A link line has no area, no label and no creation order. FORMAT.md:734-761.

LIMITS: NAV_LINKS_MAX 4000 per notebook, NAV_LINKS_PER_PAGE 64 (nav.h:10-11). The 64 cap is enforced only by nav_link_set (nav.c:314-317); a file may hold more. Past 4000, link_put returns -1 (nav.c:284), each_line fails and the WHOLE links.ini is hidden with links_writable=false (nav.c:204-215). NAV_FILE_MAX 256 KiB (nav.h:8); unknown lines at most 255 B each and 16 KiB in total (nav.c:122-131). nav.ini and links.ini fail independently (nav.c:190-218).

MAKING A LINK: link_start (editor.c:1545-1551) refuses on a read-only page or when !links_writable. The refusal is silent for the add-link shortcut (no toast); the Index button is greyed (pagesview.c:307-311). It sets link_mode and toasts 'Draw around what links...'. The next INK stroke (erase strokes don't count) ends in draw_end. If its bbox is under LINK_BOX_MIN_MM=5 mm both ways (editor.c:36, 1052-1060), it is freed, redrawn and toasted, with no undo step (editor.c:1151-1161). Otherwise page_add plus history_push_add, then link_box_drawn (editor.c:1173, 1561-1570): link_seed = s->seed, save_page, pagesview_pick(had=false). PV_PICK/PV_PICK_INDEX lead to link_to: nav_link_set plus nav_save_links, and on failure nav_load rolls back (editor.c:1574-1585, 1607-1625). Back calls link_cancel, which undoes the box only if it is still the last stroke (editor.c:1589-1599). go_to_page, pages_show and pages_name all clear link_mode (editor.c:813, 1423, 1434).

SEEDS: every new ink stroke gets nav_new_seed, which avoids any ink seed on the page and any link seed of the page, in up to 64 hash retries (editor.c:1104-1105, nav.c:402-413). That is why a link is in practice exactly ONE stroke. The format allows several strokes sharing a seed, but no UI makes that. Erase strokes get erase_seed without this check and are ignored by link boxes (nav.c:354).

BOX AND HIT-TEST: link_box loops over all strokes of the page, skips non-matching seeds and erase strokes, and takes the min/max of the points (not the rendered width). The box is made at least min_px a side around its centre, and the function returns the index of the last matching stroke (nav.c:349-372). nav_link_at uses min NAV_LINK_MIN_MM=7 mm (nav.h:14, editor.c:1664). Where boxes overlap, the link whose last stroke comes latest wins (nav.c:386-400). Nothing is cached: each tap costs 64 links x p->n seed compares plus the points of the matching strokes. link_under converts screen to page with to_page, so links work zoomed (editor.c:1660-1665, 532-535). nav_link_areas returns only links whose strokes exist (nav.c:374-384).

FOLLOWING: a finger down on the page, outside the panel and every sheet, always takes OWN_LINK (editor.c:2431-2438). On release, not moved and not held, link_follow runs (editor.c:2455-2459, 1668-1683): a page target calls go_to_page, which ends in compose_all(REFRESH_FULL), a GC16 flash (editor.c:812-833). An Index target opens the Pages view on its Index tab. A missing page toasts. A hold of LINK_HOLD_MS=600 ms without moving (editor.c:34, 2583-2584) calls link_hold, which opens pagesview_pick(had=true) with a toast giving the target's page NUMBER, never its name (editor.c:1686-1706). A second finger turns the press into a pinch (editor.c:2285). The pen never follows links (editor.c:2425-2427).

CHANGE AND REMOVE: in picking mode the header shows 'The Index' (PG_TO_INDEX) and, for an existing link, 'Remove link' (PG_UNLINK) (pagesview.c:195-208). Tiles and Index rows pick a page, and New/Copy page and ticks are hidden (pagesview.c:255, 302). PV_UNLINK calls nav_link_remove plus nav_save_links and toasts 'Link removed. Its ink stays on the page.' (editor.c:1626-1638). There is no path that removes a link's ink. Link edits are not in undo history: ActKind is only ADD/ERASE/PAPER/CLEAR (history.h:5).

INK EDITS AND LINKS: erasing (whole-stroke), undoing or clearing the ring leaves the links.ini entry inert. A redo or undo brings the box back, and the entry is kept until its page is deleted (FORMAT.md:743-747; nav.c:415-420 link_kept). The precise eraser and white ink add erase strokes (tool 3) on top, so the ring LOOKS gone but link_box still finds it: the link keeps working invisibly. Compaction at notebook close then drops ink that is erased entirely (FORMAT.md:183-206; page_droppable page.h:109, which knows nothing of links), and the link silently goes inert.

COPY AND DELETE: Copy page duplicates strokes with their seeds under a new pid (editor.c:1523-1540), and links.ini is keyed by pid, so the copy's rings are plain ink with no links. Deleting pages prunes names and links of missing pages, including links TO them, at the next nav_save/nav_save_links (editor.c:1486-1489, nav.c:415-450).

INDEX TAB (pagesview.c:145-173): rows are the named pages only (nav_index into a stack int[2000], line 156), each with its name, page number and a bar plus bold on the current section (nav_section_of). Tapping a row gives PV_OPEN, or PV_PICK while picking. Empty: 'Name a page to list it here.' / 'Page names could not be read.' The header button is 'Name this page' or 'Rename this page' for the OPEN page only, disabled when nav isn't writable (pagesview.c:209-214). The bottom row has New page, Go to page..., and Add a link in Copy page's place (pagesview.c:302-316). The tab opens by default on the first open when names exist (pagesview.c:47-51). The tab title counts names: 'Index (%d)' (pagesview.c:227-230).

NAMING: open_naming opens keyboard_open('Page name', current name) for v->current only (pagesview.c:80-84). KB_DONE gives PV_NAME, and the editor names S->nb.page_ids[S->index], restoring the old name on failure (editor.c:1643-1656). pagesview_name (the name-page shortcut) sets name_only, so Done or Cancel goes back to the page and the view gives back the tab it found (pagesview.c:33-41, 86-96; editor.c:1432-1438, 2039-2040; commits 2f7984c, 0618c73). Naming any page OTHER than the open one would need a pid parameter in both places.

GO TO PAGE: PG_JUMP opens keyboard_open('Go to page', '') on kb.page=2, the number pad (pagesview.c:368-373). Done takes strtol 1..npages to PV_OPEN, or PV_PICK while picking; otherwise it toasts and the pad stays (pagesview.c:330-340). The search is numeric only. The accent-folding name compare exists but is static (store.c:861 cmp_name).

SHORTCUTS: SHORTCUT_ADD_LINK and SHORTCUT_NAME_PAGE are the newest actions; SHORTCUT_LAST = SHORTCUT_NAME_PAGE (shortcuts.h:20-24). The files name them 'add-link' and 'name-page' (shortcuts.c k_actions). Dispatch: add-link toggles link_start/link_stop, name-page calls pages_name (editor.c:2034-2040). 'index' and 'pages' open the Pages view on a tab (editor.c:1942-1950). Buttons sheet rows sit in the Pages group (library.c:569-584, 625-631; commit 660377e). SHORTCUT_MAX=64 counts BINDINGS, not actions (shortcuts.h:4). Settings' bottom row is KOReader | Controller | Updates | Done, with Controller and Updates splitting the middle (library.c:1033-1043).

PDF: export loads its own Nav (export.c:213-220). Names become the outline with /PageMode /UseOutlines (export.c:221-235, 318-331). Each page's links come from nav_link_areas at NAV_LINK_MIN_MM (export.c:94-117). Links to pages become /Link annots with /Dest [page /Fit]; links to the Index are dropped (export.c:253-297). Raw ZIPs carry nav.ini and links.ini (export.c:513). No other module reads nav: grep finds it only in editor.c, pagesview.c and export.c.

BACKLINKS: no reverse index. nav->links is sorted by source pid; finding 'who links to P' means scanning all nlinks (at most 4000) with target_page (nav.c:301-310, static) and compares, well under 1 ms. nav_link_page resolves a target through page_index, a linear scan over npages (nav.c:336-345). Doing that for every edge in a graph is up to 4000 x 2000 = 8M compares, so build a pid-to-index table once. Whether an edge's box still exists needs that page's strokes (store_read_page per page).

LAYERING AND REFRESH: compose() blits the page canvas, then draws the panel and sheets on top; the Pages view replaces everything (editor.c:671-687). This is the place for a hotbar and a link-area overlay; the page canvas, thumbnails and PDF stay clean. Invalidations coalesce at the strongest mode until app_flush (app.c:911-919). Toasts respect a->toast_floor (app.c:481-483), which a hotbar can raise. REFRESH_FAST=DU, UI=GL16, FULL=GC16 (display.h:6-8).

TWO FINGERS: the only multi-touch input is IN_PINCH_BEGIN/MOVE/END with (x,y,x2,y2) (input.h:25). pinch() is gated by settings.pinch_zoom and by sheets (editor.c:2296). It commits after a spread above 10% OR a travel of at least 70 px, then zooms and pans, painting every 180 ms (editor.c:2302-2324). At fit zoom view_clamp centres the page back, so a two-finger drag down does nothing visible today. When zoomed it pans. The headless runner can script a two-finger drag as `pinch CX CY D D STEPS DX DY` (docs/SIM.md:66).

TESTS: tests/test_nav.c (373 lines; the per-page cap at line 255); scenarios tests/scenarios/z_index_2_links.qs (make, follow, hold, retarget, remove, Back, undo/redo, reopen) and v_shortcuts_links.qs. Editor probes are editor.links ('N boxed'), editor.link.N (target), editor.link_mode, editor.picking, editor.pages_tab (editor.c:2617-2629, pagesview.c:412-434).

SETTINGS: struct in store.h:34-73 (e.g. pinch_zoom store.h:51), read at store.c:1896, written at store.c:2031 (keep_bool, put_int). New toggles such as link-area visibility, smart shapes and gestures go here, and should also get action-registry entries so that shortcuts and gestures can bind them.
constraints: Never change .qpg: no header bump, no tool id >= 10. An invisible link area cannot be a new tool or an ext flag: 1.0.0-beta ignores ext and would draw it, and FORMAT.md's compaction rule skips any page whose strokes carry unknown ext bytes. It belongs in links.ini, a sidecar, or settings.ini.
Safe page chunks must not hold page coordinates (FORMAT.md, Chunks), and 1.0.0-beta drops them on re-save. A per-page link area therefore can't live in a chunk; links.ini is the place.

links.ini line grammar today: the target is the rest of the line, 1-15 bytes from '!' to '~' (nav.c:176-178). Any new field (area, label) means changing the parser or adding a key. beta.5 is unreleased, so this is allowed. Builds already on the device (f9d13f5) would carry the changed lines as unknown or drop them.

Size budget: a worst-case line today is about 37 B; adding four 4-digit coordinates is about 57 B; times 4000 links that is about 228 KB, against NAV_FILE_MAX 256 KiB with up to 16 KiB of carried unknown lines. That fits, but tightly. Hex coordinates, or a higher cap just for links.ini, would give margin.

Area coordinates should be page px at the notebook's page size (store_notebook_page_size): since 1.1 pages are scaled back to that size on open and in exports (FORMAT.md:122-144). Normalized units are optional extra safety.
Pages since 1.1 keep the notebook's size, and pre-1.1 versions never read links.ini, so area links are inert there (as ink links already are, FORMAT.md:952).

Link edits are not undoable today, while ink is. Any 'delete link with ink' must decide whether undo brings back the ink alone or the link too. The latter needs an in-memory ACT_LINK in history (history.h:5) or keeping the entry dormant.

Renaming a link's target from a hotbar = nav_set_name(target pid). It renames that page everywhere (Index, tiles, PDF outline). On an unnamed target it CREATES an Index entry, which makes that page a section start (nav_section_of), changing the section highlight for the pages after it. A link to the Index has no name to rename.

Every UI string in English and Spanish, fitting both orientations. The Pages view's buttons have width notes in TRANSLATORS comments, and a hotbar with up to 64 entries needs paging, as the Index uses prev/next screens.

E-ink: going to a page currently asks for a GC16 full flash (editor.c:831). Hopping between pages with the hotbar open should use GL16 until confirm, or each hop flashes. Hotbar and overlay draws should be small GL16 rects. No animation, so a graph layout must be computed, not shown converging.

Long work (a graph layout over 2000 nodes, reading every page to check link boxes) must pump input (work_pump, common.h:49-57) or be split across ticks. page_droppable-style whole-page passes are never allowed on the UI thread (page.h:105-107).
Tap-outside-to-close must swallow that tap, as the Paper sheet does (OWN_MODAL), or it will also follow a link under it, because every finger-down on the page is OWN_LINK (editor.c:2431-2438).
opportunities: (a) Non-ink link area. Extend the line to `link.<pid>=<seed>,<target>[,<x0>,<y0>,<x1>,<y1>]`, or add a separate `area.<pid>=<seed>,...` key. Keep the seed as the link's id: nav_new_seed already makes future ink avoid it (nav.c:402-413). nav_link_areas and nav_link_at (nav.c:374-400) return the stored area when present and fall back to the ink box otherwise. The PDF then gets area links for free through render_page_links (export.c:111-113).

(a) Capturing the area. Reuse the 'too small, taken back' path (editor.c:1151-1161): in area mode the next pen stroke is never page_add'ed. Its bbox becomes the area, then draw_page plus show(REFRESH_UI) restores the pixels. The live DU ink acts as rubber-band feedback for free, with no new drawing path.

(a) Visible border = optional ink sharing the link's seed. A smart shape drawn 'as a border' for an existing link can be given that link's seed, so link_box includes it. Erasing the border then leaves the area link working, and the eye shows it. That makes the owner's 'invisible by default, borders if you want' fall straight out of the existing seed model.
Overlap rule for mixed kinds: replace 'last stroke wins' with 'smallest area wins'. Nested links then behave intuitively, and area links need no stored creation order.

Eye toggle: draw dashed or dithered outlines of the visible page's link areas in compose() after the page blit (editor.c:678-679), through page_to_screen. Cache the areas per page and invalidate on draw_end, erase_end, undo/redo, clear and page change. A settings.ini bool (default off) plus a 'link-areas' action, so shortcuts and gestures can bind it.

Hotbar data is instant: nav_links_of plus nav_link_areas for the open page (at most 64), names by nav_name (binary search). Sort entries by box position, top to bottom then left to right, so the list reads like the page. Highlight the matching area on the page when an entry is pressed. Group links to the same target, with a count.

Hotbar naming: give PagesView a `name_pid` (open_naming pagesview.c:80-84 and PV_NAME editor.c:1643-1646 both use the open page today). Better, host a Keyboard in the hotbar itself so renaming never redraws the Pages view.

Link to a NEW page in one flow: picking mode hides New page (pagesview.c:302). A 'New page' target that does store_add_page, then asks for its name, makes links create Index entries the way wiki links do. That is probably the 'hook' the owner describes.

Hotbar search: build on Go to page (pagesview.c:330-340) but accept text too. A number jumps to that page; letters search names across at most 2000 entries with an accent-folding compare (expose store.c:861 cmp_name or an equivalent).
Backlinks are cheap: one O(nlinks) pass builds in-degree for every page. Show 'N links here' on Index rows and the hotbar, and include incoming links in the hotbar as a second group.

Graph data: nodes = nb->page_ids (store.h:21) plus an Index node. Names come from nav_name. Edges come from nav->links via target_page, with a pid-to-index table built once. Orphans = pages with in+out degree 0. Section membership via nav_section_of acts as containment, like Navi's parent_file (navi-core/src/graph.rs:31), useful for clustering or hulls.

Graph look on e-ink: node radius as in Navi, R_MIN + (R_MAX - R_MIN) * ln_1p(deg + 1) / log_span (navi-core/src/graph.rs:163). Orphans drawn hollow (crisp even in DU). Named pages solid and labelled. Gray dithers only in GL16 frames.

Graph layout: a deterministic, seeded static layout computed once with work_pump (Barnes-Hut or grid-approximated repulsion; plain O(n^2) at 2000 nodes is 4M pairs per iteration). Cache positions in a new sidecar such as graph.ini, which older versions ignore. Default to a local graph, the open page plus 1-2 hops, like Navi's L mode (navi README:339), and offer the whole notebook on demand.

The 'is the box still there' bit for graph and hotbar: recompute the open page's boxed links on every save_page (cheap, the editor has the strokes). Keep it in memory, or as a hint in links.ini, so the graph can grey dormant edges without reading 2000 pages.

Delete link with its ink: gather the page's ink strokes with that seed, remove them, and push one history_push_erase, as erase_end does (editor.c:1317-1354). Then show(bbox) and mark_changed. Either remove the entry too (link-only undo can't bring it back), or add an ACT_LINK history kind holding (pid, seed, old target, new target) so link edits join undo.

New actions for the registry (shortcuts.h:24), all bindable from Buttons and Gestures: hotbar, link graph, show link areas, smart shapes on/off, go-to-page search. Note that SHORTCUT_INDEX today means 'Pages view on the Index tab' (editor.c:1946-1948); the graph probably needs its own action instead of redefining 'index'.

Test hooks are already in place: the `pinch CX CY D D STEPS DX DY` drag, plus touch down/up/wait for long press (z_index_2_links.qs). New probes (editor.hotbar, editor.hotbar.N, editor.link_areas, editor.graph.nodes/edges/orphans) slot in next to editor.links and editor.link.N (editor.c:2617-2629).
risks: Existing quirk: a ring removed with the precise eraser or white ink stays a live but invisible link until notebook-close compaction drops the fully erased stroke; then it silently goes inert (nav.c:354 skips erase strokes; page_droppable knows nothing of links). The new design should either make areas independent of ink, or treat fully erased link ink as gone.

Two-finger drag vs pinch: pinch() pans on a 70 px travel (editor.c:2302-2320). A 'two-finger drag down opens Pages' gesture must be told apart from panning a zoomed page. Options: only at fit zoom (zoomed() editor.c:546), or edge-start bands. It must also still work when pinch_zoom is off (editor.c:2296 returns early).

Peek-hopping cost: each hotbar jump goes through go_to_page, which saves, maybe writes a thumbnail, loads the page (page_at, from disk on first visit), renders the full page, and requests a GC16 flash (editor.c:812-833). 'Instantly jump' needs GL16 for the hops and one GC16 at confirm, plus a clear 'back to where I was'.

Renaming from the hotbar on an unnamed target creates a section start and reshapes the Index's section grouping (nav_section_of nav.c:259-263). Users may not expect that tapping 'name' on a link adds an Index section.

The hotbar lists from links.ini, but entries whose ink is gone (undone, erased) are dormant. Using nav_links_of rather than nav_link_areas would show dead links; area-only links must be counted by the new rule. The editor.links probe already separates the two counts (editor.c:2622-2625).

links.ini over 4000 lines, or any other unreadable state, disables ALL links silently for the add-link shortcut (editor.c:1546), and the hotbar's link icon would hit the same wall. It needs a greyed state with a reason.

Area links get no visual cue in other readers: older Grimoire versions, the share page and the Live view show nothing. Only the PDF carries them as invisible /Link annots. Users may 'lose' links visually across devices; the eye toggle only helps on the device.
File size: adding areas to 4000 links approaches the 256 KiB NAV_FILE_MAX (nav.h:8). Past it, the file does not read and links go read-only (nav.c:100, 204-215).

nav_new_seed gives up after 64 tries (nav.c:404-411); on a pathological page an area-only link's seed could collide with a stroke from an older version. With an explicit area this is harmless if the area takes precedence over ink.

Graph layout over a 2000-page notebook can exceed the ~100 ms evdev buffer and the 15 s launcher watchdog if done in one go on the UI thread. It must be chunked with work_pump, or forked like exports (bgjob).

Keyboard lag (another lane): hotbar rename and search reuse the Keyboard. Hosting it inside PagesView inherits whatever makes the Index keyboard slow; a hotbar should host Keyboard directly over the page.
open_questions: Hotbar contents: links drawn ON this page (outgoing), links pointing TO it (backlinks), or both in two groups? The brief's 'index entries that are linked to in that particular page' reads as outgoing.

After 'tap to jump' with the hotbar still open, does it keep showing the ORIGIN page's links (peek mode: hop between targets, tap outside to commit, with a way back), or switch to the new page's links?
Are several links to the same target on one page shown once (grouped by Index entry) or once per link? If grouped, does long-press Delete remove every link to that target on the page?

Is the link's name the target page's Index name (nav.ini, global), or should each link get its own label (a new links.ini field) so renaming in the hotbar doesn't rename the page and make it a section?
For a link to an unnamed page, does the hotbar show 'Page N', and does long-press 'name' create an Index entry (a section start)?
In the new model, does erasing a visible border delete the link (today's rule, FORMAT.md:743-747) or only the decoration, leaving an invisible area link that the eye reveals?
Does 'Delete link' from the hotbar also delete its ink by default, and should either be undoable, which needs link edits in history?
Should new links default to area-only (invisible), with the smart-shape toggle deciding whether the drawn outline also stays as ink? And should existing ink-only links be migrated to explicit areas?
Does a link to the Index open the new graph view or the Index list? And what does the 'index' shortcut action mean once the graph exists?
Graph scope by default: the whole notebook, or a local graph around the open page? And what counts as an orphan: no links in or out, or also unnamed? Should links to the Index count?
When a gesture opens the hotbar while zoomed in, does a two-finger vertical drag pan or open the hotbar? Should the navigation gestures work only at fit zoom or from the screen edges?
Pen behaviour with the hotbar open: does pen ink outside the hotbar close it and draw, or is it swallowed like a tap-outside?

maps.area: Touch input and gestures: the Kindle touch pipeline, the simulator and runner, and constraints for a gesture recognizer and a "record a gesture" mode
maps.summary:
Grimoire has no gesture recognizer. input_evdev.c turns the multitouch panel into two streams: one finger (IN_TOUCH_DOWN/MOVE/UP, following the first contact only) and two fingers (IN_PINCH_BEGIN/MOVE/END, using the two lowest-numbered slots). Three blunt filters run first:
- a contact the panel flags as a palm (MT_TOOL_PALM) shuts off touch until every finger lifts;
- a second finger landing more than 400 ms after the first is treated as a palm;
- every touch is ignored while the pen is near and for 1 s after it leaves. This rule is global; it does not look at where the pen is.

In the editor, a single finger on the page only follows links (tap) or edits them (600 ms hold). Two fingers zoom and pan through one handler, which commits once the spread changes 10% or the midpoint moves 70 px. Sideways, the default view already pans vertically with two fingers.

All of this filtering lives in KINDLE_PLAT code (input_evdev.c), which no test covers. The simulator and the headless runner skip it completely: they push ready-made IN_TOUCH and IN_PINCH events. So palm handling, the late-finger rule and the pen-near rule have no automated coverage, and a recognizer written inside input_evdev.c could not be tested headless.

The panel is "pt_mt" (event4). It reports MT_SLOT, TOUCH_MAJOR, POSITION_X/Y (0..1859 x 0..2479, one unit per screen pixel), TOOL_TYPE 0..2, TRACKING_ID, PRESSURE 0..255 and DISTANCE. It has no BTN_TOUCH. The slot count (ABS_MT_SLOT max) is in none of the evidence.

Device logs show about 75-80 Hz touch reports and a median single-finger tap of 73 ms. Of the touches the pipeline cancelled (most of them two-finger landings), 79% (128 of 163) came within 150 ms of the first finger. The earliest touch after any pen event was 1173 ms, which is the 1 s window at work. The logs also hold long one-finger swipes, which do nothing in the editor today.

Recommended design:
- Move touch_frame into a pure shared module (touchgest.c, built like pensync.c). It takes contact frames with kernel timestamps plus pen state and view context, and returns today's events plus a new IN_GESTURE. Both input_evdev.c and the simulator feed it.
- Classify two-finger motion at the dead-zone commit:
  - spread change dominates: zoom;
  - mostly sideways motion, and the view can pan that way: pan, with the zoom held fixed;
  - otherwise: a swipe, or an edge swipe when the midpoint started in an edge band.
- Fire the action when the fingers lift, after PINCH_END.

Two things stand in the way of "write, lift the pen, swipe" feeling smooth:
- the global pen-near rule (a 1 s lockout after the pen leaves);
- a resting grip thumb, which today turns any later finger into a "palm" and shuts off touch.

Several smaller defects should be fixed before gestures go on top:
- **A cancelled touch can act as a tap.** When the pen comes near, or the pen-near rule starts, a finger that is down gets a real lift at its own position, not the off-screen cancel. A finger resting on a link or a panel button can therefore fire it.
- **A dropped lift leaves a stuck finger.** Touch has no SYN_DROPPED handling, so a lost lift keeps a phantom contact and touch stays dead until that slot is reused.
- **Touch timing is wrong after a stall.** Touch events are stamped when they are read, and touch is never read during long work, so a backlog arrives with bunched times.
- **The device scan can run mid-gesture.** The busy flag that holds back the 5 s device scan ignores contacts that are down but filtered out, so the 330 ms scan can start under a resting palm or a gesture.

The record mode should pick from a fixed list of gestures using the runtime thresholds, not match free-form shapes. It should tell the user why a try was rejected (pen near, fingers landed apart, diagonal, too short).

facts: Touch state: src/input_evdev.c:167-181. MAX_SLOTS 16 (169). Per slot: id, x, y, tool (174: 0 finger, 1 pen, 2 MT_TOOL_PALM) and down_at (175). Shared: main (the one slot followed), active, suppressed (palm: ignore until all lift, 178), suppressed_pinch (a late second contact, 179), last_x and last_y.

handle_touch (src/input_evdev.c:778-801):
- ABS_MT_SLOT is clamped to 0..15 (782).
- A new tracking id sets down_at = now_ms(), the READ time, not the kernel's, and resets tool to 0 (783-788).
- TOOL_TYPE and POSITION_X/Y are stored. TOUCH_MAJOR, MT_PRESSURE and MT_DISTANCE are ignored.
- BTN_TOUCH 0 clears every slot (795-798).
- touch_frame runs at each SYN_REPORT (799-800).
- No SYN_DROPPED handling: drain() at 803-810 passes every event straight through.

touch_frame (src/input_evdev.c:693-776):
- Counts contacts with tool != 2; s1 and s2 are the two LOWEST slot numbers, not the first to land (698-706).
- A palm contact cancels touch and suppresses (708-711).
- A pen near or a palm landing mid-pinch emits PINCH_END and suppresses (712-718).
- Two or more fingers outside the pen window start a pinch, unless the two down_at times differ by more than 400 ms. A late second finger means cancel + suppressed + suppressed_pinch (719-729). Otherwise cancel_touch, suppressed, PINCH_BEGIN, then PINCH_MOVE every frame (730-737).
- Dropping below 2 fingers emits PINCH_END (739-746).
- One finger: the first slot found becomes main; other fingers never move the pointer (747-760).
- Suppression clears only when every contact has lifted (753-754).
- palm_window then kills the main finger with a REAL lift at its last position (762-766). Otherwise DOWN/MOVE is emitted, MOVE only when the position changed (768-775).

palm_window() = P.prox || now_ms() - g_pen_left_ms < 1000 (src/input_evdev.c:665-667). It is global: no distance from the pen is checked. cancel_touch (670-678) ends a touch with IN_TOUCH_UP at (-10000, -10000), which can never be a tap.

Pen arrival while a finger is down (src/input_evdev.c:476-480) emits IN_TOUCH_UP at T.last_x/last_y, not cancel_touch, and so does palm_window (764). In the editor's OWN_LINK, an unmoved lift calls link_follow (src/editor.c:2455-2459), and on the panel the lift completes a button press, so a resting finger or palm becomes a tap.

emit_pinch (src/input_evdev.c:680-691) maps both fingers through the touch calibration and panel_to_logical (map() 221-227), so x,y and x2,y2 are in rotated logical screen pixels. Pinch events carry t_ms = now_ms() only.

The touch fd is read only in input_poll (src/input_evdev.c:1561). input_pump reads only the two pens (1505-1529); its comment says keys, touch, power and orientation wait for input_poll (1510-1513). So touch frames that arrive during long renders are read later with bunched read-time stamps.

Every node gets EVIOCSCLOCKID(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) at open (clock_mono, src/input_evdev.c:1238-1241, called at 1270). The comment there says touch never reads event times, so kernel-time touch stamps are available but unused.

The busy flag that gates the 5 s optional-device scan is P.prox || P.touching || T.active || g_pinching (src/input_evdev.c:1540-1541). A contact that is down but suppressed (a palm, a late second finger) does not count as busy. The skip investigation measured the scan at about 330-370 ms with the main thread blocked (~/KindleLab/evidence/skip-20261026-221652/investigation-result.json).

Touch device pick and grab: a device with ABS_MT_POSITION_X that is not a pen (src/input_evdev.c:1299). The first one found is grabbed with EVIOCGRAB and its POSITION_X/Y absinfo read (1368-1379). The open-time axis log covers only X, Y, P, DIST, TX, TY, MTX, MTY, MTP and MTTOOL (1283-1286), so MT_SLOT and TOUCH_MAJOR ranges are never logged.

After the native PIN or unlock, input_set_grab resyncs touch with EVIOCGMTSLOTS(ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID) and EVIOCGABS(ABS_MT_SLOT), and suppresses while any contact is down (src/input_evdev.c:1627-1640). This is the pattern a SYN_DROPPED resync would reuse.

Privacy rule: touches made while input is not grabbed (the PIN) are never logged (src/input_evdev.c:136-137), and the touch fd is drained into discard_input then (1561). Only the first 120 touch events of a session go to the log (141).

Panel identity, from ~/KindleLab/evidence/controller-20261027-014113/proc-bus-input-devices.txt:
- Name pt_mt, Phys 2-0024/input0, event4.
- PROP=2 (INPUT_PROP_DIRECT), EV=f, KEY=0. With no BTN_TOUCH, input_evdev.c:795-798 never fires on the Scribe.
- ABS="ee18000 0" decodes, with 32-bit words, to bits 47-48 and 53-59: MT_SLOT, MT_TOUCH_MAJOR, MT_POSITION_X, MT_POSITION_Y, MT_TOOL_TYPE, MT_TRACKING_ID, MT_PRESSURE, MT_DISTANCE.
- Ranges from the Grimoire log in ~/KindleLab/evidence/hang-20261026-193934-orient/ko-input-rotation.txt: MTX 0..1859, MTY 0..2479, MTP 0..255, MTTOOL 0..2.

Inferred touch buffer size, using the Linux v4.9 input core formula the skip investigation cites (events per packet = slots + 1 + one per ABS axis, MT axes counted per slot, + 7; buffer = next power of two of 8x that): with all 8 ABS bits MT axes, that is 9*slots + 8 events. That gives 512 events for 5 slots and 1024 for 10. Two moving fingers send about 7-11 events a frame at about 75 Hz (525-825 events/s), so a read stall of about 0.6-2 s would overflow it.

Statistics from 16 Grimoire device logs in ~/KindleLab/evidence (unique 'input: ev 6/7/8' lines; read-time stamps; biased to session starts by the 120-event cap):
- 767 single-finger downs.
- Move period p10 12 ms, p50 13 ms, about 75-80 Hz.
- Tap duration p10 35, p50 73, p90 153 ms (n=489).
- Of 508 touches under 250 ms, 427 moved 10 px or less and 479 (94%) stayed within the 30 px press slop.
- 163 downs ended in the off-screen cancel (pinch begin, palm, or late finger): 70 within 50 ms (mostly 11-13 ms, the next frame), 58 more within 150 ms, 22 within 400 ms, 13 after 400 ms.
- The earliest touch after any pen event was 1173 ms.
- Long one-finger swipes appear, e.g. 2042 px in 503 ms and 1659 px in 998 ms.

InType (src/input.h:15-35): IN_TOUCH_DOWN/MOVE/UP is commented 'first finger only' (20). IN_PINCH_BEGIN/MOVE/END is 'two fingers: (x,y) and (x2,y2)' (25). InEvent has x2 and y2 for the pinch (51), t_ms = 'when it was read' (52), and k_ms, the kernel time, for pen samples only (56).

Editor pinch handling:
- pinch() (src/editor.c:2280-2334). PINCH_BEGIN drops an OWN_LINK finger and cancels a panel press, uninverting it, which is a visible refresh (2284-2295).
- Nothing starts if another owner holds the pointer, the paper, music-builder or template sheet is open, or settings.pinch_zoom is off (2296).
- Commit needs a spread change of at least 10% or midpoint travel of ui_px(70), and re-anchors at the commit point (2311-2319).
- Zoom and pan are always coupled: zoom = z0*d/d0, clamped to zoom_min..4x the default, with the pinched spot kept under the midpoint (2320-2324).
- A REFRESH_FAST frame at most every 180 ms (2325-2328), and a REFRESH_UI settle at the end if it committed (2331-2333).
- Pinch events are ignored while the Pages view is open (2369-2372).

Single finger in the editor:
- One pointer owner at a time; a new down is ignored while one is held or a pinch is under way (src/editor.c:2381).
- A tap outside the paper sheet dismisses it and swallows the rest of the gesture (2412-2421). This is the precedent for the hotbar's tap-outside-to-confirm.
- A finger on the page is OWN_LINK (2432-2438). An unmoved lift follows the link (2455-2459). A hold of LINK_HOLD_MS = 600 (34) fires link_hold from editor_tick (2583-2584).
- Movement beyond the slop does nothing, so one-finger page swipes are unused today.

The press slop is ui_px(30), about 2.5 mm at 300 dpi (src/ui.c:469-474). The Library's row hold ROW_HOLD_MS is 600 (src/library.c:508). The link hit box is at least NAV_LINK_MIN_MM 7 (src/nav.h:14), tested via nav_link_at (src/editor.c:1660-1665).

The view: zoom_min = fit the whole page, zoom_default = fit the width (src/editor.c:523-529); view_clamp is at 504-518. The comment at 520-522 says that sideways the width fits and you pan with two fingers. So in landscape the default view can already scroll vertically, and a two-finger vertical drag means pan there. Upright on a same-size page, zoom_min equals zoom_default and nothing can pan.

editor_shortcut, the idle-only action dispatcher: it refuses while S->owner != OWN_NONE or S->pinching (src/editor.c:1974-1980). A menu action whose menu is already open closes it (1981-1995). So a gesture's action must be sent after PINCH_END clears S->pinching.

Simulator window (src/sim_sdl.c):
- Left mouse is the pen and the right button is the finger (3, 918-943).
- The mouse wheel sends a synthetic 300 px pinch scaled by 1.15 around the pointer (886-901).
- There is no other way to put two or more fingers down, and no SDL finger or trackpad events are handled.

Headless runner (src/sim_sdl.c; docs/SIM.md:63-66):
- 'touch down/move/up X Y' and 'tap X Y' push IN_TOUCH_* directly; a tap's down and up carry the same time (670-679).
- 'drag touch' steps 100 ms (683-704).
- 'pinch CX CY D0 D1 STEPS [DX DY]' pushes IN_PINCH_* directly with 160 ms steps (735-751).
- make_ev stamps t_ms = now_ms() (118-129); drags add future offsets.
- None of these go through palm, late-finger or pen-near logic.

Coverage: input_evdev.c is KINDLE_PLAT only (Makefile:40). pensync.c is the precedent for a pure, host-tested input module in CORE_SRC (Makefile:29; src/pensync.h:1-13; tests/test_pensync.c). No test file or scenario touches touch_frame, suppressed_pinch or palm handling. Scenarios that use pinch: f_batch2, k_pinch_gate (resting fingers must not zoom), p_power, v_controller_actions, y_all_screens, z_4_erase_zoom_rotate, y_pagesize_2_back, z_a_precise_other_size.

Raw pen hover position (src/input_evdev.c:328-338, 344-349):
- It is learned only while Live view's hover hook is set: hover_learn runs only if g_hover_fn (418), and hover_from_raw only if g_hover_fn (288).
- Otherwise the app knows only that the pen is near (P.prox), not where it is.
- The last contact position (P.x/P.y, g_pen_good) is always known.
The Kindle framework never sees touches: pen and touch are EVIOCGRABbed (src/input_evdev.c:19), so Amazon's own top-edge swipe and quick-settings menu cannot conflict with Grimoire's edge gestures.

Settings already has the 'Pinch with two fingers to zoom' checkbox (src/library.c:995, toggled at 1664). It is stored as settings.ini pinch_zoom (src/store.c:1692 default true, 1896 read, 2031 write).
constraints: Kindle and simulator must behave alike, and the headless runner must be able to test it. So the recognizer, including the palm, late-finger and pen-near rules, cannot live only in input_evdev.c (KINDLE_PLAT). It has to be a pure CORE_SRC module that both input_evdev.c and sim_sdl.c feed with contact frames, as pensync.c is.

No change to the .qpg format. Gesture bindings go in a sidecar ini, for example gestures.ini in shortcuts.ini's grammar like the pen plan's pen.ini. The pen plan notes that dotted settings.ini keys fail test_probe.c:30-40. Action names reuse shortcuts.c's single registry, so the controller, keyboard and pen sheets all see the same actions.

E-ink: there is no animation, so a gesture in progress shows nothing. A swipe should fire once (on lift, or on crossing the threshold) and never redraw live. Recognition must cost O(1) per touch frame, never block, and never call display waits. A gesture whose action renders (the Pages view, the hotbar's partial GL16 of about 200-400 ms) delays touch reading, which only happens in input_poll. Timing therefore has to come from kernel timestamps.

Order of events: emit IN_PINCH_END, which clears S->pinching, before IN_GESTURE, or editor_shortcut refuses it (src/editor.c:1980). After a gesture fires, every contact stays suppressed until all have lifted. That is today's T.suppressed rule, so a finger lifting late never leaks a tap or a link follow.

A new IN_GESTURE type must be dropped while asleep (power_asleep_drops), ignored while a book is being added (app.c:462), count as user presence (app.c:464), and get a name in main.c's event_name table (its static assert). No touch coordinates may be logged while input is not grabbed (src/input_evdev.c:136-137).

Edges and directions are in logical, rotated coordinates (map() applies panel_to_logical), so 'bottom' follows the orientation the user sees. Thresholds go in mm through dpi (ui_px; 11.8 px/mm at 300 dpi), so other panel sizes work.

Every UI string the record mode adds (gesture names, rejection reasons) must exist in English and Spanish and fit both orientations. Rejection reasons should be short sentences like those in the toast catalog.
opportunities:
STEP 0 (behavior-neutral): move touch_frame and cancel_touch into src/touchgest.c/.h, pure and in CORE_SRC.
- Input: contact frames {t_ms from the SYN_REPORT's kernel time; per contact: tracking id, logical x and y, tool, touch_major, pressure}, plus pen context {prox, touching, left_ms, last contact xy, hover xy when known}.
- Output: today's IN_TOUCH_* and IN_PINCH_* events.
- input_evdev.c keeps only slot bookkeeping and resync. sim_sdl.c gets contact-level commands that feed the same code.
- Add tests/test_touchgest.c covering the palm flag, the 400 ms late finger, the pen window, and pinch begin and end.

Fix while extracting:
(a) Pen arrival and palm_window kills should use cancel_touch (off-screen lift), not a real lift at the last position (src/input_evdev.c:477, 764).
(b) Handle SYN_DROPPED on touch: skip to SYN_REPORT, then resync every slot with EVIOCGMTSLOTS, reusing 1627-1640, and suppress until all lift.
(c) Stamp touch with ev_us of the SYN_REPORT. The fd is already CLOCK_MONOTONIC.
(d) Count a contact as busy whenever it is down, in hidkeys_scan_due's flag at 1540.
(e) Pick the pinch pair by landing order or tracking id rather than lowest slot, and end the pinch, rather than jumping, when one of its fingers lifts while a third stays.
(f) Never count tool 1 (MT_TOOL_PEN) as a finger.

Record mode in Settings > Gestures:
- Put the module in record mode: no pinch or pan side effects, every classification reported as a key such as 'touch.2.edge-bottom-up', and every rejection reported with its reason. The sheet then says why, e.g. 'The pen is near: move it away', 'Put the fingers down together', 'Swipe straight', 'Swipe farther', 'Only two fingers were seen'.
- Use the same thresholds as runtime, so whatever records will also fire.
- After one recording, show the gesture's name with Use and Try again. If another action already has the gesture, a toast says which action lost it (the Buttons sheet's convention). A 10 s timeout leaves the row as it was.

Pen-near relaxation, the change that makes write-then-swipe feel instant:
- Keep the 1 s window and P.prox suppression for single fingers and for contacts within about 40-60 mm of the pen's last contact or hover point.
- Accept a 2- or 3-finger landing inside the window when all of these hold: the fingers landed within 150 ms; every contact's TOUCH_MAJOR is under a palm threshold (to be measured); none has ever been flagged palm or pen; each contact is far from the pen; the finger separation is fingertip-like (about 10-45 mm).
- This needs hover_learn on contact frames always, not only while Live view hooks the hover (src/input_evdev.c:418).

Grip rejection: a contact within about 8 mm of a screen edge that stays still (3 mm or less) for 300 ms or more is a grip. It is left out of finger counts and the late-second-finger rule. This fixes today's case where a resting thumb becomes T.main and every finger of the other hand is refused as 'late'. An edge swipe differs from a grip by moving inward within about 300 ms.

Instrument first: log the first N multi-contact frames per session while grabbed. Include the slot count, tracking ids, tool, TOUCH_MAJOR, MT_PRESSURE, MT_DISTANCE and kernel landing and lift gaps. Coordinates are fine while grabbed; none at the PIN. Also add MT_SLOT and MT_TOUCH_MAJOR to the open-time axis log (src/input_evdev.c:1283-1286). This answers the slot count, palm signature and landing-window questions before thresholds are frozen.

Optional defaults to offer the owner: two-finger tap = undo and three-finger tap = redo, the convention in many note-taking and drawing apps. Another: two-finger swipe up inside the Pages view closes it, the reverse of opening it. One-finger edge swipes left and right for page turns: the logs show the owner already makes one-finger swipes, which do nothing today.
risks: The global pen-near rule (src/input_evdev.c:665-667) silently drops any gesture started while the pen hovers, or within 1 s of it leaving. 'Write, lift, swipe up for the hotbar' usually starts inside that second, or with the pen still hovering in the writing hand, so the headline gesture would feel broken on the device unless the rule becomes spatial or multi-finger aware.

Landscape conflict: at default zoom a two-finger vertical drag already pans the page (src/editor.c:520-522). Making it open Pages mid-screen would remove vertical scrolling sideways. The same conflict applies whenever zoomed. Edge bands or the pan limit must decide, which is harder to teach than 'two fingers down = Pages'.

Zoom and pan are coupled (src/editor.c:2320). A two-finger swipe meant for navigation zooms slightly through finger-spread wobble before it is classified. A translate classification has to hold the zoom, or swipes leave the view slightly zoomed.

A resting thumb or grip makes every later finger a 'late second contact' (more than 400 ms), which suppresses all touch until every contact lifts (src/input_evdev.c:722-729, 754). Users holding the Kindle with a thumb on the screen get dead taps today, and would get dead gestures.

Phantom contact after an evdev overflow: handle_touch ignores SYN_DROPPED, so a lost TRACKING_ID -1 leaves T.id >= 0. 'any' then stays true and T.suppressed never clears (src/input_evdev.c:753-754), and touch is dead until that slot is reused. Gestures add long multi-finger streams, and a Pages render can stall reads, which makes overflow likelier. The buffer is 512-1024 events (inferred).

A resting finger or palm becomes a tap when the pen comes near: a real lift at its position (src/input_evdev.c:477, 764) follows a link (editor.c:2459) or fires a panel button. More touch actions (the hotbar, gestures) make this costlier.

Read-time stamps: T.down_at (src/input_evdev.c:785) and emit_touch t_ms (450) are taken when the backlog is read. After a render, a swipe's frames bunch: zero apparent duration, so the velocity is wrong. A tap's lift can look late (a false hold), and landing gaps shrink or grow. The recognizer needs kernel time from the SYN_REPORT.

Ticks can fire before queued input: editor_tick runs after an 8 ms or 64-event batch with events still queued, so a hold or a pending double-tap timeout could fire before a lift that already happened. Resolve only when the last batch drained the input, as in the pen plan.

The optional-device scan can start during a gesture or under a palm, because the busy flag (src/input_evdev.c:1540) ignores suppressed contacts. That gives a 330-370 ms stall mid-gesture, breaking timing and possibly overflowing the touch buffer.

PINCH_BEGIN uninverts a panel press the first finger made (src/editor.c:2286-2292). Two-finger gestures that start on the floating panel cost two visible GL16 flashes. The bottom-edge hotbar swipe is likely to start on a panel parked at the bottom.

Untested code: none of the palm, late-finger or pen-near logic runs in the headless runner, because the simulator pushes IN_PINCH and IN_TOUCH directly. Gesture regressions on the Kindle would go unseen until the owner tests on the device.

Fingers landing too far apart: three-finger gestures need all fingers within a window that is not yet measured. Fingers that land unevenly may read as two fingers, then a pinch, then three. Fix the finger count when motion starts, the landing window ends, or the first lift comes, and use a narrow list of gestures.
open_questions: How many contacts does pt_mt report (ABS_MT_SLOT maximum), and what are the TRACKING_ID and TOUCH_MAJOR ranges? The evidence has none of these. A one-line EVIOCGABS probe at input_open would answer it. It decides whether 3-finger (or more) gestures are possible and what the evdev buffer size is.

How often does the Parade panel flag MT_TOOL_PALM in practice, and does it ever report the pen nib as MT_TOOL_PEN (tool 1, which touch_frame counts as a finger)? What TOUCH_MAJOR values do fingertips give compared with palm or hand-edge contacts? What does MT_DISTANCE report (capacitive hover?)?

How high above the screen does the pen keep P.prox (EMR hover range)? While one hand writes and the other gestures, how often does the pen stay in proximity? This sets how much of the pen-near rule has to be relaxed.
How close to each panel edge (and on the wide-bezel side) is a finger sliding in from the bezel first reported? This sets the edge-band width; about 12-15 mm is assumed.

Owner intent:
(1) Is 'from the bottom up' an edge-start pull only, or any two-finger upward drag?
(2) In landscape or zoomed views, should mid-screen two-finger drags keep panning, with navigation from the edge bands or the pan limit only (recommended)?
(3) Fire on lift (recommended) or on crossing the threshold?

Should gestures work outside the editor (Library, Settings, Pages view), for example a two-finger swipe up closing Pages? Should the Gestures list include one-finger swipes (page turns) and N-finger taps (two-finger undo, three-finger redo) as defaults?
Does SDL3 on macOS deliver trackpad touches as SDL_EVENT_FINGER_* events the simulator window could map onto the panel, or must the simulator rely on modifier-plus-right-drag emulation?

What landing-gap distribution do deliberate 3-finger touches have on this panel? 2-finger data from the logs: 70 of 163 cancels came within 50 ms and 128 within 150 ms. These are read-time stamps from session-start-biased samples, so they need kernel-time confirmation.

maps.area: Action registry, Buttons sheet, Settings (Gestures entry), settings.ini toggles, and how touch and pen-button gestures share one registry and one binding UI
maps.summary:
The registry has 37 actions (10 tools plus 27 named ones). Their meaning is split over three files. shortcuts.c holds the name<->id table and parses the files. library.c holds the labels, icons and groups (Buttons sheet rows: LearnRow/k_groups/action_label). editor.c's editor_shortcut is the single dispatcher, and only the idle editor acts. The exceptions: Erase while held always acts, menu buttons act through open menus, and the picker's next/previous act through the open picker.

The Buttons sheet can serve as the Gestures sheet almost unchanged: groups -> rows = actions -> tap a row -> "do it" -> learned. Two-press rows, the 10 s timeout, hold-0.6-s-to-forget, Reset and Done all carry over. For that it should be parametrized by a small BindKind descriptor (text/learn/forget/reset/title/back), not copied. Labels, icons, groups, kinds and scopes should move into one core registry that Buttons, Gestures and the pen plan all read.

Settings has no room for another list row (library.c:998). Controller and Updates are bottom buttons, so "Gestures between Controller and Updates" is a third bottom button. It only fits in Spanish ("Actualizaciones" is 234 px at 34 px) if KOReader shrinks from 420 to about 300 px. Then each middle button is 280 px wide (306 px sideways), with a label column of 248 px or more.

About 21 new actions cover every toggle and important setting cleanly. They form two new groups (Index, Screen) and fill out Editing and Pages. Every group stays within the sideways limit of 11 action rows plus Done. SHORTCUT_MAX (64), write_pads' 4 KiB buffer and two fixed [16] arrays must grow.

The pen plan was written before the controller-actions commits. Its line references are stale, and 6 of its 10 new action names now exist under other names; only zoom-in/zoom-out and scroll-up/scroll-down remain new. Its pen.ini can fold into a single gestures.ini (touch.* + pen.* lines; both files are unreleased). Its gesture-first Pen sheet becomes the action-first Gestures sheet the owner described. The touch-while-held cycler (side_button + drag pan/zoom) stays a Settings row.
facts: Action ids: shortcuts.h:6-25 (SHORTCUT_TOOL_BASE + ToolKind 0..9, then UNDO=20.., SHORTCUT_LAST=SHORTCUT_NAME_PAGE). Ids live only in memory; the files store names (shortcuts.h:11). maps.area: Ink pipeline and a smart shapes system (dwell-to-snap recognizer, toolbar toggle, format-safe snapped strokes)
maps.summary:
Smart shapes fit Grimoire without touching the .qpg format. The design has four parts:

1. **Recognizer.** A pure, geometry-only recognizer goes in a new src/shape.c. It runs only after the pen has been held still. editor_tick measures the hold; it runs at least every 30 ms.
2. **Snapped stroke.** The result is an ordinary Stroke. It keeps the raw stroke's tool, params snapshot, tip variant and seed, so a link drawn as a snapped box keeps working. Its points are plain samples: corners plus fill points for polygons, adaptive vertices for ellipses, and a median pressure and tilt.
3. **What the user sees.**
   - Holding the pen still shows a what-you-see-is-what-you-get preview, sent as one DU frame.
   - Lifting keeps the shape.
   - Moving on restores the freehand ink, and the stroke simply continues.
   - The first Undo brings back the freehand stroke, through a new ACT_REPLACE in history.c. A second Undo removes it.
4. **Where accidental snapping is stopped.** The geometry gates stop it, not the hold.
   - Size is measured in screen mm: lines need 12 mm, closed shapes 10 mm across.
   - The other gates are closure, winding around the centroid, a scribble budget, ShortStraw corners with segment line tests, and an RMS ellipse fit.
   - The prototype ran on the owner's real strokes (47 strokes, mostly the "erase me!" blackletter sample).
     - A hold-only trigger like Amazon's would fire on 21 of 47 at 550 ms and on 9 at 800 ms.
     - With the gates, no stroke shows a preview at written size, and only straight strokes do when the writing is 2 to 4x bigger.
     - Synthetic hand-wobbled shapes are recognized 94 to 100% of the time.

**Cost.** Recognition takes about 0.1 ms on the Kindle. The visible cost is drawing the shape's dabs, about 0.1 to 0.5 ms per mm of outline depending on the tool, plus the 188 ms DU waveform. That makes about 0.75 s from hold to a clean shape, against about 1 s for Amazon's.

**Toolbar and settings.** The toggle becomes a 12th panel button, under the eraser. It costs about 1% of the panel's scale in landscape with 4 pens pinned. The rest is two settings.ini keys (`shapes`, default 1, and `shape_hold_ms`) and two registry actions (`shapes` and `shape-last`), so controllers and the new Gestures sheet can bind them.
facts: PEN-DOWN: editor_event treats IN_PEN_LEAVE as IN_PEN_UP (src/editor.c:2376), allows one gesture at a time (src/editor.c:2381), and a pen outside the panel and sheets calls draw_begin and then the first draw_sample (src/editor.c:2430).

draw_begin (src/editor.c:1064-1118):
- pen_stroke picks ink, white or precise from the eraser end, the held eraser and the side button (src/editor.c:1071).
- The seed hash is at src/editor.c:1090; nav_new_seed then makes it unique among the page's ink strokes and links (src/editor.c:1104-1105).
- stroke_mark_tip records the tip variant (src/editor.c:1111).
- display_pen_mode(true) is for ink only; erase strokes use display_live_ink (src/editor.c:1116-1117).

draw_sample (src/editor.c:1120-1129):
- sample_of maps screen to page px (to_page).
- A kernel drop (ev->gap) resets the smoother (src/editor.c:1124).
- smoother_apply is exponential and distance-aware (src/brush.c:585-604), applied before the point is stored.
- stroke_append grows the bbox by the render tool's max radius + 2 (src/page.c:25-37).
- brush_add stamps dabs into page_canvas (src/editor.c:1127), and show(...REFRESH_FAST) sends a DU frame.

draw_end (src/editor.c:1131-1174):
- It calls display_pen_mode(false) (src/editor.c:1135).
- It adds the stroke's bbox to S->settle for a later GL16 settle (src/editor.c:1142; settle timings at src/editor.c:30-31).
- It drops erase strokes that changed nothing.
- In link mode it takes back a box smaller than LINK_BOX_MIN_MM 5 mm on both axes (src/editor.c:36, src/editor.c:1052-1060).
- page_add (src/editor.c:1165) and history_push_add (src/editor.c:1167) follow; link_box_drawn(a, s) takes s->seed (src/editor.c:1173, src/editor.c:1561-1572).

Stored points are already smoothed (docs/FORMAT.md:93-101). brush_add replays a stroke from its first point with interpolated pressure and tilt, at a dab spacing of max(0.5 px, 0.15 r) (src/brush.c:313, src/brush.c:548-581). Live drawing and re-rendering match pixel for pixel, and the probe editor.live_matches_render checks that (src/editor.c:2675). So a snapped polyline with few points renders correctly: straight segments are interpolated.

History (src/history.h:5, src/history.c):
- Only ACT_ADD, ACT_ERASE, ACT_PAPER and ACT_CLEAR exist.
- An action owns its strokes exactly while they are off the page.
- apply() is at src/history.c:151; strokes are found by pointer.
- undo_redo redraws the dirty rect with draw_page and refreshes it (src/editor.c:1405-1416).
- Nothing can swap one stroke for another yet.

Links (docs/FORMAT.md:734-760; src/nav.c:349-371):
- A link's box is the bbox of the points of the ink strokes with its seed, at least NAV_LINK_MIN_MM 7 mm a side.
- A snapped stroke that keeps the raw stroke's seed keeps the link working, because the two strokes are never on the page together.
- For a rectangle the tappable area matches the drawn border exactly.
- link_cancel undoes only one step when the top stroke has the link's seed (src/editor.c:1589-1599).

Format (docs/FORMAT.md):
- A stroke record is 64 bytes plus 18-byte points: f32 x, y, u16 pressure, i16 tilt x/y, u32 t_ms (docs/FORMAT.md:83-101).
- Tool ids 0 to 9 are all taken, and no new id is allowed (docs/FORMAT.md:258-264, 271-283).
- ext[2] bits 4 to 7 are reserved flags; every bit needs a Registry entry first (docs/FORMAT.md:290-298).
- Compaction from 1.1 on leaves alone any page with ext bytes it does not know (docs/FORMAT.md:203-208).
- 1.0.0-beta writes ext as 0 0 0 on re-save. So a 'shape' flag is costly and not needed: a snapped shape is ordinary stroke points.

Timing:
- The main loop polls with a 30 ms timeout and then ticks (src/main.c:235-248), so a dwell check in editor_tick resolves to within 30 ms, also while the pen is down. editor_tick's link hold (src/editor.c:2583) is the model.
- Pen samples come every 3 ms, about 330 a second (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:287).
- Batches are at most 64 events or 8 ms (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:9-12).
- Touch is suppressed while the pen is near and for 1 s after (src/input_evdev.c:667, 762), so no finger can modify a shape mid-hold, unlike Procreate's two-finger constrain.

Display:
- Pen mode tolerates only DU, and every REFRESH_FAST goes out as DU even with pixels lightening (src/display_fbink.c:569-579). So a preview or cancel frame needs no mode change.
- Any GL16 frame mid-stroke would call pen_leave, which waits on the pen's last marker (src/display_fbink.c:371-378). Toasts during a stroke must be avoided.
- The DU waveform is 188 ms at 24-27 °C and 294 ms at 15-18 °C (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:104-115).

Render cost:
- bench-ink: 25-130 µs per input sample by tool on the Kindle (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:19-34), with samples about 0.27 mm apart (tools/bench-ink.c:50-53). That is about 0.1-0.5 ms per mm of outline: a 40 mm circle (126 mm) takes 12-60 ms, a 300 mm frame 30-150 ms.
- page_render of a region replays every stroke that meets it.
- Long work must call work_pump (src/common.h:49-57; the pen buffer lasts 120-175 ms, docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:174-183).

Headless runner (docs/SIM.md:53-69, 92-100):
- It has raw `pen down/move/up` lines, and `wait MS` runs timers between them, so a still pen can be tested.
- The lines of one batch share one read time, and k_ms is 0 in the simulator. The recognizer must therefore be geometric (no speed), which ShortStraw already is.
- Relevant probes: editor.strokes, editor.stroke_points, editor.link_mode, editor.links (docs/SIM.md:185-205).

Prior art:
- iPadOS (from 14): pause with the pencil down to snap. Undo restores the hand-drawn version. Holding a finger on a stroke afterwards offers 'Snap to Shape'. The shape keeps its place, size and angle (https://ios.gadgethacks.com/how-to/make-perfect-shapes-notes-drawings-annotations-with-ios-14s-new-shape-recognition-tool-0337673).
- Procreate QuickShape: hold after drawing. It recognizes line, arc, polyline, ellipse, triangle and quadrilateral. A second finger constrains to circle, square or equilateral. An 'Edit Shape' button follows (https://help.procreate.com/procreate/handbook/guides/quickshape).
- GoodNotes added 'hold at the end of a line to make a perfect shape' in 5.6 after many requests (https://feedback.goodnotes.com/forums/191274-customer-suggestions-for-goodnotes/suggestions/31905625-draw-a-line-and-hold-to-convert-it-to-auto-shape-l).

Recognizer literature:
- ShortStraw (Wolin, Eoff, Hammond, SBIM 2008): resample at bbox diagonal / 40, straw window W=3, corner threshold median x 0.95, top-down line test chord/path >= 0.95, collinear merge. O(n), no timing needed. 0.979 correct-corner and 0.741 all-or-nothing accuracy against 0.824/0.278 for Sezgin (https://www.cs.ucf.edu/courses/cap6105/fall2010/readings/Wolin_Eoff_Hammond_SBIM08.pdf).
- $Q (Vatavu, Anthony, Wobbrock, MobileHCI 2018): up to 142x faster than $P. On a Cortex-A7 one classification in its hardest test took 191 ms against 9.4 s for $P (https://depts.washington.edu/acelab/proj/dollar/qdollar.html).
- $-family template matchers always return some best match and give no fitted parameters. A geometric fit (PaleoSketch-style, Paulson and Hammond, IUI 2008) yields residuals in mm that serve as confidence, plus the beautified shape.

constraints: A snapped shape must be ordinary stroke points: same tool id (0-9), the raw stroke's ToolParams snapshot (clamped ranges), ext bytes and tip variant (stroke_mark_tip). Do not use a new tool id, header version or ext flag. If a 'shape' flag is ever wanted, it needs a Registry entry for ext[2] bit 4 first, and 1.1+ compaction would then skip those pages.

The snapped stroke must keep the raw stroke's seed. nav_new_seed guarantees it is unique (src/editor.c:1104-1105), and a link's box is found by that seed (src/nav.c:349-371). Never give the replacement a fresh seed.

Shapes apply only to ink strokes (all 9 pens, including the highlighter and the side button's highlighter). Never to erase strokes: precise eraser, white ink, whole-stroke eraser (src/editor.c:1094). Never on read-only pages (refuse_readonly).

No toast and no GL16 refresh while the pen is down. A non-DU frame triggers pen_leave's wait (src/display_fbink.c:371-378, 573-574). Preview and cancel frames must be REFRESH_FAST only. Teaching toasts come after the lift.

Anything that can exceed about 50 ms on the main thread (the preview's dab rendering of a long outline, a region re-render) must call work_pump every few points; the pen buffer overflows after 120-175 ms (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:174-183). Never add a submission wait or a second wait on one marker.

The recognizer must be geometry only: no speed or timing features. Headless batches share one timestamp (docs/SIM.md:92-100), and after a stall the stored t_ms may bunch. Only the hold uses time, measured as wall time in editor_tick.
Thresholds are in screen millimetres (the hand's scale): page px = mm x dpi / 25.4 / zoom. Pinch zoom goes up to 4x (docs/DESIGN.md:70-80), and eraser_at_zoom already does the same for the eraser.

Live equals re-render must hold (probe editor.live_matches_render, src/editor.c:2675). The preview must draw the snapped stroke through stroke_brush_begin and brush_add over the page as it was before the stroke, so commit needs no redraw and a later page_render gives identical pixels.

The panel is icons only and must fit both orientations through panel_fit (src/panel.h:39-45); tests/test_panel.c encodes the measures. Every new string needs English and Spanish that fit: toasts about 1700 px at 44 px bold or two lines; the Spanish glossary uses lápiz for the pen and trazo for a stroke (po/es-glossary.md:23, 43).

settings.ini additions must be numeric, append-only and safe for 1.0.0-beta to drop. With no key the default is shapes on, per the owner's brief. The registry actions append after SHORTCUT_NAME_PAGE (src/shortcuts.h:24).
One Undo step per user moment. The snap is its own moment (the hold), so stroke plus snap is two steps. Link flows that undo 'the box' must undo both (src/editor.c:1589-1599).
opportunities:
THE GESTURE (all pens, on by default):
- Draw, then hold the tip still: within 1.0 screen mm for shape_hold_ms, default 550 ms (Amazon about 1 s).
- editor_tick checks this while S->owner == OWN_DRAW. It keeps an anchor point and time per stroke that draw_sample updates in O(1), resetting the anchor whenever a sample moves more than R from it.
- At the hold, run shape_recognize on the stroke so far, about 0.1 ms. If it accepts, show the preview, a single DU frame. If not, nothing visible happens, and nothing re-runs until the pen moves again.
- From the preview there are three outcomes, one rule each:
  - LIFT keeps the shape.
  - MOVE more than R puts the freehand ink back, and the stroke continues as if nothing happened (the brush state is untouched).
  - Holding longer does nothing more.
- Proximity loss counts as a lift (src/editor.c:2376).

PREVIEW AND CANCEL WITHOUT RE-RENDERING THE PAGE ('under-ink' tile backup):
- While shapes are on, draw_sample backs up each 64x64 tile of page_canvas the first time the live stroke's padded segment rect touches it, before brush_add. That is the page exactly as it was under the stroke, and costs only a bitmap check per sample.
- Preview: snapshot the raw-and-shape tiles (the with-raw state), restore the raw tiles from the under-ink backup, draw the shape stroke with stroke_brush_begin and brush_add (pumping every ~8 points), then show(union, REFRESH_FAST).
- Cancel: restore the with-raw snapshot, about 1 ms memcpy, then DU.
- Commit: no drawing at all; add union(raw, shape) to S->settle so the usual GL16 settle fixes the dithered grays.
- Memory: a 300 mm outline touches about 300 tiles, about 1.2 MB per snapshot. Cap it (say 8 MB) and fall back to draw_page(union) with pumping.

SNAPPED POINTS (shape_points):
- Start at the shape position nearest the user's first point, go in the user's direction, and close exactly at the start for closed shapes. The join adds only one extra dab of about 13 overlapping, so it does not show.
- Polygons: vertices at the intersections of the edges' least-squares lines, which beat the raw corner points, plus a point every 2 mm so whole-stroke erasing and hit tests stay smooth.
- Ellipses: N = clamp(ceil(2*pi / acos(1 - 0.25 px / r)), 24, 720) vertices (chord error at most 0.25 px).
- Pressure: the median of the middle 80% of the raw samples by arc length. Tilt: the median (so the calligraphy and fountain nibs keep their angle). t_ms interpolated by arc length between the raw first and last times.
- Same tool, params, ext and seed as the raw stroke.

SHAPE SET AND BEAUTIFICATION (v1):
- LINE: chord/path >= 0.97 on resampled points; max offset <= max(4% of length, 1 mm) + 0.5 mm. Snap to 0, 45, 90 or 135 degrees within about ±4 degrees.
- CLOSED shapes: gap <= 22% of the diagonal; winding around the centroid 1.7-2.6 pi; total absolute turning <= 1.6 x winding + 0.6 pi (rejects scribbles).
- RECTANGLE or QUAD: ShortStraw finds 4 segments, each passing chord/path 0.93. A rectangle when every angle is within ±15 degrees of 90; axis-aligned within ±5 degrees; a square when the sides are within 10%. Otherwise a straight-edged quad (diamonds come out of this path).
- TRIANGLE: 3 segments; equilateral or right-angled snaps within about 6-8 degrees.
- ELLIPSE: PCA frame plus a least-squares x²/A + y²/B = 1 fit; RMS radial error <= 6% of the minor axis, max <= 20%. A circle when the axis ratio >= 0.88; axis-aligned within ±6 degrees.
- v1.5: single-stroke arrow (shaft, then a barb), open polyline (an L or a zigzag with 90-degree snaps), arc.
- v2: a second short 'V' stroke held near a snapped line's end becomes an aligned arrowhead (multi-stroke awareness).
- All are tunable constants in shape.c, gated by a test corpus.

WHY THIS IS LESS ACCIDENT-PRONE THAN AMAZON'S:
- (1) A preview, never an instant commit. Continuing the stroke cancels it, so a writer who pauses mid-stroke loses nothing (the Chinese-characters complaint).
- (2) A recognizer that can say no: size in screen mm (lines >= 12 mm, closed shapes >= 10 mm across and >= 4 mm thick), closure, winding, scribble budget, fit residuals. On the owner's own writing, holds that Amazon's design would fire on 21 times in 47 strokes produced no preview.
- (3) A writing-burst gate: a stroke started within about 600 ms of the last lift and within about 8 mm of it needs a stricter fit (tolerance x0.7) and a 1.5x hold.
- (4) Undo brings back the freehand stroke.
- (5) A toolbar toggle plus an adjustable hold, the two things Amazon users asked for.
- (6) Ink only, never erasers.

'MORE AWARE' FEATURES THAT ARE CHEAP HERE:
- Paper-aware: on Dot grid (10) and Graph paper (11), 5 mm pitch, snap line ends and rectangle corners to the grid within 1 mm. On ruled papers a horizontal line snaps exactly horizontal.
- Link-aware: in link mode ('Draw around what links') a held box snaps to a rectangle or ellipse. Because a link's area is its stroke bbox (src/nav.c:349-371), the tappable area then equals the visible border. This is the 'visible borders' half of the owner's link hotbar idea.
- Zoom-aware gates.
- Later: snap endpoints to shapes snapped earlier this session (diagram connectors).

UNDO: add ACT_REPLACE to history.h:5 and history.c.
- count=2: strokes[0] is the raw stroke, strokes[1] the shape, indices[0] the position.
- Undo or redo swaps the page pointer in place and dirties union(bbox0, bbox1).
- `owns` says which of the two is off the page: owns means the shape is off, and action_free frees that one.
- At commit: page_add(raw), history_push_add(raw), then replace plus history_push_replace. Or page_add(shape) with ACT_ADD(shape) and ACT_REPLACE ordered so that one Undo shows the raw stroke.
- This matches iPadOS (undo returns the hand-drawn version). Unit-test it in a new tests/test_history.c or in test_ink.c.

RETROACTIVE SNAP (iPadOS 'Snap to Shape' without a selection tool): a new action `shape-last`.
- It runs the recognizer, with all gates but no hold, on the page's newest ink stroke when the top undo action is that stroke's ACT_ADD.
- On success: ACT_REPLACE, draw_page(union) with pumping, then REFRESH_UI. Otherwise a toast: 'No shape in the last stroke.' / 'El último trazo no es una forma.'
- Bindable to a pen-button double-click (the pen-shortcuts plan), a controller button or a Gesture. It gives writers who turn the hold off a zero-accident way to get shapes.

risks: link_cancel (src/editor.c:1589-1599) undoes a single step when the top stroke has the link's seed. After a snapped link box, that undo only swaps the shape back to the raw stroke, which stays on the page. It must undo the replace and the add together. The same applies to anything else that assumes 'last action = last stroke'.

Mid-stroke previews cost DU flicker. In slow, deliberate hands (blackletter, CJK) a still pen on a stroke-so-far that passes the gates shows a preview, then a revert when the pen moves on: two DU frames of the region. Nothing is lost, but the cancel frames on gray or image paper can leave dithering until the settle. The size and writing-burst gates and the hold setting keep this rare. The owner should test on their blackletter and on a PDF page.

Big outlines with expensive tools (marker, charcoal, highlighter, 113-133 µs per sample) can take more than 100 ms to render for the preview. Without work_pump inside the loop that draws the shape, the pen's evdev buffer overflows (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:174-183).

Pen rest jitter and the scaled pen's sparse events are not measured. The relayed pen leaves out unchanged axes, so a still pen may send no samples (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:172-176). The hold must be judged by wall time in editor_tick, never by sample spacing, and the 1 mm radius needs device data.

The negative corpus is small: 47 strokes on 3 pages, mostly one blackletter sample whose timestamps are read-time stamps. A broader set of the owner's real writing is needed before the thresholds are fixed. The gates rely mainly on size, so very large handwriting (headings at 2-4x) can still produce line snaps, if the writer holds and lifts during the preview.
Two Undo steps per shape may surprise users who expect one step per pen-down (the owner's 'one gesture, one moment' rule, from Tangent). It needs an explicit owner ruling.

Making the panel taller (PANEL_BUTTONS 12) changes test_panel.c's fits and every panel hit position in existing scenarios that tap below the eraser (undo/redo/clear/prev/next/paper/display/pen feel/library). Many .qs files tap panel coordinates and would need to be re-measured.

The under-ink tile backup adds per-sample work and memory while shapes are on. It must be exact: back up before the dab and pad by brush_max_radius + 2, as stroke_append does, or the restore leaves ghost pixels. A bug here shows as stale ink, which is worse than the slow draw_page fallback.

Snapped shapes use a uniform median pressure. A pencil or charcoal shape looks more even, 'mechanical', than the hand's stroke. This is a taste decision, and the alternative (raw pressure resampled by arc length and low-passed) keeps more character but can leave tapered blobs at the join.
open_questions: Undo after a snap: two steps, as in iPadOS (first back to the freehand stroke, then gone), or one step that removes the shape entirely?
Hold time default and choices: 550 ms with Quick / Normal / Deliberate (0.4 / 0.55 / 0.9 s)? And where does the setting live: Pen feel, the new Gestures sheet, or a long-press on the toolbar toggle?

Toolbar placement: a 12th panel button under the eraser (it costs about 1% of the panel's scale in landscape with 4 pins and shifts every button below it), or the toggle only in the tool picker's labelled row, with the panel unchanged?
Shape set for v1: line, circle/ellipse, rectangle/square/quad, triangle (and pentagon)? Should single-stroke arrows and arcs be in v1 too (Amazon has arrows), or wait for v1.5?

Which pens snap: all nine ink tools including the highlighter (straight highlights are a top request elsewhere), or a per-tool opt-out? White ink and the precise eraser never snap in this proposal; agreed?

Links: the brief's eye icon 'shows the area that is counted as tappable' and says users who want visible borders draw them with smart shapes. Does that mean links become invisible areas, stored as a rect or polygon in links.ini (still changeable in beta.5), rather than ink strokes? If so, should a shape drawn while the hotbar's link icon is active become the link's area, with the user choosing whether its ink is kept?
Grid snapping on Dot grid and Graph paper (line ends and corners to the 5 mm grid): on by default when shapes are on, or a separate toggle?
Uniform median pressure for snapped shapes (clean, technical), or keep a low-passed copy of the hand's pressure (more pencil character)?
Should a deliberate 'every stroke snaps' diagram mode (shapes=3, no hold) be offered later as the toggle's long-press option, or is hold-to-snap the only way in?

maps.area: UI rendering on e-ink (toolkit, refresh choreography, hotbar cost) and the graph Index view (layout, drawing, interaction, limits)
maps.summary:
Grimoire's UI is drawn into one 8-bit canvas (App.screen). Each loop pass presents a single union dirty rect with the strongest mode asked for: FAST=DU 188 ms, UI=GL16 271 ms, FULL=GC16 341 ms over the whole panel, and every 30th UI refresh is promoted to FULL. Measured on the host and scaled about x20 to the Kindle:

**Hotbar.** A bottom hotbar (~1820x640 px, about 1.2 Mpx) costs about 50-90 ms of CPU to compose, draw and copy, then 271 ms of GL16 with no flash, whether it opens, updates or closes. Choreography:
- Peek jumps refresh only the page area, as GL16 (no flash).
- The one GC16 flash comes when the user taps outside to confirm, which also clears the peeks' ghosting.
- A dense page renders in up to 1.2 s, so "instant" jumps need a small cache of rendered page canvases (origin page plus prefetched link targets).

**Index keyboard lag (owner's item 4) has a clear code cause.** The Pages view repaints the whole 1.78 Mpx keyboard on every pointer event, including every move (~1.0 ms host, so ~20 ms on the Kindle each). It also refreshes field and key as one big DU union and never does a GL16 settle. The Library's naming keyboard draws only on change, flushes field then key separately, and settles at 900 ms. Fix: share the Library's path.

**Graph view.** Lay it out from nav.ini + links.ini only, so no page needs loading:
- Precompute the layout with a Navi-style force layout (BFS-shell seed, then Barnes-Hut springs) and cache it in a new graph.ini sidecar. Keep it stable: new nodes are placed incrementally and a full "Tidy up" runs as a niced background job.
- Exclude the Index hub and orphans from the forces.
- Draw with 1-bit-safe marks so DU previews and GL16 settles look the same: four degree tiers (hollow ring, 25% dither, 50% dither, solid), sized by log degree; greedy labels with white knockouts.
