- Local graph = a radial ring layout around the current page, members only. Fading the rest on global positions was illegible in my mock.
- Tap a dot = preview card; tap again = open.

**Two blockers found in the toolkit:**
- canvas_line_aa scans its whole bounding box: 0.82-0.85 ms per long edge on the host, so 4000 edges would take about a minute on the Kindle. A row-span version I wrote gives identical pixels and is 40x faster.
- HitList holds only 128 entries.

I checked the proposals with mock renders built from Grimoire's own canvas/ui/font code (PNGs in scratch).
facts: Repo HEAD verified 89893aa (claude/beta5-features). All file:line below are at that commit.

Refresh modes: display.h:7-11 (FAST=DU live ink, UI=GL16 partial no flash, FULL=GC16 flash); display_fbink.c:596 maps them to WFM_DU/WFM_GL16/WFM_GC16; display_fbink.c:598 a FULL refresh always covers the whole panel (r = {0,0,PW,PH}), so any FULL flashes everything including a hotbar.

Waveform lengths measured on the owner's panel at 24-27 C: DU 188 ms, A2 94 ms, GL16 271 ms, GC16 341 ms; DU 294 ms at 15-18 C (docs/INK-PERFORMANCE.md:104-113). docs/DESIGN.md:80-83 still says DU ~120 ms (stale).

Framebuffer copy cost: fbpack_row 20-40 ns/px, a full-screen copy 45-100 ms, pumping every 64 rows (display_fbink.c:520-521, copy_rect 522-545). A 1.8 Mpx card redraw+copy measured 90-100 ms on the Kindle (INK-PERFORMANCE.md:232).

Dirty accumulator: app_invalidate unions every rect into ONE rect and keeps the strongest mode (app.c:909-917). app_flush presents it once per loop pass (app.c:920-964). Every 30th UI refresh is promoted to FULL regardless of size (app.c:931-932). Toasts are overlaid only for the present and never stored in App.screen (app.c:466-470, 945-960).

Only waits in present: pen_leave before a non-DU refresh (display_fbink.c:573-575, 374-377). A stroke enters MTK pen mode only when no standard update is still on the panel (display_fbink.c:62-66, 576-585). A GL16 hotbar close still in flight when the user starts writing makes that stroke fall back to plain DU, which can queue up to ~300 ms (INK-PERFORMANCE.md:151-157).
app_press_feedback = canvas_invert + immediate DU of the rect, bypassing the accumulator (app.c:974-978).

Editor refresh usage: live ink show(d, REFRESH_FAST) (editor.c:1128); grayscale settle show(settle, REFRESH_UI) after the pen leaves 150 ms or 1.5 s near (editor.c:28-29, 2536-2540); go_to_page = render_page_full + view_reset + compose_all(REFRESH_FULL) (editor.c:812-835); Pages view open/hide FULL (editor.c:1422-1444); paper sheet tap-outside dismisses and swallows the gesture with GL16 (editor.c:2411-2420); pinch paints compose_all(REFRESH_FAST) at most every 180 ms, commits after 10% spread or 70 px travel, settles with REFRESH_UI (editor.c:2307-2333).

compose(r) layers: page_canvas blit (or bilinear blit_view when zoomed, pumped) then panel, paper sheet, templates, display menu, music builder, tool picker (editor.c:671-687). When the Pages view is open, compose redraws the ENTIRE Pages view on every call regardless of r (editor.c:672-675). compose resets a->toast_floor = 0 on every call (editor.c:676).

Landscape: the default view fits the page width, and two-finger drags already pan vertically (editor.c:519-521 view_reset comment; view_clamp 504-517). At portrait default zoom a two-finger vertical drag does nothing visible today.

Index keyboard lag: pagesview_pointer, while the keyboard is open, calls keyboard_draw on EVERY pointer event, including moves where nothing changed. It then invalidates rect_union(key, field) as a single REFRESH_FAST and never settles with GL16 (pagesview.c:327-347, the draw at 344-345). The Library draws only when the key or field changed (library.c:1867). It presents the field first with an immediate app_flush, then the key (library.c:1870-1875), and settles the keyboard with one GL16 900 ms after typing pauses (library.c:1876-1877, 1926-1928).

keyboard_draw repaints the whole modal: 1820x980 = 1.78 Mpx with ~40 framed keys (keyboard.c:194-197 modal_rect, 240-272). Measured on the host: 1.01 ms Gothic, 0.87 ms Classic per call (bench at scratchpad/hook/bench/kbbench.c), so ~20 ms per pointer event on the Kindle at the x20 host-to-Kindle factor of INK-PERFORMANCE.md:234-235.

canvas_line_aa evaluates EVERY pixel of the segment's bounding box (canvas.c:171-185). Host benchmark: 0.817-0.845 ms per random long edge vs 0.017 ms for a 117 px edge (bench/linebench.c). A row-span version (each row evaluates only pixels within hw+1 of the line) gives bit-identical pixels and is 40x faster: 0.0214 ms per edge (bench/spanline.c, 0 differing pixels over 300 edges).
Other primitive costs on the host: canvas_disc_aa r=18 0.002 ms; full-screen canvas_fill 0.062 ms; 1820x560 round-rect fill+outline 0.093 ms (bench/linebench.c).

Fonts: stb_truetype with a 1024-slot glyph cache flushed at 3/4 full (font.c:76-88, 143-173). Gothic text faces are pixel fonts (Jersey 10, Jacquard 24) drawn without smoothing, so they are 1-bit crisp under DU (font.c:1-3, 40-50). The only label sizes are 44 px (text), 64 px (title) and 34 px (small) at 300 dpi (ui.c:94-96). font_draw_left_name truncates names without tripping the fit check (font.h:44-46).

Icons are Nerd Font MD glyphs via k_icon_cp (ui.c:99-152). Verified present in assets/TerminessNerdFontMono-Regular.ttf by rendering: F0349 magnify (search), F0208/F0209 eye/eye-off, F06D0/F06D1 eye outlines, F05E3 chart_bubble (three dots: reads as the graph), F104A graph_outline, F07CB gesture squiggle, F0741 gesture_tap, F0832/F0831 shape outline/filled (triangle, square, circle).

Widgets: ui_sheet modal card with title (ui.c:340-367); toasts sit above App.toast_floor (app.c:477-485); HitList holds at most 128 hits (ui.h:146-149), so a graph view must hit-test its own nodes; Press: a tap means slop under 30 px and the same rect, a long press 600 ms (ui.h:131-138, ui.c:466-478).

Settings: Controller and Updates are not list rows; they share the bottom button row between KOReader (420 px) and Done (380 px), each half of mid = in.w - 890 = 750 px in portrait Gothic (library.c:1028-1043). A third button at current widths gets 240 px with 208 px label room; Spanish 'Actualizaciones' needs 234 px at caps34 (measured). Shrinking KOReader and Done to 320 px gives three 293 px buttons with 261 px label room, so 'Mando', 'Gestos' and 'Actualizaciones' fit. The Settings card is 1820 px tall (library.c:928), and sideways only 18 px are left above Done (library.c:999), so there is no room for another list row.

Data limits: STORE_MAX_PAGES 2000 (store.h:7); NAV_LINKS_MAX 4000, NAV_LINKS_PER_PAGE 64, NAV_LINK_MIN_MM 7 (nav.h:9-13). Graph edges come from links.ini alone (link.<pid>=<seed>,<target>, target index or p<pid>) and names from nav.ini (FORMAT.md:717-761), so the graph needs no page loads. The hotbar's areas need the open Page: nav_link_areas, nav_link_at (nav.h:58-64).

FORMAT.md:916-926: new notebook-wide data goes in files of its own in the notebook folder, which older versions never touch. A graph.ini sidecar fits this rule, and beta.5 is unreleased so its format is free.
bgjob runs one niced child process at a time with a queue (bgjob.h:1-6, 18-36). This fits a 'Tidy up' layout job on the MT8512's second core, writing graph.ini atomically.

Navi layout (navi-core/src/graph.rs): constants REPULSION 16000, SPRING_K 0.055, SPRING_L 110, GRAVITY 0.02, DAMPING 0.9, R_MIN 5, R_MAX 22 (7-15). Node radius log-scaled: R_MIN + (R_MAX-R_MIN)*ln(1+deg+1)/ln(1+maxdeg+1) (158-162). Seed placement: BFS shells from the highest-degree hub, rings sorted by parent angle, islands packed in rings outside, orphans in an arc near the hub or a phyllotaxis spiral to the right (place_disk 807-830, arrange_around 648-695, orphans 719-745). Relaxation with Barnes-Hut theta 0.9; prerelax steps = clamp(2e6/n^2, 30, 240) (1078-1128). Local graph = BFS 1-3 hops over visible edges (323-337) used as a FADE mask, not a relayout (navi/src/app.rs:738-760). Labels only at zoom >= 0.25 with alpha ramp and truncation to 8/15/all chars by zoom (navi/src/painter.rs:337-375). Hit radius max(r*zoom, 9 px) (painter.rs:377-389).

Obsidian graph conventions (obsidian.md/help/Plugins/Graph+view): node size by incoming links; global vs local graph with a depth slider; filters Search files, Tags, Attachments, Existing files only, Orphans; color Groups by search; Display: Arrows, Text fade threshold, Node size, Link thickness, Animate (creation time-lapse); Forces: Center, Repel, Link force, Link distance; hover highlights connections, click opens, right-click menu, wheel or +/- zoom, drag or arrow-key pan. The local graph also has incoming/outgoing/neighbor link toggles (Obsidian 0.9.0 changelog and forum).

Force-layout cost (C port of Navi's step, single thread, float; bench/layoutbench.c), per step on the host: n=100/e=150 0.008 ms; n=300/e=600 0.039 ms; n=600/e=1500 0.075 ms; n=1000/e=4000 0.227 ms; n=2000/e=4000 0.564 ms. At x20 and 300 steps that is about 0.25 s on the Kindle for a few hundred pages and about 3.4 s for 2000 pages and 4000 links.

Mock renders, made with Grimoire's own canvas.c/ui.c/font.c at 1860x2480 (scratchpad/hook/bench/): graph-gothic.png and graph-classic.png (global view, 100 nodes / 124 edges, 4 fill tiers, greedy labels: draw 2.5-3.4 ms host, about 50-70 ms Kindle); graph-local.png (local mode as fade on global positions: illegible); graph-radial.png (radial depth-2 local: clean); hotbar-gothic.png and hotbar-classic.png (hotbar plus link-area overlay). At full resolution the 2x2-pixel-cell 25% and 50% Bayer fills are clearly distinct from hollow and solid (crop1.png).
constraints: Never change .qpg: link areas, numbered tags, hotbar and graph are overlays composed into App.screen, never page_canvas. Positions and pins go in a new graph.ini sidecar in the notebook folder (unknown lines carried, size limits as nav.ini), view toggles in settings.ini.
A FULL refresh flashes the whole panel (display_fbink.c:598). Peeks must use GL16 on the page region only; reserve GC16 for the commit, screen changes and graph open/close.

Every UI refresh counts toward the 30-to-FULL promotion (app.c:931). Frequent hotbar use (open, row highlight, close = 3 UI refreshes) forces a surprise full flash about every 10 uses unless the counter becomes area-weighted.
The dirty accumulator unions rects (app.c:915-916). Two far-apart updates (field and key, hotbar row and page area) become one big refresh unless flushed separately, as library.c:1871-1873 does.

Main-loop blocking over about 100 ms overflows the pen evdev buffer (scaled pen 120-175 ms, raw digitizer 50-100 ms while hovering: INK-PERFORMANCE.md:180-187). Layout, render of 4000 edges and page prefetch must call work_pump, run in slices, or run in a bgjob child. Never add MXCFB_WAIT_FOR_UPDATE_SUBMISSION or a second waiter on a marker (display_fbink.c:171-178).
No animation. Pan and zoom give feedback via DU at most every ~180 ms (the pinch precedent, editor.c:2325-2328), then one GL16 at release.

Draw graph marks 1-bit-safe (solid, hollow, ordered-dither patterns on 2x2 cells, dashed/dotted strokes) so DU frames dithered by fbpack_row look like the GL16 settle. This also keeps them distinct under display_set_invert.
Touch targets at least 10 mm (~118 px at 300 dpi, ui.h:3-4). Link areas are at least 7 mm (nav.h:13). A node's hit radius must be at least ~5 mm even when its dot is drawn at 10-15 px.
Every new string in English and Spanish and fitting both orientations (the fit check GRIMOIRE_CHECK_FIT, docs/SIM.md). Names are user data: truncate with font_draw_left_name.

Kindle and simulator alike, testable headless. Layout float results can differ between the arm64 simulator (FMA contraction on by default) and the armv7 Kindle. Store positions as data; tests assert invariants (no overlaps, orphans in the tray, current page in view), not exact coordinates.
HitList is capped at 128 (ui.h:146-149). The hotbar pages its rows (64 links per page maximum) and the graph does its own nearest-node hit test.
compose() resets toast_floor to 0 (editor.c:676). A hotbar drawn inside compose must set toast_floor to its top afterwards so toasts stay above it.
opportunities: FIX THE INDEX KEYBOARD (owner's item 4, next version): in pagesview_pointer draw only when dirty or field_dirty is non-empty; present the field first (app_flush) then the key; add the 900 ms GL16 settle. Best done by factoring one keyboard host helper (library.c:1860-1879 logic) used by the Library, the Pages view and the coming hotbar rename and search sheets. Optional extra: keyboard_draw_keys(field + changed keys only) instead of repainting all 1.78 Mpx.

Replace canvas_line_aa's bounding-box loop with the row-span loop: identical pixels, 40x faster on long lines (bench/spanline.c). It is a prerequisite for the graph and speeds the Gothic frieze and arches for free. Add canvas_disc_pattern(cx, cy, r, level): 4x4 Bayer on 2x2-pixel cells, 16 levels, for node tiers.

Hotbar refresh choreography:
- Open: compose + draw the card, then GL16 of its rect. About 50-90 ms CPU plus 271 ms on the panel; or DU first and a GL16 settle ~600 ms later for a ~240 ms perceived open. Gothic text is already 1-bit.
- Row tap: app_press_feedback DU invert at once.
- Peek: render the target into page_canvas and GL16 only the area above the hotbar; the hotbar stays and the peeked row shows selected.
- Confirm (tap outside): close, then one REFRESH_FULL that also clears the peeks' ghosts.
- Close with no jump: GL16 of the hotbar rect only.
- Swallow the confirming tap (the paper-sheet pattern, editor.c:2411-2420) so the close finishes before the next stroke and pen mode stays available.

Make peeks feel instant: keep an LRU of 2-3 rendered page canvases (4.6 MB each at 1860x2480). Hold the origin page so going back is a blit, not a re-render of up to 1.2 s (INK-PERFORMANCE.md:229). While the hotbar is open and idle, prefetch its link targets in work_pump-pumped slices. Peeks should not set nb.last_page or info_dirty (notebook.ini's 2 fsyncs) until confirmed.

Peek semantics that make 'tap outside to confirm' meaningful: the hotbar keeps listing the ORIGIN page's links while you peek. Swipe it down or press Back to return to the origin page; tap outside to stay on the page shown.

Hotbar layout (mock hotbar-gothic.png):
- A grip line on top, then a header '<page name> - N links' with the hint 'Tap outside to stay here'.
- Link rows as two-column framed chips (124 px rows): a numbered badge, the target's name (Index icon for the Index), 'p. N' at the right. Ordered by each link area's reading position (y, then x) so numbers match the page.
- A bottom tool row: Go to (F0349), New link (F0339), Areas (eye F0208, dim when off, inverted when on), and at the right Index (F05E3) opening the graph.
- About 640 px tall in portrait; three or more columns and shorter in landscape.

Eye overlay ('Areas'): cache the page's link rects (nav_link_areas, at most 64) when the page or its links change, not on every compose; live-ink frames call compose at a high rate. Draw a dashed 4 px outline plus a numbered corner tag matching the hotbar row. The mock shows a full diagonal hatch competes with handwriting; keep hatch for press feedback or as an option. Persist the toggle in settings.ini and make it assignable to Gestures and Shortcuts.

Make the FULL promotion area-weighted (sum refreshed area, promote after ~8 screens' worth) so typing, hotbar toggles and small settles stop causing random full flashes. Optionally let app_flush present two disjoint rects separately when their union would be more than ~1.5x their sum.

Graph data model:
- Nodes: every named page (the Index entries), every page with an outgoing or incoming link, and the open page. Unnamed unlinked pages are hidden behind an 'All pages' toggle and appear as tiny hollow dots.
- Edges: links deduped per page pair; width 2.5 px, plus 1 px per extra link up to 5.
- Links to the Index: a small lozenge badge on the page's dot, not edges. The mock shows an Index hub turns the global graph into a hairball; a 'Show the Index' toggle can add it as a lozenge hub at its linkers' centroid with no forces.

Graph layout:
- Navi's place_disk seed (BFS shells from the top-degree hub, rings sorted by parent angle, islands outside), then about 300 Barnes-Hut spring steps with Navi's constants. Deterministic jitter seeded by page id, not index.
- Orphans excluded from forces and laid in a 'Not linked yet' tray: below the graph in portrait, right in landscape.
- Cache positions in graph.ini (pos.<pid>=x,y in integer world units, pin.<pid>=1, links=<generation>).
- Incremental: a new node goes at its placed neighbours' centroid plus one rest length, then 20-50 relax steps on its 2-hop neighbourhood with others fixed (well under 10 ms).
- Full relayout ('Tidy up', or a first open with more than ~400 nodes) as a bgjob child; meanwhile show the O(n+e) seed placement and swap with one GL16 when done.

Graph drawing:
- Render into the graph's own offscreen canvas; compose only blits from it.
- Cull to the viewport. Order: edges, then white knockout disc around each dot, then dots, then labels.
- Degree tiers: 0 hollow ring, 1 = 25% dither, 2-3 = 50% dither, 4+ solid. Size = Navi's log formula, 10-30 px at fit, unnamed pages at 0.75x.
- Open page: concentric double ring. Selected: 8 px ring, its edges 6 px, label as an inverted chip.
- Labels: greedy by priority (selected, current, neighbours, named by degree), 4 candidate positions, occupancy test against placed labels and dots, white knockout box, 34 px, at most ~320 px wide. 'p. N' labels for unnamed pages only when zoomed or in local mode.
- Measured: 100 nodes about 50-70 ms on the Kindle. Worst case 2000/4000 at fit zoom about 1-2 s with span lines, so render pumped.

Graph interaction:
- Tap a dot (nearest within max(r, 5 mm)) to select: a bottom card shows name, page and links, with Rename, Local and Open buttons. Tap again or Open to jump (FULL). Tap empty space to deselect.
- One-finger or pen drag pans with a DU preview of the offset-blitted render every ~180 ms, re-rendered with GL16 at release. Pinch zooms with a nearest-neighbour scaled preview, then GL16. Double-tap zooms 2x; a Fit button resets.
- Pen hover over a dot can show its name as a small DU tooltip (e-ink's hover).
- Long-press a dot to rename; pen hold-then-drag pins it.
- Toggles, all assignable to Shortcuts and Gestures: Local (off, 1, 2), Orphans (show, hide, only), All pages, Show Index, List (the existing Index list).

Local graph: a radial ring layout (Navi positions_radial / place_rings). The current page sits at the centre, depth-1 on one ring, depth-2 on an outer ring, angle-sorted by parent; only members are drawn. It is O(n+e), instant and deterministic. The mock (graph-radial.png) is clean; fading the rest on global positions (graph-local.png) is not.

Make one Index destination: the Pages view's Index tab gains a Graph/List switch, and the hotbar's Index button opens the same view. Probes for the headless runner: editor.graph.nodes, .edges, .selected, .node.<pid> (tier, radius, visible), .labels.
New icons need only k_icon_cp entries: search F0349, eye F0208/F0209, graph F05E3, gestures F07CB, smart shapes F0832 (glyphs verified present in the bundled font).
Settings 'Gestures' button between Controller and Updates: shrink KOReader and Done to 320 px so three 293 px icon+label buttons fit, including Spanish 'Actualizaciones'.
risks: canvas_line_aa as it stands makes a graph unusable: about 16 ms per long edge on the Kindle, so 4000 edges would take about a minute.

Peek page renders of up to 1.2 s on dense pages break the brief's 'instant jump' unless page canvases are cached or prefetched; prefetch must be pumped and must stop the moment a stroke or gesture starts.
The FULL-every-30-UI rule will flash the screen unpredictably during heavy hotbar and keyboard use; the first flash may land on a hotbar open.

Two-finger vertical drags already pan the page sideways (landscape) and when zoomed in. The proposed two-finger down/up gestures collide with pinch-pan there and need disambiguation (input agent), or must be portrait-default-zoom only.

A hotbar close in flight (GL16 271 ms) when writing resumes forces that stroke off MTK pen mode onto plain DU, which can lag up to ~300 ms. Swallowing the confirming tap mitigates this; making 'pen down outside = confirm and keep writing' would not.
GL16-only peeks accumulate ghosting if the user peeks many pages without confirming; Back to the origin should also use FULL, or a FULL should follow after N peeks.
Global graph with the Index as a node becomes a hairball, since nearly every page links to the Index (mock evidence). Local-as-fade is illegible on e-ink (mock graph-local.png).
Full layout for 2000 pages and 4000 links is about 3.4 s on the Kindle and must not run on the main thread unpumped. The bgjob queue runs one child at a time, so a PDF mirror can delay 'Tidy up'.
Layout determinism differs between the arm64 simulator and the armv7 Kindle (FMA, libm). Tests must not compare exact coordinates; positions should persist in graph.ini so a recompute rarely happens.

compose() redraws a full-screen modal on every call when it is open (editor.c:672-675). Hosting the graph the same way without an offscreen cache would re-render thousands of edges on every settle or compose.
The dense diagonal hatch for link areas obscures handwriting (mock). Users may also mistake overlay patterns for ink unless the overlay is visibly UI: dashed outline plus numbered tag.
Live view streams App.screen (app.c:933). The hotbar, link-area overlay and graph would reach viewers unless excluded the way toasts and the chip are.
docs/DESIGN.md:80-83 states DU ~120 ms while measured DU is 188 ms (INK-PERFORMANCE.md:108). Latency budgets should use the measured figures.
open_questions: While peeking, should the hotbar keep the origin page's links (my proposal: it enables Back to the origin) or switch to the new page's links?
Does a pen stroke outside the hotbar confirm and close it while keeping the ink, or is it swallowed like a finger tap? Swallowing is safer for pen-mode latency.
Which pages are graph nodes by default: named pages plus linked pages (proposed), or every page? Do links to the Index show as a hub node or as a badge (proposed: badge, with a toggle for the hub)?
Should the hotbar also list backlinks ('Linked here from'), Obsidian-style, as a second tab or section?
Should the graph open global (all pages, current page marked) or local around the current page by default, and should the last mode be remembered per notebook in graph.ini?
Is 'Go to' a page-number pad only, as today, or a name search over the Index too (letters filter names live, digits jump to a page)?
In Gestures recording, should the gesture trace be drawn live? That costs DU frames like ink and would use the live-ink path.
Should user-dragged (pinned) node positions travel with the notebook in graph.ini and in raw ZIP exports, as nav.ini and links.ini do?

specs.experience:
How the owner lives it, screen by screen. Sizes are px at 300 dpi; text is 44 px, titles 64 px, small text 34 px.

0. AFTER UPDATING
- The first time a notebook opens, a 6 s two-line toast appears: "New: two fingers up show this page's links. Two fingers down show all pages." / "Novedad: dos dedos hacia arriba muestran los enlaces de esta página; hacia abajo, todas las páginas." It is bit 0 of settings.ini hints.
- The panel has two new icon buttons:
  - Smart shapes, directly under the eraser. It shows a filled triangle-square-circle glyph (F0831) when on, and the outline glyph (F0832) with a 4 px diagonal slash when off. It never uses the inverted 'selected' look, which means 'current pen' on this panel.
  - Links, a chain glyph (ICON_LINK) directly under Next. A 7 px solid dot in its corner says this page has links, like the tool button's 'more here' mark.

1. WRITING
Nothing changes unless the pen pauses. With Smart shapes on (the default):
- Draw a box, then keep the tip still (within 1 mm) for 0.55 s. The wobbly line turns into a clean rectangle in one DU frame.
- Lift to keep it. Move on and your own line comes back and simply continues.
- Handwriting never snaps: geometry gates, not the hold, decide.
- After the first snap, a tip (on lift, never mid-stroke): "Shape made. Undo takes it away; the panel's shapes button turns this off."

2. MAKING A LINK (the page never leaves)
1. Open the Links bar with two fingers up or the panel's Links button. On a page with no links it says "No links on this page yet." and its New link button is the primary (inverted) one.
2. Tap New link. The bar closes (GL16 of its rect) and a banner card, 1100x130 at the top centre, says "Draw around what links." with a Cancel button. The banner stays as long as link mode lasts.
3. Draw a ring around 'see Chapter 2' with the pen. Holding at the end can snap it to a rectangle or an ellipse.
4. On lift the ring disappears; its pixels come back from the under-ink tile backup (no page re-render). A dotted box shows the area: the stroke's bounding box.
5. The Find sheet rises over the page bottom, titled "Where does the link go?". Its rows:
   - New page...
   - The Index
   - "Choose from the pages..." (the thumbnail picker)
   - then the Index entries, filtered live by the keyboard; typing digits offers "Page 12".
6. Tap 'Chapter 2'. The sheet closes and a toast says "Linked to Chapter 2. Tap it with a finger to go there; hold it for more." That is bit 1 of hints the first time; afterwards it is just "Linked to Chapter 2."
7. The dotted box stays until the next touch, or 4 s, then leaves with the next settle.

Other outcomes:
- One Undo removes the link.
- A ring under 5 mm both ways: "Too small for a link. Draw around it again." Link mode stays.
- Cancel or Close menu: "No link made."
- New page... appends a page at the end of the notebook, so existing page numbers never move. It asks for the new page's name at once: a keyboard over the page, Cancel = leave it unnamed. Then: "Linked to the new page 53." You stay where you were.

3. FOLLOWING
A one-finger tap inside an area goes there, as today (GC16). The pen always draws, even on a link.

4. LONG PRESS ON A LINK (the second owner ruling)
- After a 600 ms still hold (LINK_HOLD_MS, unchanged), a dotted border draws around the area in DU while the finger is still down: visible about 190 ms later.
- Then a small card opens beside the area (GL16), 840 px wide, about 724 px tall:
  - Header: the target's name in bold (or 'Page 12', or 'The Index'), and in small text "Page 12".
  - Rows of 124 px, each icon + text:
    - Go there
    - Rename in the Index, or "Add to the Index..." when the target has no name
    - Change where it goes
    - a rule, then Delete link
- The notebook page stays fully in view.
- What each row does:
  - Rename opens the keyboard over the page bottom, titled "Name in the Index". Done says "Page 12 is in the Index as Chapter 2."
  - Change where it goes opens the Find sheet in pick mode. The dotted border stays.
  - Delete link says "Link deleted. Undo brings it back." Any ink border the user drew stays: it is ordinary ink.
  - A tap outside closes the card and is swallowed.
- On a read-only page only Go there is live; a line says "This page is read-only."
- A link to the Index has no Rename row.

5. BROWSING WITH THE LINKS BAR
- Two fingers up (or the panel button) raise the bar from the bottom (GL16, about 0.3 s).
  - Header: "Links on this page (4)", with a small tappable "2 pages link here" (it opens the Index map around this page), and a close X at the right.
  - Below: numbered chips in reading order, the same numbers the eye draws on the page.
- Tap chip 2, 'Chapter 2':
  - The chip inverts at once (DU) and the page area above the bar becomes page 12 (GL16, no flash).
  - The header becomes a back button "Page 3", then "Looking at Chapter 2, page 12".
  - The chips are still page 3's, so you can hop: tap chip 3 to look at another.
- Ways out:
  - Tap the page above the bar with a finger: the bar closes, you stay on page 12, and one clean GC16 flash clears the peeks' ghosting. That tap never follows a link.
  - Put the pen down on the page: the same, and the stroke is kept.
  - Back returns to page 3 with the bar still open.
  - X, the panel's Links button or two fingers down close the bar and keep the page shown.
- Long press a chip: the same card as on the page. The dotted border shows when page 3 is on screen; while you are peeking, the card says which page the link is on instead.
- The bottom row has four labelled buttons:
  - Go to (magnifier)
  - New link (chain with plus)
  - Areas (eye: an outline 'eye off' glyph when off, inverted 'eye' when on)
  - Index map, at the right (the three-bubbles glyph)
- More than 6 links: a small pager in the header (back and next icons with '1 / 3').

6. SEEING AREAS
- Tap Areas: every link area of the page shows a 4 px dashed outline with a numbered corner tag that matches its chip.
- The setting persists (settings.ini link_areas) until turned off.
- The first time, a tip: "Dotted boxes show where a finger tap follows a link. They never print."

7. VISIBLE BORDERS
A visible border is drawn as ink with Smart shapes, around the link. It is not part of the link: deleting the link keeps the ink, and erasing the ink keeps the link.

8. INDEX MAP
- Open it from the bar's Index map button, from a new "Map" button on the Pages view's Index tab, or with the index-map action. It is full screen (GC16).
- What it shows:
  - Every linked page is a dot and every link an edge.
  - Named pages are labelled, and the open page has a double ring.
  - Dots get fuller and bigger as they are more connected: hollow, light dither, half dither, solid.
  - Unlinked pages sit hollow and small in a "Not linked yet" tray.
- Interaction:
  - Tap a dot: a bottom card shows its name, "Page 12. Links to 3, linked from 2", and Open, Around it, Rename.
  - Tapping the selected dot again, or Open, goes there.
  - Pinch, or the −, Fit and + buttons, zoom; one finger drags to pan.
  - "All pages | Around this page" switches the view, List opens the Index list, and Back returns to the page.

9. GO TO (FIND)
- Open it from the bar, from the Pages view's Go to page..., or with go-to-page. It is a bottom sheet over the page with the keyboard, field "Page number or name".
- Digits give "Go to page 12"; letters list matching Index entries, ignoring accents. A tap goes there (GC16).

10. PAGES VIEW
Two fingers down, or the page chip, as before. Close it with Back, or with two fingers up.

11. SETTINGS > GESTURES
- Settings' bottom row becomes KOReader | Controller | Gestures | Updates | Done.
- The sheet lists "Gestures: on (tap to turn off)" and then six groups. Each row reads 'action: gesture', e.g. "Pages view: 2 fingers down".
- Recording:
  1. Tap a row. A card asks "Do the gesture for Pages view", under it "Swipe or tap with two or three fingers, or use the pen's button."
  2. Do it. The card shows "2 fingers down" large, with Use, Try again and Cancel. If the gesture belongs elsewhere: "Now for Next page. Use moves it here."
  3. A refused try says why, e.g. "Put the fingers down together."
- Holding a row 0.6 s forgets its gestures. Reset gestures brings back the built-ins.

12. ZOOMED IN, OR SIDEWAYS (where the page can scroll)
Mid-screen two-finger drags pan exactly as today. A navigation swipe starts in the 15 mm band at the screen's edge. The Gestures sheet's footer and the record card say so: "When the page can scroll, swipe from the edge."
specs.gestures:
VOCABULARY. A fixed list. Free-form shapes are never matched, and every name is short and in both languages.
- touch.2: down, up, left, right, tap, double.
- touch.3: down, up, left, right, tap, double. Offered only when the panel reports at least 3 MT slots (InputCaps.touch_slots from a new EVIOCGABS(ABS_MT_SLOT) probe at input_open).
- pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>: the pen plan's slots, recorded in the same sheet.
- Reserved, never recordable:
  - a one-finger tap or hold (links and UI);
  - a two-finger spread or squeeze while pinch zoom is on;
  - a two-finger drag the view can follow (a pan).
- One-finger swipes are not in v1 (owner question).
- Names (EN/ES):
  - '2 fingers down' / '2 dedos abajo'
  - '2 fingers up' / '2 dedos arriba'
  - '2 fingers left' / '2 dedos izq.'
  - '2 fingers right' / '2 dedos der.'
  - '2-finger tap' / 'Toque con 2 dedos'
  - '2-finger double tap' / 'Doble toque, 2 dedos'
  - the same for 3
  Measured: two-press rows such as '2 dedos der. / 2 dedos izq.' fit at 1395 px.

DEFAULTS. Built in, never written to a file:
- touch.2.down = pages
- touch.2.up = links (the bar)
- touch.2.left = next-page
- touch.2.right = previous-page. Clamped, never creates a page; at the end a toast: "This is the last page." / "Es la última página."
- touch.2.tap, touch.2.double and touch.3.* unbound. A two-finger tap fires easily from a resting hand; calm wins. The sheet suggests them under a 'Try' line: "Ideas: two-finger tap for Undo, three-finger tap for Redo."
- Pen defaults are the pen plan's: Button.triple = clear-page, Button.hold = clear-page.
- Close swipes, built in, not bindable:
  - while the Links bar is open, two fingers down close it, keeping the page shown;
  - while the Pages view is open, two fingers up close it.
  These are 'the reverse of the opening swipe'; they hold even when the user rebinds the opening gestures, because the bar is bottom-bound and Pages is a top sheet.

RECOGNIZER. A new pure module, src/touchgest.c/.h, in CORE_SRC (like pensync.c). Both input_evdev.c and sim_sdl.c feed it contact frames:
- t_ms = the SYN_REPORT's kernel CLOCK_MONOTONIC time;
- per contact: tracking id, logical x and y, tool, touch_major;
- pen context: prox, touching, left_ms, last contact xy, hover xy (hover_learn always on, not only for Live view).

The editor (or the Library in record mode) pushes view context whenever view_clamp changes the zoom or offsets:
- can_pan_x / can_pan_y: page larger than the view on that axis at the current zoom;
- pinch_zoom; gestures_on; record.

Rules (thresholds in mm through dpi; 11.81 px/mm at 300 dpi):
1. FINGER COUNT is fixed at the first of: motion commit, the end of the landing window (150 ms for 2 fingers, 250 ms for 3), or the first lift. More than 3 contacts: suppressed.
2. COMMIT is today's dead zone: a spread of at least 10% or midpoint travel of at least 70 px. Then:
   - spread_px = |d - d0| and trans = |mid - mid0|;
   - spread_px >= 0.6 x trans: ZOOM. Pinch moves are tagged PM_ZOOM, today's behaviour; ignored when pinch_zoom is off.
   - Otherwise TRANSLATE, along the dominant axis if within 30 degrees of it, else DIAGONAL.
3. TRANSLATE:
   - The drag is a PAN (tagged PM_PAN, zoom held at its commit value so spread wobble no longer zooms) when the view can pan on that axis AND the midpoint did not start in the 15 mm (177 px) edge band the swipe moves away from (the top band for down, the bottom band for up, the right band for left, the left band for right).
   - Otherwise it is a SWIPE candidate, tagged PM_SWIPE; the editor ignores those moves, so nothing redraws.
   - A DIAGONAL drag pans if the view can pan, else it is refused ('Swipe straight').
4. A SWIPE FIRES AT THE FIRST LIFT when all of these hold:
   - travel >= 20 mm (236 px);
   - at most 1000 ms since landing;
   - both fingers moved the same way (cosine >= 0.8) by similar amounts (ratio 0.5 to 2).
5. TAP: every finger lifts within 300 ms of landing, none moved more than 5 mm (59 px), and the lifts fall within 150 ms of each other.
   DOUBLE: a second tap with the same finger count starts within 350 ms of the first one's last lift (the owner's pen ruling). Only a count whose double is bound waits; otherwise the tap fires at once.
6. EVENT ORDER: IN_PINCH_END (clears S->pinching) comes first, then IN_GESTURE {g, fingers, x, y = start midpoint}. Then every contact stays suppressed until all have lifted (today's T.suppressed rule), so a late finger never leaks a tap or a link follow.
7. TIMEOUTS (a pending double, the 3-finger landing window) resolve only when App.input_drained says the last batch emptied the queue (the pen plan's guard).

PEN AND PALM, the calm part:
- Single fingers keep today's global 1 s pen window.
- A 2- or 3-finger landing inside the window, or while the pen hovers, is accepted only when all hold:
  - the fingers landed within 150 ms;
  - none was ever flagged palm or pen (tool 1 or 2);
  - every touch_major is under the palm threshold, to be set from the step-1 device log;
  - each contact is at least 50 mm from the pen's last contact point, and 60 mm from its hover point while P.prox;
  - finger separation is 10 to 45 mm.
- GRIP: a contact within 8 mm of an edge that stays within 3 mm for 300 ms is a grip. It leaves the finger count and the late-finger rule, so a resting thumb no longer kills every later touch. An edge swipe differs from a grip by moving inward within 300 ms.
- A valid swipe refused only because the pen was near shows "Move the pen away, then swipe." / "Aparta el lápiz y desliza." at most once per 10 minutes. Nothing else is ever silent-and-weird.

TOUCH DEFECTS FIXED FIRST (behaviour-neutral step):
- pen arrival and the palm window end a finger with cancel_touch (off-screen), never a real lift (input_evdev.c:477, 764);
- SYN_DROPPED resync with EVIOCGMTSLOTS, suppressing until all lift;
- kernel timestamps;
- the busy flag counts every down contact;
- the pinch pair is chosen by landing order;
- tool 1 is never a finger;
- MT_SLOT and TOUCH_MAJOR join the open-time axis log;
- PINCH_BEGIN restores a panel press it cancels with DU, not GL16.

DISPATCH:
- IN_GESTURE goes to the editor. It looks up gesturemap (touch source) and calls editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y), with no shortcuts_enabled gate.
- Gestures follow the shortcut rules: idle editor only; a menu's own gesture closes it; the close swipes above.
- The Library handles IN_GESTURE only in record mode. Pages view handles only its close swipe.
- New InType IN_GESTURE is added to:
  - main.c event_name (static assert);
  - power_asleep_drops (dropped while asleep);
  - the app.c:462 BOOK_RUNNING guard;
  - note_input.

LEARN FLOW (Settings > Gestures; the Buttons sheet's code parametrized by a BindKind):
- Tap a row. touchgest goes to record mode (no pinch or pan side effects, every classification and refusal reported) and so does pengesture.
- The card (sheet_rect, 1400 px wide, about 900 tall) shows:
  - title "Do the gesture for %s";
  - body "Swipe or tap with two or three fingers, or use the pen's button.";
  - footer "When the page can scroll, swipe from the edge."
- Refusals update one line (GL16 of that line only):
  - "Move the pen away first."
  - "Put the fingers down together."
  - "Swipe in a straight line."
  - "Swipe farther."
  - "Move both fingers the same way."
  - "Two fingers spreading is kept for zoom."
  - "One finger is kept for taps and links."
- Recognized: the name at 64 px with Use, Try again and Cancel.
  - Use applies the binding. When the gesture belonged to another action, the line said "Now for %s. Use moves it here." beforehand, and a toast follows: "That gesture is no longer for %s."
  - The same thresholds as runtime, so whatever records also fires.
- Timeouts: 10 s with no attempt keeps the row as it was. A second tap on the row stops.
- Rule per source, as in Buttons: a gesture does one action, and an action has at most one touch gesture and one pen gesture.

THE GESTURES SHEET
- Rows of 140 px (draw_menu), at most 12 in landscape:
  - "Gestures: on (tap to turn off)" (settings.ini gestures)
  - Index..., Pages..., Editing..., Tools..., Menus..., Screen...
  - Reset gestures
  - Done
- Each group sheet has at most 11 action rows plus Done (the Actions section).
- Rows show 'Label: touch gesture, pen gesture', e.g. "Undo: 2-finger tap, Pen: double-click", or "none".
- Hold-eraser is shown only for pen gestures (it needs a release).
- Not recordable at all: language, calibrate, the shortcuts toggle, the gestures toggle.
specs.hotbar:
NAME AND ROLE
In the UI it is 'Links' ('Enlaces'): the links drawn on this page, read as the Index entries they lead to. It is a bottom sheet in the editor's sheet family: it joins sheet_open, front_menu, menu_action, close_front and open_menu, so its own action closes it, Close menu closes it, and other bindings never act through it or its keyboards.

CONTENT
- One chip per link of the open page (outgoing), in reading order: sorted by area top, and by left edge when two tops are within 10 mm.
- Numbered 1..n. The eye draws the same numbers on the page.
- Each chip:
  - a 56 px outlined disc with the number (34 px bold);
  - the target's Index name in bold 44 px, cut with font_draw_left_name; or 'Page 12' in regular weight for an unnamed page; or a list glyph and 'The Index';
  - at the right, 'p. 12' in 34 px.
- Two links to the same target are two chips, so the numbers always match areas.
- Backlinks are not listed. The header's small chip "%d pages link here" ("%d páginas enlazan aquí") opens the Index map around this page, hidden when 0.
- Legacy links not yet migrated count when their ink box exists. Dormant ones (no area, ink gone) are not listed, as today.

LAYOUT, UPRIGHT (1860x2480)
- Card x=20, w=1820, bottom 20 px above the screen edge.
- Top padding 20, then the header (110):
  - origin state: title "Links on this page (%d)" ("Enlaces de esta página (%d)"), the backlink chip after it, a 90x90 X at the right, and the pager (back icon, '1 / 3', next icon, 300 px) left of the X when there are more than 6;
  - peek state: a 300x90 back button (ICON_BACK + 'Page 3'), then "Looking at %s, page %d" ("Viendo %s, página %d"), and the X.
- Chips: 2 columns, 878x124, 24 px column gap, 16 px row gap. At most 3 rows (6 per screen).
- Tool row: 16 px gap, then four buttons 425x150 (icon above a 34 px caps label), 20 px gaps:
  - Go to / Ir a
  - New link / Nuevo enlace
  - Areas / Áreas
  - Index map / Mapa (at the right).
- Height = 316 + rows x 140: 456 (empty, one row of text) to 736. The page keeps at least 1724 px above.

LAYOUT, SIDEWAYS (2480x1860)
- Card x=20, w=2440. Chips in 3 columns of 784x124, 2 rows (6 per screen). The same header and tool row.
- Height 456 to 596.

OTHER RULES
- toast_floor is set to the card's top after compose.
- The card draws over the floating panel where they overlap, as other sheets do.
- Empty state: one line "No links on this page yet." ("Esta página aún no tiene enlaces."), and New link drawn as BTN_PRIMARY.
- Read-only page or links.ini not readable: New link is drawn disabled, but a tap on it toasts the reason, "This page is read-only." or "Links could not be read in this notebook.", never silence.

OPENING
Two fingers up, the panel's Links button, or the 'links' action. Compose the card into App.screen and GL16 its rect: about 50-90 ms of CPU plus 271 ms. Header hint the first 3 times: "Tap a link to look. Tap the page to stay." (hints bits 3-4 count).

TAP A CHIP: JUMP INSTANTLY, KEEP THE BAR (PEEK)
1. app_press_feedback inverts the chip at once (DU).
2. The origin page is saved once, before the first peek, as go_to_page does.
3. The target's canvas comes from a 2-entry LRU of rendered page canvases (4.6 MB each). The editor's page_canvas keeps the origin, so Back is a blit. A miss renders with work_pump; a dense page can take up to 1.2 s, and the inverted chip covers that wait.
4. Compose the peek canvas at fit (view_reset for the peek) and GL16 only the page area above the card. No GC16.
5. The chips stay the origin's. The selected chip is inverted, and the header switches to the peek state.
6. Peeks never set nb.last_page or info_dirty, and never write thumbnails.
7. While the bar is open and idle, the visible chips' targets are prefetched in pumped slices. Prefetch stops at any input.

COMMIT (STAY)
- A finger tap anywhere outside the card, the panel included (the paper sheet's rule), commits and closes. The tap is swallowed (OWN_MODAL), so it never follows a link or presses a panel button.
- Commit makes the peeked page current: index, last_page, page_at, the peek canvas swapped into page_canvas. The origin's thumbnail is written if needed, then one REFRESH_FULL (GC16) clears the peeks' ghosts.
- Pen down outside the card commits and closes too, and the stroke draws: ink is never lost. The card's region is recomposed and sent with that stroke's DU frames (pen-mode friendly) and added to S->settle. No flash while writing.
- X, the Links button, the 'links' action, Close menu and two fingers down all close the bar AND keep the page shown, the same as commit: 'closing keeps what you see'. With no peek, closing is just GL16 of the card rect.

BACK
'Page 3' blits the origin back and GL16s the page area; the bar stays. After 5 or more peeks without a commit, Back uses REFRESH_FULL instead, to clear ghosting.

LONG PRESS A CHIP (600 ms, still)
- It opens the same link card as a long press on the page, anchored above the chip, keeping the 840 px width.
- Not peeking: the origin area gets its dotted border.
- Peeking: there is no border, since the origin is not on screen, and the card's header adds "On page 3".
- The card's actions are the same: Go there, Rename in the Index / Add to the Index..., Change where it goes, Delete link.
  - Go there from the card is a commit to that page.
  - Rename hosts the keyboard over the page: kbhost; the card stays visible above the keyboard in portrait.

THE FOUR BOTTOM ICONS
- GO TO opens the Find sheet in go mode. The bar closes first, keeping any peeked page.
- NEW LINK closes the bar (committing any peek, so the link is made on the page you see) and starts link mode.
- AREAS toggles settings.link_areas, saved with settings_save:
  - the button goes from the outline 'eye off' glyph (F06D1) on a plain button to the inverted 'eye' glyph (F0208);
  - then a GL16 of the button plus each area's rect, flushed separately when they are far apart;
  - no toast, since the result is visible; the first time only, tip bit 2.
- INDEX MAP opens the map (GC16). The bar closes; the map's Back returns to the page.

PAGING
The header pager moves through screens of 6 chips with a GL16 of the chip grid only. Up to 64 links means 11 screens.
specs.link_areas:
MODEL (owner ruling, 2026-10-27)
- A link is an invisible rectangle on its page, stored in links.ini, plus a target.
- Making a link leaves no ink. The area shows only when the eye is on, or while the link is being made, or with the dotted border of a long press.
- A visible border is optional ordinary ink, drawn with Smart shapes, and independent of the link.

MAKING
1. link_start shows the top banner, 1100x130 at y=24 (GL16 of its rect): "Draw around what links." / "Dibuja alrededor de lo que enlaza." with a 260x100 Cancel button.
2. The next ink stroke draws live as usual (DU rubber band), with the under-ink tile backup on. Smart shapes may preview a rectangle or ellipse.
3. On lift the stroke is never page_add'ed:
   - Its point bbox in page px becomes the area, or the snapped shape's bbox.
   - Its pixels come back from the tile backup (memcpy, about 1 ms); without a backup, draw_page(bbox) pumped.
   - The dotted box is drawn and sent as DU, then folded into the settle.
4. Under 5 mm both ways (LINK_BOX_MIN_MM): toast and stay in link mode.
5. The Find sheet opens in pick mode.
6. On a pick, an ACT_LINK history step {pid, seed = nav_new_seed, before: none, after: target + area} goes on the page's history, links.ini is saved, and a toast follows. On a save failure: roll back (nav_load) and toast "Could not save the link."
7. Back or Cancel at any point: "No link made." There is nothing to undo, because no ink was added.

Entry points: the bar's New link, the Index tab's Add a link, the add-link action.

FOLLOW, HIT TEST AND OVERLAP
- A finger tap uses nav_link_at: the stored area, made at least NAV_LINK_MIN_MM = 7 mm a side around its centre, as today.
- The rule changes from 'last stroke wins' to 'smallest area wins', so nested links behave and no creation order needs storing. Ties go to the higher seed.
- Pen never follows.

LONG PRESS (the second ruling; replaces link_hold's Pages view)
At 600 ms:
1. The dotted border is drawn: the area inflated 8 px, 5 px black dashes (20 on, 14 off) with a 3 px white halo on both sides so it reads over ink, and solid 24 px corner Ls so the box shape is unmistakable. It is sent as DU and flushed on its own (visible about 190 ms later).
2. Then the card, placed below the area (32 px gap). If that does not fit, above; then right; then left; else bottom-centre. The card stays 24 px inside the screen and avoids S->panel by sliding horizontally. GL16.

Card actions:
- Go there: follows.
- Rename in the Index / Add to the Index...: nav_set_name on the target pid through an editor-hosted keyboard.
- Change where it goes: Find pick mode, then ACT_LINK with before = old target and after = new target.
- Delete link: ACT_LINK with before = link and after = none, then save, toast and the border's GL16 removal.
- A tap outside closes the card, swallowed, with a GL16 of the card plus the border.
- Undo and Redo of ACT_LINK rewrite links.ini and redraw the overlay if the eye is on. A failure toasts and keeps the history intact.

EYE OVERLAY
- Drawn in compose() right after the page blit, before the panel: a 4 px dashed outline (16 on, 12 off, white 2 px halo) and a 52x52 tag at the area's top-left corner (white fill, 3 px frame, number 34 px bold).
- Areas are cached per page (at most 64 rects, in screen space through page_to_screen) and invalidated on page change, link edits, undo/redo, zoom or pan.
- Live-ink composes reuse the cache, so the cost is a rect test per area.
- UI only: never in page_canvas, thumbnails, PDF or the sleep image. Live view streams it like the panel.

BORDERS
- Ordinary ink strokes with fresh seeds.
- The 'border shares the link's seed' trick is deliberately NOT used. It would bring back ink-dependence and the precise-eraser quirk.

MIGRATION OF BETA.5 LINKS (made the old way: an inked lasso whose seed is the link's)
- A links.ini line without an area is a legacy link.
- When the editor loads a page (load_page), each legacy link of that page gets area = link_box of its ink (the raw point bbox, not inflated, ignoring erase strokes) and the links file is marked dirty. It is saved at the next save_page through nav_save_links.
- The lasso ink stays on the page as ordinary ink. Its seed stays reserved, because nav_new_seed still avoids link seeds.
- A legacy link whose ink is already gone stays legacy and dormant, as today.
- Until a page is visited, its legacy links keep working through the old ink-box fallback (hit test and PDF export both prefer the area and fall back to ink). So migration is invisible and lazy, and needs no whole-notebook pass on the UI thread.
- After migration, erasing the old lasso no longer breaks the link. The beta.5 precise-eraser quirk (a link that works invisibly until compaction drops its ink) disappears with it.
specs.smart_shapes:
TRIGGER
- Ink strokes only: all nine pens, the highlighter included. Never erase strokes, white ink, the precise eraser or read-only pages.
- The tip must stay within 1.0 screen mm of an anchor for shape_hold_ms (default 550; choices Quick 400, Normal 550, Slow 900).
- draw_sample updates the anchor in O(1): a sample more than 1 mm from the anchor resets the anchor and its time. editor_tick (it runs at least every 30 ms, pen down too) checks for the hold by wall time, never by sample spacing (a still relayed pen may send nothing).
- At the hold, shape_recognize runs once on the stroke so far (about 0.12 ms on the Kindle). A refusal changes nothing, and the recognizer does not run again until the pen moves.

SHAPES IN V1 (all tunable constants in src/shape.c)
- LINE: chord/path >= 0.97, max offset <= max(4% of length, 1 mm) + 0.5 mm, at least 12 mm long. Snaps to 0/45/90/135 degrees within 4 degrees.
- ARROW: a line plus one barb. A 3-segment polyline whose last two segments meet at 20 to 70 degrees, each barb 15 to 45% of the shaft. Becomes a straight shaft with two symmetric barbs.
- CLOSED shapes, common gates:
  - gap <= 22% of the diagonal;
  - winding around the centroid 1.7 to 2.6 pi;
  - total absolute turning <= 1.6 x winding + 0.6 pi (rejects scribbles);
  - at least 10 mm across and 4 mm thick.
- RECTANGLE / SQUARE / QUAD (diamond): ShortStraw finds 4 segments, each with chord/path >= 0.93. A rectangle when every angle is within 15 degrees of 90, axis-aligned within 5 degrees, a square when the sides are within 10%. Otherwise a straight-edged quad.
- TRIANGLE: 3 segments. Equilateral or right-angled snaps within 7 degrees.
- ELLIPSE / CIRCLE: PCA frame plus a least-squares fit. RMS radial error <= 6% of the minor axis, maximum <= 20%. A circle when the axis ratio is >= 0.88; axis-aligned within 6 degrees.

CONFIDENCE AND ACCIDENT DEFENSES (why it is calmer than Amazon's)
1. The geometry gates above decide, not the hold. On the owner's 47 real strokes, holds that a hold-only trigger would fire on 21 times gave no preview at all.
2. A preview, never an instant commit: moving on cancels it, so a writer who pauses mid-stroke (blackletter, CJK) loses nothing.
3. Size gates are in screen mm, so they follow zoom.
4. Writing-burst gate: a stroke started within 600 ms and 8 mm of the last lift needs tolerances x0.7 and a 1.5x hold.
5. One toggle on the panel plus an adjustable hold: the two things Amazon users asked for.
6. Shapes are never offered on erasers.

PREVIEW
- While shapes are on, draw_sample backs up each 64x64 tile of page_canvas the first time the live stroke's padded segment rect (brush max radius + 2) touches it, before brush_add.
- At an accepted hold:
  1. snapshot the with-raw tiles;
  2. restore the raw tiles from the under-ink backup;
  3. draw the snapped stroke through stroke_brush_begin/brush_add, calling work_pump every 8 points;
  4. show(union, REFRESH_FAST): one DU frame, pen mode kept.
- Pen moves more than 1 mm: restore the with-raw snapshot (memcpy, then DU). The stroke continues untouched.
- Lift (or LEAVE): commit with no redraw; union(raw, shape) joins S->settle for the usual GL16.
- Memory cap 8 MB of tiles. Past it, fall back to draw_page(union), pumped.
- No toast and no GL16 while the pen is down.

STORAGE
- The snapped result is an ordinary Stroke: the raw stroke's tool id (0-9), ToolParams snapshot, ext bytes, tip variant and seed. Only the points differ:
  - polygon corners at the intersections of the least-squares edge lines, plus a point every 2 mm;
  - ellipses with N = clamp(ceil(2 pi / acos(1 - 0.25 px / r)), 24, 720) vertices;
  - start nearest the user's first point, in the user's direction, closed exactly;
  - pressure = the median of the middle 80% of samples; tilt = the median; t_ms interpolated by arc length.
- No format change, no ext flag. Live equals re-render holds (editor.live_matches_render).

UNDO
- One pen-down is one moment. The raw stroke is never added; only the snapped stroke is page_add'ed with one ACT_ADD, so one Undo removes the shape entirely. (Owner question; iPad-style two-step is the alternative.)
- link_cancel's 'undo the box' is gone with ink-free links, so the replace/undo interplay risk disappears.

RETROACTIVE
- Action shape-last ('Shape the last stroke' / 'Dar forma al último trazo') runs the recognizer with all gates but no hold on the page's newest ink stroke, when the top undo action is that stroke's ACT_ADD.
- On success: one ACT_ERASE + ACT_ADD pair pushed as a single history step (history_push_replace, count 2), then draw_page(union) pumped and REFRESH_UI.
- Otherwise a toast: 'No shape in the last stroke.' / 'El último trazo no es una forma.'
- Bindable to a pen double-click, a pad or a gesture.

TOGGLE
- P_SHAPES panel button under the eraser (see the panel note in the Actions section).
- Tap: settings.shapes flips, settings_save, the button repaints (GL16 of the button), and a toast: 'Smart shapes on. Hold the pen still at the end of a shape.' / 'Formas inteligentes activadas. Mantén el lápiz quieto al final de una forma.' or 'Smart shapes off.' / 'Formas inteligentes desactivadas.'
- The tool picker gets a labelled row under the ink row: 'Smart shapes' with an On/Off chip, and 'Hold' with a Quick/Normal/Slow cycle chip, 520 px each. Words live where there is room for words.
- Actions: 'shapes' (toggle), 'shape-last', 'shape-hold' (cycle; toast 'Shape hold: Normal (0.55 s)').

PAPER AWARENESS (v1, on with shapes)
On Dot grid and Graph papers, line ends and rectangle corners snap to the 5 mm grid within 1 mm. On ruled papers a near-horizontal line snaps exactly horizontal.

DEVICE TUNING
An empty file grimoire/shape-log turns on a log of each hold's features and decision (size in mm, winding, residuals, corners, kind or reason, ms), never coordinates.
specs.graph_view:
NAME AND ENTRY
- 'Index map' / 'Mapa del índice'. A full-screen view hosted like the Pages view (OWN_MAP; it joins sheet_open and the menu family).
- Opened from the Links bar's Index map button, from the Pages view Index tab's new 'Map' header button (beside 'Rename this page'), and with the 'index-map' action.
- The 'index' action keeps meaning the Index list.

DATA (no page loads)
- Built from nav.ini, links.ini and nb->page_ids, with a pid-to-index table built once.
- Nodes: every page.
- Edges: links deduped per unordered page pair, with a count.
- A link to the Index is a 16 px lozenge badge at the source dot's upper right, not an edge: an Index hub turns the map into a hairball.
- Degree d = the number of distinct linked neighbours (in or out), +1 if the page links to the Index.
- Orphan = d 0. A named orphan is still labelled: an entry nothing links to yet.

LOOK (1-bit-safe, so DU previews and GL16 settles look the same, and inversion keeps them distinct)
- Fill tiers by degree:
  - d 0: hollow 3 px ring;
  - d 1: 25% dither (4x4 Bayer on 2x2-px cells) plus ring;
  - d 2-3: 50% dither plus ring;
  - d >= 4: solid.
- Radius at fit = 14 + 16 x ln(1+d) / ln(1+dmax) px (14 to 30), unnamed pages x0.75. So orphans are both smaller and hollow, progressively.
- Open page: a concentric double ring, 6 px apart. Selected: an 8 px ring, its edges at 6 px, and its label as an inverted chip.
- Edges: 3 px black anti-aliased lines (the row-span canvas_line_aa); a pair with 2 or more links gets 5 px. Direction appears only in the selection card.
- Drawing order: edges, a white knockout disc per dot, dots, labels.
- Labels: named pages in bold 34 px, at most 320 px wide (font_draw_left_name), placed greedily by priority (selected, current, neighbours, then named by degree). Four candidate spots, each tested against placed labels and dots, with a white knockout box; a label that collides is skipped until zoomed. 'p. 12' for unnamed pages only at 2x zoom or more, or in Around mode.

LAYOUT
- graph.c, pure, in CORE_SRC. Navi's place_disk seed: BFS shells from the top-degree hub, rings sorted by parent angle, islands packed outside. Then 300 Barnes-Hut spring steps (theta 0.9) with Navi's constants (REPULSION 16000, SPRING_K 0.055, SPRING_L 110, GRAVITY 0.02, DAMPING 0.9).
- Deterministic jitter seeded by page id.
- Orphans are excluded from the forces and laid in the 'Not linked yet (%d)' tray, in notebook order: below the graph upright, right of it sideways, 40 px pitch.
- With more than 200 orphans, the tray collapses to a row: 'Not linked yet: 1834 pages. Show'.
- Positions are cached in graph.ini.
- Incremental placement: a new node goes at its placed neighbours' centroid plus one rest length, then 50 relax steps on its 2-hop neighbourhood with the others fixed (under 10 ms).
- When to compute the full layout:
  - first open with 400 linked nodes or fewer: synchronous, work_pump every 2 steps (about 0.25 s on the Kindle);
  - more than 400 nodes, or 'Tidy up': a bgjob child writes graph.ini atomically while the view shows the O(n+e) seed placement, then swaps with one GL16 when it ends.
- Never on the UI thread unpumped.

AROUND THIS PAGE
- A radial ring layout (Navi's positions_radial): the centre page in the middle, depth 1 on a ring, depth 2 on an outer ring, angle-sorted by parent.
- Only members are drawn, so it is instant and deterministic. Fading the rest on global positions was illegible in the mocks.

SCREEN, UPRIGHT
- Header (190 px, the Pages view's): Back 150x150, the title 'Index map' at 64 px, a segmented 'All pages | Around this page' ('Todas | Alrededor', 2 x 340), and List (opens the Index tab).
- The map area in between.
- Bottom row (170 px): −, Fit and + buttons (220x140), the tray toggle chip 'Unlinked: Show/Hide' ('Sin enlaces: Mostrar/Ocultar'), and 'Tidy up' ('Ordenar').
- Selecting a dot replaces the bottom row with a 320 px card:
  - its name at 64 px;
  - 'Page 12. Links to 3, linked from 2' ('Página 12. Enlaza a 3, enlazada desde 2');
  - Open, Around it, Rename (Rename hosts kbhost over the map).
- Sideways: the same, with the tray on the right.

INTERACTION
- Tap a dot: the nearest within max(r x zoom, 59 px = 5 mm) is selected, with a GL16 of the card and the affected dots' region.
- Tap the selected dot again, or Open: go_to_page (GC16).
- Tap empty space: deselect.
- One-finger or pen drag: pan, with an offset-blit DU preview every 180 ms and a GL16 re-render at release.
- Pinch: zoom from 0.25x to 6x, with a nearest-neighbour scaled DU preview and a GL16 at release. −/+ step x1.5 and x0.67. Fit resets.
- No hover tooltips in v1.
- Back returns to the page (GC16).

PERFORMANCE AND CACHE
- Rendered into the map's own offscreen canvas; compose only blits from it, so settles and toasts never re-render edges. Culled to the viewport.
- The draw pumps every 64 edges.
- Mocks: 100 nodes take about 50-70 ms on the Kindle; 2000 nodes with 4000 edges take about 1-2 s with span lines.
- graph.ini keeps view mode and tray state per notebook.
- Layout floats may differ between the arm64 sim and the armv7 Kindle. Tests assert invariants, not coordinates.

PROBES
editor.map (open), editor.map.nodes, .edges, .orphans, .selected, .mode, .node.<pid> ('tier r x y visible'), .labels.
specs.actions:
ONE REGISTRY
- Action metadata moves out of library.c into a UI-free src/actions.c next to shortcuts.c. Per action:
  - id and file name;
  - label + msgctxt;
  - icon and group;
  - pair (the second action of a two-press row);
  - kind (TOGGLE, MENU, STEP, CYCLE, ONE_SHOT, MOMENTARY);
  - sources mask (KEY | PAD | TOUCH | PEN).
- The Buttons sheet, the Gestures sheet, the probes and the pen plan all read it.
- One dispatcher: editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y). editor_shortcut wraps it, anchored at the last pen point or the screen centre.

NEW NAMES (appended after name-page; ids live in memory only)
- Index:
  - links: MENU, the Links bar.
  - index-map: MENU.
  - go-to-page: MENU, the Find sheet.
  - link-areas: TOGGLE, the eye. No toast, since the result is visible.
- Editing:
  - shapes: TOGGLE, with a toast.
  - shape-last: ONE_SHOT.
  - shape-hold: CYCLE, with a toast.
- Pages: zoom-out / zoom-in (STEP pair) and scroll-up / scroll-down (STEP pair), as the pen plan defines them; scroll continues onto the next or previous page.
- Screen:
  - invert: TOGGLE, REFRESH_FULL.
  - light-down / light-up and warmth-down / warmth-up: STEP pairs. A new non-blocking light_cached(); with the level unknown the step toasts 'Light not ready yet.' and does nothing, never calling the blocking light_get. Toast 'Light 12 of 24'.
  - lock-rotation: TOGGLE. It locks the CURRENT orientation (no GC16 relayout). Toast 'Rotation locked.' / 'Rotation follows the Kindle.'
  - pinch-zoom: TOGGLE, with a toast.
  - theme: TOGGLE, a relayout like app_set_rotation's leave/enter.
  - side-button: CYCLE; the toast is the Settings sentence without '(tap to change)'.
  - mirror-pdf: TOGGLE, with a toast.
  - sleep: ONE_SHOT, editor_save_now plus a public app_request_sleep.
- Totals: 18 new names, 55 actions in all.
- Not bindable to touch or pen: language, calibrate, the shortcuts toggle, the gestures toggle. Hold-eraser is pen and pad only.

FEEDBACK BY KIND (e-ink)
- Toggles with no visible result get exactly one toast, the eraser-mode pattern.
- Toggles with a visible result get none.
- MENU actions close their own menu and swap with the menu in front.
- Gestures follow the same idle-only gate (owner == OWN_NONE, not pinching), plus the close swipes.

GROUPS (shared by the Buttons and Gestures sheets; each at most 11 rows plus Done sideways)
- Index (7): Links on this page; Index map; The Index (list); Go to page; Add a link; Name this page; Show link areas.
- Pages (7): Previous / next page; First / last page; Scroll up / down; Zoom out / in; Fit the page; New page; Pages view.
- Editing (9): Undo; Redo; Eraser; Erase while held (Buttons only); Eraser mode; White ink; Clear the page; Smart shapes; Shape the last stroke.
- Tools (11): unchanged.
- Menus (7): unchanged.
- Screen (9): Invert; Light down / up; Warmth down / up; Lock rotation; Pinch to zoom; Style; Pen button while touching; Mirror PDFs; Sleep.
- Lists: Buttons = 6 groups + Reset + Done = 8 rows. Gestures = master row + 6 groups + Reset + Done = 9 rows.

LIMITS RAISED
- SHORTCUT_MAX from 64 to 160 bindings.
- write_pads' 4 KiB buffer becomes a computed size.
- library.c:1116-1117's text[16] and rows[16] become arrays sized by a GROUP_ROWS_MAX of 12, with a _Static_assert over every group.
- test_shortcuts.c:110's named count and the learn-everything test are updated.

SETTINGS BOTTOM ROW
- KOReader shrinks from 420 to 300 px (its label is 140 px). Controller | Gestures | Updates share the middle: (in.w - 300 - 380 - 4 x 30) / 3, which is 280 px upright Gothic, 282 Classic and 306 sideways. That leaves a label column of 248 px or more, so 'Actualizaciones' (234) fits.
- Gestures uses the gesture glyph F07CB: 'Gestures' / 'Gestos'.
- The entry is not gated by Enable shortcuts.
- The 10 scenario taps on Controller and Updates and the TRANSLATORS note ('about 240 px') are updated, and test_i18n checks the three words fit at 34 px in both styles.

PANEL
- PANEL_BUTTONS goes from 11 to 13: P_SHAPES under the eraser (pen group) and P_LINKS under Next (navigation group).
- Upright everything fits at full size. Sideways with the maximum 4 pins, panel_fit gives space 0.5 and scale 0.94: 94 px buttons, about 8 mm.
- test_panel.c gets the new measures.
- A new runner command 'tap panel <id>' taps by hit id, so scenarios stop hard-coding panel coordinates. The panel scenarios are migrated to it in the same step.
specs.data_and_formats:
NO .qpg CHANGE: no header bump, no tool id >= 10, no ext flag. Snapped shapes are ordinary strokes. Link areas, gestures, the map and tips live in sidecars or in settings.ini.

LINKS.INI (2.0.0-beta.5, unreleased, so free to change)
- Line: link.<pid>=<seed 1-8 hex>,<target>[,<x0>,<y0>,<x1>,<y1>]
  - target: index | p<pid>; 1 to 15 bytes from '!' to '~', now excluding ','.
  - x0, y0, x1, y1: decimal integers 0..65535 in page px at the notebook's page size, with x0 < x1 and y0 < y1, clamped to the page.
  - A line without the four numbers (or with bad ones) is a legacy ink link, migrated lazily (see the Link areas section).
- Overlap rule: smallest area wins, then the higher seed.
- A worst-case line is about 56 B, so 4000 links take about 224 KB. links.ini gets its own cap NAV_LINKS_FILE_MAX = 512 KiB. nav.ini stays at 256 KiB, and the 16 KiB unknown-line carry stays.
- Device build f9d13f5 reading the new file: a long line fails its parser and is carried as unknown, and past 16 KiB its whole links.ini goes read-only (never overwritten). A short line ('p1,1,2,3,4') parses there as an inert unknown target. Acceptable because beta.5 is unreleased; documented in FORMAT.md's moving-between-versions table.
- 1.2.0 to beta.4 never read links.ini.
- Export: render_page_links uses the area, falling back to the ink box. Raw ZIPs keep raw/links.ini.

HISTORY (memory only)
- ACT_LINK joins history.h: {pid, seed, before {exists, target, area}, after {...}}. It owns no strokes.
- history_undo/redo returns the kind, and the editor applies ACT_LINK to nav and saves.
- history_push_replace (count 2: raw out, shape in) is added for shape-last.

GESTURES.INI (new; root, beside shortcuts.ini, controller.ini and the pen plan's file, which it absorbs)
- Grammar is shortcuts.ini's: '#' and ';' comments, trimmed key=value, a later duplicate wins, names case-insensitive.
- Keys:
  - touch.<2|3>.<down|up|left|right|tap|double>=<action|nothing>
  - pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>=<action|nothing|pan|zoom> (drag only takes pan or zoom; Eraser only double and triple).
- Overlay model: built-in defaults are never written. A line overrides one, '=nothing' switches a default off, and Reset deletes the file. So later default changes still reach users.
- Writes are whole and atomic and contain only explicitly set slots. Unknown well-formed lines are carried (2 KiB); refused lines are counted and toasted when the sheet opens.
- Bounded read of 64 KiB, through shortcuts.c's bounded reader factored out.
- Example:
  # Grimoire: gestures (Settings > Gestures). Built in: touch.2.down=pages, touch.2.up=links, touch.2.left=next-page, touch.2.right=previous-page, pen.Button.triple=clear-page, pen.Button.hold=clear-page
  touch.2.tap=undo
  touch.3.tap=redo
  touch.2.left=nothing
  pen.Button.double=links

GRAPH.INI (new; per notebook folder, ignored by older versions)
- Lines:
  # Grimoire: the Index map's layout
  v=1
  links=<8 hex: FNV-1a of the sorted page-pair edge list>
  view=all|around
  unlinked=show|hide
  pos.<pid>=<x>,<y>   (integers -32768..32767, world units)
  pin.<pid>=1         (reserved; dragging nodes is not in v1)
- Unknown lines are carried (nav.ini's rules). The file is 256 KiB at most; 2000 pos lines are about 44 KB.
- A file that does not read is simply recomputed; it is a cache.
- Raw ZIPs include raw/graph.ini.

SETTINGS.INI (undotted 0/1 or numeric keys, append-only, missing = default)
- link_areas=0|1, default 0.
- shapes=0|1, default 1. 2 is reserved for 'lines only'.
- shape_hold_ms=300..1500, default 550.
- gestures=0|1, default 1.
- hints=<bitmask>, default 0. Bits:
  - 0: the gestures tip;
  - 1: the first link;
  - 2: the eye;
  - 3-4: the bar hint count;
  - 5: the first snap;
  - 6: pen-near.
- All five keys join the settings.* probes and FORMAT.md's table.

FIND (NAME SEARCH)
store.c's static fold_next/cmp_name are exposed as i18n_fold_next and i18n_name_match (prefix and substring, accent-folded, case-insensitive) for the Find sheet. There is no new file.

DOCS
- FORMAT.md: links.ini v2, gestures.ini, graph.ini, the settings keys, and the moving-between-versions rows.
- SHORTCUTS.md: the new actions and groups, gestures, 'not only shortcuts_enabled'.
- DESIGN.md: the Links bar, the link card, the Index map, Smart shapes, gestures; also fix DU 120 ms to 188 ms.
- SIM.md: the new runner commands and probes.
specs.eink_and_performance:
REFRESH CHOREOGRAPHY
Measured: DU 188 ms, GL16 271 ms, GC16 341 ms (whole panel) at 24-27 C.
- Links bar:
  - open: compose (about 50-90 ms CPU) plus GL16 of the 1.34 Mpx card;
  - close with no peek: GL16 of the card;
  - chip press: DU invert at once;
  - peek: GL16 of the page area above the card only;
  - stay (finger): one GC16;
  - stay (pen): DU of the card region with the stroke's frames, then the normal settle;
  - Back: GL16, or GC16 after 5 or more peeks;
  - pager: GL16 of the chip grid.
- Link long press: the border in DU, flushed first (app_flush between), then the card in GL16.
- Eye: GL16 of each area's band; rects far apart are flushed separately so the union stays small.
- Link mode: banner GL16. Rubber band: live DU, removed by tile restore plus DU, then the settle.
- Find sheet and every keyboard (kbhost, the Library's proven path, shared):
  - draw only when the field or a key changed, never on unchanged pointer moves;
  - flush the field first, then the key, separately;
  - one GL16 settle 900 ms after typing pauses;
  - never compose the page or a full-screen view per keystroke.
  This is the fix the other lane is landing for the Index keyboard. Every new keyboard host (the bar's rename, the link card's rename, Find, the new page's name, the map's rename) goes through kbhost, so the lag cannot come back.
- Index map: open and close GC16; pan and zoom previews DU at most every 180 ms, then GL16 at release; selection GL16 of the card plus the dots' region.
- Shapes: preview DU, cancel DU, commit via the settle. Never GL16 or a toast while the pen is down (pen_leave's wait).
- Gestures: nothing is drawn during a gesture; the action's own refresh is the feedback. The record card updates its reason line with GL16 of that line only.

FULL PROMOTION
- Replace 'every 30th UI refresh becomes FULL' (app.c:931) with an area budget: the UI-refreshed area adds up, and once it reaches 8 screens, the next refresh that is already FULL resets it. If the budget runs 50% over, the next UI refresh covering at least 50% of the screen is promoted. Refreshes under 25% of the screen (chips, keys, the eye, dialogs) are never promoted.
- So a surprise flash never lands on a bar open or a keystroke.

NEVER BLOCK THE PEN
- No MXCFB_WAIT_FOR_UPDATE_SUBMISSION and no second waiter on a marker, anywhere.
- Long work pumps (work_pump) or is split:
  - peek renders (up to 1.2 s on dense pages) pump every 64 rows and stop prefetching at any input;
  - shape previews pump every 8 points;
  - the map pumps every 64 edges and every 2 layout steps;
  - the big layout runs in a bgjob child;
  - Find matching over at most 2000 names is under 1 ms.
- Lazy link migration runs only on pages the editor already loaded, at the cost of one link_box per legacy link (microseconds).

PRIMITIVES
- canvas_line_aa becomes row-span: bit-identical and 40x faster on long edges (0.02 ms against 0.82 ms per edge on the host). This is a prerequisite for the map.
- New:
  - canvas_dash_rect(r, thick, on, off, halo) for borders and the eye;
  - canvas_disc_pattern(cx, cy, r, level) with a 4x4 Bayer on 2x2-px cells for node tiers;
  - canvas_slash for the off Shapes icon.
- Everything new is 1-bit-safe (solid, hollow, ordered dither, dashes), so DU frames match GL16 settles.

MEMORY
- Peek LRU: 2 x 4.6 MB.
- Shape tile backup: capped at 8 MB.
- Map offscreen canvas: 4.6 MB.
- Area cache: 64 rects.

INPUT SAFETY
- Touch read stalls during renders are timed by kernel timestamps after step 1.
- The device scan's busy flag counts suppressed contacts, so the 330 ms scan never starts mid-gesture.
- A pending double tap or hold resolves only when App.input_drained is set.

LIVE PEN MODE
- The bar's confirming finger tap is swallowed, so its close settles before the next stroke and that stroke keeps MTK pen mode.
- The pen-commit path sends the bar's removal as DU together with the stroke, so pen mode is never broken by a GL16 in flight.
