owner_questions.question: While you hop between links in the Links bar, should the bar keep listing the links of the page you started on, or switch to the links of the page you are looking at?
options: Keep the starting page's links, with a Back button to return (hub and spoke)
Switch to the shown page's links (walk the chain)
owner_questions.recommended: Keep the starting page's links, with Back
owner_questions.why: 'Tap outside to confirm' only means something if the bar is a peek from where you were. Keeping the origin's chips lets you compare several targets, and Back always returns. Walking the chain makes 'where am I' harder on e-ink and loses the way home.

owner_questions.question: With the bar open, what does putting the pen down on the page do?
options: Stay on the shown page, close the bar, and keep the stroke
Stay and close, but swallow the stroke as a tap is swallowed
owner_questions.recommended: Stay, close and keep the stroke
owner_questions.why: Calm means never losing ink. The bar's removal is sent as DU together with the stroke, so pen mode is not broken. A finger tap is still swallowed, so it never follows a link by accident.

owner_questions.question: Renaming a link from its card or the bar: does it rename the target page in the Index (global), or give the link its own label?
options: Rename the target's Index name (an unnamed target becomes an Index entry, which starts a section)
A per-link label stored in links.ini, leaving page names alone
owner_questions.recommended: Rename the target's Index name, with the row worded 'Rename in the Index' or 'Add to the Index...' and a toast naming the result
owner_questions.why: Your brief reads links as Index entries, and one name per place keeps the Index, the bar, the map and the PDF outline in agreement. The wording and toast make the global effect visible, so nothing surprises.

owner_questions.question: Are making, deleting and retargeting a link undoable with the normal Undo button?
options: Yes: each is one Undo step on its page (new in-memory ACT_LINK)
No: Delete asks for confirmation instead
owner_questions.recommended: Yes, one Undo step each
owner_questions.why: Undo is already the panel's safety net. A confirmation dialog on e-ink costs a refresh and a tap every time, while Undo costs nothing until it is needed.

owner_questions.question: Undo after a shape snapped: one step that removes the shape, or two steps (first back to your freehand line, then gone) like iPadOS?
options: One step removes the shape (one pen-down, one moment)
Two steps: freehand first, then gone
owner_questions.recommended: One step
owner_questions.why: It matches your 'one gesture, one moment' undo rule. The preview is the moment to decide (moving on keeps your line), and 'Shape the last stroke' covers people who want snapping only on demand.

owner_questions.question: Default two-finger left and right swipes: turn pages?
options: Yes: left = next page, right = previous (clamped, never creating a page)
Leave them unbound
owner_questions.recommended: Yes
owner_questions.why: The brief says gestures serve navigation by default. A 20 mm straight two-finger swipe is deliberate, and the panel's arrows remain the visible twin. Two-finger taps stay unbound, because a resting hand triggers them too easily.

owner_questions.question: Where the page can scroll (sideways, or zoomed in), how do the navigation swipes work?
options: Mid-screen two-finger drags pan as today; navigation swipes start in a 15 mm band at the screen's edge
Navigation swipes win everywhere and panning moves to one finger
Navigation swipes only when the view is at its scroll limit
owner_questions.recommended: Pan mid-screen, navigate from the edge band
owner_questions.why: It keeps today's scrolling intact. The 'scroll limit' option would make overscroll open Pages by surprise. Upright at the fitted view nothing scrolls, so swipes work anywhere there.

owner_questions.question: Should the panel get both new buttons (Smart shapes under the eraser, Links under Next), making 13?
options: Both (sideways with 4 pins the panel scales to 94%)
Only Smart shapes on the panel; Links by gesture or the page chip
Neither: Smart shapes only in the tool picker
owner_questions.recommended: Both
owner_questions.why: Every gesture needs a visible twin, and you called the links 'the hook'. The cost is small: about 8 mm buttons in the worst sideways case. The panel can still fold.

owner_questions.question: Should pen-button gestures be recorded in the same Settings > Gestures sheet instead of the pen plan's separate Pen button sheet?
options: One action-first Gestures sheet for touch and pen (gestures.ini absorbs pen.ini)
Keep a separate gesture-first Pen button sheet
owner_questions.recommended: One sheet
owner_questions.why: It is one place to learn, and one rule: per action, at most one touch gesture and one pen gesture. Both files are unreleased. The pen plan's held-button cycler stays a Settings row.

owner_questions.question: How should gestures.ini store bindings?
options: Overlay: built-in defaults are never written; lines override them and '=nothing' turns one off
A whole file like controller.ini, which freezes the defaults at the first change
owner_questions.recommended: Overlay
owner_questions.why: Later default improvements still reach you, and Reset is just deleting the file. It matches the pen plan's rule.

owner_questions.question: What should the Index map show when it opens?
options: All pages, the current page ringed, unlinked pages in a 'Not linked yet' tray
Around this page (1-2 hops) by default
Remember the last mode per notebook
owner_questions.recommended: All pages, and remember the switch per notebook in graph.ini
owner_questions.why: The brief asks for all pages as dots, with orphans visibly different. Around this page is one tap away, and remembering the mode means it opens the way you left it.

owner_questions.question: Does the existing 'index' action (in shortcut files since 1.2.0) now open the map?
options: No: 'index' stays the Index list; a new 'index-map' action opens the map
Yes: 'index' opens the map
owner_questions.recommended: Keep 'index' as the list and add 'index-map'
owner_questions.why: Bindings people already learned keep doing what they did. The list and the map are one tap apart (List and Map buttons).

owner_questions.question: Should one-finger horizontal swipes (which your device logs show you already making) turn pages?
options: Not in v1
Offer them as assignable gestures, unbound
Bind them to page turns by default
owner_questions.recommended: Offer them as assignable, unbound
owner_questions.why: One finger is reserved for taps and links, and a palm sliding while writing must never turn a page. Recordable but off respects your habit without risking accidents.

owner_questions.question: Does the 'link areas' eye stay on between sessions?
options: Persist it in settings.ini (off by default)
Reset it to off every time a notebook opens
owner_questions.recommended: Persist it
owner_questions.why: It is a viewing preference like the others, and someone who wants to see areas should not have to keep turning it on.

risks: Pen-near rule: until the spatial, multi-finger relaxation ships and its thresholds are tuned from the device log, 'write, lift, swipe up' will often be refused, because it lands inside the 1 s pen window. The rate-limited 'Move the pen away' toast keeps that from feeling like a hang. Freeze thresholds only after the log gives the slot count, TOUCH_MAJOR values and hover range.

Panel growth: 13 buttons change every hit position below the eraser. The 'tap panel <id>' runner command must land in the same step, or dozens of scenarios break at once. Sideways with 4 pins the panel scales to 94%.

Peek render cost: dense or PDF-backed pages render in up to 1.2 s. The LRU, prefetch and instant chip inversion hide most of it, but a cold peek on a heavy page will still feel slow. Prefetch must abort on any input or it will steal the pen's time.
Ghosting: GL16-only peeks accumulate ghosts. The GC16 on commit and on Back after 5 peeks clears them; the area-weighted FULL rule must not starve the panel of cleanups elsewhere.

Migration on the owner's device: device build f9d13f5 cannot read area lines. Opening a notebook back on that build after the new one has saved makes its links.ini read-only there (carried, never overwritten), or makes short lines inert. Tell the owner not to downgrade.

Tile backup bugs show as stale ink, which is worse than slowness. It must back up before every dab with the brush's max radius + 2 padding, and fall back to a pumped draw_page past 8 MB. editor.live_matches_render must run after every snap and link ring in the tests.

Smart shapes negative corpus is small (47 strokes, mostly one blackletter sample, read-time stamps). Large headings at 2-4x size can still preview a line if held. The shape-log switch and an evening of the owner's writing are needed before the gates are final.

A gesture-opened sheet over the panel: PINCH_BEGIN cancelling a panel press costs a visible restore. It is changed to DU, but a bottom-edge swipe starting on a bottom-parked panel still flickers once.

Rename creates sections: 'Add to the Index...' on an unnamed target makes it a section start, which moves the Index tab's section highlight for the pages after it. The toast names it, but users may still be surprised in the Pages view.

Index map scale: the first layout of 2000 pages and 4000 links is about 3.4 s and runs in a bgjob child. The single-job queue can delay it behind a PDF mirror; the seed placement must look acceptable meanwhile. Float differences between the arm64 sim and the armv7 Kindle forbid coordinate-exact tests.
Record mode vs runtime drift: if the sheet's thresholds ever diverge from runtime, recorded gestures will fail later. Both read the same touchgest constants, enforced by a unit test.
SHORTCUT_MAX, write_pads' buffer and the [16] row arrays must grow in the same step as the new actions. Otherwise learning fails silently ('Could not save') or a group overflows the stack.
Light steps: calling light_get with an unknown level blocks 95-191 ms and overflows the pen buffer. Only the new light_cached may be used on the input path.

Spanish fit: the bottom-row 'Actualizaciones', the bar's four caps labels, the card rows and the record-card reasons all need GRIMOIRE_CHECK_FIT runs upright and sideways in both styles. The '2 dedos izq./der.' abbreviations are already measured as necessary.
Live view streams App.screen, so the bar, the link card, the eye and the map reach viewers as the panel does. If that is unwanted while teaching, they need display_skip_overlay rects.

specs.angle:
FLOW AND SPEED. Every choice below is judged by four questions: does the pen hand stay on the page, how many taps does it take, how many milliseconds on this panel (DU 188 ms, GL16 271 ms, GC16 341 ms, measured), and can it fire by accident. Five rules come out of that.

1. Browse, then commit. Jumping between linked pages is a preview, not a trip:
   - a hotbar tap shows the target page above the card with a GL16 of the page area only (no flash);
   - rendered canvases are cached and prefetched, so a hop is a buffer swap plus one refresh;
   - only tapping the page commits, with one GC16 flash that also clears the peek ghosting;
   - closing the hotbar with its own close goes back to where you started.
   One rule to learn: "outside stays, the hotbar's close goes back."
2. Two hands, two jobs. The pen hand writes and taps UI; the other hand navigates with two fingers.
   - Every link action has a pen-only path: pen taps on the hotbar, the link card and Link to..., plus a proposed pen-button double-click that opens the hotbar.
   - Every link action also has a finger path.
   - Two-finger gestures are accepted right after writing when the fingers are far from the pen. Today a global 1 s pen-near lockout kills "write, lift, swipe".
3. No modal trips. Making, renaming, retargeting and deleting a link never leaves the page for the Pages view. The page stays visible above every sheet, and a link card opens beside the link itself.
4. Nothing new interrupts writing.
   - A smart shape needs a still hold, passes geometry gates that say no to handwriting, and shows a preview that moving on cancels.
   - Gestures need two or three fingers landing together.
   - Overlays (link areas, hotbar, cards) are drawn above the page, never into it.
   - No GL16 or toast ever lands while the pen is down.
5. Latency budgets, honest for e-ink. No animation; feedback is one refresh per decision.
   - gesture lift to hotbar on screen: about 0.35-0.4 s;
   - cached peek: about 0.35-0.45 s;
   - shape preview: about 0.75-0.9 s after the pen stops (Amazon about 1 s, with no way out);
   - keyboard key: under 0.2 s, with the Index keyboard's lag designed out of every new keyboard.
specs.experience:
A day with it in the owner's hands (portrait unless said; px at 300 dpi, 11.81 px/mm).

1. OPENING A NOTEBOOK
- Nothing new is in the way. The panel has one more button under the eraser: Shapes, a filled-shapes glyph when on.
- If links.ini still has beta.5 links (inked lassos), they work at once: until they are migrated, their ink's box is their area.
- They become stored areas when their page is visited, or a few seconds after opening through an idle job, one page per idle tick.
- Their lasso ink stays on the page as plain ink.

2. WRITING WITH SHAPES ON
- Letters never snap.
- Drawing a box around a heading and holding the pen still for 0.55 s shows a clean rectangle in its place: one DU frame, about 0.2 s.
- Lift: it stays as one ordinary stroke with the pen's own look. Keep moving instead: the freehand ink comes back and the stroke simply continues.
- Undo removes the shape.
- The Shapes button turns the feature off (toast "Shapes off."). The tool picker's ink row has "Shapes: Normal", cycling Off / Quick / Normal / Deliberate.

3. MAKING A LINK, PEN HAND ONLY (about 2-3 s, 2 taps plus the lasso)
- Double-click the pen's button (proposed default) or swipe two fingers up: the hotbar appears at the bottom.
- Tap New link with the pen. The card folds into a 140 px strip: "Draw around what links. [Cancel]".
- Circle the words and lift. The circle's ink disappears and a dashed rectangle marks the new area.
- The Link to... sheet docks at the bottom. It docks at the top instead when the area is in the lower part of the screen, so the area stays in view. It holds:
  - a search line;
  - Recent targets, then the Index's entries;
  - New page and The Index buttons.
- Tap "Chapter 3". The sheet folds back into the hotbar, with Chapter 3 as a new numbered entry; toast "Linked to Chapter 3."
- From the add-link shortcut or a gesture it is the lasso plus one tap, then straight back to writing.
- New page: the keyboard asks for a name while the page stays visible above it. Done adds the page at the end, names it (a new Index entry) and links to it. You stay where you are. This is the wiki-style hook: links create Index entries.

4. FOLLOWING
- A finger tap on an area jumps there with one GC16, as today.
- Every jump puts the page you left on a back list. Two fingers to the right (proposed default) or the hotbar's Back chip brings you back.

5. BROWSING WITH THE HOTBAR (the hook)
- Two fingers up anywhere on the fitted page. A card appears at the bottom (GL16, no flash, about 0.35 s):
  - "Links on Chapter 2";
  - the entries numbered in reading order (1 is the link highest on the page), each with its Index name and page number;
  - then "Linking here" for pages that link to this one.
- Tap entry 2: the page above the card becomes that page (GL16 of the page area, about 0.4 s, because it was rendered in the background while you looked). The entry stays selected, and the header says "Showing Chapter 5. Tap the page to stay.", with a "Back to Chapter 2" chip.
- Tap entry 3: that page.
- Tap the page itself, with finger or pen: you are there. The card goes, and one GC16 flash marks the arrival and clears peek ghosts. The tap does nothing else.
- Or ✕, two fingers down, or the hotbar's gesture again: you are back on Chapter 2 exactly as you left it.

6. FIXING A LINK WITHOUT LEAVING THE PAGE
- Hold a finger on a link for 0.6 s. A dashed border shows exactly what is tappable, and a small card opens beside it: "Chapter 5 · p. 31", Go there, Rename, Change where it goes, Delete link.
- Rename opens the keyboard at the bottom, with the page still visible above. Done renames that Index entry everywhere.
- Change where it goes opens Link to... with the current entry marked.
- Delete link removes the area (toast "Link deleted. Undo brings it back."), and Undo does bring it back.
- A tap anywhere else closes the card and does nothing else.
- In the hotbar, holding an entry opens the same card above the card, with that entry's areas dashed on the page.

7. SEEING LINKS
- The hotbar's eye starts dim (off). Turned on, every area on the page gets a dashed outline, plus its number in a black disc matching the hotbar's numbers. The choice is kept.
- Visible borders, if wanted, are drawn with the pen (hold to snap a box). They are plain ink: erasing one never touches the link, and deleting the link never touches the border.

8. FINDING A PAGE
- The hotbar's Go to opens the keyboard on letters, with digits as its top row.
- "cap" lists Index entries with a word starting so (accents folded: "indice" finds "Índice"). "12" lists Page 12 first.
- Tap a result: you go there (GC16), and Back returns.

9. THE MAP
- The hotbar's Index button opens a full-screen graph centred on your page, which has a double ring.
- Every page is a dot:
  - named pages are labelled and sized by how many links they have;
  - solid when well linked, 50% then 25% dither for fewer, a hollow ring for none;
  - unlinked unnamed pages are small hollow dots clustered around their section's named page;
  - pages before any name wait in a "Not linked yet" tray.
- Tap a dot: a card with name, page, links out and in, Open, Rename, Local. Tap it again: you go there.
- Drag pans and pinch zooms, with DU previews and one GL16 when you let go.
- Local cycles off / 1 / 2 steps; Unlinked cycles shown / hidden / only; List switches to the Index list.

10. PAGES
- Two fingers down anywhere on the fitted upright page opens the Pages view; two fingers up inside it closes it.
- Sideways or zoomed in, two-finger drags keep scrolling. Starting in the top or bottom 25 mm opens Pages or the hotbar.
- A one-time toast teaches this the first time a two-finger drag scrolls instead.

11. MAKING IT YOURS
- Settings' bottom row: KOReader | Controller | Gestures | Updates | Done.
- Gestures lists: "Touch gestures: on", Editing..., Tools..., Pages..., Index..., Menus..., Screen..., Reset gestures, Done.
- Example: in Index..., tap "Back to the page before: Two fingers right", then do a three-finger swipe left. The row now says so, and a toast names the action that lost that gesture.
- A rejected try says why ("Put the fingers down together.").
- Every toggle and important setting is a row here and in Controller > Buttons.
specs.gestures:
VOCABULARY (a fixed list; recording means doing one of these, never free-form shapes)
- Two fingers: up, down, left, right (swipes), tap, hold.
- Three fingers: up, down, left, right, tap. Offered only when the panel reports at least 3 MT slots (InputCaps.touch_slots, logged in step 1); the simulator has 10.
- Pen-button gestures from the pen plan, recorded in the same sheet (owner question):
  - Button and Button 2: Click, Double-click, Triple-click, Hold;
  - eraser end: two and three taps on blank paper.
- Reserved, never bindable:
  - a one-finger tap or hold (UI, links, the hotbar);
  - a two-finger spread or squeeze while pinch zoom is on;
  - a two-finger drag where the view scrolls that way and the drag does not start in the edge band.
- File names: touch.two-up, two-down, two-left, two-right, two-tap, two-hold, three-up, three-down, three-left, three-right, three-tap; pen.Button.double and so on.
- UI names (EN / ES): "Two fingers up" / "Dos dedos arriba" ... "Two-finger tap" / "Toque con dos dedos", "Two-finger hold" / "Mantener dos dedos", "Three fingers left" / "Tres dedos izquierda". Two-press rows use the compact "2 up / 2 down" / "2 arriba / 2 abajo", which fits the 1470 px row column at 44 px bold.

DEFAULTS (built in, never written to a file)
- touch.two-down = pages; touch.two-up = links (the hotbar).
- pen.Button.triple = clear-page and pen.Button.hold = clear-page (today's behaviour, from the pen plan).
- Proposed (owner questions): touch.two-right = go-back, touch.two-tap = undo, touch.three-tap = redo, pen.Button.double = links.
- OPPOSITE CLOSES: when the menu in front is bound to a swipe, the opposite swipe closes it. Two up inside the Pages view closes it; two down on the hotbar closes it and goes back to the origin page. The menu's own binding also closes it (the registry's menu rule).

RECOGNIZER: src/touchgest.c
It is pure CORE_SRC, fed by input_evdev.c and sim_sdl.c alike and host-tested like pensync.c.
- Per SYN_REPORT frame it takes:
  - the kernel time;
  - the contacts {tracking id, logical x and y, tool, touch_major};
  - pen context {prox, left_ms, last contact x and y};
  - a view context the active screen pushes: {scrolls_v, scrolls_h, pinch_zoom, gestures_on, record}.
- It returns today's IN_TOUCH_* and IN_PINCH_* events plus IN_GESTURE.
- Thresholds are in mm through dpi.

1. LANDING
- The first contact at t0 gives IN_TOUCH_DOWN, as today.
- A second contact within 150 ms: the first finger is cancelled with today's off-screen up at -10000 (never a tap), IN_PINCH_BEGIN follows, and the session can become a gesture.
- A second contact 150-400 ms after t0: zoom or pan only, never a swipe or tap. Record mode says "Put the fingers down together."
- Later than 400 ms: a palm, suppressed (today's rule).
- A third contact within 250 ms of t0 makes three fingers; a later one suppresses the session.
- The finger count is fixed at the first of: the motion commit, t0 + 250 ms, the first lift.

2. COMMIT (today's dead zone, unchanged)
- It commits when the spread changes by 10% or more (|d/d0 - 1| >= 0.10), or the midpoint travels 6 mm (70 px) or more.
- It is classified once, there:
  a. Two fingers, pinch zoom on, and the spread change is at least 0.6 x the midpoint travel: ZOOM (today's pinch).
  b. More than 30 degrees off an axis: PAN if the view scrolls, else rejected ("Swipe in a straight line").
  c. Vertical, two fingers, scrolls_v, and the midpoint did not start in the matching edge band: PAN, with the zoom held at its commit value. The band is the top 25 mm (295 px) for down and the bottom 25 mm for up. Holding the zoom fixes today's wobble, where a drag zooms slightly.
  d. Horizontal: the same, with scrolls_h and 25 mm left and right bands.
  e. Otherwise: a SWIPE in that direction, and the view does not move. Three fingers skip a-d: a swipe or a rejection.
- scrolls_v = the view is taller than the screen AND two-finger panning is on (pinch zoom on).
  - Upright at the fitted view it is false: two fingers up or down ANYWHERE is a swipe.
  - Sideways (the width fits) and zoomed in it is true: mid-screen drags scroll, and edge starts navigate.
  - With pinch zoom off, nothing pans, so vertical drags are swipes everywhere.

3. END, AT THE FIRST LIFT
- A SWIPE is accepted when all of these hold:
  - the midpoint travelled at least 20 mm (236 px) along the axis;
  - off-axis travel is at most tan 30 degrees of that;
  - every finger moved at least 12 mm, with a cosine of 0.8 or more against the midpoint's direction;
  - the largest finger travel is at most 2 x the smallest;
  - the first lift came within 1000 ms of t0;
  - the spread changed by 25% or less.
  It emits IN_PINCH_END and then IN_GESTURE {value = gesture id, x, y = the midpoint at landing}. Otherwise it is rejected ("Swipe farther", "Too slow: swipe in under a second", "Move the fingers together").
- No commit yet: a TAP candidate. Every finger travelled 5 mm (59 px) or less, the first lift came within 300 ms of the last landing, and every lift within 150 ms of the first. IN_GESTURE fires at the last lift. There are no multi-finger double taps in v1, so nothing ever waits.
- HOLD: no commit, all fingers down, each moved 3 mm or less, 600 ms since the last landing. It is decided in input_poll only after a touch read came back empty, so a queued lift is never misread as a hold.
- After any end or rejection, every contact stays suppressed until all have lifted (today's T.suppressed), so a late finger never leaks a tap or a link follow.

4. PEN NEAR (what makes "write, lift, swipe" instant)
- One finger keeps today's rule: ignored while the pen is near and for 1 s after it leaves.
- Two or three fingers are accepted inside that window when all of these hold:
  - they landed within 150 ms of each other;
  - no contact was ever flagged palm (tool 2) or pen (tool 1);
  - each TOUCH_MAJOR is under the palm threshold, measured in step 1 (provisional: 1.6 x the session's median fingertip major);
  - every contact is at least 50 mm (590 px) from the pen's last contact;
  - the fingers are 8-70 mm apart.
- Otherwise the gesture is rejected ("The pen is near: move it away").

5. GRIP
- A contact within 8 mm of an edge that stays within 3 mm for 300 ms is a grip. It is left out of finger counts and of the late-finger rule.
- So a thumb resting at the edge no longer turns every later finger into a "palm" and kills touch.

6. INPUT FIXES FOLDED IN (input_evdev.c)
- When the pen arrives or the palm window starts, a finger is ended with cancel_touch (off-screen), never a real lift. A resting finger can no longer fire a link or a button.
- SYN_DROPPED: resync with EVIOCGMTSLOTS, as input_set_grab does, then suppress until all fingers lift.
- Touch is stamped with the SYN_REPORT's kernel time.
- The device-scan busy flag counts any contact that is down.
- The pinch pair is chosen by landing order, not lowest slot.
- Tool 1 (pen) is never counted as a finger.

EVENT CONTRACT
- IN_PINCH_BEGIN at the second landing (as today), so S->pinching blocks single-finger owners.
- IN_PINCH_MOVE.value: 0 WAIT (dead zone), 1 ZOOM, 2 PAN (zoom locked), 3 SWIPE (view untouched). The editor obeys the value instead of deciding itself.
- IN_PINCH_END, then IN_GESTURE in the same batch. PINCH_END clears S->pinching, so editor_shortcut's idle gate (editor.c:1980) accepts the action.
- IN_GESTURE.value = gesture id (> 0). Only in record mode, value = -reason for a rejection.
- IN_GESTURE is added to:
  - main.c's event_name table (static assert);
  - power_asleep_drops (dropped while asleep);
  - the BOOK_RUNNING guard (app.c:462);
  - note_input (app.c:464).
- When PINCH_BEGIN cancels a panel press the first finger made, the button is restored with a DU frame, not GL16. A hotbar pull that starts on a panel parked at the bottom then costs no flash.

DISPATCH
- Editor: editor_gesture(a, id, x, y)
  - looks the gesture up in gestmap;
  - applies the opposite-close rule;
  - calls editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y), the pen plan's anchored entry; zoom anchors at the midpoint.
- With any keyboard open, gestures do nothing: typing is never thrown away.
- Library: only the Gestures sheet's record mode listens. Other screens ignore gestures in v1.
- Gestures work with Enable shortcuts off. The master switch is settings.ini gestures (default 1), the Gestures list's first row.
- One-time hint: the first time a two-finger vertical drag scrolls a view while two-up or two-down is bound, a toast says "To open Pages or links here, start at the top or bottom edge." / "Para abrir Páginas o enlaces aquí, empieza en el borde de arriba o de abajo." (settings.ini edge_hint = 1 afterwards).

SETTINGS > GESTURES (the Buttons sheet, parametrized by a BindKind descriptor, not copied)
- Entry: the Settings bottom row becomes KOReader (300 px, was 420) | Controller | Gestures | Updates | Done (380 px).
  - The three middle buttons are 280 px upright in Gothic, 282 in Classic, 306 sideways, with label columns of 248 px or more. Spanish "Actualizaciones" (234 px) fits.
  - Gestures uses icon F07CB.
  - Centres at about 580, 890 and 1200 at y 1930 upright; 863, 1199 and 1536 at y 1695 sideways.
- List (9 rows, fits sideways under 12): "Touch gestures: on (tap to change)", Editing..., Tools..., Pages..., Index..., Menus..., Screen..., Reset gestures, Done.
- Group sheets: rows from the shared registry.
  - "Undo: Two-finger tap" or "Undo: none".
  - With pen gestures: "Undo: Two-finger tap, Double-click".
  - Two-press rows learn two gestures in turn.
- LEARNING
  - Tap a row: it inverts, and the hint line reads "Do the gesture for Undo: two or three fingers, or the pen's button."
  - touchgest enters record mode: no zoom or pan, every classification reported, and every rejection reported with its reason, using the same thresholds as runtime, so whatever records will also fire.
  - A recognized gesture binds at once: gestures.ini is written atomically, and the map changes only after the write succeeds.
  - If another action had the gesture, a toast says "That gesture is no longer for Pages."
  - A reserved gesture says why ("That one zooms the page.").
  - A one-finger tap stays UI: the same row stops learning, another row switches.
  - A 10 s timeout leaves the row as it was.
  - Holding a row 0.6 s forgets it: "No gestures for Undo now."
  - Reset gestures deletes gestures.ini, bringing back the built-in defaults.
- Rule per source: a gesture does one action; an action has at most one touch gesture and one pen gesture.
- Rejection toasts (EN / ES):
  - "The pen is near: move it away." / "El lápiz está cerca: apártalo."
  - "Put the fingers down together." / "Apoya los dedos a la vez."
  - "Swipe in a straight line." / "Desliza en línea recta."
  - "Swipe farther." / "Desliza más lejos."
  - "Too slow: swipe in under a second." / "Muy lento: desliza en menos de un segundo."
  - "Only one finger was seen." / "Solo se vio un dedo."
  - "That one zooms the page." / "Ese gesto amplía la página."

SIMULATOR AND RUNNER (both feed touchgest, so the Kindle and the Mac behave alike)
- Window:
  - Shift + right-drag = two fingers 25 mm apart, moving together;
  - Alt + right-drag = three fingers;
  - Ctrl + right-click = a two-finger tap;
  - the wheel stays the pinch.
- Runner commands, frames 13 ms apart on a virtual clock:
  - "finger ID down|move|up X Y [MAJOR] [TOOL]";
  - "swipe N X Y DX DY STEPS [SEP] [LANDGAP]";
  - "tapn N X Y [SEP] [MS]".
  "pinch" and "tap" keep working unchanged.
- Probes: touch.gesture, touch.reject, touch.class, touch.contacts, gestures.ACTION, library.gestures_group.
specs.hotbar:
WHAT IT IS
- A bottom sheet over the open page. It lists the Index entries this page links to, for browse-then-commit navigation.
- In the registry it is a MENU (action "links"):
  - its own gesture, button or key opens and closes it;
  - another menu's binding swaps it for that menu;
  - Close menu closes it.
- It joins sheet_open, front_menu, menu_action, close_front and open_menu (editor.c:1374-1376, 1906-1965).
- Code lives in src/hotbar.c, hosted by the editor like dispmenu. hotbar_pointer returns HB_* results (PEEK, COMMIT, CANCEL, BACK, NEW_LINK, SEARCH, EYE, GRAPH, CARD) that the editor acts on, the PagesView pattern.

CONTENT
- "On this page": one entry per distinct target among the page's live links (stored areas, plus beta.5 links whose ink is still there). Entries follow the reading order of each target's first area: areas whose vertical centres are within 10 mm count as one line, read left to right. The entry number (1, 2, 3...) is the number the eye shows on the page.
  - A named target shows its Index name in bold.
  - An unnamed target shows "Page 31" in regular weight.
  - The Index shows "The Index" with the list icon.
  - A deleted page shows "Missing page", 50% dithered.
  - The right column shows "p. 31" at 34 px, with a second line "×2" when two links on this page go there.
- "Linking here" (recommended, owner question): pages whose links go to this one, one entry per source page in notebook order, with a ↩ icon instead of a number. Hidden when there are none. It is built by one pass over at most 4000 links with a pid-to-index table, under 1 ms.
- Empty: "No links on this page yet." / "Esta página aún no tiene enlaces.", with New link drawn as the primary button.
- More than 6 entries: paged, 6 per screen, with ‹ 1/3 › in the header.

LAYOUT (300 dpi; ui_frame in the theme's shape; App.toast_floor = the card's top, set after compose resets it)
- PORTRAIT: the card is at x 20, 1820 wide, and ends 20 px above the screen's bottom. From the top:
  - 24 px padding;
  - a 40 px grip strip (a 160 x 8 px bar);
  - a 96 px header:
    - the Back chip, only when there is somewhere to go back to, at most 560 px wide;
    - the title "Links on Chapter 2" / "Enlaces en Capítulo 2", 44 px bold, truncated with font_draw_left_name;
    - paging ‹ and ›, 118 x 96 each;
    - ✕, 118 x 96;
  - R rows (R = 1..3) of 124 px chips with 16 px gaps, in 2 columns of 876 px;
  - 16 px, a 3 px rule, 16 px;
  - a 132 px tool row;
  - 24 px padding.
  - Height = 335 + 140 R: 475, 615 or 755 px. At 755 (30% of 2480), 1705 px of the page stay visible above.
- CHIP: a 64 px badge disc (a white 34 px bold digit on black) at the left, the name from x + 104, and a 150 px right column. Nothing wraps.
- LANDSCAPE: the card is 2440 wide, with 3 columns of 784 px, R at most 2, height at most 615 px (33% of 1860).
- TOOL ROW, left to right. Each button is an icon over a 34 px caps word, as Settings' bottom buttons; 431 px wide upright, 586 sideways.
  - Go to: magnify F0349, "Go to" / "Ir a".
  - New link: link-plus F0339, "New link" / "Nuevo enlace".
  - Areas: eye F0208 on an inverted button when on; eye-off F0209 in a 50% dither (dim) when off; "Areas" / "Zonas".
  - Index: F05E3, "Index" / "Índice", at the right.

INTERACTIONS (finger and pen alike on the card). The one rule: outside stays, the hotbar's own close goes back.
- TAP AN ENTRY. The chip inverts at once (DU press feedback), then PEEK:
  - the page above the card becomes the target: the canvas cache, then a GL16 of the page area only;
  - the entry stays selected;
  - the header reads "Showing Chapter 5. Tap the page to stay." / "Mostrando Capítulo 5. Toca la página para quedarte.";
  - the panel's page chip shows the peeked page's number.
  The list keeps showing the ORIGIN's links, so you hop between targets. A peek never sets notebook.ini's last page, never writes a thumbnail and never edits the peeked page. A peek shows the target at its default view; the origin's zoom and offset are kept for going back.
- TAP THE SELECTED ENTRY AGAIN: commit, the same as tapping the page.
- AN ENTRY FOR THE INDEX opens the Index list (commit, then FULL). A missing page gives the toast "That link's page is not in this notebook."
- TAP THE PAGE OUTSIDE THE CARD commits.
  - A finger commits on lift, so a second finger landing turns it into a gesture instead.
  - The pen commits on pen down, and its stroke is swallowed until pen up.
  - The card closes. After any peek, one GC16 full refresh (the arrival signal; it also clears ghosting). Without a peek, a GL16 of the card rect only.
  - The tap does nothing else: no link follow, no ink.
  - The origin goes on the back list. Committing a peek reached through Back pops the list instead, as a browser's Back does.
- THE PANEL stays live. Its buttons commit first, then act: Next page while peeking goes to the peeked page + 1.
- BACK CHIP
  - While peeking, it shows the origin again (a canvas swap and GL16); the card stays.
  - When not peeking, it peeks the top of the back list ("Back to Chapter 1").
- CANCEL closes and goes back to the origin page: GC16 if anything was peeked, else GL16 of the card. Any of these cancels:
  - ✕;
  - a one-finger drag down of 15 mm (177 px) or more that starts on the grip or header;
  - two fingers down;
  - the links gesture or key again;
  - Close menu;
  - the Back key.
- HOLD AN ENTRY 0.6 s (30 px slop): the link card opens above the hotbar, aligned with that chip's column.
  - That entry's areas on the origin page get the selected dashed border; while peeking, the origin is shown first.
  - The choices are the same as on the page: Go there, Rename, Change where it goes, Delete link.
  - For a ×N entry they read "Delete 2 links" and "Change where they go", and act on all N.
- BOTTOM ICONS
  - Go to: commits a peek if there is one, then opens the search sheet. The keyboard sits over the bottom of the page, with up to 4 result rows above it; it opens on letters, with the number row as digits.
    - Letters filter Index names. The compare folds accents and case and matches the start of any word: starts of a name first, then starts of a word, then other matches, then notebook order.
    - A typed number puts "Page N" first.
    - A result tap goes there at once (GC16); Done goes to the first result. The page you left goes on the back list.
  - New link: commits a peek if there is one, then link mode on this page. The card folds into the 140 px strip; after the link is made, the hotbar comes back with the new entry.
  - Areas: toggles the eye (settings.ini link_areas, action link-areas), with a GL16 of the areas' rects and the button only.
  - Index: commits a peek if there is one, then opens the graph view (FULL).
- OTHER ACTIONS WHILE OPEN follow the registry:
  - menu actions swap or close it;
  - every other action is refused while a sheet is open (editor.c:2010), so a two-finger tap cannot undo something hidden behind the card.
- OPENING: the links action (two fingers up by default, a pen double-click proposed, any key or pad).
  - On a read-only page it opens for browsing; New link is greyed and explains with a toast.
  - With links.ini unreadable it reads "Links could not be read." and New link is greyed.

INSTANT JUMPS
- CANVAS CACHE: an LRU of up to 3 rendered page canvases beside page_canvas, 4.6 MB each at 1860x2480 (5.3 MB at 1986x2648).
  - The key is page id + the page's edit generation + the paper/picture generation + the page size.
  - A peek is a swap of buffer pointers, never a copy.
  - The origin's canvas is kept, so going back is a swap.
- PREFETCH, in editor_tick only when input drained and no owner holds the pointer:
  - the first 3 entries' targets, then the top of the back list;
  - rendered into spare canvases one 160-row band per tick, at most about 80 ms on a dense page;
  - stopped the moment a pen or finger lands.
  Pages not yet in memory load through page_at, pumped.
- UNCACHED PEEK (tapped before prefetch got there): the render is pumped with work_pump every 64 rows and presented once. That is typically 0.1-0.3 s, up to 1.2 s on the densest pages.
- ON ALLOCATION FAILURE the cache shrinks to nothing and peeks render uncached: slower but correct.

PROBES
- editor.hotbar
- editor.hotbar.entries
- editor.hotbar.N (e.g. "p3 x2", "index", "back p7")
- editor.hotbar.peek
- editor.hotbar.rect
- editor.back ("depth top")
- editor.canvas_cache ("hits misses entries")
- editor.search.results, editor.search.N
specs.link_areas:
WHAT A LINK IS NOW
- A link is an invisible rectangle on its page, in page px at the notebook's page size, with a target: a page or the Index. No ink is part of it.
- A visible border is optional ink the user draws (smart shapes make a clean one). It is never part of the link: erasing the border never touches the link, and deleting the link never touches the border.

MAKING ONE (pen)
1. START from any of these:
   - the hotbar's New link;
   - the add-link action (key, pad, gesture);
   - the Index tab's Add a link (until step 23 it keeps its current route);
   - the pen plan's pen gestures.
   It is refused WITH a toast, not silently as the shortcut is today:
   - on a read-only page, with the existing read-only message;
   - when links.ini cannot be written: "Links could not be saved here." / "Aquí no se pueden guardar enlaces."
2. LINK MODE: a 140 px strip docks at the bottom: "Draw around what links." / "Rodea lo que enlaza." plus Cancel (300 x 100). The next ink stroke is the lasso. The eraser end erases as usual and does not count.
3. THE LASSO is live DU ink in the pen's own brush, so the rubber band needs no new drawing path. With shapes on, holding still snaps it to a rectangle or an ellipse (link-aware: only those two, gates x 1.3); lifting keeps the snapped box.
4. ON LIFT
   - Under 5 mm both ways (LINK_BOX_MIN_MM): taken back, toast "Too small for a link: draw around what links.", and link mode stays on.
   - Otherwise the stroke is never page_add'ed:
     - its pixels come back from smart shapes' under-ink tile backup (about 1 ms), or from draw_page(bbox), pumped, when shapes are off;
     - area = the stroke's point bbox (or the snapped shape's bbox), clamped to the page;
     - a dashed outline of the area is drawn: one GL16 of the bbox.
5. THE LINK TO... SHEET takes the hotbar card's place.
   - It docks at the TOP instead when the area's centre is in the bottom 45% of the screen, so the area stays visible.
   - Header: "Link to..." / "Enlazar con..." and ✕.
   - A search line: "Search the Index, or a page number" / "Busca en el índice, o un número de página". A tap opens the keyboard; it filters live, as Go to does.
   - 2 x 3 chips, paged:
     - first Recent: the targets of this session's last links and the last pages visited, this page left out, at most 4;
     - then the Index in notebook order.
   - Bottom row:
     - New page (+);
     - The Index (list icon);
     - "Keep the outline as ink" / "Dejar el contorno como tinta" (owner question; recommended: offered, off by default, remembered as settings.ini link_keep_ink).
   - Height: 838 px portrait, 698 landscape (3 x 2 chips).
6. TAP AN ENTRY
   - nav_link_set and nav_save_links run. On failure, nav_load rolls back, with the toast "Could not save the link."
   - One ACT_LINK undo step is pushed. It also owns the kept outline stroke, which gets a fresh seed.
   - The dashed outline goes, unless the eye is on.
   - Toast: "Linked to Chapter 3." / "Enlazado con Capítulo 3."
   - Started from the hotbar, you return to the hotbar with the new entry; otherwise to the page.
   - NEW PAGE:
     - the keyboard opens, titled "Name the new page" / "Nombre de la página nueva", with the page visible above;
     - Done adds a page at the end (store_add_page), names it with nav_set_name (an empty name leaves it unnamed), links to it, and stays on the origin page;
     - toast: "Linked to the new page 41."
7. CANCEL (Cancel, ✕, Close menu, or add-link again): no link is made and nothing on the page changes ("No link made.").

FOLLOWING AND HIT-TEST
- A finger tap follows the link (go_to_page, GC16, as today) and pushes the origin onto the back list.
- The pen never follows from the page, because it writes. The pen follows through the hotbar.
- Hit box = the stored area grown to at least 7 mm a side around its centre (NAV_LINK_MIN_MM, as today).
- Where hit boxes overlap, the SMALLEST wins, so nested links behave. A tie goes to the earlier line in links.ini. This replaces "the latest stroke wins", which needed ink order.
- The open page's areas are cached: at most 64 rects, with seeds and entry numbers.
  - The cache is rebuilt on a page change, on link edits and on migration.
  - Ink edits invalidate it only while the page still has beta.5 links on the ink fallback.
  - Nothing is recomputed on each tap.

SHOWING (the eye; settings.ini link_areas, off by default and kept)
- compose() draws the overlay after the page blit and before the panel, for every area on screen:
  - the HIT BOX (what the eye promises is what a finger hits), outlined 6 px outside;
  - 3 px black dashes, 18 px on and 12 off, with a 2 px white halo on each side, readable over ink and gray paper;
  - all 1-bit, so DU and GL16 match;
  - the entry's number in a 52 px black disc with a white 34 px bold digit, straddling the top-left corner, moved inside at a screen edge.
- page_canvas, thumbnails, the PDF and the share page never get the overlay.
- Shown even with the eye off:
  - the new area while it is being made (the same style);
  - a held link's area, in the SELECTED style: 5 px dashes, 24 on and 12 off, plus 16 px solid corner squares.

THE LINK CARD (second ruling: the dotted border and the dialog, with the page in view)
- A finger held still on an area for 0.6 s (LINK_HOLD_MS, 30 px slop):
  - the selected dashed border at once, by DU, presented with its own app_flush;
  - then the card beside it, by GL16.
- The card is 760 px wide, 700 px tall:
  - a 104 px title row: "Chapter 5" in 44 px bold, "p. 31" at 34 px;
  - 4 buttons of 124 px with 12 px gaps:
    - Go there / Ir allí;
    - Rename / Renombrar: "Name page 31" / "Nombrar la página 31" for an unnamed page, greyed for the Index;
    - Change where it goes / Cambiar a dónde lleva;
    - Delete link / Borrar enlace.
- PLACEMENT: 24 px to the right of the area if it fits within the screen's 20 px margin; else left; else below; else above. It is clamped to the screen, never covers the area when any placement avoids it, and avoids the panel when it can.
- Go there follows the link.
- RENAME
  - The keyboard opens over the bottom of the page, through the shared keyboard host, starting with the current name.
  - Done calls nav_set_name(target pid) and nav_save; on failure the old name is restored.
  - Naming an unnamed page shows the toast "Page 31 is now in the Index." / "La página 31 ya está en el índice.", so the new section start is no surprise.
- CHANGE WHERE IT GOES opens Link to... with the current target marked; a tap retargets the link (one ACT_LINK step).
- DELETE LINK: nav_link_remove, then a save and one ACT_LINK step. Toast: "Link deleted. Undo brings it back." / "Enlace borrado. Deshacer lo recupera."
- A TAP ANYWHERE OUTSIDE closes the card on lift and is swallowed (the paper sheet's precedent).
- The Pages view's picking mode (PG_TO_INDEX, PG_UNLINK, pagesview_pick) is retired once this ships.

INKED VS INVISIBLE
- New links are invisible areas. Ink near a link is only ever decoration the user drew, or the kept outline: a separate stroke with a fresh seed.
- COPY PAGE now copies the page's links to the copy: same seeds, areas and targets, under the new page id. Areas are not visible ink, so they would otherwise vanish from the copy silently.
- PDF: render_page_links uses nav_link_areas, which returns stored areas, so area links export as /Link annotations with no change. Links to the Index stay dropped, as today.

MIGRATING BETA.5 LINKS (the owner's device)
- A line without an area (link.<pid>=<seed>,<target>) is a LEGACY link.
- Until it is migrated it behaves exactly as today: its area is the point bbox of that page's ink strokes with its seed (link_box, erase strokes ignored). Every reader therefore works without a rewrite: the editor, the PDF export, the hotbar and the graph.
- ON PAGE LOAD (page_at): each legacy link on that page gets area = link_box's raw bbox (NOT the 7 mm grown box) and is marked dirty. links.ini is written at the next save_page or when leaving the page.
- The lasso ink is untouched and is plain ink from then on: a stored area always beats seed matching.
- IDLE MIGRATION: after a notebook opens with legacy lines, editor_tick handles one such page per idle tick (input drained, no owner):
  - pages already in memory are used as they are;
  - other pages are read with store_read_page, pumped;
  - then links.ini is saved once.
  A notebook is migrated a few seconds after opening. If interrupted, it resumes next time.
- A lasso hidden by the precise eraser or white ink still has its stroke, so it migrates to a working area (the eye shows it) instead of silently dying at compaction. Today's quirk is gone.
- A legacy link with no ink at all stays dormant, as today, and is pruned only with its page.
- Device builds of beta.5 (f9d13f5) read a new line's target as "p3,412,980,...":
  - over 15 bytes, the line is carried as unknown;
  - shorter, it is an unknown target that does nothing.
  This is harmless: beta.5 is unreleased and the device gets the new build.
specs.smart_shapes:
TRIGGER
- Draw, then hold the tip still: every sample within 1.0 screen mm of the hold anchor for shape_hold_ms.
- shape_hold_ms defaults to 550. The tool picker offers Quick 400, Normal 550 and Deliberate 900.
- draw_sample keeps an anchor (a point and a wall time) in O(1), resetting it whenever the pen moves more than 1.0 mm from it.
- editor_tick checks the anchor at most every 30 ms while owner == OWN_DRAW, including while the pen is down.
- The hold is wall time measured in the tick, never sample spacing: a still pen may send no samples at all.

RECOGNIZER: src/shape.c
It is pure and geometry only (no speed features, because headless batches share one timestamp), about 0.12 ms on the Kindle. It resamples to diag/40, then applies gates and fits. All sizes are in SCREEN mm: page px = mm x dpi / 25.4 / zoom.
- LINE
  - chord/path >= 0.97;
  - max offset <= max(4% of the length, 1 mm) + 0.5 mm;
  - length >= 12 mm;
  - snaps to 0, 45, 90 or 135 degrees within ±4 degrees.
- CLOSED SHAPES
  - the gap is at most 22% of the diagonal;
  - the winding around the centroid is 1.7-2.6 pi;
  - the total absolute turning is at most 1.6 x the winding + 0.6 pi, so scribbles fail;
  - at least 10 mm across and 4 mm thick.
- RECTANGLE / SQUARE / QUAD
  - ShortStraw finds 4 segments, each with chord/path >= 0.93;
  - a rectangle when every corner is 90 ± 15 degrees; axis-aligned within ±5 degrees; a square when the sides are within 10%;
  - otherwise a straight-edged quad, which covers diamonds;
  - vertices sit at the intersections of the least-squares edge lines.
- TRIANGLE: 3 segments; equilateral or right-angle snaps within 6-8 degrees.
- ELLIPSE / CIRCLE
  - a PCA frame plus a least-squares fit of x²/A + y²/B = 1;
  - RMS radial error at most 6% of the minor axis, maximum at most 20%;
  - a circle when the axis ratio is 0.88 or more; axis-aligned within ±6 degrees.
- v1.5 (step 18): a single-stroke ARROW (a line, then one or two barbs 15-60 degrees off its end), an open POLYLINE (L shapes, zigzags with 90-degree snaps), an ARC.
- v2: a short V held near a snapped line's end becomes that line's arrowhead.
- WRITING-BURST GATE: a stroke started within 600 ms and 8 mm of the last lift needs a 1.5 x hold and tolerances x 0.7.
- PAPER-AWARE
  - On Dot grid and Graph paper (5 mm pitch), line ends and rectangle corners snap to the grid within 1 mm (settings.ini shape_grid, default 1).
  - On ruled papers a near-horizontal line snaps exactly horizontal.
- LINK-AWARE: in link mode only rectangles and ellipses are tried, with gates x 1.3, and the link's area is the snapped bbox.

PREVIEW, COMMIT AND CANCEL (one rule each)
- At the hold, recognition runs once. A refusal shows nothing, and nothing re-runs until the pen moves again.
- ACCEPT
  - The snapped stroke keeps the raw stroke's tool, ToolParams snapshot, ext bytes, tip variant and SEED.
  - Its points:
    - polygons: the vertices plus a point every 2 mm;
    - ellipses: N = clamp(ceil(2 pi / acos(1 - 0.25 px / r)), 24, 720) vertices, starting nearest the user's first point and going the user's way;
    - pressure: the median of the middle 80% by arc length; tilt: the median; t_ms interpolated by arc length.
  - It is drawn over the page as it was before the stroke (the under-ink tile backup) through stroke_brush_begin and brush_add, with work_pump every 8 points.
  - One DU frame of union(raw, shape) shows it.
  - No toast and no GL16 while the pen is down (pen mode tolerates only DU).
- LIFT KEEPS IT
  - The shape is page_add'ed in place of the raw stroke with ONE history_push_add. One gesture is one moment: Undo removes the shape (owner question).
  - union(raw, shape) joins S->settle for the usual GL16 settle.
  - Nothing is redrawn at commit.
- MOVING MORE THAN 1.5 mm from the anchor (hysteresis over the 1.0 mm hold radius) CANCELS: the with-raw tile snapshot is copied back (about 1 ms), then one DU frame. The brush state was never touched, so the stroke simply continues.
- Holding longer does nothing more. The pen leaving proximity counts as a lift.
- UNDER-INK TILE BACKUP: while shapes are on, draw_sample copies each 64 x 64 tile of page_canvas the first time the live stroke's segment rect, padded by brush max radius + 2, touches it, and always before brush_add.
  - Capped at 8 MB; a 300 mm outline needs about 300 tiles.
  - Past the cap, preview and cancel fall back to draw_page(union), pumped.
  - Live still equals re-render (editor.live_matches_render after each snap).

WHO SNAPS
- All nine ink pens, the highlighter included (straight highlights), and the side button's highlighter.
- Never white ink, the precise eraser, the whole-stroke eraser, or a read-only page.

TOOLBAR, SETTINGS, ACTIONS
- PANEL: P_SHAPES, a 12th button directly under the eraser. PANEL_BUTTONS becomes 12 (test_panel.c); in landscape with 4 pins that costs about 1% of the panel's scale.
  - On: the filled-shapes glyph (F0831) on a plain button. Off: the outline glyph (F0832) with a 4 px diagonal slash.
  - It is never inverted, so the inverted button keeps meaning "the tool in use".
  - A tap toggles it, with toasts "Shapes on. Hold the pen still at the end of a line or shape." / "Formas activadas. Mantén el lápiz quieto al final de una línea o forma." and "Shapes off." / "Formas desactivadas."
- TOOL PICKER: a third labelled control in the ink row, "Shapes: Normal" / "Formas: normal". It cycles Off / Quick / Normal / Deliberate, writing shapes 0/1 and shape_hold_ms 400/550/900. The panel icon is explained here, where there is room for words.
- One teaching toast after the first snap ever: "Shape made. Undo takes it away." / "Forma hecha. Deshacer la quita." (settings.ini shape_taught = 1 afterwards).
- ACTIONS
  - shapes: a toggle;
  - shape-last: snaps the newest ink stroke afterwards, with no hold. It runs only when the top undo action is that stroke's ADD. It makes one ACT_REPLACE step, which Undo turns back into the freehand stroke. When the gates refuse: "No shape in the last stroke." / "El último trazo no es una forma." It is bindable to a pen-button double-click, a key, a pad button or a gesture, which gives writers who turn the hold off a zero-accident way in.
- DEVICE TUNING: an empty grimoire/shape-log file logs each hold's features and decision: sizes in mm, winding, residuals, kind or reason, ms taken. It never logs coordinates.

WHY IT IS CALMER THAN AMAZON'S
1. A preview, never an instant commit. Moving on cancels with nothing lost: the pause in Chinese characters or blackletter costs nothing.
2. A recognizer that can say no: size, closure, winding, scribble budget, fit residuals. Replaying the owner's 47 real strokes, a hold-only trigger like Amazon's would fire on 21 of them at 550 ms; with these gates none snaps at written size, and only straight strokes snap to lines when the writing is 2-4 x bigger.
3. The writing-burst gate.
4. Ink pens only, never erasers or white ink.
5. A toolbar toggle and an adjustable hold, the two things Amazon's users asked for.
6. One Undo removes a shape. shape-last offers snapping with no hold at all.
specs.graph_view:
HOSTING
- src/graphview.c is a full-screen editor view like the Pages view, but with its own offscreen canvas (screen size, 4.6 MB, freed on close). compose() only blits it, never re-renders edges.
- It joins front_menu, menu_action, close_front, open_menu and sheet_open as SHORTCUT_GRAPH (file name "graph").
- Ways in:
  - the hotbar's Index button;
  - the graph action;
  - a new Graph button (150 px square) in the Pages view's Index tab header, which shrinks "Name this page" to 570 px.
- Its List switch goes to the Index tab.
- Open and close are GC16, since the whole screen changes.

DATA (no page loads)
- Nodes: every page (pid, index, name, and its section head via nav_section_of).
- Edges: links.ini links between pages, deduped per unordered pair, with direction bits and multiplicity.
- Links to the Index: a small lozenge badge on the source dot with a count, not edges. An Index hub turns the global graph into a hairball.
- Degree = distinct neighbours.
- A pid-to-index table is built once, instead of page_index per edge: at most 4000 edges, under 1 ms.

LOOK (1-bit-safe marks, so DU previews and GL16 settles look the same, and inversion keeps them distinct)
- SIZE: Navi's log formula, r = 10 + 22 x ln(2 + deg) / ln(2 + maxdeg) px at fit zoom. Unnamed pages are x 0.75.
- FILL BY DEGREE, progressively lighter as the owner asked:
  - 0: a hollow 3 px ring (the orphan look);
  - 1: a 25% Bayer fill on 2 x 2 px cells inside a ring;
  - 2-3: a 50% fill;
  - 4 or more: solid.
  New canvas_disc_pattern provides the fills.
- THE OPEN PAGE: a double ring with a 6 px gap.
- SELECTED: an 8 px ring and 5 px edges. Outgoing edges are solid and incoming dashed, so direction reads without arrowheads. Its label is an inverted chip.
- EDGES: 2.5 px anti-aliased lines, +1 px per extra link up to 5 px. They are drawn under white knockout discs (r + 4) so dots stay crisp, with the row-span canvas_line_aa from step 19.
- LABELS: named pages, 34 px, at most 320 px (truncated as names), on a white knockout box.
  - Placed greedily by priority: the selected page, the open page, its neighbours, then named pages by degree.
  - Each label tries 4 candidate positions with an occupancy test against placed labels and dots.
  - "p. 31" labels for unnamed pages appear only when zoomed in or in Local.
- UNLINKED UNNAMED PAGES (most pages in most notebooks): small hollow dots, pulled near their section's named page by a weak invisible spring, so a section reads as a small galaxy (Navi's parent containment).
- THE TRAY: pages before the first named page with no links wait in "Not linked yet (N)" / "Aún sin enlaces (N)", below the graph in portrait and to its right in landscape.

LAYOUT: src/graphlayout.c (pure, host-tested)
- SEED: Navi's place_disk: BFS shells from the top-degree hub, rings sorted by parent angle, islands outside. Jitter is deterministic, seeded by page id (not index), so inserting a page moves nothing else.
- RELAX
  - about 300 Barnes-Hut steps (theta 0.9) with Navi's constants: REPULSION 16000, SPRING_K 0.055, SPRING_L 110, GRAVITY 0.02, DAMPING 0.9;
  - section springs at 0.3 x SPRING_K and 0.6 x SPRING_L;
  - tray nodes stay out of the forces.
- COST AND WHERE IT RUNS
  - About 0.25 s on the Kindle for a few hundred pages; about 3.4 s for 2000 pages and 4000 links.
  - Up to about 300 nodes: in-process, pumped, before the first frame.
  - Larger, or Tidy up: the O(n+e) seed layout shows at once, a bgjob child relaxes it and writes graph.ini atomically, and one GL16 swaps the picture when the child ends.
- STABLE
  - Positions persist in graph.ini.
  - A new page is placed at its placed neighbours' centroid plus one rest length (or beside its section head), then 30 relax steps run over its 2-hop neighbourhood with everything else fixed: under 10 ms.
  - Nothing moves between visits unless the user asks for Tidy up.
- Tests assert invariants (no overlaps, the tray's membership, the open page in view), never exact coordinates: floats differ between arm64 and armv7.

VIEWPORT AND CONTROLS
- It opens "following you" (Navi's way), centred on the open page:
  - at the zoom that fits everything, if that keeps dots at least 10 px;
  - else at the zoom that fits the page's 2-step neighbourhood.
- The Local and Unlinked choices are remembered per notebook in graph.ini.
- HEADER (190 px, as the Pages view):
  - Back;
  - the title "Index", with Graph | List chips;
  - Local: cycles "Local: off / 1 step / 2 steps" / "Local: no / 1 paso / 2 pasos" around the selected or open page. It uses a radial ring layout: instant, deterministic, members only. Fading the rest on global positions proved illegible on e-ink.
  - Unlinked: cycles "shown / hidden / only" / "se ven / ocultas / solo";
  - Fit / Encajar;
  - Tidy up / Ordenar (in the overflow, only after positions exist).

INTERACTION
- TAP A DOT (the nearest within max(r, 5 mm = 59 px); HitList's 128 cap does not apply, the view hit-tests its own nodes): it is selected, and a bottom card appears: "Chapter 5 · p. 31 · 3 links out, 2 in" / "3 enlaces salen, 2 entran", with Open, Rename and Local. GL16 covers the card and the dot's neighbourhood.
- TAP THE SELECTED DOT AGAIN, OR OPEN: go there (GC16). The graph closes and the origin goes on the back list.
- TAP EMPTY SPACE: deselect.
- ONE FINGER OR THE PEN DRAGS: pan. The offscreen picture is shown shifted as a DU preview, at most every 180 ms. At release it is re-rendered (culled to the viewport, pumped) and settled with one GL16.
- PINCH: a nearest-neighbour scaled preview, then a re-render and GL16.
- DOUBLE TAP (350 ms gap): zoom 2 x at that point.
- HOLD A DOT 0.6 s, or the card's Rename: the keyboard host renames that Index entry. An unnamed page gains one, with the same toast as the link card.
- DRAW COST: about 50-70 ms on the Kindle for 100 nodes; about 1-2 s for 2000 nodes and 4000 edges at fit, pumped, with one GL16 at the end. Nothing is drawn progressively.
- PROBES: editor.graph, editor.graph.nodes, .edges, .orphans, .tray, .selected, .node.<pid> ("x y tier radius visible").
specs.actions:
ONE REGISTRY
- src/actions.c is UI-free (N_() markers only). Per action it holds:
  - id and file name;
  - label and msgctxt;
  - icon and group;
  - pair (the second action of a two-press row);
  - kind;
  - sources mask: KEY | PAD | TOUCH | PEN.
- library.c's LearnRow, k_groups and action_label move there. shortcuts.c keeps the parsing.
- The Buttons sheet, the Gestures sheet, the probes and SHORTCUTS.md's table all read it.
- editor_shortcut stays the one dispatcher, as editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y), with editor_shortcut as a wrapper.

KINDS
- TOGGLE: self-inverse; a toast only when the result is not visible.
- MENU: opens; its own binding closes it; another menu's binding swaps it.
- STEP pairs: two-press rows.
- CYCLE: a toast names the new state.
- ONE_SHOT.
- MOMENTARY: hold-eraser only, KEY | PAD, because it needs a release.

NEW ACTIONS: 22, taking the registry from 37 to 59. File name: kind, label EN / ES.
Index group:
- links: MENU, "Links on this page" / "Enlaces de esta página" (the hotbar).
- graph: MENU, "Index graph" / "Mapa del índice".
- go-to-page: MENU, "Go to page" / "Ir a una página" (the search sheet).
- go-back: ONE_SHOT, "Back to the page before" / "Volver a la página anterior". It pops the back list; when empty, the toast "Nothing to go back to." / "No hay a dónde volver."
- link-areas: TOGGLE, "Show link areas" / "Mostrar zonas de enlace".
Editing group:
- shapes: TOGGLE, "Smart shapes" / "Formas inteligentes".
- shape-last: ONE_SHOT, "Shape the last stroke" / "Dar forma al último trazo".
Pages group (the pen plan's names, reconciled with what exists: its panel, zoom-reset, next-pen and previous-pen already exist as fold-panel, fit-page, next-tool and previous-tool, and are NOT added):
- zoom-out / zoom-in: STEP, 1.25 x per press around the anchor (the pen or the midpoint); fit-page resets.
- scroll-up / scroll-down: STEP, 75% of the screen. Past the edge it continues onto the previous or next page with the zoom kept (the owner's pen ruling).
Screen group:
- invert: TOGGLE, full refresh through the DM_INVERTED path.
- light-down / light-up and warmth-down / warmth-up: STEP, toast "Light 12 of 24" / "Luz 12 de 24". They use a new non-blocking light_cached(); while the level is unknown they toast and skip the step, and never call light_get (95-191 ms) on the input path.
- follow-rotation: TOGGLE, "Turn with the Kindle". Off LOCKS THE CURRENT orientation, a new meaning: no snap back to portrait and no surprise relayout. A toast confirms.
- pinch-zoom: TOGGLE, with a toast.
- theme: TOGGLE between Classic and Gothic. ui_set_theme, then a leave/enter relayout as app_set_rotation does.
- side-button: CYCLE 0..3. The toast is Settings' sentence without "(tap to change)".
- mirror-pdf: TOGGLE, with a toast.
- sleep: ONE_SHOT. editor_save_now, then a public app_request_sleep.
- gestures: TOGGLE, sources KEY | PAD only, since a gesture cannot turn gestures back on.
Unchanged:
- Existing names keep their meaning; "index" stays the Index list (owner question).
- add-link and name-page move from the Pages group to the Index group.
- Language, calibration and the shortcuts toggle are not actions.

GROUPS (each at most 11 rows sideways; the [16] row arrays at library.c:1116-1117 get a _Static_assert and a bound)
- Editing (9): undo, redo, eraser, hold-eraser, eraser-mode, white, clear-page, shapes, shape-last.
- Tools (11): unchanged.
- Pages (7): previous / next page, first / last page, zoom out / in, scroll up / down, new-page, fit-page, pages.
- Index (8): links, graph, index, go-to-page, go-back, add-link, name-page, link-areas.
- Menus (7): tool-picker, paper, display, pen-feel, fold-panel, library, close-menu.
- Screen (10): invert, light down / up, warmth down / up, follow-rotation, pinch-zoom, theme, side-button, mirror-pdf, sleep, gestures (the gestures row only in Buttons).
- The Buttons list has 6 groups + Reset + Done = 8 rows; the Gestures list adds its master row for 9.

FEEDBACK BY KIND
- Toasts for results you cannot see: pinch-zoom, follow-rotation, mirror-pdf, side-button, shapes, eraser-mode, light and warmth.
- No toast where the result is visible: white, invert, theme, link-areas, the menus.
- link-areas repaints only its areas' rects, with GL16.
- shapes repaints its panel button with GL16 and toasts.

LIMITS RAISED
- SHORTCUT_MAX 64 -> 160, since the same map now holds TOUCH and PEN bindings.
- write_pads' 4 KiB buffer becomes a computed size.
- test_shortcuts.c's 10 + 8 + 19 count and its learn-everything test are updated.

BINDINGS
- ShortcutBinding.gamepad becomes uint8 source {KEY, PAD, TOUCH, PEN}. lookup, learn, forget and pads_for take the source; app.c passes it.
- Per source: a binding does one action. PAD, TOUCH and PEN give an action at most one binding each (the Buttons rule, generalized). Keys keep shortcuts.ini's many-to-one.
- Built-in duplicates stay legal: the D-pad starters, and the pen's triple-click and hold both clearing the page.

CONTEXT GATES (unchanged meaning)
- Actions act only in the idle editor.
- Menu actions work through open menus.
- Nothing acts through a keyboard.
- The hotbar, link card, Link to..., search and graph count as sheets, so a two-finger tap cannot undo behind them.
specs.data_and_formats:
NOTHING IN .qpg CHANGES
- No header bump, no tool id of 10 or more, no ext flags.
- Smart shapes are ordinary strokes; link areas live in links.ini; overlays are UI only.

links.ini (beta.5 and unreleased, so it is free to change)
  # Grimoire: links on pages
  link.<pid>=<seed: 1-8 hex>,<target>,<x0>,<y0>,<x1>,<y1>
- target is "index" or "p<pid>": 1-15 bytes from '!' to '~', now excluding ','.
- The area is decimal page px at the notebook's page size (store_notebook_page_size), half-open, with x0 < x1 <= page_w and y0 < y1 <= page_h.
  - Read values are clamped to the page.
  - An empty or inverted area makes the line unreadable, and it is carried as an unknown line.
- A line without the four numbers is a beta.5 LEGACY link: it falls back to its ink and is migrated, as in link_areas.
- Fields after the area are reserved: up to 32 bytes are kept verbatim and written back.
- Example: link.17=0a3f91c2,p23,412,980,1210,1104
- Size: the worst line is about 57 B, so 4000 links take about 228 KB.
  - links.ini's read cap rises from 256 to 512 KiB (a separate NAV_LINKS_FILE_MAX) for margin; nav.ini keeps 256 KiB.
  - NAV_LINKS_MAX 4000 and NAV_LINKS_PER_PAGE 64 stay.
- The writer always writes the area for links that have one. Legacy links keep their short form until migrated.
- Seeds remain the link's id. nav_new_seed keeps steering new ink away from link seeds, so a stray stroke can never extend a legacy link's ink box.

graph.ini (new, in the notebook folder; older versions never touch it)
  # Grimoire: the Index graph's layout
  graph=1
  local=0|1|2
  unlinked=show|hide|only
  links=<FNV-1a 32-bit hex of the sorted link set>   (stale: incremental placement)
  pos.<pid>=<x>,<y>   (integer world units, 1 = 1 px at zoom 1, origin at the centre)
  pin.<pid>=1         (reserved for v2 dragging)
- Unknown lines are carried (up to 16 KiB).
- Reads are bounded at 256 KiB; 2000 pos lines take about 44 KB.
- It is written atomically after a layout changes, never on every open.
- Raw ZIP exports carry it with nav.ini and links.ini.

gestures.ini (new, in the root beside controller.ini; it absorbs the pen plan's unreleased pen.ini)
  # Grimoire: gestures (Settings > Gestures). Built in unless a line says otherwise:
  # touch.two-down=pages, touch.two-up=links, pen.Button.triple=clear-page, pen.Button.hold=clear-page
  touch.two-right=go-back
  touch.two-tap=undo
  touch.two-down=nothing
  pen.Button.double=links
- Grammar: shortcuts.ini's: # and ; comments, trimmed key=value, a later duplicate wins, case-insensitive names.
- OVERLAY MODEL: defaults are built in, lines override them, and "=nothing" switches one off. Defaults added later therefore still reach the owner, unlike controller.ini's whole-file freeze.
  - Only slots that were set are written.
  - When no slot is left, the file is removed. Reset deletes it.
- Well-formed lines this version cannot use (a newer gesture or action) are kept, up to 2 KiB, and written back.
- Malformed lines are refused and counted; a toast reports them when the sheet opens.
- The file is read in app_init, by the Controller sheet's Reload, and each time the Gestures sheet opens, so edits made over USB show.

settings.ini (undotted numeric keys, since test_probe.c:29-39 refuses dotted ones; a missing key means its default, and 1.0.0-beta drops them on save so the default returns)
- shapes 1: 0 off, 1 hold to snap; 2 and 3 are reserved for "lines only" and an every-stroke diagram mode.
- shape_hold_ms 550: 300..1500; the picker offers 400 / 550 / 900.
- shape_grid 1.
- shape_taught 0.
- link_areas 0.
- link_keep_ink 0.
- gestures 1.
- edge_hint 0.
All are added to FORMAT.md's table and to the settings.* probes (app.c:1022-1037).

IN MEMORY ONLY
- History kinds (history.h:5):
  - ACT_LINK {seed, before {has, target, area}, after {...}, an optional owned outline stroke};
  - ACT_REPLACE {raw, shape, index} for shape-last.
  - undo_redo reads the kind; ACT_LINK sets nav and saves links.ini, and on a failed save shows a toast and leaves the history unchanged.
  - Undo stays per page, like all undo.
- The back list: up to 32 page ids per open notebook.
  - Pushed by link follows, hotbar commits, search results, graph opens, and the Pages view's tile and Index row opens.
  - Not pushed by next or previous page. Cleared when the notebook closes.
- The canvas cache (3), the area cache (64), Recent targets (4), and the under-ink tile backup.

DOCS
- FORMAT.md: links.ini v2, graph.ini, gestures.ini, the settings keys, and the Moving-between-versions rows:
  - area links are inert before beta.5 and in the device's beta.5 builds;
  - every older version ignores gestures.ini and graph.ini;
  - .qpg is unchanged.
- SHORTCUTS.md: the registry table, the sources, the gestures.
- DESIGN.md: the hotbar, Link to..., the link card, the graph, the refresh choreography. Its DU figure becomes the measured 188 ms, not about 120 ms.
- SIM.md: the new runner commands and probes.
- TESTING.md.
specs.eink_and_performance:
BUDGETS
Measured on the owner's panel at 24-27 °C: DU 188 ms, GL16 271 ms, GC16 341 ms. Framebuffer copy costs 20-40 ns/px. Kindle CPU is taken as about 20 x the host.
For each interaction, the CPU work, then the refresh, then the time felt:
- Two-finger swipe to hotbar
  - CPU: recognition under 20 µs per frame; composing the 1820 x 755 card takes about 30-50 ms, and copying its 1.37 Mpx 27-55 ms.
  - Refresh: GL16 of the card, 271 ms.
  - Felt: about 0.35-0.4 s after the lift.
- Entry press: an immediate DU inversion of the chip (app_press_feedback).
- Peek from the cache
  - CPU: the canvas swap costs nothing; composing the page area about 15 ms (a bilinear blit sideways, about 60-120 ms); copying 3.2 Mpx 63-127 ms.
  - Refresh: GL16 of the page area only, 271 ms.
  - Felt: about 0.35-0.45 s.
  - Uncached, add a pumped render: typically 0.1-0.3 s, up to 1.2 s.
- Commit after peeks: GC16 full (copy 45-100 ms plus 341 ms). It clears ghosting and resets the flash counter. A commit with no peek is a GL16 of the card rect.
- Cancel after peeks: swap back, then GC16 full. A cancel with no peek is a GL16 of the card.
- Eye toggle: GL16 of the areas' rects.
  - One union when the areas overlap or cover more than 40% of the screen.
  - Otherwise one flush per cluster, the way library.c presents the field and then the key.
- Link card
  - The selected dashed border goes out first by DU, presented with its own app_flush.
  - Then the card by GL16 (760 x 700, copy about 15 ms).
  - The two are never one big union.
- Link lasso lift: the restore from the tile backup takes about 1 ms, then a GL16 of the bbox.
- Smart shape
  - CPU: recognition 0.12 ms; dabs 0.1-0.5 ms per mm of outline (a 40 mm circle 12-60 ms, a 300 mm frame up to 150 ms, pumped every 8 points).
  - Refresh: DU, 188 ms.
  - Felt: visible about 0.75-0.9 s after the pen stops.
  - A cancel costs about 1 ms plus a DU.
- Graph open
  - CPU: offscreen render 50-70 ms for 100 nodes, up to 1-2 s for 2000 nodes and 4000 edges, pumped.
  - Refresh: GC16.
  - Pan and zoom show DU previews at most every 180 ms; release brings a re-render and one GL16.
- Search keystroke: filtering up to 2000 names with accent folding takes under 2 ms. The key and the field each get a small DU; the results list settles with GL16 at the 900 ms pause.

THE INDEX KEYBOARD LAG STAYS FIXED
Every keyboard in this design (hotbar search, Link to... search, Rename, New page, graph rename) goes through one keyboard host. That is the other lane's helper if it lands first; otherwise it is factored from library.c:1860-1879. The host:
- draws only when the key or the field changed, never on a move that changed nothing (pagesview.c:344-345 redraws on every move today);
- presents the field with its own app_flush, then the key, as two small DU refreshes, never one union;
- settles with one GL16, 900 ms after typing pauses;
- redraws only the changed key and the field, not the whole 1.78 Mpx modal;
- is never drawn from a full-screen compose. The hotbar is a compose layer that draws only the rect asked for; it never copies the Pages view's redraw-everything pattern (editor.c:672-675).
A keyboard.draws probe lets scenarios assert at most 1 field draw and 1 key draw per keystroke, and none per move.

REFRESH RULES
- Never GL16 or GC16 while a stroke is live: pen mode tolerates DU only. Every toast in this design waits for the lift.
- Taps and pen touches outside the hotbar or a card are swallowed. The close refresh (at most 341 ms) has then usually ended before the next stroke starts; a stroke that starts during it falls back to plain DU for that stroke only.
- FULL promotion becomes area-weighted:
  - sum the GL16 area, and promote after 8 screens' worth instead of every 30th UI refresh (app.c:931);
  - any natural FULL (a commit, a page turn) resets the sum.
  Using the hotbar and the keyboard then stops causing surprise flashes.
- Overlays and sheets are composed into App.screen above the page canvas. page_canvas, thumbnails and PDFs stay clean.
- Live view mirrors App.screen, so its viewers see the hotbar and cards, as they see the panel.
- No animation: gestures show nothing while the fingers move, and a swipe fires once, on lift.
- Dashed outlines, dither tiers, the dim eye and the Shapes slash are 1-bit patterns (2 x 2 px Bayer cells), so DU frames and GL16 settles look the same and survive invert.

NEVER BLOCK THE PEN (its evdev buffer overflows after about 100 ms)
- Anything that may pass about 50 ms is pumped (work_pump every 64 rows or every 8 shape points) or split across idle ticks. That covers:
  - peek renders;
  - prefetch: one 160-row band per idle tick, only when input drained and no owner holds the pointer;
  - legacy migration: one page per idle tick;
  - graph drawing;
  - graph layout: pumped, or a bgjob child for large notebooks;
  - shape dabs.
- Touch timing uses kernel SYN times, so a backlog read after a render neither bunches a swipe nor fakes a hold. Holds resolve only when the touch read came back empty.
- No MXCFB_WAIT_FOR_UPDATE_SUBMISSION and no second wait on a marker. The only wait stays pen_leave before a non-DU refresh.
- light_get is never called on the input path; light_cached replaces it there.

MEMORY
- Canvas cache: at most 3 x 4.6 MB (5.3 MB at 1986 x 2648). It is the first thing dropped when an allocation fails.
- Graph offscreen canvas: 4.6 MB, only while the graph is open.
- Tile backup: at most 8 MB, only during a stroke.
- Graph layout arrays: about 2000 x 32 B.
