owner_questions.question: What does the hotbar list?
options: Only the links drawn on this page
This page's links, then a 'Linking here' section of pages that link to it
Two tabs: On this page | Linking here
owner_questions.recommended: This page's links, then a 'Linking here' section of pages that link to it
owner_questions.why: Following a link and then coming back is the most common hop. Listing backlinks under the outgoing links turns 'where was I referenced?' into one tap, with no extra tab to press. It costs under 1 ms (one pass over at most 4000 links), and the section is hidden when there are none.

owner_questions.question: When several links on one page go to the same entry, how does the hotbar show them?
options: One entry marked ×N; Delete there removes all N, while a long press on the page removes one
One entry per link
owner_questions.recommended: One entry marked ×N; Delete there removes all N, while a long press on the page removes one
owner_questions.why: Your brief calls the rows 'index entries': a destination listed once reads as an index. Removing one specific link stays exact through the page's long-press card.

owner_questions.question: What is a link's name?
options: Its target page's Index name. Rename renames that page everywhere, and naming an unnamed page adds it to the Index, starting a section there
Each link gets its own label in links.ini, separate from the page's name
owner_questions.recommended: Its target page's Index name. Rename renames that page everywhere, and naming an unnamed page adds it to the Index, starting a section there
owner_questions.why: Names then live in one place, like wiki links, and the Index stays the hook: renaming from a link fixes the name everywhere. When a rename creates a section start, a toast says so.

owner_questions.question: When making a link, can the lasso stay on the page as a visible border?
options: Never (the ruling as written)
A 'Keep the outline as ink' chip in Link to..., off by default and remembered
The same chip, on by default
owner_questions.recommended: A 'Keep the outline as ink' chip in Link to..., off by default and remembered
owner_questions.why: A kept outline is a separate stroke with its own seed, so it stays decoration and is never part of the link, as the ruling requires. It saves drawing the same circle twice when you want a visible border.

owner_questions.question: After a smart shape snaps, what does Undo do?
options: One step removes the shape
Two steps: the first brings back the freehand stroke, the second removes it (as on iPad)
owner_questions.recommended: One step removes the shape
owner_questions.why: It follows your 'one gesture, one moment' undo rule. The preview is the safety net: moving the pen instead of lifting cancels the snap with nothing lost. shape-last still offers a separate undoable step for snapping afterwards.

owner_questions.question: Where do the two-finger navigation swipes start?
options: Anywhere when the page cannot scroll that way (upright at the fitted view); from the top or bottom 25 mm when it can (sideways, or zoomed in)
Always from the 25 mm edge bands
Always anywhere, giving up two-finger scrolling
owner_questions.recommended: Anywhere when the page cannot scroll that way (upright at the fitted view); from the top or bottom 25 mm when it can (sideways, or zoomed in)
owner_questions.why: Upright, you get your exact gesture with no aiming. Sideways or zoomed, vertical scrolling keeps working, and the rule never depends on where the page happens to be scrolled. A one-time toast teaches the edge start.

owner_questions.question: When does a swipe act?
options: When the fingers lift
As soon as the fingers have travelled 20 mm
owner_questions.recommended: When the fingers lift
owner_questions.why: Reversing the drag cancels it. A flick lifts within about 100-200 ms, and the e-ink refresh that follows (about 270 ms) dominates the delay anyway.

owner_questions.question: Which extra touch gestures should come built in?
options: Only two fingers down (Pages) and two fingers up (hotbar)
Also two fingers right = Back to the page before
Also two-finger tap = Undo and three-finger tap = Redo
owner_questions.recommended: Also two-finger tap = Undo and three-finger tap = Redo
owner_questions.why: Back is what makes link-hopping feel safe. Undo with the other hand keeps the pen hand writing; it is a common convention in note-taking apps and is gated by strict tap rules. The three-finger tap is offered only if the panel reports three contacts (step 1 finds out). Note: this option includes the two-finger-right Back as well.

owner_questions.question: Should a double-click of the pen's button open the hotbar by default?
options: Yes
No: leave it unbound
owner_questions.recommended: Yes
owner_questions.why: It gives a path with the pen hand only. The triple-click and hold that clear the page keep working; with both counts bound, only the double-click waits 350 ms (your multi-tap gap).

owner_questions.question: Should one Gestures sheet record both touch and pen-button gestures?
options: One Gestures sheet for both (it replaces the pen plan's separate Pen button sheet; the touch-while-held cycler stays a Settings row)
Keep the Pen button sheet separate
owner_questions.recommended: One Gestures sheet for both (it replaces the pen plan's separate Pen button sheet; the touch-while-held cycler stays a Settings row)
owner_questions.why: One action-first place, as your brief describes: pick an action, then do any gesture for it. It also means one file (gestures.ini) and one rule per source.

owner_questions.question: While peeking from the hotbar, what does the pen do on the page?
options: Touching the page outside the card commits to the page shown and is swallowed, like a finger tap
It commits and draws
owner_questions.recommended: Touching the page outside the card commits to the page shown and is swallowed, like a finger tap
owner_questions.why: It is the same 'tap outside to confirm' for both hands. It also gives the close refresh (at most 341 ms) time to finish, so the next stroke keeps the fast pen mode.

owner_questions.question: How does the graph open?
options: The whole notebook, centred on your page
A local view, 2 steps around your page
Whatever you used last, starting with the whole notebook
owner_questions.recommended: Whatever you used last, starting with the whole notebook
owner_questions.why: Your brief asks for all pages as dots. Remembering Local for those who prefer it makes it one choice, not a tap on every visit.

owner_questions.question: How does the graph show pages that are neither named nor linked?
options: Small hollow dots around their section's named page; those before any name go in a 'Not linked yet' tray
Hidden until Unlinked is set to shown
All of them in the tray
owner_questions.recommended: Small hollow dots around their section's named page; those before any name go in a 'Not linked yet' tray
owner_questions.why: They are visibly different, hollow and small, as you asked, but still placed where they belong, so the map doubles as a table of contents.

owner_questions.question: What does the existing 'index' action do once the graph exists?
options: It stays the Index list, with a new 'graph' action for the map
It opens the graph
owner_questions.recommended: It stays the Index list, with a new 'graph' action for the map
owner_questions.why: Files that already bind 'index' keep their meaning in every version, and the Index list and the graph view each switch to the other in one tap.

owner_questions.question: Where does the Shapes toggle go on the panel?
options: A 12th panel button under the eraser
At the panel's bottom, under Library, so no existing button moves
Only in the tool picker
owner_questions.recommended: A 12th panel button under the eraser
owner_questions.why: It sits with the pen-behaviour buttons, where your eye looks for it. In landscape with 4 pins it costs about 1% of the panel's scale. Scenario taps below the eraser have to be re-measured, which is test work, not something you feel.

owner_questions.question: How long must the pen be held still for a shape to snap (default)?
options: 400 ms (Quick)
550 ms (Normal)
900 ms (Deliberate)
owner_questions.recommended: 550 ms (Normal)
owner_questions.why: It is quicker than Amazon's 1 s. The geometry gates, not the hold time, are what stop accidents, and the picker offers the other two.

owner_questions.question: Should shapes snap to the grid on Dot grid and Graph paper?
options: On by default
Off by default
Not offered
owner_questions.recommended: On by default
owner_questions.why: On a 5 mm grid, a box or line that lands exactly on the dots is what you would draw with a ruler, and the snap only reaches 1 mm.

owner_questions.question: Does the link-areas eye stay on between sessions?
options: Yes, saved in settings.ini
No, it turns off each time a notebook opens
owner_questions.recommended: Yes, saved in settings.ini
owner_questions.why: Someone who wants to see the areas wants it every time, and it is one tap to switch either way.

owner_questions.question: Where does 'New page' in Link to... add the page?
options: At the end of the notebook
After the last page of the current section
owner_questions.recommended: At the end of the notebook
owner_questions.why: It is predictable and never reshuffles the page numbers other links show. The page is named at creation, so the Index finds it wherever it sits.

risks:
False gestures from the writing hand. Relaxing the pen-near lockout for two- and three-finger landings could let a palm or knuckles fire Pages, the hotbar or Undo.
- Mitigation: measure first (step 1).
- Require fingertip-sized contacts that land together 50 mm or more from the pen.
- Keep the 1 s rule for single fingers.
- Report every rejection, and keep a constant that falls back to today's rule.
The panel's MT slot count and touch_major ranges are unknown. Three-finger gestures, and the proposed three-finger Redo, may be impossible on the Scribe; the vocabulary must hide them.
Sideways or zoomed in, two fingers down mid-screen scrolls instead of opening Pages. The edge-band rule plus a one-time hint may still feel inconsistent with the upright 'anywhere'.

How two-finger drags feel will change: pan now holds the zoom fixed, swipes no longer move the view, and touch timing switches to kernel time. k_pinch_gate guards the dead zone but not the feel, so the owner must test on the device.

Peek state leaks. Any path that could edit while peeking (pen down, panel actions, shortcuts, a sleep, an autosave) must commit first or be blocked. Missing one means writing on the wrong page, or saving the wrong last page.

Peek ghosting and memory:
- GL16 peeks accumulate ghosting until the GC16 at commit or cancel.
- The canvas cache takes up to about 16 MB.
- When an allocation fails the cache must shrink to nothing, making peeks slow but correct.

Migrating the owner's real beta.5 links is a one-way rewrite of links.ini. Using the 7 mm grown box or counting erase strokes would silently change tappable areas, so fixtures should be copies of the device's actual notebooks.
links.ini with areas nears the old 256 KiB cap at 4000 links, so the cap rises to 512 KiB. A device beta.5 build reading a bigger file hides every link.

Renaming from a link renames the page everywhere and can create a section start, which changes the Index's section highlight for the pages after it. The toast mitigates this, but the owner may prefer per-link labels.

A graph of 2000 pages takes about 3.4 s to lay out on the Kindle, so it needs a bgjob child. bgjob runs one job at a time, so a PDF mirror can delay Tidy up. canvas_line_aa must be fixed first, or 4000 edges take about a minute to draw.
Changing the FULL promotion to area-weighted changes when the screen gets its cleaning flash. Too lax lets ghosting build up over long sessions.

Parametrizing the Buttons sheet for Gestures risks regressions in the Controller flow, and moving the Settings bottom buttons breaks 10 scenario taps plus y_all_screens.qs:631. A missed tap would press Gestures instead of Controller.

The pen plan is unimplemented, and its references are stale: 6 of its 10 new action names now exist under other names. Merging pen.ini into gestures.ini and using the shared registry require that lane to adopt this design.
The keyboard-lag lane may land a helper with a different API. The hotbar, link card and search keyboards must adapt to it; the keyboard.draws budget test catches a regression whichever helper wins.

Area links are invisible to other readers: older Grimoire versions, the share page, and Live view's page-only modes. Only the PDF carries them. Moving between versions, a user may think links were lost.
Live view viewers see the hotbar, the link card and the graph, because Live view mirrors the screen as it does the panel. This may surprise someone streaming their notes.

specs.angle:
ROBUSTNESS AND E-INK ENGINEERING. The design aims for five things:
- No action without clear intent. Palms, a writing hand resting on the screen, a hovering pen, half-finished gestures and pauses in handwriting all do nothing.
- Honest latency on two slow cores and e-ink. Every interaction has a stated refresh mode and cost. GC16 flashes only on a deliberate screen change, never more than once for it. No animation.
- Formats that cannot hurt old data. .qpg is untouched. links.ini only gains an additive line type. Each new sidecar is either an overlay on built-in defaults or a pure cache.
- Graceful failure. An unreadable file goes read-only and says so. A memory or render failure falls back to a slower path, never to wrong pixels.
- Full headless testability. One pure touch recognizer is fed by both the Kindle and the simulator, and every new surface has probes and scenarios.

Five decisions carry this angle:
1. One pure recognizer, src/touchgest.c, replaces touch_frame. Gestures come from a fixed vocabulary, fire when the fingers lift, and must pass strict time and geometry gates. Anything ambiguous is rejected; in record mode the sheet says why. Single-finger taps keep today's latency and rules.
2. A link is an invisible rectangle. links.ini gains `area.<pid>=<seed>,<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>` lines beside the unchanged `link.` lines. beta.5 ink links migrate lazily, page by page, taking their ink box as the area; their ink stays as ordinary ink. Link edits join undo (ACT_LINK), so Delete needs no confirmation.
3. The hotbar is a 1-bit card refreshed with GL16. Each peek (a tentative jump) is a GL16 refresh, with the origin page cached, and the one GC16 comes at the commit. Peeks never write notebook.ini, so a crash, sleep or power-off during a peek reopens on the origin page.
4. Smart shapes never commit on a pause. A hold shows a preview; moving on cancels it; lifting keeps it; the first Undo returns the hand-drawn stroke. Geometric gates, not the hold, are what stop accidents.
5. The Index map is built from nav.ini and links.ini only, with no page reads. Its layout is cached in graph.ini, a cache any version may delete. Long layouts run in a bgjob child. Rendering is offscreen and pumped, and every mark is 1-bit safe.
specs.experience:
The owner's view, upright unless stated (1860x2480, 11.8 px per mm).

1. WRITING. Nothing changes under the pen. The panel gains one button, Shapes (a circle, triangle and square outline), directly under the eraser. It shows as selected because shapes are on by default.

2. DRAWING A BOX (smart shapes). The owner draws a rough rectangle and holds the nib still at the end. After 0.55 s, one DU frame replaces the wobbly outline with a clean rectangle in the same pen, size and angle: the preview.
- Lifting keeps it. The usual GL16 settle cleans the grays 150 ms after the pen leaves.
- Writing on instead puts the freehand ink back at the first movement, and the stroke continues as drawn.
- Pausing mid-letter in blackletter or kanji does nothing: those strokes fail the shape gates, so no preview appears.
- The first Undo brings back the hand-drawn rectangle; a second Undo removes it.
- Tapping the panel's Shapes button turns shapes off (toast 'Shapes off.').

3. OPENING THIS PAGE'S LINKS (the hotbar). Two fingers swipe up anywhere on an upright page. On lift, a card rises from the bottom in one GL16 refresh (about 0.35 s). It holds:
- a grip bar and the title 'Links on this page · 3';
- numbered chips in two columns ('1 Meeting notes p. 12', '2 Page 20', '3 The Index'), in the order the links sit on the page, top to bottom then left to right;
- a tool row: Go to (magnifier), Link (chain), Areas (eye, dimmed while off) and Index (dots).
An empty page shows 'No links on this page yet.' with Link as the main button. The card also opens from the 'links' action (a key, controller button or pen button) and from a 0.6 s hold on the panel's page chip, so it never depends on gestures alone.

4. HOPPING (peek).
- Tapping chip 1 shows page 12 above the card at once: GL16, no flash, about 0.4 s from the cache (longer only the first time a dense page is drawn).
- Chip 1 gets a thick frame, the title reads 'Showing p. 12 · Tap the page to stay', and a 'Back to p. 3' button appears at the left of the tool row.
- Chip 2 shows page 20 the same way. The list is still page 3's links.
- Tapping the page above the card commits: the card closes, page 20 becomes the open page, and one GC16 flash clears any ghosting. That tap does nothing else: it never follows a link or draws.
- Back, a two-finger swipe down, or a one-finger drag down on the grip returns to page 3 instead.
- A pen touch outside the card commits the same way, and its stroke is not drawn.

5. MAKING A LINK.
- Link (in the card, or the 'add-link' action) closes the card and shows a slim bar at the bottom: 'Draw around what links', with Cancel.
- The owner circles a word with the pen. A dashed 4 px line follows the nib (DU; it is UI, not ink).
- On lift the dashes become a dotted rectangle around the circle's box, and a bottom sheet asks 'Where does it go?'. It offers the Index entries as chips (paged, in Index order), plus New page, The Index, Page number and All pages.
- Tapping 'Meeting notes' makes the link ('Linked to Meeting notes.'). The dotted rectangle disappears unless Areas is on. No ink was added: the page looks exactly as before.
- Undo removes the link.
- New page asks for a name on a keyboard over the page, adds the page at the end and links to it. The owner stays on the current page.
- A circle under 5 mm both ways says 'Too small for a link: draw around what links.' and waits for another.

6. FOLLOWING A LINK. A finger tap inside a link's invisible area (at least 7 mm a side) goes there, with a GC16 flash as today. When links are nested, the smallest area under the finger wins.

7. SEEING AREAS. Areas (the eye) in the card turns on dashed outlines, each with a numbered corner tag matching its chip. They are drawn over the page as UI only: never in the page, PDF or thumbnails. The choice is remembered (settings.ini link_areas), and the 'link-areas' action toggles it from anywhere.

8. CHANGING A LINK. A 0.6 s finger hold on a link at once draws a heavy dotted border around its area (DU). A small dialog then opens beside it (GL16), with the page still in view. It shows the target ('-> Meeting notes, p. 12') and four buttons:
- Rename... For an unnamed target it reads 'Name page 20...' and adds an Index entry. The keyboard opens over the page, and the dotted border stays visible above it.
- Change where it goes...
- Redraw the area.
- Delete link. It shows 'Link deleted. Undo brings it back.' Any border the owner drew around the link is ordinary ink and stays.
A tap outside closes the dialog and does nothing else. The same dialog opens, placed above the card, from a 0.6 s hold on a hotbar chip.

9. PAGES AND BACK. Two fingers swipe down: the Pages view opens (GC16). A two-finger swipe up while it is open closes it (the mirror of its gesture), as does its Back button.

10. SIDEWAYS OR ZOOMED. Two fingers in the middle of the page pan it as today, now with the zoom held still. Navigation still works from the edges: a two-finger swipe down that starts in the top 25 mm opens Pages, and one up from the bottom 25 mm opens the hotbar. So does a swipe in a direction the page cannot scroll any further.

11. THE INDEX MAP. Index (the dots) in the card, or the 'index-map' action, opens a full-screen map (GC16).
- Pages are dots joined by lines. The open page is a double ring at the centre, and named pages are labelled.
- Well-linked pages are solid, lightly linked ones dithered. Pages with no links are hollow rings in a 'Not linked yet' tray.
- Tapping a dot selects it and shows a card: the name, 'p. 12 · 3 out · 2 in', and Open, Rename and Local. Tapping the dot again opens the page.
- One finger pans (a coarse DU preview, crisp GL16 at release); a pinch zooms.
- Local shows only the open page and its neighbours up to two links away.

12. SETTINGS > GESTURES.
- Settings' bottom row reads KOReader | Controller | Gestures | Updates | Done.
- Gestures lists the groups (Editing, Tools, Pages, Index, Menus, Screen), an on/off row, Reset and Done.
- In a group, each action shows its gesture ('Pages: 2 fingers down', 'Undo: none').
- Tap a row and do the gesture: it is learned. If it belonged to another action, a toast says 'That gesture is no longer for Undo.'
- A try that is not clean is refused with the reason: 'Put the fingers down together.', 'Swipe straight.', 'Swipe farther.', 'The pen is near: move it away.'
- Holding a row 0.6 s clears it. All of this works with controller shortcuts off.

13. WHEN THINGS GO WRONG.
- links.ini does not read: the card says 'Links could not be read.', and Link explains why instead of doing nothing.
- 64 links on a page: Link says 'This page has 64 links: delete one to add another.'
- A gesture made with the pen hovering nearby, or while a palm moves, does nothing. Only record mode says why; outside it, a one-time hint per session explains the pen rule.
- A notebook with 2000 pages and 4000 links: the card, the dialog and link following cost the same as in a small notebook. The map opens on a quick seed layout and settles once the background layout finishes.
specs.gestures:
VOCABULARY (fixed, nothing free-form)
- 2 fingers: swipe up, down, left, right; tap.
- 3 fingers: the same five. They are offered only once the device log shows the panel reports 3 or more contacts; ABS_MT_SLOT's maximum is unknown today.
- 1 finger: swipe up, down, left, right. Only when the swipe starts on the page, not on the panel or a sheet.
- File keys: touch.2.up, touch.2.down, touch.2.left, touch.2.right, touch.2.tap, touch.3.*, touch.1.*.
- UI names (EN / ES): '2 fingers up' / '2 dedos arriba', '2-finger tap' / 'Toque con 2 dedos', '1 finger left' / '1 dedo izq.'. Two-press rows use the short forms ('2 dedos izq. / 2 dedos der.' measures 1395 px, within the 1470 px column).
- Reserved, never recordable: a one-finger tap or hold (UI, links, the hotbar); a two-finger spread or squeeze while pinch zoom is on; a two-finger drag the view can follow (pan).

DEFAULTS. Built in, and never written while unchanged:
- touch.2.down = pages
- touch.2.up = links (the hotbar)
Everything else is unbound, including two-finger left/right and taps (owner question). The pen plan's defaults (Button.triple and Button.hold = clear-page) live in the same map.

RECOGNIZER: src/touchgest.c
Pure, in CORE_SRC, built and host-tested like pensync.c.

Inputs, per SYN frame:
- the kernel time: SYN_REPORT's event time, converted to now_ms's clock (the fd is already CLOCK_MONOTONIC);
- each contact: tracking id, logical x and y (after calibration and rotation), tool, touch_major, pressure;
- pen context: prox, touching, left_ms, last contact point, and the hover point with its age;
- view context, pushed by the screen: can_pan up/down/left/right, zoom_ok, gestures_on, record, w, h, dpi.

Outputs: today's IN_TOUCH_* and IN_PINCH_* events, plus IN_GESTURE. Its fields:
- value: the gesture id (> 0), or in record mode a negative rejection reason;
- x, y: the start midpoint; x2, y2: the end midpoint.
Cost: O(1) per frame, no allocation, signed 32-bit time differences.

A session runs from the first contact down to the last lift. Within a session:
1. ONE FINGER. Exactly today's stream: IN_TOUCH_DOWN at once, MOVE on change, UP at lift, with no added latency. The single-finger rules are unchanged:
   - a palm flag suppresses;
   - the pen near, or gone less than 1000 ms, suppresses.
2. LANDING. A second contact makes the session multi-finger.
   - The finger count is fixed at the first of: any contact moving 3 mm (35 px); 250 ms after the first landing; the first lift.
   - The first finger's stream ends with the off-screen cancel, never a real lift, so it can never tap.
   - Two fingers count for a swipe or tap only if they landed within 200 ms of each other (three fingers: within 250 ms).
   - Up to 400 ms still allows zoom (today's rule). Later than 400 ms is a palm, as today.
   - A contact landing after the count is fixed rejects the gesture ('too many fingers'), except during a committed zoom, where extra contacts are ignored as today.
3. RESTING CONTACTS (a grip thumb, the writing palm). A contact counts as resting if it stayed within 3 mm for 300 ms before the gesture's first finger, or if the panel flags it MT_TOOL_PALM.
   - It is left out of the count and the landing window, provided every gesture finger is at least 40 mm (472 px) from it.
   - If it moves more than 3 mm during the gesture, the gesture is rejected ('hand moved').
   - This replaces today's 'any later finger is a late palm', for multi-finger gestures only.
4. PEN RULES for multi-finger gestures (single fingers keep the global 1 s rule):
   - pen touching: reject;
   - pen in proximity: accept only if its hover point is known (no older than 50 ms) and every finger is at least 60 mm (709 px) from it and from the last pen contact point; else reject ('pen near');
   - pen gone less than 300 ms: reject;
   - pen gone 300-1000 ms: accept if every finger is at least 40 mm from the last pen contact point.
   The hover rule needs hover_learn to run on raw digitizer frames always, not only while Live view hooks it (input_evdev.c:418 and 288). It is a cheap per-frame update and never runs at the PIN. Until the step-1 device log has been read, ship the conservative variant: pen in proximity always rejects, and the 300 ms floor applies.
5. SIZE GUARDS. The gesture is rejected if any contact:
   - has a TOUCH_MAJOR above T_palm (set from the device log; until then the guard is off and only logged);
   - is closer than 8 mm or farther than 70 mm from the other finger (two-finger gestures);
   - has ever been tool 1 (MT_TOOL_PEN).
6. CLASSIFY at the dead zone. With d0 = the finger distance when the count was fixed, mid0 = the midpoint then, spread_px = |d - d0| and trans = |mid - mid0|:
   - ZOOM when zoom_ok, the spread has changed by at least 10%, and spread_px >= 1.5 x trans. This is today's coupled zoom and pan: IN_PINCH_BEGIN with value TG_ZOOM, then MOVE.
   - TRANSLATE when trans >= 6 mm (70 px, today's travel) and trans >= 1.5 x spread_px.
   - Neither yet: keep waiting. Once max(spread_px, trans) reaches 15 mm (177 px), the larger one wins. Resting fingers that never reach the dead zone do nothing, so k_pinch_gate stays green.
   A TRANSLATE is then split by its dominant axis. It must be within 30 degrees of an axis; otherwise it is a PAN if the view can pan freely, else a reject ('swipe straight').
   - PAN when the view can move that way AND the start midpoint is outside that direction's edge band. The bands are the top 25 mm (295 px) for down, the bottom 25 mm for up, and the left or right 15 mm (177 px) for horizontal. IN_PINCH_BEGIN carries value TG_PAN, and the editor moves ox and oy with the zoom held at its value, which ends today's zoom wobble.
   - SWIPE otherwise. Nothing is drawn while a swipe is tracked (no animation).
7. FIRE at the first lift, after IN_PINCH_END for a pan or zoom, so that S->pinching is already clear.
   - A swipe fires if all of these hold: net travel along the axis >= 20 mm (236 px); off-axis travel <= 0.58 x the along-axis travel; each finger's displacement has cosine >= 0.8 to the other's, with a length ratio between 0.5 and 2; the spread changed by no more than 25%; first landing to first lift <= 1200 ms. Sliding back under 20 mm cancels it: a half-made gesture is undone by reversing it.
   - An N-finger tap fires if all fingers landed within the window, all lifted within 150 ms of each other, first landing to last lift took <= 300 ms, and no contact moved more than 5 mm (59 px).
   - A 1-finger swipe fires if it travels at least 30 mm (354 px) along the axis in at most 600 ms, within 30 degrees, and started on the page.
8. After a fire or a reject, every contact stays suppressed until all have lifted (today's T.suppressed), so a late lift never leaks a tap or a link follow.

EDITOR CONTEXT. The editor pushes it through input_touch_context whenever:
- view_clamp changes ox, oy or zoom;
- a sheet opens or closes;
- the screen changes;
- settings change.
It carries:
- can_pan per direction, from the clamp limits;
- zoom_ok = pinch_zoom is on and no sheet that blocks pinch is open (paper, music, templates, Pages view);
- gestures_on.
Other screens push 'gestures off', except the Gestures sheet while it records.

DISPATCH. IN_GESTURE goes through app routing. Like every new InType it is:
- dropped while asleep (power_asleep_drops);
- ignored while a book is being added (app.c:462);
- counted as presence by note_input (app.c:464);
- named in main.c's event_name table, whose static assert checks its size.
On SCR_EDITOR, editor_gesture(a, g, x, y) looks the gesture up in the gesture map and calls editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y), the pen plan's anchor-aware dispatcher. All of editor_shortcut's gates therefore apply: idle only, menu actions through open menus, nothing through a keyboard.

MIRROR RULE. While a menu is in front (hotbar, Pages view, Index map, link dialog), the mirror of that menu's own gesture acts as that menu's action, which closes it. The mirror swaps up with down and left with right, with the same finger count. So:
- swipe up opens the hotbar, and swipe down closes it (back to the origin);
- swipe down opens Pages, and swipe up closes it.
One-finger swipes are dispatched only if the finger started on the page (OWN_LINK) and the press did not become a link hold.

GESTURES SHEET (Settings > Gestures). In library.c, MOD_GESTURES shares MOD_BUTTONS' draw code, handlers, tick and probes through a BindKind descriptor.
- List: Editing, Tools, Pages, Index, Menus, Screen, 'Gestures on the page: on (tap to change)', Reset gestures, Done. That is 9 rows, under the 12-row sideways limit.
- Group: one row per action, with two-press rows for pairs. Each row reads 'Action: gesture' or 'Action: none'. Actions a touch cannot do are left out: hold-eraser and the gestures switch.
- Learning:
  - Tap a row: it inverts and reads 'Do the gesture for Pages...'. touchgest enters record mode: no pinch or pan side effects, and the same thresholds as runtime, so whatever records will also fire.
  - An accepted gesture is bound. Rule: one gesture per action per source, and a gesture does one action. A gesture taken from another action toasts 'That gesture is no longer for %s.'
  - A rejection toasts its reason, and learning continues.
  - A second tap on the row stops learning. A 10 s timeout leaves the row as it was.
  - A 0.6 s hold clears the row; a cleared default is written as '=nothing'.
  - One-finger taps keep working as UI while learning.
- Pen gestures, once the pen plan lands, record in the same rows ('Undo: 2-finger tap / pen double-click'). The pen plan's gesture-first Pen sheet is then not needed; its touch-while-held cycler stays a Settings row.
- Rejection reasons (EN / ES):
  - 'Put the fingers down together.' / 'Apoya los dedos a la vez.'
  - 'Swipe straight.' / 'Desliza en línea recta.'
  - 'Swipe farther.' / 'Desliza más lejos.'
  - 'The pen is near: move it away.' / 'El lápiz está cerca: apártalo.'
  - 'That was a pinch: it zooms.' / 'Eso fue un pellizco: hace zoom.'
  - 'Your hand moved: try again.' / 'La mano se movió: inténtalo otra vez.'
  - 'Only %d fingers were seen.' / 'Solo se vieron %d dedos.'

SIMULATOR AND RUNNER
- Window: Shift + right-drag = two fingers 25 mm apart moving together; Alt + right-drag = three fingers; Ctrl + right-click = a two-finger tap; the wheel stays the pinch. SDL3 trackpad finger events are optional and must be checked on macOS first.
- Runner, at contact level through touchgest:
  - 'finger ID down|move|up X Y [MAJOR] [TOOL]' lines form one frame until 'frame [MS]' (default 13 ms);
  - 'swipe N X Y DX DY [STEPS] [SEP] [LANDGAP]';
  - 'tapn N X Y [SEP] [MS]';
  - 'pen hover' and 'pen leave' drive the pen context.
  The legacy 'tap', 'touch', 'drag touch' and 'pinch' still push events directly, so every existing scenario stays green.
- Probes: touch.gesture (the last gesture key), touch.reject (the last reason key), touch.contacts, touch.suppressed, gestures.ACTION, library.gestures.learning.
specs.hotbar:
WHAT IT LISTS. The open page's outgoing links: one chip per link, at most 64, from nav_links_of plus the cached areas.
- Order: as the page reads, by each area's top edge quantized to 15 mm bands, then by its left edge. The numbers 1..N match the eye overlay's tags.
- Chip labels:
  - a named target: its Index name (nav_name, binary search);
  - an unnamed page: 'Page 12';
  - the Index: 'The Index', with the Index icon;
  - a deleted page, or a target this version does not know: 'Page not here' (a tap toasts; a long press offers Delete);
  - a legacy link with neither area nor ink: 'No area: redraw it', with a hollow dashed badge.
- Backlinks are not in the card; the map's card shows them (owner question).

LAYOUT, UPRIGHT. Card at x 20, 1820 px wide, its bottom edge 20 px above the screen's, padding 24 px. From the top:
- a 36 px grip strip with a 160 x 10 px rounded bar (drag it down to close);
- a 120 px header. Left: 'Links on this page · N' at 44 px bold, or while peeking 'Showing p. 12 · Tap the page to stay' (truncated). Right, when N > 6: a pager '<  1/3  >' (two 118 x 110 buttons);
- chips in 2 columns of 878 x 124 px with 16 px gaps, up to 3 rows (6 per screen). Each chip has a 72 px numbered badge, the label at 44 px bold (cut short by font_draw_left_name), and 'p. 12' at 34 px, right-aligned. The frame is 3 px, or 8 px on the chip of the page being shown;
- a 120 px tool row: 'Back to p. 3' (380 px, primary style, only while peeking), then Go to, Link, Areas and Index, each 280 x 120 with an icon and a 34 px word ('Ir a', 'Enlazar', 'Áreas', 'Índice').
Height = 344 + rows x 124 + (rows - 1) x 16: 472 px for 0-2 links, 612 for 3-4, 752 for 5 or more. At least 1708 px of page stays visible above it.

LAYOUT, SIDEWAYS (2480 wide). 3 columns of 800 x 124, up to 2 rows. The tool buttons (240 x 110) and the pager sit at the right of the header, and Back replaces the title while peeking. Height 468 px, 25% of 1860.

The card is drawn above the panel and every editor sheet. Because compose resets a->toast_floor, the card sets it to its own top afterwards.

OPENING IT
- the 'links' action (by default the 2-up gesture; also any key, controller button or pen button);
- a 0.6 s hold on the panel's page chip, checked in editor_tick as link_hold is.
Opening the card disarms link mode. 'links' is a MENU action: it joins front_menu, menu_action, close_front, open_menu and sheet_open. So:
- its own action closes the card;
- another menu's action swaps to that menu;
- Close menu closes it;
- every other shortcut is refused while it is up, so nothing (no undo, no page turn) happens behind a peek.

INTERACTIONS. Finger or pen: the card is UI.
- PRESS A CHIP. app_press_feedback inverts it at once (DU). That link's area is also drawn as a dashed outline on the page if it is visible above the card (DU), so the owner sees which link it is even with Areas off. Moving off the chip beyond the 30 px slop cancels both.
- TAP A PAGE CHIP (released within the slop, in under 600 ms): PEEK.
  - On the first peek: save_page (pumped), keep the origin's canvas in the peek cache, and remember origin = S->index.
  - Then load the target (page_at). Take its canvas from the cache or render it (render_page_full, pumped). Set S->index, but never nb.last_page or info_dirty. view_reset, redraw the page area and the card, and send one REFRESH_UI.
  - The list stays the origin's.
- TAP AN INDEX CHIP, OR THE INDEX BUTTON. If peeking, return silently to the origin (the map covers the screen anyway). Close the card and open the Index map (GC16). Until the map exists (step 18), this opens the Pages view's Index tab.
- TAP OUTSIDE THE CARD (a finger anywhere else, the panel included): COMMIT.
  - If peeking: nb.last_page = index, set info_dirty, write_thumb_if_needed, drop the cache, close the card, and compose_all(REFRESH_FULL). That is the one flash, and it also clears the peeks' ghosting.
  - If not peeking: close with a REFRESH_UI of the card's rect only.
  - Either way the touch becomes OWN_MODAL until it lifts (the paper sheet's pattern, editor.c:2412-2421): no link follow, no panel press.
- PEN DOWN OUTSIDE. The same commit, and the stroke is swallowed (OWN_MODAL until the pen lifts). Drawing it would race the closing refresh: a GL16 or GC16 still on the panel keeps the stroke off MTK pen mode (up to about 300 ms of lag), and a flash under live ink is worse. No toast mid-stroke.
- LONG PRESS A CHIP (600 ms within the slop). If peeking, return to the origin first (GL16), since the link lives there. Then the link dialog opens above the card, lined up with the chip. The link's area gets the heavy dotted border if it is above the card; otherwise the chip stays inverted as the marker. The choices are the same as on the page.
- CLOSE WITHOUT COMMITTING: CANCEL. Triggered by Back, the 'links' action again, the mirror gesture (2-down), a one-finger 20 mm drag down starting on the grip strip or the header, or Close menu.
  - If peeking: swap the origin canvas back, set S->index = origin, and compose_all with REFRESH_UI, or REFRESH_FULL after 3 or more peeks, because GL16 ghosting builds up.
  - Otherwise: a REFRESH_UI of the card's rect.
- PAGER. < and > redraw only the chips (REFRESH_UI of the chip area).
- GO TO. Opens the search sheet over the page, through the shared keyboard host. Digits mean a page number; letters search the Index names, accent-folded. A pick peeks, like a chip (tap outside to stay). From the 'go-to-page' action, without the card, a pick goes straight there (GC16).
- LINK. Closes the card (cancelling a peek first) and arms link mode (see link_areas).
- AREAS. Toggles settings.link_areas. Off: the eye-off-outline icon in plain style. On: a filled eye with BTN_SELECTED. It redraws the page's link outlines with a REFRESH_UI of the union of the visible areas plus the button.
- EMPTY AND FAILURE STATES:
  - an empty page: 'No links on this page yet.', with Link as the primary button;
  - links.ini unreadable: 'Links could not be read.'; Link and Areas are disabled, and tapping Link toasts the reason;
  - a read-only page: Link is disabled and shows the read-only toast.
- SLEEP OR A POWER HOLD WHILE PEEKING changes nothing on disk: notebook.ini still names the origin. Leaving the editor (editor_leave) cancels the peek before saving.

PEEK CACHE
- Up to 3 page canvases, 4.6 MB each at 1860x2480: the origin, pinned, plus the two most recent targets, keyed by page id.
- Swapped in by exchanging structs, not by memcpy.
- Any allocation failure falls back to rendering.
- Freed when the card closes.
- Possible later addition: while the card is idle for 300 ms, prefetch the next targets in pumped 64-row slices, stopping at the first input.

PROBES: editor.hotbar (0/1), editor.hotbar.n, editor.hotbar.N ('label|target'), editor.hotbar.peek (the origin page number, or 0), editor.hotbar.screen, notebook.last_page, and, for refresh assertions, display.full_count (GC16 presents since start) and display.last_mode.
specs.link_areas:
MODEL
- A link is (page id, seed, target, area). The area is an axis-aligned rectangle in page px at the notebook's page size, stored in links.ini (see data_and_formats).
- The area is invisible. It is never in page_canvas, thumbnails, the share page or Live view's page layer. Only overlays in App.screen show it: the eye, the dotted border, and the dashed line while it is being drawn.
- The seed stays the link's id. nav_new_seed keeps it unique per page and already avoids link seeds, so new ink never takes it.
- A visible border is the owner's own ink (smart shapes or freehand) and is never part of the link. Erasing it leaves the link; deleting the link leaves it.

HIT TEST (nav_link_at)
- Each link's box is its area, or, for an unmigrated legacy link, the box of its ink strokes' points. The box is padded to at least 7 mm a side around its centre (NAV_LINK_MIN_MM).
- Under the finger, the link with the SMALLEST padded box wins (ties: the lower seed). This replaces 'last stroke wins', so nested links behave and area links need no creation order.
- The editor caches the open page's areas (at most 64 rects). The cache is rebuilt on a page change and on link edits; for unmigrated links only, also on draw_end, erase_end, undo/redo and clear.
- nav_link_areas also returns areas first, so the PDF's /Link annotations (export.c:94-117) follow the areas with no change to export.

MAKING ONE (link mode)
- Arm: Link in the hotbar, the 'add-link' action, or the Index tab's Add a link. A refusal now says why:
  - a read-only page: the read-only toast;
  - links.ini unreadable: 'Links could not be read.';
  - 64 links on the page: 'This page has 64 links: delete one to add another.'
- Armed: a bottom bar (1820 x 130 px, GL16) reads 'Draw around what links', with Cancel. It shows the mode for as long as it lasts, instead of a 4 s toast. Pressing 'add-link' again, Close menu, Cancel, a page change or leaving the editor disarms it, with nothing written.
- Lasso: the next pen contact becomes OWN_LASSO, whatever the tool, eraser end and button included.
  - Its points (page px, decimated to at most 4096) are drawn as a dashed 4 px black line (12 on, 8 off) into App.screen.
  - The line is an overlay layer that compose redraws, so a recompose never wipes it.
  - Each new segment is shown with REFRESH_FAST under display_live_ink(true). Pen mode is not needed, and DU suits 1-bit.
  - Nothing goes into page_canvas, the page or history, and smart shapes never apply in link mode.
- Lift: take the box of the points.
  - Smaller than 5 mm both ways (LINK_BOX_MIN_MM): the dashes are recomposed away, the toast 'Too small for a link: draw around what links.' shows, and the mode stays armed.
  - Otherwise the area is that box, clamped to the page. The dotted rectangle replaces the dashes in one REFRESH_UI of their union, and the bar becomes the Link-to sheet.
- Link-to sheet. It is the hotbar's frame in pick mode, with the same chips and pager, titled 'Where does it go?' / '¿Adónde va?'.
  - Chips: first 'New page' / 'Página nueva' and 'The Index' / 'El índice', then the Index entries in Index order (nav_index).
  - Tool row: Page number (number pad), Go to (search), All pages (the Pages view in picking mode, the old path, GC16), Cancel.
- A pick: nav_link_set(pid, seed, target) plus the area, then nav_save_links.
  - On failure, nav_load rolls back and the toast says 'Could not save the link.' (today's pattern).
  - On success, one ACT_LINK is pushed (undo removes the link) and the toast says 'Linked to %s.' / 'Enlazado a %s.'. The dotted rectangle is recomposed away unless Areas is on.
- New page asks 'Name the new page' on a keyboard over the page. The page is added (at the end, store_add_page) and named only on Done; an empty name leaves it unnamed. Cancel leaves no page behind, and the editor stays on the origin.
- Seed: nav_new_seed(a hash of the time and position), so it differs from every ink seed and link seed on the page.

SHOWING AREAS (the eye; settings.ini link_areas, default 0; action 'link-areas')
- In compose(r), after the page blit and before the panel, each cached area that meets r gets:
  - a dashed outline: 4 px black dashes (12 on, 10 off) over a 2 px white halo, so it reads over dark ink;
  - a numbered tag at its top-left corner, kept inside the screen: a 56 x 56 px white box with a 3 px frame and the number at 34 px bold.
- 1-bit only: it looks the same under DU and GL16, and stays distinct under display_set_invert.
- Cost: at most 64 rect tests per compose, which matters because live ink calls compose often.
- Zoom-aware through page_to_screen. Visible on peeked pages too: their areas are computed at the peek.

LONG PRESS ON A LINK (owner ruling 2)
- Trigger: a finger held 600 ms (LINK_HOLD_MS) within the 30 px slop on a link. The pen keeps drawing.
- At once, a heavy dotted border goes around the area inflated by 8 px: 5 px dashes (16 on, 10 off) on a 9 px white underlay. It is presented alone with REFRESH_FAST and an immediate app_flush (about 0.2 s). The dialog is then presented with REFRESH_UI, so the two far-apart rects never merge into one big refresh.
- Dialog: a card 780 px wide and 678 px tall.
  - The target line (110 px): '-> Meeting notes, p. 12', truncated.
  - Four 118 px buttons with 16 px gaps: Rename..., Change where it goes..., Redraw the area, Delete link (primary style).
  - Rename reads 'Name page %d...' for an unnamed page. It is disabled for the Index, for an unknown target, and when nav.ini cannot be written.
- Placement, beside the area:
  - below it, if it fits within a 24 px margin; else above; else on the side with more room; always clamped to the screen;
  - it never covers the area, unless the area is larger than the screen minus the dialog (then bottom centre).
- Rename: the keyboard over the page, through the shared keyboard host, titled 'Rename page 12' or 'Name page 20'.
  - Done = nav_set_name(target pid) + nav_save, restoring the old name on failure (the pattern of editor.c:1643-1656, with a pid parameter instead of the open page).
  - It renames that page everywhere: the Index, the tiles, the PDF outline.
  - Naming an unnamed page makes it an Index entry and a section start, which the button's wording says.
- Change where it goes: the Link-to sheet for this link; ACT_LINK records the old target.
- Redraw the area: link mode for this link ('Draw the link's new area'). The new box replaces the area (ACT_LINK).
- Delete link: nav_link_remove, then save. ACT_LINK keeps the record for undo. The toast says 'Link deleted. Undo brings it back.' / 'Enlace eliminado. Deshacer lo recupera.' The dialog and border are recomposed away with a REFRESH_UI of their union: at most the dialog plus the area.
- A tap outside closes it and is swallowed (OWN_MODAL). The dispatcher treats it as a menu, so Close menu closes it.

UNDO OF LINK EDITS
- A new in-memory history kind, ACT_LINK {pid, seed, before, after}, lives in the page's history. A record is a target plus an area; 'before' is empty for an add, 'after' for a delete.
- So 'one moment, one step' holds: making, retargeting, redrawing and deleting are each one undo step.
- Undo and redo re-apply the record and save links.ini. A save that fails rolls back with nav_load, toasts, and drops the step.
- Nothing about links is ever in the .qpg.

MIGRATING beta.5 LINKS (owner ruling 1)
- When the editor loads a page (page_at), each of its links that has no area but does have ink strokes with its seed gets an area: the unpadded box of those strokes' points, rounded outward to whole px.
- The links are marked dirty, and the next nav_save_links (with the page's save) writes them.
- The ink is untouched and stays as ordinary ink.
- Migration is lazy, per page, so opening a notebook never reads all its pages.
- Until a page has been visited, its links behave exactly as before (the ink-box fallback). The PDF does the same through nav_link_areas, so migrated and unmigrated links look the same to the owner.
- A link whose ink is already gone at migration keeps no area. The hotbar lists it as 'No area: redraw it'.
- Effects:
  - the precise-eraser and white-ink quirk ends, because the area no longer depends on ink;
  - erasing or undoing the old ring no longer kills the link;
  - compaction can drop the ring safely.
- A links.ini that is not writable is not migrated; the fallback works anyway.
specs.smart_shapes:
TRIGGER
- Draw, then hold the nib still within 1.0 screen mm (11.8 px) for shape_hold_ms (default 550 ms). The radius is measured on screen, so zoom does not change it.
- editor_tick checks this every 30 ms or less while S->owner == OWN_DRAW:
  - the hold is timed from the kernel time of the last sample that moved more than 1 mm from the anchor; draw_sample updates the anchor in O(1);
  - it is judged only when the last input batch drained the queue (App.input_drained, as in the pen plan), so a backlog is never mistaken for stillness;
  - it is judged by wall time, because a still relayed pen may send no samples at all;
  - one evaluation per still period.
- Applies to ink strokes of the nine pens only. Never to erase strokes (precise eraser, white ink, the whole-stroke eraser), never on a read-only page, never in link mode.

RECOGNIZER: src/shape.c, pure and geometric. It uses no timing features, because the runner's batches share one time.
- Resample at bbox diagonal / 40, and reject anything below the size gates.
- LINE: chord/path >= 0.97; max offset <= max(4% of the length, 1 mm) + 0.5 mm; length >= 12 mm. The angle snaps to 0, 45, 90 or 135 degrees within 4 degrees.
- CLOSED, a prerequisite for every shape below:
  - the end gap <= 22% of the diagonal;
  - winding around the centroid between 1.7 and 2.6 pi;
  - total absolute turning <= 1.6 x winding + 0.6 pi, which rejects scribbles;
  - at least 10 mm across and 4 mm thick.
- RECTANGLE / SQUARE / QUAD: ShortStraw finds 4 corners, and each segment has chord/path >= 0.93. If every angle is within 15 degrees of 90 it is a rectangle: axis-aligned when within 5 degrees, a square when the sides are within 10%. Otherwise it is a straight-edged quad, which is how diamonds come out.
- TRIANGLE: 3 segments; it snaps to equilateral or right-angled within 6 to 8 degrees.
- ELLIPSE / CIRCLE: a PCA frame plus a least-squares fit of x^2/A + y^2/B = 1. RMS radial error <= 6% of the minor axis, maximum <= 20%. A circle when the axis ratio >= 0.88; axis-aligned when within 6 degrees.
- v1.5: single-stroke arrow, open polyline (with 90-degree snaps), arc, and grid snapping of line ends and corners on Dot grid and Graph paper.
- WRITING-BURST GATE: a stroke started within 600 ms and 8 mm of the previous lift needs fits 0.7x as tight and a 1.5x longer hold.
- Cost: about 0.12 ms on the Kindle for a 3000-sample stroke (5.8 us on the host, x20).

THE SNAPPED STROKE (shape_points)
- An ordinary Stroke. It keeps the raw stroke's tool id (0-9), ToolParams snapshot, ext bytes, tip variant (stroke_mark_tip) and SEED.
- Its points start at the shape point nearest the user's first point and run in the user's direction. Closed shapes close exactly at the start.
- Polygons: vertices at the intersections of the edges' least-squares lines, plus a point every 2 mm so whole-stroke erasing and hit tests stay smooth.
- Ellipses: N = clamp(ceil(2 pi / acos(1 - 0.25 px / r)), 24, 720) vertices.
- Pressure: the median of the middle 80% of the raw samples by arc length. Tilt: the median. t_ms: interpolated by arc length.
- No new tool id, header version, ext flag or chunk. Older versions draw it as the pen stroke it is.

PREVIEW, CANCEL, COMMIT. No GL16 and no toast while the pen is down: a non-DU frame would call pen_leave's wait.
- Preview:
  1. The region is the raw stroke's bbox united with the shape's bbox, padded by the brush's max radius + 2.
  2. Copy that region of page_canvas, with the raw ink in it.
  3. draw_page(region) renders the page without the stroke in progress; it is not page_add'ed until the lift.
  4. Stamp the shape with stroke_brush_begin and brush_add, calling work_pump every 8 points.
  5. show(region, REFRESH_FAST): one DU frame.
  Live equals re-render holds by construction, since this is page_render plus the brush.
- Cancel: when the nib moves more than 1 mm from the hold point, the saved copy goes back (memcpy, about 1 ms) with one DU frame. The raw stroke's BrushState was never touched, so the stroke continues seamlessly.
- Commit: lifting during the preview does page_add(raw) and history_push_add. history_push_replace then swaps raw for shape in place: a new ACT_REPLACE, count 2, owning whichever stroke is off the page. The pixels already show the shape, and the region joins S->settle for the usual GL16 settle.
- Undo: the first undo puts the hand-drawn stroke back; the second removes it. This is iPadOS's behaviour, and an owner ruling, since the snap is its own moment.
- Fallback: if the region copy cannot be allocated, that stroke gets no preview (nothing visible happens). A preview render that would exceed about 300 ms is still pumped and never blocks the pen.

TOGGLE AND SETTINGS
- Panel: P_SHAPES, a 12th button directly under the eraser, in the pen-behaviour group. Icon F0832 (shape-outline), BTN_SELECTED while on. PANEL_BUTTONS becomes 12; sideways with 4 pins, panel_fit scales the panel to about 0.99. The collapsed panel shows a 20 px corner mark while shapes are on. Before the button lands, scenarios are converted to symbolic panel taps so no coordinates shift (implementation step 13).
- Tool picker: a labelled third control in the ink row, 'Shapes' / 'Formas'.
- Pen feel: a row 'Smart shapes: Normal (tap to change)' cycling Off, Quick 0.4 s, Normal 0.55 s, Deliberate 0.9 s.
- settings.ini:
  - shapes: 0 off, 1 on, missing = 1. Numeric and append-only, so 2 = lines only or 3 = every stroke can come later;
  - shape_hold_ms: 300-1500, default 550.
- Actions:
  - 'shapes': the toggle;
  - 'shape-last': snaps the newest ink stroke now, with every gate but no hold, only when the top undo step is that stroke's ACT_ADD; otherwise it toasts 'No shape in the last stroke.' / 'El último trazo no es una forma.'
  Both can be bound to keys, controllers, gestures and pen buttons.
- Toasts, never mid-stroke:
  - after a toggle: 'Shapes on. Hold the pen still at the end of a line or shape.' / 'Formas activadas. Mantén el lápiz quieto al final de una línea o forma.', and 'Shapes off.' / 'Formas desactivadas.';
  - once, after the first snap (a settings.ini tips bit): 'Shape made. Undo brings your own line back.' / 'Forma hecha. Deshacer devuelve tu trazo.'

ACCIDENTAL-INPUT DEFENSES, strongest first:
1. A hold only previews; moving on restores everything.
2. Gates that can say no: size in screen mm, closure, winding, the scribble budget, corner and fit residuals. On the owner's own writing, the hold alone would fire 21 times in 47 strokes; the gates turned none of them into a preview at written size.
3. The writing-burst gate.
4. Undo returns the freehand stroke.
5. A toolbar toggle plus an adjustable hold: the two things Amazon's users asked for.
6. Ink only: never erasers, never the link lasso.

DEVICE TUNING: an empty grimoire/shape-log file makes each hold log its features and its decision: size in mm, winding, residuals, corners, the kind or the reason, and ms taken. It never logs coordinates.
specs.graph_view:
WHAT IT SHOWS. Built from nav.ini and links.ini only. No page is read, so it opens equally fast in any notebook.
- Nodes: every named page, every page with a link in or out, and the open page. Unnamed pages with no links are counted in a chip ('+1,870 pages with no links'); 'All pages' adds them to the tray.
- Edges: links deduplicated per unordered page pair, 3 px wide plus 1 px per extra link, up to 6 px. No arrowheads in v1.
- Links to the Index: a small lozenge badge on the page's dot, not edges, because a hub makes a hairball. 'Show the Index' adds it as a lozenge hub at its linkers' centroid, with no forces.
- Degree tiers, by in + out degree after dedup. All are 1-bit safe, so DU previews and GL16 frames look the same:
  - 0: hollow ring (4 px);
  - 1: 25% Bayer dither;
  - 2-3: 50% dither;
  - 4 or more: solid.
  The dithers come from canvas_disc_pattern: a 4x4 Bayer matrix on 2x2-pixel cells.
- Radius: 10-30 px at fit, by Navi's log formula R_MIN + (R_MAX - R_MIN) x ln(1 + deg + 1) / ln(1 + maxdeg + 1). Unnamed pages are drawn at 0.75x.
- Orphans (degree 0) are left out of the forces and laid out, in notebook order at a 40 px pitch, in a 'Not linked yet' / 'Sin enlaces aún' tray: a 300 px band at the bottom when upright, 420 px at the right when sideways.
- The open page: a concentric double ring. The selected page: an 8 px ring, its edges at 6 px, its label an inverted chip.
- Labels: named pages, 34 px, at most 320 px wide (font_draw_left_name).
  - Placed greedily by priority: selected, open page, neighbours, then named pages by degree.
  - 4 candidate positions each; a label is skipped if it would overlap a placed label or dot.
  - Each sits on a 6 px white knockout.
  - 'p. N' labels for unnamed pages appear only when zoomed 2x or in Local.

SCREEN. A full-screen modal hosted by the editor like the Pages view, but drawn from its own offscreen canvas: compose only blits it and never re-renders on a compose.
- Top bar, 140 px: Back; 'Index map' / 'Mapa del índice' with '48 pages · 63 links'; chips Local, All pages, Index, List and Fit. List goes to the Pages view's Index tab, which gains a Map button.
- Selection card, 260 px at the bottom: the name (44 px bold), 'p. 12 · 3 out · 2 in' / 'p. 12 · 3 salen · 2 entran', and buttons Open, Rename and Local (300 x 118).

INTERACTION
- Tap a dot: the nearest centre within max(r, 5 mm = 59 px), found by the map's own hit test because HitList holds only 128 entries. It is selected, with a REFRESH_UI of the old and new selection boxes plus the card.
  - Tap it again, or Open: go to the page (GC16) and close the map.
  - Tap empty space: deselect.
  - Long press a dot, or Rename: the naming keyboard over the map (shared keyboard host).
- One-finger (or pen) drag on empty space pans. An offset blit of the offscreen render is presented with REFRESH_FAST at most every 180 ms (the pinch precedent), with newly exposed strips left white. At release: a pumped re-render and one REFRESH_UI.
- A pinch zooms, with a nearest-neighbour scaled preview, then the same release. Fit resets the view.
- Gestures follow the menu rules: 'pages' swaps to the Pages view; Close menu or Back returns to the page the map was opened from.
- Local: a radial layout (Navi's place_rings). The open or selected page sits at the centre, depth-1 neighbours on one ring and depth-2 on an outer ring, sorted by parent angle; only members are drawn. O(n + e), instant and deterministic. Fading the rest of the global layout instead was illegible in the mock renders.
- Default: global, centred and zoomed on the open page so its neighbours fit. The last mode is remembered in graph.ini.

LAYOUT
- Seed: Navi's place_disk. BFS shells grow from each component's top-degree hub, with rings sorted by parent angle, and components packed outward by size. Jitter is deterministic, from a hash of the page id (never its index).
- Relax: about 300 Barnes-Hut (theta 0.9) spring-electrical steps with Navi's constants (REPULSION 16000, SPRING_K 0.055, SPRING_L 110, GRAVITY 0.02, DAMPING 0.9). Orphans and the Index hub are excluded.
- Where it runs:
  - up to 150 nodes: in-process, calling work_pump every 5 ms (about 0.1 s on the Kindle);
  - more nodes, or no cache: a niced bgjob child (bgjob.h) computes it and writes graph.ini atomically, while the map shows the O(n + e) seed placement. The result is swapped in with one REFRESH_UI, and only while the map is open and idle (no input for 500 ms). For 2000 pages and 4000 links the child takes about 3.4 s.
- Incremental: a new node goes at its placed neighbours' centroid plus one rest length, then 40 steps run over its 2-hop neighbourhood with everything else fixed (under 10 ms). A full relayout runs when more than 10% of the nodes changed, or on 'Tidy up' (a long press on Fit).
- Determinism: the same graph gives the same positions on one platform. arm64 and armv7 may differ (FMA, libm), so positions persist in graph.ini, and tests assert invariants, never coordinates.

RENDERING COST
- Edges need canvas_line_aa rewritten to draw row spans: bit-identical, and about 40x faster on long edges. As it stands, 4000 long edges would take about a minute on the Kindle.
- Culled to the viewport. Drawing order: edges, knockout discs, dots, labels. work_pump every 64 edges.
- 100 nodes: about 50-70 ms on the Kindle. Worst case, 2000 pages and 4000 links at fit: about 1-2 s, pumped, behind the seed frame.

DATA BUILD: one pass over nav->links with a pid -> index open-addressing table (4096 slots), built once per open. It yields in and out degrees, dedup and components in O(n + e): under 5 ms for 4000 links.

FAILURE
- graph.ini unreadable, or of another generation: ignored and recomputed. It is a cache; an unreadable file is not overwritten that session.
- No memory for the 4.6 MB offscreen canvas: 'Not enough memory for the map.', and the List opens instead.

PROBES: editor.graph (0/1), editor.graph.nodes, .edges, .orphans, .selected, .mode, .node.PID ('tier radius visible'), .labels.
specs.actions:
ONE REGISTRY. A new, UI-free src/actions.c holds, per action:
- id (in memory only), file name, label + msgctxt, icon, group;
- pair: the second action of a two-press row;
- kind;
- sources mask: KEY | PAD | TOUCH | PEN.
Who does what:
- shortcuts.c keeps the parsing and the Buttons map;
- gesturemap.c (new, pure) keeps touch and pen bindings;
- library.c's LearnRow, k_groups and action_label move into the registry, and both the Buttons and Gestures sheets read it;
- editor_shortcut stays the single dispatcher. It becomes editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y), as the pen plan proposes, so zoom and scroll anchor at the pen or at the gesture's midpoint.

KINDS AND FEEDBACK
- TOGGLE: self-inverse, with a toast only when nothing visible changes. Existing: white, fold-panel, eraser-mode, add-link (arm or cancel). New: shapes, link-areas, invert, pinch-zoom, rotation-lock, mirror-pdf, gestures (the master switch; KEY|PAD only).
- MENU: opens; its own action closes it; another menu swaps; it joins front_menu, menu_action, close_front, open_menu and sheet_open. Existing: pages, index, tool-picker, paper, display, pen-feel, library, close-menu. New: links (the hotbar), index-map, go-to-page (the search sheet). The link dialog and the Link-to sheet close with close-menu but have no action of their own.
- STEP pairs (two-press rows). Existing: previous/next page, previous/next tool, picker-previous/next, first/last page. New:
  - zoom-out/zoom-in and scroll-up/scroll-down: the pen plan's, the only four of its names still new;
  - light-down/light-up and warmth-down/warmth-up: these use a new non-blocking light_cached(). With the level unknown, a step toasts and does nothing, never calling the 95-191 ms light_refresh on the input path.
- CYCLE, with a toast naming the new state:
  - side-button: 0..3, the Settings sentences without '(tap to change)';
  - theme: Classic or Gothic, with a relayout like app_set_rotation's leave and enter, then GC16.
- ONE-SHOT. Existing: tool:* (10), undo, redo, clear-page, new-page, fit-page, name-page. New: shape-last; sleep (a public app_request_sleep after editor_save_now).
- MOMENTARY: hold-eraser only. It needs a release, so it is KEY|PAD only; the pen's equivalent is the pen plan's drag slot.
- Excluded from every source: language, calibrate, and the shortcuts switch, since a binding that turns off its own source is a trap.

NEW NAMES: 22, appended after SHORTCUT_NAME_PAGE, taking the registry from 37 to 59 actions: links, index-map, link-areas, go-to-page, shapes, shape-last, zoom-in, zoom-out, scroll-up, scroll-down, invert, light-down, light-up, warmth-down, warmth-up, pinch-zoom, rotation-lock, side-button, theme, mirror-pdf, sleep, gestures.
- 'index' keeps its 1.2.0 meaning: the Index list.
- rotation-lock locks the CURRENT orientation, a new semantic, so a gesture never causes a surprise relayout. Settings' 'Turn with the Kindle' off still snaps to portrait.

GROUPS. Shared by Buttons and Gestures; each has at most 11 action rows so it fits sideways.
- Editing (9): undo, redo, tool:eraser, hold-eraser, eraser-mode, white, clear-page, shapes, shape-last.
- Tools (11): unchanged.
- Pages (8 rows): previous/next page, first/last page, zoom-out/zoom-in, scroll-up/scroll-down, new-page, fit-page, pages, go-to-page.
- Index (6): links, index, index-map, add-link, name-page, link-areas.
- Menus (7): tool-picker, the picker pair, paper, display, pen-feel, library, close-menu.
- Screen (10 rows): invert, the light pair, the warmth pair, pinch-zoom, rotation-lock, side-button, theme, mirror-pdf, sleep, gestures.
The Buttons list is then 6 groups + Reset + Done = 8 rows; the Gestures list is 6 groups + the on/off row + Reset + Done = 9 rows.

BINDING RULE, one for both sheets: per source, a binding does one action and an action has at most one binding.
- Built-in duplicates stay legal as defaults: the D-pad starter lines, and the pen plan's triple and hold both bound to clear-page.
- Learning a binding that another action holds moves it, and the toast names the action that lost it.

SAFETY LIMITS RAISED WITH THE NEW ACTIONS
- SHORTCUT_MAX: 64 -> 192.
- write_pads' 4096-byte buffer: a computed size instead.
- MOD_BUTTONS' text[16]/rows[16]: a bound check plus a _Static_assert (library.c:1116-1134 overflows today past 15 rows).
- test_shortcuts.c:110 and its learn-everything test (136-150): updated.
- test_actions (new): every action has a label in both languages, a group and a kind, and every group fits.

SCOPE: keys and controllers still act only in the idle editor (SHORTCUTS.md:147). In v1, gestures also dispatch only in the editor; the Gestures sheet records them in Settings.
specs.data_and_formats:
NEVER TOUCHED: the .qpg page format. No header bump, no tool id >= 10, no ext flag, no chunk holding page coordinates. Smart shapes are ordinary strokes. Link areas, overlays, the hotbar and the map are not in pages.

links.ini (2.0.0-beta.5, unreleased, so it may change)
  # Grimoire: links drawn on pages
  link.12=0a1b2c3d,p7
  area.12=0a1b2c3d,410,1220,380,140
- link.<pid>=<seed>,<target>: byte for byte today's grammar. The target is 'index' or 'p<pid>', 1-15 bytes from ! to ~.
- area.<pid>=<seed>,<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>: decimal integers in page px at the notebook's page size (store_notebook_page_size), with 0 <= x, y; 1 <= w, h; x + w and y + h <= 6000.
  - The last line for a pid and seed wins.
  - An area line whose link line is missing is dropped at the next save, and logged.
  - A malformed area line is carried verbatim as an unknown line, and its link falls back to the ink box. Nothing is lost.
  - An area outside the page after a page-size change is clamped; if nothing is left after clamping, the link has no area.
- A link with an area uses it. A link without one uses the box of its ink strokes (the beta.5 rule), so files written by the device's f9d13f5 build read unchanged.
- Size: a worst-case pair of lines is about 63 bytes, so 4000 links take about 252 KB, plus up to 16 KiB of carried lines. links.ini therefore gets its own cap, NAV_LINKS_FILE_MAX = 512 KiB; nav.ini keeps 256 KiB. NAV_LINKS_MAX (4000) and NAV_LINKS_PER_PAGE (64) are unchanged.
- What f9d13f5 (on the device) does with a new file:
  - it reads every link. line, and ink links keep working where their ink is (migration never removes it);
  - it carries area. lines as unknown lines, up to 16 KiB (about 430 links);
  - past 16 KiB of area lines, or past 256 KiB in all, it refuses the file: links are read-only there and the file is never overwritten.
  1.2.0 to beta.4 never read links.ini.
- Writes stay whole-file and atomic (write_file_atomic). Unreadable files are still never overwritten.

gestures.ini (new, in root/ beside shortcuts.ini and controller.ini)
  # Grimoire: gestures (Settings > Gestures). Built in unless a line says otherwise:
  # touch.2.down=pages, touch.2.up=links, pen.Button.triple=clear-page, pen.Button.hold=clear-page
  touch.2.tap=undo
  touch.2.up=nothing
  pen.Button.double=links
- It overlays the built-in defaults: an absent line means the default, and '=nothing' switches one off. Later default changes therefore still reach the owner. Reset deletes the file. It is written whole and atomically, with only the slots the owner set.
- Grammar is shortcuts.ini's: '#' or ';' comments, trimmed key=value, a later duplicate wins, case-insensitive.
- Keys: touch.<1|2|3>.<up|down|left|right|tap>, and the pen plan's pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>. This file absorbs the planned pen.ini; both are unreleased.
- Values: an action name, 'nothing', or pan/zoom in a pen drag slot.
- Reading:
  - bounded at 64 KiB, with the shortcuts.c helper;
  - a malformed line is refused and counted (a toast when the sheet opens);
  - a well-formed line this version cannot use (a later gesture or action) is kept verbatim, up to 2 KiB, and written back;
  - a file that does not read (too big, NUL bytes, not a regular file): built-in defaults in memory, the file is never overwritten, and the sheet says 'gestures.ini could not be read' and offers Reset.
- Not in settings.ini: test_probe.c:29-39 and store.c reserve dotted pen. and touch. keys for calibration.

graph.ini (new, in the notebook folder; a CACHE)
  # Grimoire: the Index map's layout (a cache: deleting it loses nothing)
  gen=5f3a9c21
  mode=global
  pos.12=-310,442
- gen: a hash of the node and edge sets the positions belong to. Positions are integer world units. mode is global or local, with depth 1 or 2.
- Unknown lines are carried (255 B each, 16 KiB in all), under a 256 KiB cap.
- An unreadable file is ignored and not overwritten that session. A mismatched gen is updated incrementally or recomputed.
- Older versions never read it, and raw ZIP exports leave it out, since it is a cache.

settings.ini: undotted, numeric, append-only keys. A missing default-on key reads as on, since 1.0.0-beta drops unknown keys.
- shapes: 0 off, 1 on (missing = 1); later 2 = lines only, 3 = every stroke.
- shape_hold_ms: 300-1500 (missing = 550).
- link_areas: 0/1 (missing = 0).
- gestures: 0/1 (missing = 1).
- tips: a bitmask of one-time hints already shown (1 = the first snap, 2 = the hotbar hint after the first link). Older versions drop it, so a hint may show again, which is harmless.
All go in FORMAT.md's table and in the settings.* probes (app.c:1022-1037).

IN MEMORY ONLY: the history kinds ACT_REPLACE (a shape snap) and ACT_LINK (link edits), the per-page area cache, the peek cache, and the map's offscreen canvas.

LIMITS AND HUGE NOTEBOOKS
- The hotbar lists at most 64 links for a page, paged 6 per screen. A file holding more for a page keeps them, and the hotbar lists them all.
- Past 4000 links, the whole links.ini hides (today's rule), and every links surface says 'Links could not be read.'
- Backlink counts for the map: one O(nlinks) pass.
- Search over 2000 names: one accent-folding compare per name per keystroke (store.c's cmp_name made public), a few ms.
specs.eink_and_performance:
RULES FOR EVERY NEW SURFACE
- Screens only call app_invalidate; app_flush presents. No MXCFB_WAIT_FOR_UPDATE_SUBMISSION, no second wait on one marker, and no new display calls at all.
- Overlays use 1-bit marks only (dashes, hollow and solid shapes, ordered dithers on 2x2 cells). A DU frame and the later GL16 then look alike, and inversion keeps them distinct.
- Two far-apart rects (a dotted border and its dialog, a keyboard field and its key) are flushed separately with an explicit app_flush, as library.c:1870-1875 does, never as one union.
- Long work pumps (work_pump every 64 rows, 64 edges or 8 shape points) or runs in a bgjob child. Nothing on the UI thread may run more than about 100 ms between pumps.
- touchgest's frames carry kernel times, and input_pump also reads touch into touchgest (O(1) per frame). A 1.2 s render then no longer bunches or overflows touch: the inferred 512-1024-event buffer lasts only 0.6-2 s of two moving fingers.
- No toast and no GL16 while the pen is down, because a non-DU frame calls pen_leave's wait. Shape previews and the lasso use REFRESH_FAST only, and their toasts wait for the lift.
- No animation. A gesture shows nothing until it fires. Pans and the map's preview use DU at most every 180 ms, then one GL16.

REFRESH AND COST TABLE. Kindle; CPU times are host times x20; waveforms are DU 188 ms, GL16 271 ms and GC16 341 ms at 24-27 C (DU 294 ms when cold).
- Gesture recognition: under 5 us per frame. Firing on lift adds 13-30 ms.
- Hotbar open or close: the card is at most 1820 x 752 = 1.4 Mpx. Draw and copy take 50-90 ms, plus 271 ms of GL16: about 0.35 s, no flash.
- Chip press: an invert plus a DU of 878 x 124, immediate (app_press_feedback).
- Peek:
  - cache hit: a struct swap plus a full-screen GL16 (45-100 ms copy + 271 ms), about 0.4 s;
  - cache miss: page_at (from disk on the first visit) plus render_page_full, up to 1.2 s on a dense page, pumped.
- Commit: one GC16 (341 ms + copy). Cancel: GL16, or GC16 after 3 peeks.
- Link long press: the dotted border by DU in about 0.2 s, then the dialog (780 x 678) by GL16 in about 0.3 s.
- Link-mode lasso: DU per batch of segments, as ink; at the end, a GL16 of the lasso's box.
- Eye on or off: a GL16 of the union of the visible areas.
- Smart shape: recognition 0.12 ms. The preview is a pumped region render, plus dabs at 0.1-0.5 ms per mm of outline, plus a 188 ms DU: about 0.75 s from hold to clean shape typically, under 0.9 s for a 40 mm circle. Cancel is a 1 ms memcpy plus DU.
- Index map:
  - open: GC16 after the seed placement (O(n + e)) and a pumped render (about 50-70 ms for 100 nodes; 1-2 s for 2000 pages and 4000 links with span lines);
  - selection: GL16 of small rects;
  - pan: DU every 180 ms, then GL16 at release;
  - full layout: in a bgjob child, 0.25 s for a few hundred nodes, about 3.4 s for 2000 pages and 4000 links.
- Settings > Gestures: as the Buttons sheet (GL16 rows).

FLASH BUDGET
- GC16 is used only for deliberate screen changes: committing a peek, opening and closing the map, going to a page, the Pages view, theme or invert.
- The every-30th-GL16 promotion (app.c:931) stays. A hotbar session costs 2-3 GL16s, so at most one promoted flash per ten uses, and each commit's GC16 resets the counter.
- Area-weighted promotion is left out: it would change the ghosting of writing everywhere.

MEMORY
- Peek cache: up to 3 x 4.6 MB.
- Map offscreen canvas: 4.6 MB.
- Shape preview region copy: up to 4.6 MB.
Each allocation failure has a slower path that draws the same pixels.

KEYBOARD LAG. The other lane's fix is kept. Every keyboard the new surfaces open (hotbar rename, link dialog rename, Link-to's New page name, search, map rename) goes through the one keyboard host helper:
- draw only when keyboard_pointer reports a change;
- flush the field first, then the key;
- one GL16 settle 900 ms after typing pauses;
- never redraw the 1.78 Mpx modal on a pointer move;
- host the keyboard over the page directly, never inside the Pages view, whose compose redraws the whole screen on every call (editor.c:672-675).
A probe, kb.draws, lets scenarios assert at most one keyboard draw per key change.

INPUT HEALTH FIXES that gestures depend on (the touchgest step):
- A finger cut off by the pen's arrival ends with the off-screen cancel, never a real lift that could tap a link or button (input_evdev.c:477, 764).
- SYN_DROPPED on touch resyncs every slot with EVIOCGMTSLOTS and suppresses touch until all contacts lift, reusing input_set_grab's pattern (1627-1640).
- The device scan's busy flag counts every contact that is down, suppressed or not (1540), so the 330-370 ms scan never starts under a palm or a gesture.
- The pinch pair is chosen by landing order, not by the lowest slot number.

owner_questions.question: Where does 'two fingers up' open the hotbar?
options: Anywhere the page cannot scroll up; from the bottom 25 mm band when it can (sideways or zoomed)
Only from the bottom 25 mm band, always
Anywhere, always (then two-finger vertical panning is lost sideways)
owner_questions.recommended: Anywhere the page cannot scroll up; from the bottom 25 mm band when it can (sideways or zoomed)
owner_questions.why: Upright at fit zoom nothing scrolls, so 'anywhere' is the easiest gesture to make. Sideways or zoomed, the middle of the page must keep panning, and the edge band settles the conflict without a mode. Pages (two fingers down) uses the same rule with the top band.

owner_questions.question: While peeking, does the hotbar keep listing the origin page's links?
options: Keep the origin's list until a commit or cancel
Switch to the shown page's links after each jump
owner_questions.recommended: Keep the origin's list until a commit or cancel
owner_questions.why: It is what makes hopping between several targets possible, and 'Back to p. 3' meaningful. To follow a chain, the owner commits (tap outside) and swipes up again.

owner_questions.question: What does a pen touch outside the open hotbar do?
options: Commit and swallow that stroke
Commit and draw the stroke
Ignore the pen until the hotbar is closed
owner_questions.recommended: Commit and swallow that stroke
owner_questions.why: Drawing it races the closing refresh. A GL16 or GC16 still on the panel keeps the stroke off MTK pen mode (up to about 300 ms of lag), and a flash under live ink is worse. Swallowing is the paper sheet's rule, applied to the pen.

owner_questions.question: What is a link's name in the hotbar, and what does Rename change?
options: The target page's Index name (renaming renames that page; naming an unnamed page adds an Index entry)
A label of the link's own, stored in links.ini
owner_questions.recommended: The target page's Index name (renaming renames that page; naming an unnamed page adds an Index entry)
owner_questions.why: The brief calls the hotbar's entries 'index entries'. Per-link labels would need UTF-8 in links.ini and would drift from the Index and the PDF outline. The button says 'Name page 20...' so adding a section is never a surprise.

owner_questions.question: Undo after a smart shape snaps: how many steps?
options: Two: the first brings back the hand-drawn stroke, the second removes it
One: undo removes the shape entirely
owner_questions.recommended: Two: the first brings back the hand-drawn stroke, the second removes it
owner_questions.why: The hold is its own moment, which keeps the owner's 'one gesture, one moment' rule. Returning the freehand stroke is the cheapest cure for an unwanted snap, and it matches iPadOS.

owner_questions.question: Where does the Shapes toggle go?
options: A 12th panel button directly under the eraser
The last panel button, after Library
Only in the tool picker's ink row (no panel change)
owner_questions.recommended: A 12th panel button directly under the eraser
owner_questions.why: It is a pen-behaviour toggle and belongs with the eraser. The scenario churn is absorbed by first converting scenarios to symbolic panel taps (step 13). Sideways with 4 pins it costs about 1% of the panel's scale.

owner_questions.question: Which shapes in the first release?
