options: Line, rectangle/square/diamond, triangle, circle/ellipse; arrows, polylines, arcs and grid snapping in a follow-up
The same plus single-stroke arrows now
Lines and rectangles only, to start
owner_questions.recommended: Line, rectangle/square/diamond, triangle, circle/ellipse; arrows, polylines, arcs and grid snapping in a follow-up
owner_questions.why: These four have measured recognition of 94-100% with zero false previews on the owner's writing. Arrows add a corner pattern that resembles handwriting (a 'v' after a line) and need their own negative corpus first.

owner_questions.question: Should any gestures besides the two navigational ones be bound by default?
options: No: everything else starts unbound and one recording in Gestures binds it
Two-finger left/right = next/previous page
Two-finger tap = undo, three-finger tap = redo
owner_questions.recommended: No: everything else starts unbound and one recording in Gestures binds it
owner_questions.why: Zero accidental input is the priority. next-page on the last page adds a page, and three-finger support is unknown until the device log. The Gestures sheet makes binding a single tap plus the gesture.

owner_questions.question: How does the Index map open?
options: Global, centred and zoomed on the open page, remembering the last mode per notebook
Local (the open page and two links deep) by default
Always global at fit
owner_questions.recommended: Global, centred and zoomed on the open page, remembering the last mode per notebook
owner_questions.why: It shows where the page sits in the whole notebook, which is what the owner asked for (all pages as dots), while the open page and its neighbours stay readable. Local is one tap away and is instant.

owner_questions.question: Which pages are dots on the map?
options: Named pages, linked pages and the open page; unnamed unlinked pages behind 'All pages' in the tray
Every page, always
owner_questions.recommended: Named pages, linked pages and the open page; unnamed unlinked pages behind 'All pages' in the tray
owner_questions.why: A 2000-page notebook would otherwise be a cloud of identical hollow rings that costs seconds to draw on e-ink. Orphans stay visible (hollow, smaller, in their own tray) and countable.

owner_questions.question: Should the hotbar also list backlinks (pages that link here)?
options: No: the map's card shows links in and out
A second tab in the hotbar ('Linked here')
owner_questions.recommended: No: the map's card shows links in and out
owner_questions.why: The brief asks for the links on this page. A tab doubles the card's states and refreshes, and backlinks are one tap away in the map. It can be added later at no format cost (one O(nlinks) pass).

owner_questions.question: What does the existing 'index' action do once the map exists?
options: It keeps opening the Index list; a new 'index-map' action opens the map
'index' opens the map
owner_questions.recommended: It keeps opening the Index list; a new 'index-map' action opens the map
owner_questions.why: 'index' has been in shortcuts.ini since 1.2.0. Changing its meaning silently changes what existing bindings do.

owner_questions.question: Should the pen plan's pen.ini and its gesture-first Pen sheet fold into gestures.ini and the action-first Gestures sheet?
options: Yes: one file, one binding rule, one sheet for touch and pen
Keep them separate
owner_questions.recommended: Yes: one file, one binding rule, one sheet for touch and pen
owner_questions.why: Both are unreleased. Two files with two binding rules would confuse, and the owner asked for one place where anything the controller can do is assigned. The pen's hold-while-writing cycler stays a Settings row.

owner_questions.question: How soon after writing may a two-finger gesture be accepted?
options: Rejected while the pen hovers; accepted 300 ms after it leaves if the fingers are 40 mm from the last pen point (first build)
Also accepted while the pen hovers, if the fingers are 60 mm from it (after the device log confirms hover tracking and palm sizes)
Today's rule: no touch for 1 s after the pen leaves
owner_questions.recommended: Rejected while the pen hovers; accepted 300 ms after it leaves if the fingers are 40 mm from the last pen point (first build)
owner_questions.why: 'Write, lift, swipe up' must feel instant, but a resting writing hand must never fire anything. The spatial hover rule depends on data that only the step-1 log can give.

owner_questions.question: Should the link dialog keep 'Change where it goes' and 'Redraw the area' beside Rename and Delete?
options: Keep all four
Rename and Delete only, as in the ruling's minimum
owner_questions.recommended: Keep all four
owner_questions.why: Areas are invisible, so Redraw is the only way to fix a migrated or badly drawn area without deleting the link. Change where it goes replaces today's hold-to-retarget, which otherwise disappears.

risks: The pen-near rule can make the headline gesture feel broken. 'Write, lift, swipe up' starts inside today's 1 s lockout, and often with the pen still hovering. Mitigation: the step-1 device log, the conservative 300 ms + 40 mm rule first, then the spatial hover rule, and a one-time-per-session hint when a swipe is refused only because of the pen.

The panel's slot count, TOUCH_MAJOR range and palm flagging are unknown. Three-finger gestures and the palm-size guard are gated on the step-1 log; until then the guard only logs and the three-finger rows stay hidden.

Sideways and zoomed views pan with two fingers, so navigation there needs edge bands or the scroll limit, which is harder to teach than 'anywhere'. Mitigation: the Gestures sheet's rows, the one-time hint, and the hotbar's other entries (the 'links' action, the page-chip hold).

Peek renders of up to 1.2 s on dense pages break 'instant'. Mitigation: the cached origin makes Back immediate, recent targets are cached, and prefetch can follow. Many GL16 peeks build up ghosting; a cancel after 3 peeks uses GC16, and the commit always does.

The 12th panel button shifts every button below the eraser in about 83 scenario files, and sideways with 4 pins the panel shrinks to about 0.99. Mitigation: step 13 converts scenarios to symbolic panel taps first; test_panel covers the fits.

Smart shapes in slow, deliberate hands can show a preview and then revert: two DU frames of a region, which can leave dithering on gray or image paper until the settle. The negative corpus is small (47 strokes) and its timestamps are read-time. Mitigation: the gates, the burst gate, an adjustable hold, the shape-log tuning on the device, and the toggle.

History grows two in-memory kinds (ACT_REPLACE and ACT_LINK). Both locate strokes by pointer, as today, and ACT_LINK must survive a failed save. Mitigation: a new test_history.c, and the rule that a failed save drops the step and reloads nav from disk.

The owner's device runs f9d13f5. If it is ever used again after migration, it keeps working only while area lines total under 16 KiB (about 430 links), and it refuses (never overwrites) a bigger file. Area-only links are inert there. This is documented in FORMAT.md's moving-between-versions table.

Area-only links are invisible in every other reader (older versions, the share page, Live view's page layer). Only the PDF carries them, as invisible /Link annotations. An owner who wants a visible cue must draw a border; the eye helps only on the device.
Smallest-wins replaces last-drawn-wins, so beta.5 links with overlapping boxes may resolve differently after the update. Acceptable while beta.5 is unreleased; covered by test_nav.

The map's layout differs between arm64 (the simulator) and armv7 (the Kindle) because of FMA and libm. Tests assert invariants only, and positions persist in graph.ini. A queued PDF mirror delays a full layout in bgjob's single queue, so the seed layout stays on screen meanwhile.
Rewriting canvas_line_aa touches every Gothic UI drawing. It must be bit-identical (a 300-edge comparison test plus the golden shots), or the UI changes everywhere.

Kindle RAM headroom is not measured: the peek cache, the map's offscreen canvas and the shape preview copy add up to about 23 MB at worst. Every allocation has a fallback that renders the same pixels more slowly.

Changing Settings' bottom row breaks 10 scenario taps; y_all_screens.qs:631 would land on Gestures instead of Controller. The taps are updated in the same step, with test_i18n checking the label widths.
Any new keyboard surface that bypasses the shared keyboard host brings the Index keyboard's lag back. The kb.draws probe is asserted in every scenario that types.
Swallowing the tap outside the hotbar also swallows taps on the panel. That is consistent with the paper sheet, but the owner may expect the panel to stay live; the tap still commits.

scores.notes:
Covers the whole brief and both rulings, and is the most coherent as a GUI.

Strengths:
- Every gesture has a labelled twin.
- Link mode shows a banner with Cancel.
- The link card sits beside the area with the page in view.
- One-step snap undo, which matches the owner's one-gesture-one-moment rule.
- Never inverts a panel toggle. On the panel, BTN_SELECTED means the current tool (editor.c:266).
- Navigational defaults that follow the brief: 2-down Pages, 2-up bar, 2-left/right page turns.
- shape-hold is assignable.
- The Index map shows every page, with tiered orphans.

Bends:
- X, two fingers down, the Links button and Close menu all keep the peeked page ('closing keeps what you see'). That empties the owner's explicit 'TAP OUTSIDE to confirm': there is no cancel except Back.
- Chips are per link, not per Index entry.
- The eye's off state is an outline 'eye-off' glyph, not dimmed.
- The dotted box stays 4 s after a link is made. The ruling allows it only while the link is being made.
- The gestures on/off toggle is not an action, against 'everything with a toggle'.

Internal slips:
- It says 18 new actions but lists 22.
- One-finger swipes are 'not in v1' in the vocabulary but 'assignable, unbound' in its owner question.

Cost:
- A 13-button panel, scaled to 0.94 sideways with 4 pins.
- Area-weighted FULL promotion changes ghosting for all writing, not only the hotbar.
- The Find sheet's keyboard can cover a freshly drawn area that sits low on the page.

The closest reading of the owner's literal words.

Where it matches the brief:
- Hotbar entries are Index entries (xN when several links go to one target).
- 'Outside stays, the hotbar's close goes back', and the header teaches it: 'Tap the page to stay'.
- The eye is literally dimmed when off.
- The Index button opens a graph titled 'Index' with Graph | List chips: 'a more detailed view of the index'.
- Every page is a dot. Unlinked unnamed pages cluster around their section's named page, as in Navi.
- Prefetch plus a 3-entry canvas LRU makes jumps 'instant'.
- Link to... offers Recent targets and docks at the top when the area is low on the screen.
- The back list makes hopping safe.
- Idle migration finishes the beta.5 rewrite, and Copy page copies links.
- One-step snap undo. Gestures do nothing while a keyboard is open.

Bends:
- A 'Linking here' backlinks section added to a hotbar the owner said should 'simply show' this page's entries.
- xN Delete in the bar removes every link to that target ('delete any link').
- Its recommended defaults (two-finger tap = undo, three-finger tap = redo) are not navigational and risk resting-hand accidents.
- The 'Keep the outline as ink' chip stretches ruling 1.
- shape_grid, link_keep_ink and the hold time are settings with no action.

Risks:
- Panel buttons stay live during a peek (commit, then act) while every other outside tap is swallowed.
- Biggest scope: 23 steps, a back list, Recent targets, idle page reads, section springs, about 16 MB of caches.
- Area-weighted FULL promotion.
- 19 owner questions, against a synthesis limit of 8.

The safest engineering plan.

Strengths:
- Device instrumentation before any thresholds are set.
- Symbolic panel taps are added before the panel grows.
- Keeps the every-30th FULL rule.
- input_pump reads touch.
- Resting-contact and 'hand moved' guards.
- Conservative pen-near staging.
- Separate area. lines keep the device's f9d13f5 build fully compatible.
- The lasso is a dashed UI overlay, never ink, which honours ruling 1 most cleanly.
- 'Redraw the area' is genuinely needed once areas are invisible.
- Peeks never touch notebook.ini.
- Every failure state is spoken.

Where it bends the brief:
- No prefetch in v1, so the first jump to a dense or PDF page takes up to 1.2 s ('tap to instantly jump').
- The map hides unnamed unlinked pages behind 'All pages' ('all pages ... as dots').
- It recommends two-step undo after a snap, against the owner's documented one-gesture-one-moment rule.
- The v1 shape set is minimal: no arrows or grid ('whatever else', 'more aware').
- Only two default gestures.
- Pressing a chip outlines the area even with the eye off (a minor stretch of ruling 1).
- The hold time is not assignable.
- The page-chip hold that opens the hotbar is invisible.

UX and consistency defects:
- Per-direction can_pan means a two-finger drag that starts at the scroll limit opens Pages or the hotbar by surprise (overscroll).
- The Shapes panel button is BTN_SELECTED (inverted) while on. On the panel, inverted means the current tool, and shapes are on by default, so an always-black button sits right under the eraser.

judges.winner: A (calm and discoverable), narrowly over B. A is the most coherent, discoverable GUI in Grimoire's existing language. Its main bend, that closing the bar keeps the peeked page, is a small fix: graft B's confirm/cancel semantics. B is the most literal reading of the brief but carries the most scope and accident risk. C should supply the engineering order and the input safety.
best_ideas_to_graft: From B: the hotbar rule 'tap outside stays; the bar's own close (X, mirror swipe, its action, Close menu, Back) returns to the origin page', with the peek header 'Showing <name>. Tap the page to stay.' This matches the owner's 'TAP OUTSIDE to confirm'.
From B: a dimmed eye when off, as the owner literally asked ('dims off by default'). Draw the dimmed glyph inside a normal frame so it does not read as BTN_DISABLED gray.

From B: the Index button opens a view titled 'Index' with Graph | List chips, so the graph IS 'a more detailed view of the index'. Every page is a dot, and unlinked unnamed pages cluster near their section's named page (Navi's parent containment).
From B: Link to... shows Recent targets first and docks at the TOP when the new area sits in the lower part of the screen, so the area stays visible. Search opens only on tap.
From B: prefetch link targets in idle bands (input drained, aborted at first contact) so peeks are actually instant. C ships with no prefetch.

From B: a back list plus a go-back action (bindable, not default-bound unless the owner agrees); Copy page copies the page's links; gestures are ignored while any keyboard is open; a finger commits on lift, so a second landing finger becomes a gesture instead.
From B: idle migration of legacy beta.5 links (one page per idle tick, pumped), so the owner's notebooks finish migrating instead of staying half-legacy indefinitely.

From C: step 1 is a device touch log (slot count, TOUCH_MAJOR, palm flags, hover range) before any gesture threshold is frozen; three-finger gestures stay hidden until it shows the panel supports them.
From C: convert scenarios to symbolic 'tap panel NAME' BEFORE the panel grows; keep the every-30th FULL rule unless device testing proves the area-weighted rule does not worsen writing ghosting.

From C: input_pump also reads touch into touchgest; resting-contact (grip/palm) exclusion with a 'hand moved' reject; conservative pen-near staging (reject while hovering, accept 300 ms after the pen leaves at 40 mm or more), with the spatial hover rule added after the log.

From C: 'Redraw the area' in the link card, since an invisible area cannot otherwise be fixed. Also the lasso as a dashed UI overlay that never touches page_canvas, the 64-link refusal toast, and spoken reasons for every refusal.
From C: separate area.<pid>=<seed>,x,y,w,h lines leave link. lines byte-identical for the device's f9d13f5 build. Weigh this against A/B's inline form and pick one.

From A: keep its never-inverted Shapes panel glyph (filled when on, outline plus slash when off), one-step snap undo, per-link numbering that matches the eye's tags, the shape-hold action, and the 'not bindable to touch' list. Offer the Links panel button only as an owner question.
From A/B: per-axis 'can the view scroll' (not C's per-direction rule), so a drag that starts at the scroll limit pans nowhere rather than opening Pages by surprise.
flaws_to_fix: A: X, two fingers down, the Links button and Close menu all KEEP the peeked page, so 'tap outside to confirm' confirms nothing. Make the bar's own closes cancel back to the origin (B/C).

A: its action count says 18 new names but lists 22; one-finger swipes are 'not in v1' in its vocabulary but 'assignable, unbound' in its owner question; the gestures on/off toggle is missing from the registry despite 'everything with a toggle'.
A: the dotted box stays 4 s after a link is made. Ruling 1 allows the area to show only while being made, with the eye on, or on a long press. End it when the target is picked.
A: the Find sheet's keyboard in pick mode can hide a freshly drawn area low on the page. Dock it at the top for low areas (B).
A and B: area-weighted FULL promotion changes cleanup flashes for ALL writing, not only the hotbar and keyboard. Keep the existing rule, or exempt only small UI rects, until it is device-tested.

B: its recommended defaults (two-finger tap = undo, three-finger tap = redo) contradict 'by default the gesture system will serve the user navigationally' and invite resting-hand accidents. Ship them unbound, as suggestions in the sheet (A).
B: panel buttons stay live during a peek (commit, then act) while every other outside tap is swallowed. Pick one rule: a panel tap during a peek commits and is swallowed (paper-sheet precedent).
B: the 'Linking here' backlinks section makes the hotbar less 'simple'. Use A's header chip ('N pages link here', opening the map) or C's map card instead.

B: an xN entry's Delete removes every link to that target, so the hotbar cannot delete 'any link' individually. Either keep per-link chips with the target name, or let the card list the N areas to delete one.
B: 19 owner questions, over the synthesis limit of 8; settings such as shape_grid and link_keep_ink have no actions.
C: per-direction can_pan turns a two-finger drag that starts at the scroll limit into a Pages or hotbar swipe (the overscroll surprise A rejected). Use per-axis.

C: the Shapes panel button is BTN_SELECTED (inverted) while on. On the panel, inverted means the current tool (editor.c:266), and shapes are on by default, so an always-black button sits under the eraser.
C: no prefetch, so first peeks take up to 1.2 s on dense or PDF pages ('instantly jump').
C: it recommends two-step undo after a snap, against the owner's documented one-gesture-one-moment undo rule. Default to one step.

C: the Index map hides unnamed unlinked pages by default. The brief asks for all pages as dots, with orphans visually progressive. Show them small and hollow (B's section clustering) and collapse only past a threshold.
C: the hotbar's only discoverable entry besides the gesture is an invisible page-chip hold. Pair it with a visible entry (A's Links button, or the Index tab).

All: each card and sheet must set toast_floor after compose, and the hotbar must be added to sheet_open/front_menu so a gesture or shortcut never acts behind a peek. A, B and C state this with different completeness; make it one checklist item.
brief_requirements_missed: ALL THREE: 'you would record a gesture to get whatever you want' is read as picking from a fixed gesture vocabulary. Free-form gestures are ruled out without asking the owner. The choice is defensible on e-ink, but it needs one owner question or an explicit line in the Gestures sheet.
A: 'TAP OUTSIDE THE HOTBAR to confirm you want to work in the new page' is diluted, because every other close also keeps the peeked page.
A and C: the hotbar lists one chip per link, not 'the index entries that are linked to in that particular page'. Two links to one entry show as two rows (B groups them).
A and C: the eye 'dims off by default', but both draw an outline eye-off glyph rather than a dimmed eye (B is literal).

A: the gestures on/off master switch is a toggle that cannot be assigned. B: shape_grid, link_keep_ink and the shape hold have no action. C: the shape hold has no action. NONE makes the sleep-screen mode assignable ('everything with a toggle or important setting').
B: the hotbar adds a backlinks section beyond 'simply show' this page's entries.
B: from the hotbar, 'delete any link' deletes all xN links to the target.
B: recommended non-navigational defaults (two-finger tap = undo, three-finger tap = redo) bend 'by default ... navigationally'.
B: the 'Keep the outline as ink' chip stretches ruling 1 ('making a link no longer leaves ink'), though it is off by default and asked.
C: 'tap to instantly jump' is bent: no prefetch, so a first peek can take up to 1.2 s.
C: 'all pages ... as dots' is bent: unnamed unlinked pages are hidden behind 'All pages' by default.
C: 'whatever else' and 'more aware' are thin in v1: no arrows, and grid snapping is deferred.
C: two-step undo after a snap is recommended against the owner's one-gesture-one-moment rule.
A: the area stays visible for 4 s after linking, beyond ruling 1's 'shown only ... while the link is being made'.
C: pressing a chip outlines the area with the eye off, a minor stretch of ruling 1's 'shown only when the eye toggle is on'. Ruling 2 covers the long press, not the plain press.
Ruling 2 ('a small dialog beside it'): all three comply. A's card is the largest (840x724) and is placed below first. B places it to the right first, the most literal 'beside'.

scores.notes:
Checked against 89893aa. What holds up: the touch defects it fixes first are real. input_evdev.c:477 and :764 end a finger with a real IN_TOUCH_UP at its last position. drain() has no SYN_DROPPED handling. The busy flag at :1540 ignores suppressed contacts. touch_frame takes the two lowest slots. Its claim about f9d13f5 reading the long link line is exact: link_parse rejects a target of 16 bytes or more, so the line is carried, and past NAV_UNKNOWN_MAX (16 KiB) each_line fails and the whole file goes read-only. A short line becomes an inert target, since target_page rejects ','. My panel_fit recomputation gives 13 buttons, sideways, 4 pins, scale 0.93 with space 0.5; the spec says 0.94, close. Settings formula: (1640-300-380-120)/3 = 280. The upright hotbar arithmetic fits (2x878+24 = 1780 = 1820-40). Axis-level can_pan, so overscroll never navigates, is the right call.

What breaks:
(1) Hotbar tap outside commits at finger DOWN, swallowed in the paper-sheet style (editor.c:2412-2421). The first finger of a two-finger swipe down closes the bar there. The IN_GESTURE that arrives at lift then finds no bar and maps touch.2.down to pages: the Pages view opens with a GC16.
(2) Default touch.2.left = next-page is 'clamped, never creates a page', but the dispatcher's next-page is P_NEXT, which adds a page on the last page (editor.c, the 'next page on the last page adds one' branch). That needs a separate action or a source flag.
(3) The area-weighted FULL rule, 'under 25% never promoted', also stops the every-30th cleanup that writing's GL16 settles get today (app.c:931 counts every UI flush). Ghosting under writing would then only clear at page turns.
(4) Pen-near relaxation assumes 'hover_learn always on' gives a hover point. raw_hover returns false until pensync_hover_learn has learned the mapping from contact frames, so the 60 mm hover rule has no data at first.
(5) Pen down outside the bar commits and draws. A GL16 or GC16 still on the panel makes quiet_now false, so that stroke falls off MTK pen mode, and the peek ghosting gets no GC16.
(6) The PM_* tag value for legacy sim pinch events (value 0) is unspecified.

The tile backup works but is complex. 13 panel buttons plus 20 steps is a large scope.

Best interaction engineering of the three on the hotbar:
- A finger commits on LIFT, so a second finger landing becomes the gesture. Only this spec avoids the commit-then-open-Pages trap.
- The panel stays live and commits first.
- Copy page now copies area links. Without that, ink-free links vanish from copies silently; the other specs miss it.
- scrolls_v = taller AND pinch_zoom on. That matches pinch() returning early with pinch_zoom off (editor.c:2296): with it off, nothing pans, so swipes work everywhere. The other specs leave a dead PAN class there.

What breaks:
(1) The event contract 'IN_PINCH_MOVE.value 0 = WAIT, the editor obeys the value' contradicts 'pinch and tap keep working unchanged'. The legacy runner pinch (sim_sdl.c ~735-751) and the window's mouse-wheel pinch push value 0, so the editor would never zoom. k_pinch_gate, f_batch2, z_4_erase_zoom_rotate and others break.
(2) Idle migration reads unvisited pages with store_read_page in editor_tick, 'pumped'. store_read_page has no work_pump; only page_render pumps (page.c:244-268). A dense page read on the UI thread can overrun the 120-175 ms pen buffer.
(3) Pen-near relaxation while the pen HOVERS uses only the last contact point (50 mm) with an 8-70 mm finger window. Palm heel plus pinky sliding to the next line can pass as 'two down' and open Pages. It also recommends two-finger tap = undo as a default.
(4) Area-weighted FULL changes ghost cleanup under writing (settles count today).
(5) No symbolic panel taps: the 12th button means re-measuring about 44 scenario files by hand.
(6) The graph lays out every page, including about 2000 unlinked ones on section springs, so the bgjob runs on most opens of big notebooks.

Also unconfirmed: the 3-entry canvas LRU plus band prefetch, a back list and a 'keep outline as ink' chip. The chip is a stretch against ruling 1. The ×N grouping is consistent and explained. Biggest scope of the three (23 steps).

The most correct against the code:
- links.ini gains separate area.<pid>= lines and leaves link. lines byte-identical. On f9d13f5, link lines read unchanged and area lines are carried until about 16 KiB, which matches carry() and NAV_UNKNOWN_MAX. A link line without ink is just dormant there.
- input_pump also drains touch. Today only input_poll reads touch (:1561), so a 1.2 s render can overflow the inferred 512-1024-event buffer; kernel stamps alone do not fix that.
- It keeps the every-30th promotion, rightly noting that writing settles count.
- Symbolic 'tap panel NAME' scenarios are converted BEFORE the 12th button (44 of 131 scenarios tap raw coordinates).
- The pen rule is evidence-first and conservative: reject while hovering, accept 300 ms after the pen leaves if fingers are at least 40 mm from its last contact. It correctly sees that hover needs learned data.
- Resting contacts are generalized beyond edges.
- The shape preview uses draw_page(region): simpler than a tile backup and live==render by construction, at the cost of a pumped region render.
- A probe for the longest unpumped stretch, and the map limited to named and linked nodes, keep cost bounded.

What breaks:
(1) The same hotbar trap as spec 1. Tap outside commits on down (OWN_MODAL), and the mirror gesture '2-down cancels to origin' starts with a finger on the page. That commits instead (GC16), then the gesture maps to pages.
(2) PINCH_BEGIN is sent only at classification, so pinch()'s own 10%/70 px dead zone (editor.c:2311-2319) re-applies from that point: a double dead zone and sticky zoom. The editor must skip it for TG_ZOOM and TG_PAN, which is not stated.
(3) can_pan is per DIRECTION, so a drag starting at a scroll limit becomes a swipe ('So does a swipe in a direction the page cannot scroll'). Overscroll opens Pages, an accident path.
(4) The sideways hotbar overflows: 3x800+2x16 = 2432 > 2440-48 = 2392. The height formula is off too (rows=1 gives 468, not 472).
(5) P_SHAPES uses BTN_SELECTED while on, and on is the default. On this panel inverted means the current tool (tool_style), so the button would read as permanently selected.
(6) Two-step shape undo goes against the owner's one-gesture-one-moment rule (it is asked as a question).
(7) Unnamed orphans are hidden behind 'All pages' (a partial reading of 'all pages as dots').
(8) Copy page loses area links (not addressed).

best_ideas_to_graft: From spec 2: commit the hotbar on finger LIFT, not on down. A second finger landing cancels the pending commit and the touch becomes a gesture. This fixes the trap in specs 1 and 3 where the first finger of a two-finger close swipe commits and the gesture then opens Pages.

From spec 2: scrolls_v/h = the view is larger than the screen AND pinch_zoom is on. This matches pinch() returning early when pinch zoom is off (editor.c:2296), so with it off every two-finger straight drag is a swipe and no gesture is left dead.
From spec 2: Copy page copies the page's links (same seeds, areas and targets, new pid). Ink-free links would otherwise vanish from copies silently.
From spec 1: can_pan per AXIS, not per direction, so a drag at a scroll limit never navigates. Navigation from a view that can scroll comes only from the edge bands.

From spec 1: never invert the Shapes panel button, because inverted means the current tool. Show the filled glyph when on and the outline glyph with a slash when off, and use the labelled picker row for the words.
From spec 3: separate area.<pid>=<seed>,x,y,w,h lines, leaving link. lines byte-identical, so the owner's f9d13f5 device still reads every link line.
From spec 3: input_pump also drains touch into touchgest (O(1) per frame), so 1.2 s renders cannot overflow the touch evdev buffer. Stamp each frame with SYN_REPORT's kernel time.
From spec 3: keep the every-30th FULL promotion. Writing's GL16 settles count toward it, so an area-weighted rule would change ghost cleanup under writing.
From spec 3: convert scenario panel taps to a symbolic 'tap panel NAME' (validated by probing the hit under each old coordinate) before PANEL_BUTTONS grows.

From spec 3: step 1 is device instrumentation (slot count, TOUCH_MAJOR, palm flags, landing gaps), and the conservative pen rule ships until the log is read: reject while the pen hovers; 300 ms + 40 mm after it leaves.
From spec 3: a sim probe for the longest unpumped main-thread stretch, asserted under 100 ms in the big-notebook map scenario.

From spec 1: the Find sheet. Digits jump to a page; letters run an accent-folded name search through an exported cmp_name. Add New page... (append, then name it) as a link target, giving wiki-style links that create Index entries.
From spec 2 and spec 3: the pen touching outside the hotbar commits and the stroke is swallowed, so the close refresh never races MTK pen mode.

Shape preview: start with spec 3's draw_page(region) plus a region copy, which is simple and live==render by construction. Add spec 1/2's under-ink tile backup later only if the device log shows the region render is too slow.
flaws_to_fix: Specs 1 and 3: the hotbar's tap-outside commit fires on finger DOWN (the paper-sheet pattern). Their two-finger close swipe begins with that finger, so the bar commits and closes, and the IN_GESTURE at lift maps touch.2.down to 'pages': the Pages view opens with a GC16. Commit on lift instead, and cancel the pending commit when a second finger lands.

Spec 2: IN_PINCH_MOVE.value 0 = WAIT, with 'the editor obeys the value'. The legacy runner 'pinch' and the sim's mouse-wheel pinch push value 0, so the editor would never zoom and every pinch scenario fails. Make 0 mean 'legacy, decide yourself', or route the legacy commands through touchgest.

Spec 3: PINCH_BEGIN is emitted only at classification, so pinch()'s own 10%/70 px dead zone (editor.c:2311-2319) applies a second time from that point. When touchgest has already committed, the editor must skip its dead zone (TG_ZOOM/TG_PAN).
Spec 3: can_pan per direction turns a drag that starts at a scroll limit into a swipe, so overscroll opens Pages. Use axis-level can_pan plus the edge bands.

Specs 1 and 2: area-weighted FULL promotion (spec 1: refreshes under 25% of the screen are never promoted) removes the periodic GC16 cleanup that stroke settles get today: app.c:931 counts every GL16 flush. Keep the current rule, or exempt only overlay rects and keep counting the settles.

Spec 2: idle migration reads unvisited pages with store_read_page in editor_tick and calls that 'pumped'. store_read_page has no work_pump; only page_render pumps. Migrate lazily on load, or in a bgjob child.

Spec 1: touch.2.left = next-page is described as 'clamped, never creates a page', but the dispatcher's next-page is P_NEXT, which adds a page on the last page. Define a separate action, or a per-source flag.

Spec 1: the pen touching outside the bar commits AND draws. A GL16 or GC16 still in flight keeps that stroke off MTK pen mode, and the peek ghosting gets no GC16. Swallow the stroke as specs 2 and 3 do.

Spec 1: relaxing the pen-near rule by hover distance assumes a hover point exists. raw_hover() returns false until pensync_hover_learn has learned the mapping from contact frames, so stage it as spec 3 does.

Spec 2: while the pen hovers, the pen-near relaxation checks distance only from the last contact (50 mm), with an 8-70 mm finger window. A writing hand sliding to the next line (palm heel plus pinky moving in parallel at least 20 mm) can pass as two fingers down and open Pages. It also recommends two-finger tap = Undo as a default.

All three specs: the long-press dotted border is presented as one DU rect covering the area, which dithers the gray ink inside it until some GL16 lands. Present only the four border strips with DU, and settle them with GL16 when the card closes.
Spec 3: the sideways hotbar chips overflow: 3 x 800 + 2 x 16 = 2432 against 2440 - 48 = 2392. The height formula is also off by 4 px.
Spec 3: P_SHAPES uses BTN_SELECTED while on, and on is the default. Inverted means the current tool on this panel (tool_style), so the button reads as a permanently selected tool.

Specs 1 and 2: 'a failed save leaves history unchanged' after an ACT_LINK undo is not what happens: history_undo has already moved the action to the redo stack. It must be pushed back explicitly, or dropped as spec 3 does.
Specs 1 and 3: Copy page silently loses area-only links. Copy them to the new pid, or say so.

All three specs: link migration marks links.ini dirty 'for the next save_page'. If save_page skips unchanged pages, the areas are never written. Flush dirty links when leaving the page and the notebook.
Spec 2: no symbolic panel taps. The 12th button forces re-measuring the 44 scenario files that tap raw coordinates.

Spec 2: the graph lays out every page, about 2000 nodes in a big notebook, with section springs, so most opens of big notebooks run the bgjob. Exclude unnamed unlinked pages from the forces, as specs 1 and 3 do.
brief_requirements_missed: Spec 1: 'closing keeps what you see' (✕, two fingers down and the Links button all keep the peeked page). That empties the brief's 'TAP OUTSIDE THE HOTBAR to confirm you want to work in the new page' of meaning, because every close confirms.
Spec 3: the Index map hides unnamed pages with no links behind 'All pages', showing only a count. The brief asks for all pages as dots, with orphans drawn progressively smaller or hollow.

Spec 3: the Shapes button's inverted 'selected' look, together with two-step undo, cuts against the owner's one-gesture-one-moment rule. It is asked as a question rather than designed to the owner's known rule.

Spec 2: the 'Keep the outline as ink' chip pulls against ruling 1 ('making a link no longer leaves ink'), even off by default. Its recommended extra defaults (two-finger tap Undo, three-finger tap Redo, two fingers right = Back, pen double-click = Links) go beyond 'by default the gesture system will serve the user navigationally'.

Specs 1 and 3: the two-finger close swipe on the hotbar does not work as specified (it commits, then opens Pages), so 'long press / tap / tap outside to confirm' plus the gesture closes do not behave as the brief's smooth flow intends.

All three: 'everything with a toggle or important setting can be assigned' is met through the shared registry, but all three deliberately exclude language, calibration and the shortcuts toggle. That is defensible, but the owner should be told.

final.one_paragraph: After this work, two fingers moved upward on the page bring up a Links bar along the bottom. It lists the Index entries that this page links to, numbered in reading order. Tap an entry and the page above the bar turns into that page straight away, with no flash. Tap the page to stay there, or close the bar to go back to where you started. Hold an entry, or hold a finger on a link on the page, and a dotted border shows exactly what counts as tappable. A small card opens next to it with Rename, Change where it goes, Redraw the area and Delete link, and the page stays in view the whole time. Making a link no longer leaves ink. You circle the words, a dashed line follows the pen but is never ink, and you pick where it goes from Recent targets or the Index, or make a new page and name it. Your existing beta.5 links keep working: each one's circle becomes its tappable area the first time its page opens, and the circle stays on the page as ordinary ink. Two fingers moved down open the Pages view, and two fingers to the left or right turn the page. Settings gets a Gestures button between Controller and Updates: tap an action, do the gesture, and if Grimoire refuses it, it says why. Every toggle and important setting becomes an action you can bind to a gesture, a key, a controller button, and later the pen's button. Smart shapes snap a box, circle, triangle or line only when you hold the pen still and the shape really is one. Moving on brings your own line back, and one Undo removes the shape. The Index button opens a map of the whole notebook as dots. Well-linked pages are solid, lightly linked ones are dithered, and unlinked pages are small hollow rings beside their section. It ships in seven Kindle builds, and you test each one. The first fixes the touch input and records how your panel behaves. The second brings gestures and the Links bar, then come ink-free links with the long-press card, then Settings > Gestures, then Smart shapes, then the map, and last the pen-button gestures.

plan.experience:
Upright unless said otherwise. Sizes are px at 300 dpi (11.8 px per mm); text is 44 px, titles 64 px, small text 34 px. [Pn] names the build that brings each part.

0. AFTER THE UPDATE [P2]
- The first time a notebook opens, one two-line toast shows for 6 s: 'New: two fingers up show this page's links. Two fingers down show all pages.' / 'Novedad: dos dedos hacia arriba muestran los enlaces de esta página; hacia abajo, todas las páginas.' This is settings.ini hints bit 0.
- The panel has a new Links button under Next: a chain glyph (question 7). A 7 px solid dot in its corner means this page has links. P5 adds a Shapes button under the eraser.

1. OPENING THE LINKS BAR [P2]
- Open it with two fingers up anywhere on the upright, fitted page, with the Links button, or with the 'links' action from a key, a controller button, or later a pen button.
- When the fingers lift, a card rises from the bottom in one GL16 refresh: about 0.35 s, no flash.
- Header: 'Links on this page (3)' / 'Enlaces de esta página (3)', with an X at the right.
- Below the header: numbered chips in reading order, one per Index entry this page links to (question 1). For example: '1 Meeting notes   p. 12', '2 Page 20   p. 20', '3 The Index'.
  - Two links to the same entry show once, marked '×2'.
  - The eye draws the same numbers on the page.
- Bottom row, four labelled buttons: Go to (a magnifier), New link (a chain with a plus), Areas (an eye, dimmed while off) and Index (three bubbles).
- On an empty page: 'No links on this page yet.' / 'Esta página aún no tiene enlaces.', with New link shown as the main, inverted button.
- The first 3 times, the header adds a hint: 'Tap a link to look. Tap the page to stay.'

2. HOPPING (PEEK) [P2]
- Tap chip 1. It inverts at once (DU) and the page above the bar becomes page 12, with a GL16 of that area only.
  - About 0.4 s, because it was rendered in the background while you looked.
  - The first time, a dense or PDF page can take up to 1.2 s; the inverted chip shows the wait.
  - The panel's page chip shows 12.
- The header becomes '‹ Page 3   Showing Meeting notes. Tap the page to stay.' with the X.
- The chips are still page 3's links, so tapping chip 2 shows page 20 instead.
- To stay: tap the page above the bar with a finger. It counts when the finger lifts.
  - The bar closes and page 20 becomes the open page.
  - One GC16 flash marks the arrival and clears any ghosting from the peeks.
  - That tap does nothing else: it never follows a link or presses a panel button.
  - A pen touch there also stays, and its stroke is not drawn.
  - A tap on the panel also stays, and the button is not pressed.
- To go back:
  - '‹ Page 3' shows page 3 again and keeps the bar open.
  - X, two fingers down, the Links button again, Close menu or the Back key close the bar and return to page 3 exactly as you left it, zoom included.
  - That return is GL16, or GC16 after 3 or more peeks, to clear ghosting.
- Anything that acts on the page you see stays on it first: New link, Go to, Index, or another menu's button or key.
- Peeks never write notebook.ini. If the Kindle sleeps, powers off or crashes during a peek, the notebook reopens on page 3.

3. HOLDING A LINK (THE SECOND RULING) [P3]
- Hold a finger still on a link for 0.6 s.
  - A heavy dotted border appears around the link's area at once, in about 0.2 s. Only the four border strips are refreshed, by DU.
  - Then a small card opens beside the area by GL16: to the right if it fits, else left, below, above.
  - The notebook page stays in view.
- The card (780 x 666):
  - Title: 'Meeting notes · p. 12'.
  - Rename in the Index. For an unnamed page it reads 'Add page 20 to the Index...'. A link to The Index has no rename row.
  - Change where it goes...
  - Redraw the area
  - Delete link
- Rename: the keyboard opens over the page, with the card and the border still visible above it. Done shows 'Page 12 is in the Index as Meeting notes.'
- Change where it goes: Link to... opens with the current target marked.
- Redraw the area: you draw a new area for this same link.
- Delete link: 'Link deleted. Undo brings it back.' / 'Enlace borrado. Deshacer lo recupera.' A border you drew yourself is ink, and it stays.
- A tap outside closes the card and does nothing else.
- On a read-only page the card shows only the target, with the line 'This page is read-only.'
- In the bar, holding a chip for 0.6 s opens the same card, above the bar.
  - If you are peeking, the bar first returns to the page the links are on.
  - The entry's areas get the dotted border.
  - A '×2' entry offers 'Delete 2 links' and 'Change where they go', and adds the line 'To change one, hold it on the page.'

4. MAKING A LINK, WITHOUT INK [P3; in P2, New link still uses today's flow]
1. Tap New link in the bar, use the 'add-link' action, or tap 'Add a link' on the Index tab.
2. The bar folds into a 130 px strip at the bottom: 'Draw around what links.' / 'Rodea lo que enlaza.', with Cancel.
3. Circle the words with the pen. A dashed 4 px line follows the nib by DU. It is screen UI, never ink.
4. When you lift, the dashes become a dotted rectangle around the circle's box.
5. Link to... opens at the bottom, or at the top when your rectangle is in the lower part of the screen, so it stays visible.
   - Chips: New page..., The Index, up to 4 Recent targets, then the Index entries, paged.
   - Tool row: Search, Choose from the pages..., Cancel.
6. Tap 'Meeting notes'.
   - The toast says 'Linked to Meeting notes.'
   - The dotted rectangle goes away unless Areas is on.
   - The page looks exactly as it did before.
   - If you started from the bar, the bar comes back with the new entry.
   - One Undo removes the link.
Other outcomes:
- New page...: a keyboard over the page asks 'Name the new page'.
  - Done appends a page at the end of the notebook, so page numbers never move. It names the page, making it a new Index entry, and links to it. You stay where you are: 'Linked to the new page 53.'
  - Cancel makes no page.
- Too small (under 5 mm both ways): 'Too small for a link: draw around what links.' Link mode stays on.
- Cancel: 'No link made.'
- A refusal always says why: the page is read-only, links.ini cannot be read, or the page already has 64 links.

5. FOLLOWING
- A finger tap inside a link's area goes there with a GC16 flash, as today.
- Where areas are nested, the smallest one under the finger wins.
- The pen always writes, even on a link.

6. SEEING AREAS [P2]
- Areas, in the bar, draws a dashed outline and a numbered tag on every link area of the page. The numbers match the chips.
- The choice is remembered.
- The outlines are never drawn into the page, the PDF, the thumbnails or the sleep image.
- The first time, a tip: 'Dotted boxes show where a finger tap follows a link. They never print.'

7. VISIBLE BORDERS
A visible border is ink you draw yourself; Smart shapes make a clean box. It is never part of the link: erasing it keeps the link, and deleting the link keeps the border.

8. GO TO [P2]
- Open it from the bar's Go to, from 'Go to page...' in the Pages view, or with the 'go-to-page' action.
- A keyboard opens over the page, with the field 'Page number or name'.
  - Typing '12' puts 'Go to page 12' first.
  - Typing 'reu' lists 'Reunión': accents and case are ignored.
- Tapping a result goes there (GC16), and the page you left goes on the back list.

9. PAGES VIEW AND PAGE TURNS [P2]
- Two fingers down open the Pages view (GC16); two fingers up close it.
- Two fingers left or right turn the page (question 5). At the end of the notebook: 'This is the last page.' A gesture never adds a page; the panel's + still does.

10. SIDEWAYS OR ZOOMED IN [P2]
- Where the page can scroll, a two-finger drag in mid-screen pans as today, now without the zoom drifting.
- Navigation swipes start in an edge band: 25 mm at the top and bottom, 15 mm at the sides (question 4).
- The first time a drag scrolls instead of opening something, a tip: 'To open Pages or links here, start at the top or bottom edge.'

11. SMART SHAPES [P5]
- Draw a box and hold the nib still for 0.55 s. One DU frame shows a clean rectangle in the same pen and size.
- Lift to keep it. Move on instead and your own line comes back, and the stroke simply continues.
- Handwriting never snaps.
- One Undo removes the shape.
- The panel's Shapes button toggles the feature: a filled glyph when on, an outline with a slash when off, never inverted.
- The tool picker gets a row reading 'Smart shapes: On' and 'Hold: Normal'.

12. THE INDEX MAP [P6]
- Open it from the bar's Index button, from the Graph chip on the Index tab, or with the 'index-map' action. It fills the screen (GC16) and is titled 'Index', with a Graph | List switch.
- What it shows:
  - Every page is a dot.
  - The open page has a double ring, and named pages are labelled.
  - Well-linked pages are solid; less-linked ones are half or quarter dithered.
  - Unnamed pages without links are small hollow dots clustered around their section's named page. Unlinked pages that come before any name sit in a 'Not linked yet' tray.
- Interaction:
  - Tap a dot: a card shows the name, 'p. 12 · 3 out · 2 in', and Open, Around it, Rename.
  - Tap the dot again to go there.
  - Drag with one finger to pan and pinch to zoom: rough DU previews while moving, one crisp GL16 when you let go.

13. SETTINGS > GESTURES [P4]
- The Settings bottom row reads KOReader | Controller | Gestures | Updates | Done.
- The sheet lists, in order:
  - 'Gestures: on (tap to change)';
  - Editing..., Tools..., Pages..., Index..., Menus..., Screen...;
  - Reset gestures;
  - Done.
- Each row inside a group reads 'Action: gesture', for example 'Pages view: 2 fingers down'.
- Tap a row and a card asks 'Do the gesture for Undo'. When Grimoire recognises it, the card shows '2-finger tap' large, with Use, Try again and Cancel.
  - If the gesture belonged to another action, the card first says 'Now for Redo. Use moves it here.'
  - A try Grimoire refuses says why, for example 'Put the fingers down together.' or 'The pen is near: move it away.'
- Hold a row for 0.6 s to clear it. Reset gestures brings back the built-in ones.
- It all works with controller shortcuts off.

14. WHEN THINGS GO WRONG
- If links.ini cannot be read, the bar says 'Links could not be read.' and New link says why instead of doing nothing.
- A gesture refused only because the pen was near shows 'Move the pen away, then swipe.' at most once every 10 minutes.
- In a notebook of 2000 pages and 4000 links, the bar, the card and following a link cost the same as anywhere else. The map opens on a quick placement and tidies itself once its background layout finishes.
plan.gestures:
ONE VOCABULARY, fixed (question 6). Nothing free-form.
- touch.2.up, touch.2.down, touch.2.left, touch.2.right, touch.2.tap.
- touch.3.*: the same five. Offered only when the step-1 device log, and InputCaps.touch_slots from a new EVIOCGABS(ABS_MT_SLOT) probe, show at least 3 contacts.
- touch.1.up, touch.1.down, touch.1.left, touch.1.right: one-finger swipes, recordable but never bound by default. They are recognised only when the finger started on the page (not on the panel or a sheet), did not become a link hold, and travelled at least 30 mm in at most 600 ms, within 30 degrees of an axis.
- pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>: the pen plan's slots, recorded in the same sheet in P7. The 350 ms multi-tap gap is the owner's pen ruling.
- Edge swipes are not separate gestures. The edge band is only a rule for telling a swipe from a pan.
- Reserved, never recordable:
  - one-finger tap and hold (UI, links, the bar);
  - a two-finger spread or squeeze while pinch zoom is on;
  - a two-finger drag the view can follow (a pan).
- Names (EN / ES):
  - '2 fingers up' / '2 dedos arriba'
  - '2 fingers down' / '2 dedos abajo'
  - '2 fingers left' / '2 dedos izq.'
  - '2 fingers right' / '2 dedos der.'
  - '2-finger tap' / 'Toque con 2 dedos'
  - the same pattern for 3 fingers and 1 finger.
  Two-press rows use the short forms: '2 dedos izq. / 2 dedos der.' measures 1395 px, inside the 1470 px column.

BUILT-IN DEFAULTS. Never written to a file.
- touch.2.down = pages
- touch.2.up = links (the bar)
- touch.2.left = next-page and touch.2.right = previous-page (question 5). When a gesture moves past the last page it toasts 'This is the last page.' / 'Es la última página.' and never adds a page.
- pen.Button.triple = clear-page and pen.Button.hold = clear-page, as today.
- Two-finger and three-finger taps stay unbound. The sheet suggests them on a 'Try' line: 'Ideas: two-finger tap for Undo, three-finger tap for Redo.'
- MIRROR RULE: while a menu is in front, the mirror of that menu's own bound gesture closes it. The mirror has the same finger count with up and down, or left and right, swapped. So two fingers up close the Pages view, and two fingers down close the bar (back to the origin page). The menu's own gesture also closes it.

RECOGNIZER: src/touchgest.c/.h
Pure code in CORE_SRC, built and host-tested like pensync.c. input_evdev.c and sim_sdl.c both feed it contact frames.

Inputs per SYN_REPORT:
- the kernel CLOCK_MONOTONIC time;
- per contact: tracking id, logical x and y after calibration and rotation, tool, touch_major, pressure;
- pen context: prox, touching, left_ms, last contact point, and the hover point with its age, when the pensync hover mapping has been learned;
- view context, pushed by the editor whenever view_clamp, the sheets, the screen or the settings change:
  - scrolls_v = the view is taller than the screen AND pinch_zoom is on;
  - scrolls_h, the same for width;
  - zoom_ok, gestures_on, record, keyboard_open.

Cost: O(1) per frame, no allocation, signed 32-bit time differences.

1. ONE FINGER. Exactly today's stream: IN_TOUCH_DOWN at once, MOVE on change, UP at lift, with no added latency. The global 1 s pen window still applies to single fingers.

2. LANDING
- A second contact within 150 ms (provisional, set from the log): the first finger ends with the off-screen cancel (never a tap), IN_PINCH_BEGIN goes out with value 0, and the session can become a gesture.
- A second contact 150-400 ms after the first: zoom or pan only, never a swipe or tap.
- More than 400 ms later: a palm, suppressed (today's rule).
- A third contact within 250 ms makes three fingers.
- The finger count is fixed at the first of: any contact moving 3 mm; the end of the landing window; the first lift. A contact that lands later rejects the gesture, except during a committed zoom.

3. COMMIT (today's dead zone)
The session commits when the spread changes by 10% or more, or the midpoint travels at least 70 px. It is classified once, there:
- ZOOM if zoom_ok and spread_px >= 0.6 x trans.
- Otherwise TRANSLATE along the dominant axis. More than 30 degrees off axis is a PAN if either axis scrolls, else a reject ('Swipe in a straight line').
- A TRANSLATE is a PAN when the view scrolls on that AXIS (per axis, never per direction, so a drag that starts at a scroll limit never navigates by surprise) and the start midpoint is outside that direction's edge band. The bands are 25 mm (295 px) at the top for down and at the bottom for up, and 15 mm (177 px) at the sides.
- Otherwise it is a SWIPE candidate, and nothing moves on screen.
- Three fingers are never ZOOM or PAN.

4. EVENT CONTRACT
IN_PINCH_MOVE.value carries the class:
- 0 = legacy, the editor decides as today. The runner's 'pinch' and the simulator's mouse wheel push 0, so every existing pinch scenario keeps working.
- 1 = ZOOM: the editor skips its own 10%/70 px dead zone, since touchgest has committed, and re-anchors at the first classified move. This fixes the double dead zone.
- 2 = PAN: offsets only, with the zoom held at its commit value. This ends today's zoom wobble.
- 3 = SWIPE: the editor ignores the moves.
IN_PINCH_END comes first, then IN_GESTURE {value = gesture id, x, y = start midpoint, x2, y2 = end midpoint} in the same batch, so S->pinching is already clear when editor_shortcut checks it.
In record mode a rejection arrives as IN_GESTURE with a negative value, the reason code.

5. FIRING, at the first lift
- A SWIPE fires when all of these hold:
  - travel along the axis >= 20 mm (236 px);
  - off-axis travel <= tan 30 degrees of that;
  - each finger moved >= 12 mm, with cosine >= 0.8 to the midpoint's direction;
  - the largest finger travel is at most 2x the smallest;
  - the spread changed by 25% or less;
  - no more than 1000 ms from the first landing.
  Sliding back under 20 mm cancels it.
- A TAP: every contact lifts within 150 ms of the others, at most 300 ms from the first landing to the last lift, and no contact moves more than 5 mm.
- No multi-finger double taps in v1, so nothing ever waits. Pending timeouts, like the 3-finger landing window, resolve only when the last input batch drained the queue (App.input_drained).
- After a fire or a reject, every contact stays suppressed until all have lifted (today's T.suppressed), so a late finger never leaks a tap or a link follow.

6. RESTING CONTACTS (a grip thumb, the writing palm)
- A contact counts as resting if it stayed within 3 mm for 300 ms before the gesture's first finger, or if the panel flags it MT_TOOL_PALM.
- It is left out of the finger count and of the landing rule, provided every gesture finger is at least 40 mm from it.
- If it moves more than 3 mm during the gesture, the gesture is rejected ('Your hand moved: try again.').
- This replaces today's rule that any later finger is a late palm, for multi-finger gestures only.

7. PEN NEAR, staged (single fingers keep the global 1 s rule)
P2 ships the conservative rule. For a multi-finger gesture:
- pen touching: reject;
- pen in proximity: reject;
- pen gone less than 300 ms: reject;
- pen gone 300-1000 ms: accept when every finger is at least 40 mm from the pen's last contact point.
P4, after the step-1 log is read: also accept while the pen hovers, when the hover mapping is learned (hover_learn then runs on contact frames always, not only for Live view), the hover point is no older than 50 ms, and every finger is at least 60 mm from it.
Size guards, from the log: TOUCH_MAJOR above T_palm rejects (the guard only logs until the log is read); fingers closer than 8 mm or farther than 70 mm apart reject; a contact ever reported as tool 1 is never a finger.
A valid swipe refused only because of the pen toasts 'Move the pen away, then swipe.' / 'Aparta el lápiz y desliza.' at most once per 10 minutes.

8. INPUT FIXES, folded into the extraction (step 2)
- Pen arrival and the palm window end a finger with the off-screen cancel, never a real lift (input_evdev.c:477, 764).
- SYN_DROPPED resyncs every slot with EVIOCGMTSLOTS and suppresses until all lift (the pattern at 1627-1640).
- Kernel timestamps.
- input_pump also drains touch into touchgest, so a 1.2 s render no longer overflows the inferred 512-1024-event buffer.
- The device-scan busy flag counts every down contact.
- The pinch pair is chosen by landing order.
- When PINCH_BEGIN cancels a panel press, the button is restored with DU, not GL16.

DISPATCH
- IN_GESTURE gets a name in main.c's event_name (with its static assert), is dropped while asleep, is ignored while a book is being added (app.c:462), and counts as presence (app.c:464).
- On SCR_EDITOR, editor_gesture looks it up in gesturemap, applies the mirror rule, then calls editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y, SRC_TOUCH).
- So every existing gate holds: idle only; menu actions act through open menus; nothing acts through a keyboard; and all gestures are ignored while any keyboard is open.
- SRC_TOUCH and SRC_PEN never create a page from next-page.
- Gestures do not need Enable shortcuts. The master switch is settings.ini gestures (default 1).
- Elsewhere: the Pages view honours only the mirror close; the Library listens only in record mode.
- A one-time hint, the first time a two-finger vertical drag scrolls while 2-up or 2-down is bound: 'To open Pages or links here, start at the top or bottom edge.' / 'Para abrir Páginas o enlaces aquí, empieza en el borde de arriba o de abajo.'

THE GESTURES SHEET (Settings > Gestures, P4)
It is the Buttons sheet's code, parametrized by a BindKind descriptor {title, prompt, sources, text, learn, forget, reset}, not a copy.
- List: 'Gestures: on (tap to change)', Editing..., Tools..., Pages..., Index..., Menus..., Screen..., Reset gestures, Done. That is 9 rows, under the 12-row sideways limit.
- Group rows read 'Action: touch gesture, pen gesture' or 'Action: none'. Hold-eraser and the gestures switch are left out.
- RECORDING
  - Tap a row. touchgest goes into record mode: no zoom or pan side effects, every class and every rejection reported, with the same constants as at runtime, so whatever records will also fire. A unit test checks they stay the same.
  - A card opens (1400 wide):
    - title 'Do the gesture for %s' / 'Haz el gesto para %s';
    - body 'Swipe or tap with two fingers, or use the pen's button.';
    - footer 'When the page can scroll, swipe from the edge.' / 'Si la página se desplaza, desliza desde el borde.'
  - Rejections update one line with a GL16 of that line only:
    - 'The pen is near: move it away.' / 'El lápiz está cerca: apártalo.'
    - 'Put the fingers down together.' / 'Apoya los dedos a la vez.'
    - 'Swipe in a straight line.' / 'Desliza en línea recta.'
    - 'Swipe farther.' / 'Desliza más lejos.'
    - 'Move both fingers the same way.' / 'Mueve los dos dedos igual.'
    - 'Your hand moved: try again.' / 'La mano se movió: inténtalo otra vez.'
    - 'Two fingers spreading is kept for zoom.' / 'Separar dos dedos es para el zoom.'
    - 'One finger is kept for taps and links.' / 'Un dedo es para tocar y enlaces.'
  - A recognised gesture shows its name at 64 px with Use / Try again / Cancel ('Usar' / 'Otra vez' / 'Cancelar'). If it belongs to another action, the card first says 'Now for %s. Use moves it here.', and Use then toasts 'That gesture is no longer for %s.'
  - gestures.ini is written atomically, and the map changes only after the write succeeds.
  - 10 s with no attempt leaves the row as it was. A second tap on the row stops recording. A 0.6 s hold clears the row (a cleared default is written as '=nothing'). Reset deletes gestures.ini.
- BINDING RULE, the same for both sheets: per source, a binding does one action, and an action has at most one binding per source (touch, pen, pad). Keys keep shortcuts.ini's many-to-one. Built-in duplicates stay legal.

SIMULATOR AND RUNNER
- Window: Shift + right-drag = two fingers 25 mm apart moving together; Alt + right-drag = three fingers; Ctrl + right-click = a two-finger tap. The wheel stays the pinch (value 0).
- Runner, through touchgest on a virtual clock:
  - 'finger ID down|move|up X Y [MAJOR] [TOOL]', grouped into a frame until 'frame [MS]' (default 13 ms);
  - 'swipe N X Y DX DY [STEPS] [SEP] [LANDGAP]';
  - 'tapn N X Y [SEP] [MS]';
  - 'pen hover' and 'pen leave' drive the pen context.
  The legacy 'tap', 'touch', 'drag touch' and 'pinch' still push events directly.
- Probes: touch.gesture, touch.reject, touch.class, touch.contacts, touch.suppressed, gestures.ACTION, library.gestures_group, library.gestures.learning.
plan.hotbar:
WHAT IT IS
'Links' / 'Enlaces': the Index entries this page links to.
- In code it is src/linkbar.c. The editor hosts it like dispmenu, and linkbar_pointer returns LB_* results (PEEK, COMMIT, CANCEL, BACK, NEW_LINK, GOTO, EYE, INDEX, CARD) that the editor acts on.
- It is a MENU action ('links'), so it joins sheet_open, front_menu, menu_action, close_front and open_menu (editor.c:1374-1376, 1906-1965). Its own action closes it, another menu's action swaps, and Close menu closes it.
- While it is up, every other shortcut is refused (editor.c:2010), so nothing (no undo, no page turn) happens behind a peek.
- Opening it disarms link mode.

CONTENT (question 1 decides grouped versus per-link; grouped is the default)
One entry per distinct target among the page's live links: stored areas, plus beta.5 links whose ink still exists.
- Order: reading order of each entry's first area. Area tops within 10 mm count as one line, read left to right.
- Entries are numbered 1..n, and the eye tags every area with its entry's number.
- Labels:
  - a named target: its Index name, bold 44 px, cut with font_draw_left_name;
  - an unnamed page: 'Page 20', regular weight;
  - a link to the Index: the list glyph and 'The Index';
  - a deleted page or an unknown target: 'Page not here', 50% dithered. A tap toasts 'That link's page is not in this notebook.'; a long press offers Delete;
  - a legacy link with no area and no ink is not listed (dormant, as today).
- Right column: 'p. 12' at 34 px, and '×2' on a second line when two links on this page go to the same entry.
- Backlinks are not a list section. From P6 the header carries a small chip, '%d pages link here' / '%d páginas enlazan aquí', that opens the Index map around this page. It is hidden when the count is 0.

LAYOUT, UPRIGHT (1860 x 2480)
The card is at x 20, 1820 wide, its bottom 20 px above the screen edge. From the top:
- 16 px padding;
- a 36 px grip strip with a 160 x 8 px bar;
- a 100 px header:
  - origin: the title 'Links on this page (%d)' / 'Enlaces de esta página (%d)' with an X (118 x 100) at the right. When there are more than 6 entries, a pager ‹ 1/3 › (two 118 x 100 buttons) sits left of the X;
  - peek: a back chip '‹ Page 3' (at most 380 px), then 'Showing %s. Tap the page to stay.' / 'Mostrando %s. Toca la página para quedarte.' (truncated), then the X;
- R rows of chips (R = 1..3): 2 columns of 878 x 124, 24 px column gap, 16 px row gap (2 x 878 + 24 = 1780 = 1820 - 40);
- 20 px gap;
- a 140 px tool row: four buttons of 430 x 140 with 20 px gaps (4 x 430 + 60 = 1780), each an icon over a 34 px caps word;
- 20 px padding.
Height = 316 + 140 R: 456 (empty, or one row), 596 or 736 px. At least 1724 px of page stays visible.
CHIP: a 64 px black disc with the white number in 34 px bold, the name from x + 96, and a 150 px right column. Nothing wraps.

LAYOUT, SIDEWAYS (2480 x 1860)
The card is 2440 wide, with 3 columns of 784 x 124 (3 x 784 + 2 x 24 = 2400 = 2440 - 40), at most 2 rows (6 per screen). Tool buttons are 585 x 140. Height 456 or 596 px, at most 32% of 1860.

The card draws above the panel and every editor sheet. After compose resets a->toast_floor, the card sets it to its own top (editor.c:676).

TOOL ROW
- Go to / Ir a (magnifier F0349)
- New link / Nuevo enlace (link-plus F0339)
- Areas / Áreas (eye F0208):
  - off: the eye glyph in a 50% ordered dither inside a NORMAL frame, so it reads as dimmed, not as BTN_DISABLED gray;
  - on: a solid eye on a selected (inverted) button. Inverted means 'on' inside sheets; only the panel reserves it for the current tool.
- Index / Índice (three bubbles F05E3)
TRANSLATORS width note: 'about 400 px at 34 px caps'.

OPENING
- Two fingers up (default), the Links panel button (question 7), or the 'links' action.
- The card is composed into App.screen and its rect GL16'd: about 50-90 ms of CPU plus 271 ms.
- On a read-only page the bar opens for browsing, with New link drawn disabled; a tap on it toasts 'This page is read-only.'
- If links.ini is unreadable: 'Links could not be read.' New link and Areas are disabled, and New link toasts the reason when tapped.

TAP AN ENTRY: PEEK
1. app_press_feedback inverts the chip at once (DU).
2. A peek is a display state only. S->index, S->page, the page's history and link hit tests all stay on the origin until a commit, so autosave, undo or a link tap can never act on the peeked page.
3. The peek canvas comes from a 3-entry LRU of rendered canvases (the origin pinned, plus two targets). On a miss it renders with the pumped page reader and page_render (pumped).
4. compose blits the peek canvas at the target's default view instead of page_canvas, and only the page area above the card is sent as GL16. No GC16.
5. The selected chip keeps an 8 px frame. The header switches to the peek state, and the panel's page chip shows the peeked number.
6. Peeks never set nb.last_page or info_dirty and never write thumbnails.
7. Tapping the selected entry again commits, the same as tapping the page.
8. An entry for The Index commits, then opens the Index list (FULL).

COMMIT (STAY)
- FINGER outside the card, the panel included: the touch becomes OWN_MODAL. The commit happens on LIFT within the 30 px slop. If a second finger lands first, the pending commit is cancelled and the touch becomes a gesture. This fixes the trap in which the first finger of a two-finger close swipe committed and the gesture then opened Pages.
- PEN outside: commits on pen down, and the stroke is swallowed until pen up. That keeps the next stroke on MTK pen mode, since the closing refresh is not raced.
- Commit makes the peeked page current: index, page_at, the peek canvas swapped into page_canvas. It sets last_page and info_dirty, writes the origin's thumbnail if needed, closes the card and sends one REFRESH_FULL (GC16), which clears the peeks' ghosts.
- With no peek, the tap outside only closes, with a GL16 of the card rect, and is swallowed.
- The origin goes on the back list. Committing a page reached through Back pops the list instead, as a browser's Back does.

CANCEL (BACK TO THE ORIGIN)
- Triggered by: X; the 'links' action or the Links button again; two fingers down (the mirror); a one-finger drag of 15 mm or more down that starts on the grip or header; Close menu; the Back key.
- If peeking: the origin canvas is swapped back at the zoom and offset it had. Then compose_all with REFRESH_UI, or REFRESH_FULL after 3 or more peeks, because GL16 ghosting builds up.
- Otherwise: a GL16 of the card rect.

BACK CHIP
- While peeking: shows the origin again (canvas swap, GL16 of the page area). The bar stays.
- When not peeking and the back list is not empty: 'Back to Chapter 1' peeks the top of the back list.

ACTS ON THE SHOWN PAGE, SO IT COMMITS FIRST
- New link: commit, then link mode on that page. The bar folds into the link-mode strip and comes back afterwards with the new entry.
- Go to: commit, then the Find sheet.
- Index: commit, then the Index map (P6), or the Pages view's Index tab before P6.
- Another menu's button or key: commit, then swap.

LONG PRESS AN ENTRY (600 ms within the slop)
- If peeking, first return to the origin with a GL16, because the links live there.
- Then the link card opens above the card, aligned with the chip's column. The entry's areas get the heavy dotted border (four DU strips each).
- The card's rows are those of the page's card. For a ×N entry they read 'Delete %d links' and 'Change where they go', with the line 'To change one, hold it on the page.' / 'Para cambiar uno, mantenlo pulsado en la página.' Delete removes all N as one ACT_LINK group step.
- Before P3 the long press opens today's retarget path (pagesview_pick).

AREAS: toggles settings.link_areas and saves. A GL16 of the button, plus a GL16 of the union of the visible areas, flushed separately when they are far apart. No toast; the first time only, hints bit 2.

PAGER: ‹ and › redraw the chip grid only, with a GL16.

INSTANT JUMPS
- Canvas LRU: up to 3 x 4.6 MB (5.3 MB at 1986 x 2648). The key is page id + the page's edit generation + paper generation + page size. A peek swaps structs, never memcpys. The cache is freed when the card closes, and an allocation failure shrinks it to nothing: slower peeks, the same pixels.
- Prefetch runs in editor_tick only when App.input_drained and no owner holds the pointer:
  - the targets of the visible entries, then the top of the back list;
  - one 160-row render band per tick;
  - pages not in memory load through the new pumped page reader (step 10);
  - it stops at the first contact.

CHECKLIST FOR EVERY NEW SURFACE (bar, link card, link-mode strip, Link to..., Find, Index map, record card)
- joins sheet_open, front_menu, menu_action, close_front and open_menu;
- sets toast_floor after compose;
- swallows its tap outside on lift (pen on down);
- never draws while the pen is down;
- every keyboard goes through kbhost.

PROBES: editor.bar (0, open, peek), editor.bar.entries, editor.bar.N ('p12 x2', 'index'), editor.bar.peek (the shown page or 0), editor.bar.rect, editor.back ('depth top'), editor.canvas_cache ('hits misses entries'), notebook.last_page.
plan.link_areas:
MODEL (ruling 1)
- A link is (page id, seed, target, area). The area is an axis-aligned rectangle in page px at the notebook's page size, stored in links.ini on an area. line next to the unchanged link. line.
- The area is invisible. It never goes into page_canvas, thumbnails, the share page, the PDF page image or the sleep image. Only overlays in App.screen show it: the eye, the dashed lasso while drawing, the dotted rectangle until a target is picked, and the heavy border of a long press.
- The seed stays the link's id. nav_new_seed keeps it unique per page and already makes new ink avoid link seeds.
- A visible border is the owner's own ink (smart shapes or freehand), with its own seed, and is never part of the link. Erasing it keeps the link; deleting the link keeps it.
- The trick of giving a border the link's seed is deliberately not used: it would bring back the dependence on ink and the precise-eraser quirk.

HIT TEST
- Each link's box is its area. An unmigrated legacy link uses the point box of its ink strokes instead, erase strokes ignored.
- The box is padded to at least 7 mm a side around its centre (NAV_LINK_MIN_MM).
- The SMALLEST padded box under the finger wins; a tie goes to the lower seed. This replaces 'last stroke wins', so nested links behave and no creation order is stored.
- The editor caches the open page's boxes (at most 64, with entry numbers). The cache is rebuilt on page change, link edits and migration. While legacy links remain on the page, it is also rebuilt on draw_end, erase_end, undo/redo and clear.
- nav_link_areas also prefers areas, so the PDF's /Link annotations (export.c:94-117) follow without any change to export. Links to the Index stay dropped from the PDF, as today.

MAKING ONE (P3)
1. ARM from the bar's New link, the 'add-link' action or the Index tab's Add a link. A refusal says why:
   - read-only: the read-only toast;
   - links.ini unreadable: 'Links could not be read in this notebook.';
   - 64 links on the page: 'This page has 64 links: delete one to add another.'
2. STRIP: 1820 x 130 at the bottom, GL16: 'Draw around what links.' / 'Rodea lo que enlaza.' with Cancel (260 x 100). Pressing add-link again, Close menu, Cancel, a page change or leaving the editor disarms it, and nothing is written.
3. LASSO: the next pen contact is OWN_LASSO, whatever the tool, the eraser end included, and smart shapes never apply.
   - Its points (page px, decimated to at most 4096) draw a 4 px black dashed line (12 on, 8 off) as an overlay layer that compose redraws.
   - Each batch of segments goes out as REFRESH_FAST under display_live_ink(true).
   - Nothing touches page_canvas, the page or history, so no tile backup is needed.
4. LIFT:
   - Under 5 mm both ways (LINK_BOX_MIN_MM): the dashes are recomposed away, the toast is 'Too small for a link: draw around what links.' / 'Demasiado pequeño para un enlace: rodea lo que enlaza.', and the mode stays.
   - Otherwise the area is the points' box, clamped to the page. One REFRESH_UI of the union swaps the dashes for a dotted rectangle (3 px dashes, white halo).
5. LINK TO... (the bar's frame in pick mode)
   - Title: 'Where does the link go?' / '¿Adónde va el enlace?'
   - It docks at the TOP (y 20) when the area's centre is in the lower 45% of the screen, otherwise at the bottom.
   - Chips: New page... / Página nueva..., The Index / El índice, up to 4 Recent targets (this session's link targets and the last visited pages, this page left out), then the Index entries in Index order, paged.
   - Tool row: Search (opens Find in PICK mode; kbhost docks the keyboard on the side away from the area), Choose from the pages... (today's Pages-view picker, the only part of picking mode that is kept), Cancel.
6. PICK:
   - nav_link_set plus the area, then nav_save_links. On failure, nav_load rolls back and the toast is 'Could not save the link.'
   - On success, one ACT_LINK step and the toast 'Linked to %s.' / 'Enlazado con %s.' The first time it adds 'Tap it with a finger to go there; hold it for more.' (hints bit 1).
   - The dotted rectangle ends at the pick (unless the eye is on). Ruling 1 shows areas only while a link is made.
   - If the flow started from the bar, the bar comes back.
7. NEW PAGE...: kbhost asks 'Name the new page' / 'Nombre de la página nueva' over the page. Done does store_add_page at npages (the end), then nav_set_name; an empty name leaves the page unnamed. Then the link, and the toast 'Linked to the new page %d.' The editor stays on the origin. Cancel adds no page and returns to Link to....
8. CANCEL at any point: 'No link made.' / 'No se hizo ningún enlace.' Nothing to undo.

THE EYE (P2; settings.ini link_areas, default 0, remembered; action 'link-areas')
- In compose(r), after the page blit and before the panel, for every cached box that meets r:
  - the HIT box, so what the eye promises is what a finger hits;
  - a 4 px black dashed outline (16 on, 12 off) on a 2 px white halo;
  - a 52 x 52 white tag with a 3 px frame and the entry number in 34 px bold, at the top-left corner, kept inside the screen.
- 1-bit only, so DU and GL16 look alike and inversion keeps it distinct.
- At most 64 rect tests per compose, and the live-ink composes reuse the cache.
- In P2 the boxes come from the legacy ink fallback; from P3 they are stored areas.

LONG PRESS (ruling 2, P3)
- At 600 ms within the 30 px slop, the heavy border goes around the box inflated 8 px:
  - 5 px black dashes (20 on, 14 off) on a 3 px white halo on both sides;
  - solid 24 px corner Ls.
  Only the four strips go out by DU, with their own app_flush, so the gray ink inside is not dithered. The card follows by GL16. When the card closes, card and strips are GL16'd.
- Card: 780 x 666.
  - Title row (110): target name in 44 px bold plus 'p. 12' at 34 px.
  - Four 118 px rows with 12 px gaps:
    - Rename in the Index / Renombrar en el índice. For an unnamed page: 'Add page %d to the Index...' / 'Añadir la página %d al índice...'. Disabled for The Index, an unknown target, or an unwritable nav.ini.
    - Change where it goes... / Cambiar a dónde lleva...
    - Redraw the area / Volver a dibujar la zona
    - Delete link / Borrar enlace
  - TRANSLATORS width: 'about 700 px at 44 px'.
- PLACEMENT: 24 px to the right of the box if it fits within a 20 px margin; else left; else below; else above. It is clamped to the screen, never covers the box when any placement avoids it, and slides horizontally to avoid the panel.
- Rename: kbhost over the page, titled 'Name in the Index'. Done calls nav_set_name(target pid) plus nav_save, with the pid parametrised (the pattern at editor.c:1643-1656), and restores the old name on failure. Naming an unnamed page toasts 'Page %d is in the Index as %s.' so the new section start is no surprise.
- Change where it goes: Link to... with the current target marked, then an ACT_LINK retarget.
- Redraw the area: link mode for this link ('Draw the link's new area'); the new box replaces the old one as an ACT_LINK step.
- Delete link: nav_link_remove, a save and an ACT_LINK step. Toast 'Link deleted. Undo brings it back.'
- A tap outside closes the card and is swallowed (OWN_MODAL, on lift). Close menu closes it.
- The Pages view's hold path (link_hold, PG_UNLINK, PG_TO_INDEX) is retired in P3.

UNDO
- ACT_LINK lives in the page's history (memory only): {pid, seed, n, records[n] of before {exists, target, area} and after {...}}. n > 1 is the ×N group delete or retarget.
- Undo and redo re-apply the records and save links.ini.
- If the save fails: nav_load restores what is on disk, the step is explicitly dropped from the stack it was just moved to (new history_drop_last_redo / _undo), and the toast is 'Could not save the links: that change was not undone.' This fixes the history_undo behaviour verified at history.c:177.
- Redo after the target page was deleted does nothing.

COPY PAGE: copies the page's links (same seeds, areas and targets) to the copy's pid. Any legacy link is migrated first, since the source page is loaded.

MIGRATING THE OWNER'S BETA.5 LINKS (ruling 1)
- A link. line with no area. line is LEGACY. It keeps working exactly as today, through the ink-box fallback, in the editor, the bar, the eye and the PDF.
- ON PAGE LOAD (page_at): each legacy link of that page whose ink exists gets an area = the UNPADDED point box of its ink strokes (never the 7 mm grown box), erase strokes ignored, rounded outward to whole px. The links are marked dirty.
