- IDLE: after a notebook opens with legacy lines, editor_tick handles one such page per idle tick (input drained, no owner). Pages in memory are used directly; others are read with the pumped page reader. The main.longest_unpumped_ms probe must stay under 100 ms.
- FLUSH: save_page never writes links.ini (it saves only a dirty page, editor.c:751), so nav_save_links runs explicitly whenever links_dirty: on leaving a page, in the 2 s idle autosave tick, at notebook close and at editor_leave.
- The lasso ink stays as ordinary ink, and its seed stays reserved.
- A lasso hidden by the precise eraser or white ink still has its stroke, so it migrates to a working area that the eye shows. The silent death at compaction is gone.
- A legacy link with no ink stays dormant and is pruned only with its page.
- If links.ini is unwritable, nothing migrates and the fallback keeps working.
plan.smart_shapes:
TRIGGER
- Draw, then hold the nib still within 1.0 screen mm (11.8 px) for shape_hold_ms. The default is 550; the choices are Quick 400, Normal 550 and Slow 900.
- draw_sample keeps the anchor in O(1): a sample more than 1 mm from the anchor moves it and resets its kernel time.
- editor_tick (at least every 30 ms, pen down too) checks the hold by wall time, never by sample spacing, because a still relayed pen may send nothing. It checks only when App.input_drained, so a backlog is never mistaken for stillness.
- It evaluates once per still period.
- It applies to ink strokes of all nine pens, the highlighter and the side button's highlighter included. It never applies to erase strokes, white ink, the precise or whole-stroke eraser, read-only pages, or the link lasso.

RECOGNIZER: src/shape.c, pure and geometric (no timing features, because runner batches share one time). About 0.12 ms on the Kindle. It resamples at the bbox diagonal / 40. Sizes are in screen mm: page px = mm x dpi / 25.4 / zoom.
- LINE: chord/path >= 0.97; max offset <= max(4% of the length, 1 mm) + 0.5 mm; at least 12 mm long. Snaps to 0, 45, 90 or 135 degrees within 4 degrees.
- CLOSED (a prerequisite for the shapes below):
  - the end gap is at most 22% of the diagonal;
  - winding around the centroid is 1.7-2.6 pi;
  - total absolute turning is at most 1.6 x the winding + 0.6 pi, which rejects scribbles;
  - at least 10 mm across and 4 mm thick.
- RECTANGLE / SQUARE / QUAD: ShortStraw finds 4 segments, each with chord/path >= 0.93. Every angle within 15 degrees of 90 makes a rectangle: axis-aligned within 5 degrees, a square when the sides are within 10%. Otherwise a straight-edged quad, which is how diamonds come out.
- TRIANGLE: 3 segments. Equilateral or right-angled snaps within 7 degrees.
- ELLIPSE / CIRCLE: a PCA frame plus a least-squares fit. RMS radial error at most 6% of the minor axis, maximum at most 20%. A circle when the axis ratio is >= 0.88; axis-aligned within 6 degrees.
- PAPER-AWARE (v1, no setting): on Dot grid and Graph paper, line ends and rectangle corners snap to the 5 mm grid within 1 mm. On ruled papers a near-horizontal line snaps exactly horizontal.
- v1.5 (step 22, shipped only if the corpus gate passes): single-stroke ARROW (a shaft, then one or two barbs at 20-70 degrees, each 15-45% of the shaft), open POLYLINE with 90-degree snaps, and ARC.

CONFIDENCE AND ACCIDENT DEFENCES, strongest first
1. A hold only previews. Moving on restores your line, and the stroke continues untouched.
2. Gates that can say no: size in screen mm, closure, winding, the scribble budget, fit residuals. On the owner's 47 real strokes, a hold-only trigger like Amazon's would fire 21 times; these gates gave no preview at written size.
3. Writing-burst gate: a stroke started within 600 ms and 8 mm of the last lift needs tolerances 0.7x as wide and a 1.5x hold.
4. One Undo removes the shape.
5. A panel toggle plus an adjustable hold, both assignable: the two things Amazon's users asked for.
6. Never on erasers, white ink or the lasso.

PREVIEW (the simple path, live equals re-render by construction)
1. At an accepted hold, the region = union(raw bbox, shape bbox), padded by the brush's max radius + 2.
2. Copy that region of page_canvas (the with-raw pixels).
3. draw_page(region) renders the page without the stroke in progress. The raw stroke is not page_add'ed until lift. This is pumped every 64 rows.
4. Stamp the snapped stroke with stroke_brush_begin and brush_add, calling work_pump every 8 points.
5. show(region, REFRESH_FAST): one DU frame, and pen mode is kept.
- Moving more than 1.5 mm from the anchor (hysteresis over the 1.0 mm hold radius) puts the saved copy back (a memcpy) with one DU frame. The raw BrushState was never touched.
- Lift or LEAVE: page_add(shape) with ONE history_push_add. The raw stroke is never added. No redraw; the region joins S->settle for the usual GL16.
- Holding longer does nothing more.
- No GL16 and no toast while the pen is down.
- If the region copy cannot be allocated, that stroke gets no preview.
- An under-ink tile backup comes later only if the shape-log shows region renders over about 300 ms on the owner's pages.

STORAGE
The snapped stroke is an ordinary Stroke: the raw stroke's tool id (0-9), ToolParams snapshot, ext bytes, tip variant and seed. Only the points differ:
- polygons: vertices at the intersections of the least-squares edge lines, plus a point every 2 mm;
- ellipses: N = clamp(ceil(2 pi / acos(1 - 0.25 px / r)), 24, 720) vertices;
- the stroke starts nearest the user's first point, runs in the user's direction, and closed shapes close exactly;
- pressure is the median of the middle 80% of samples by arc length; tilt is the median; t_ms is interpolated by arc length.
No format change and no ext flag. Older versions draw it as the pen stroke it is.

UNDO: one pen-down is one moment, so one Undo removes the shape. This is the owner's documented undo rule, and it is decided here, not asked.

shape-last ('Shape the last stroke' / 'Dar forma al último trazo')
- Runs all the gates, but no hold, on the page's newest ink stroke when the top undo step is that stroke's ACT_ADD.
- It makes one ACT_REPLACE step (count 2: raw out, shape in), so Undo brings the freehand stroke back. Then draw_page(union), pumped, and REFRESH_UI.
- Otherwise it toasts 'No shape in the last stroke.' / 'El último trazo no es una forma.'
- It gives a zero-accident way in for writers who turn the hold off.

TOGGLE
- Panel: P_SHAPES, a new button directly under the eraser, in the pen-behaviour group.
  - On: the filled glyph F0831 on a plain button. Off: the outline glyph F0832 with a 4 px diagonal slash (canvas_slash).
  - NEVER inverted: on this panel, inverted means the current tool (editor.c tool_style).
- Tap: settings.shapes flips, then settings_save and a GL16 of the button. Toasts:
  - 'Smart shapes on. Hold the pen still at the end of a shape.' / 'Formas inteligentes activadas. Mantén el lápiz quieto al final de una forma.'
  - 'Smart shapes off.' / 'Formas inteligentes desactivadas.'
- Tool picker: a labelled row under the ink row with two 520 px chips, 'Smart shapes: On' and 'Hold: Normal', so the icon is explained where there is room for words.
- Actions: 'shapes' (TOGGLE), 'shape-hold' (CYCLE; toast 'Shape hold: Normal (0.55 s)'), 'shape-last'.
- One-time tip after the first snap (hints bit 5): 'Shape made. Undo takes it away; the panel's shapes button turns this off.'

DEVICE TUNING: an empty grimoire/shape-log file logs each hold's features and decision: size in mm, winding, residuals, corners, kind or reason, and ms taken. It never logs coordinates. One evening of the owner's writing then sets the final thresholds.
plan.graph_view:
NAME AND ENTRY
- One Index destination. The view is titled 'Index' / 'Índice', with a Graph | List switch. List goes to the Pages view's Index tab (the existing list), whose header gains a Graph button.
- Open it from the bar's Index button, from that Graph button, or with the new 'index-map' action ('Index map' / 'Mapa del índice' in the Buttons and Gestures sheets).
- The 'index' action keeps its 1.2.0 meaning: the list. A link to The Index still opens the list.
- Hosting: src/mapview.c, full screen, like the Pages view, but drawn from its own offscreen canvas (screen size, 4.6 MB, freed on close). compose only blits it, so settles and toasts never re-render edges.
- It joins the sheet family and its checklist.
- Open and close are GC16.

DATA (no page loads)
- Built from nav.ini, links.ini and nb->page_ids in one O(n + e) pass, with a pid-to-index open-addressing table (4096 slots).
- Edges: links between pages, deduplicated per unordered pair, with direction bits and multiplicity.
- Links to The Index: a 16 px lozenge badge at the source dot's upper right, not edges, because an Index hub makes a hairball.
- Degree = the number of distinct linked neighbours.

NODES: every page is a dot, in three bands.
1. FORCE NODES: named pages, pages with any link, and the open page. Only these enter the force layout.
2. SATELLITES: unnamed pages with no links that have a named page before them. They are small hollow dots placed deterministically on phyllotaxis rings around their section's named page (nav_section_of) after the layout. They are never in the forces, so a 2000-page notebook costs no more than its linked part. When a section has more than 60 satellites, 60 are drawn plus a '+N' label; zooming to 2x or more shows them all.
3. TRAY: unnamed, unlinked pages before the first named page sit in a 'Not linked yet (%d)' / 'Aún sin enlaces (%d)' tray: below the graph upright, right of it sideways, at a 40 px pitch, in notebook order. With more than 200 it collapses to 'Not linked yet: %d pages. Show'.

LOOK (1-bit-safe marks, so DU previews match GL16 settles and inversion keeps them distinct)
- Fill by degree, getting progressively lighter as the owner asked:
  - 0: a hollow 3 px ring;
  - 1: a 25% Bayer dither (4x4 on 2x2-px cells) inside a ring;
  - 2-3: a 50% dither;
  - 4 or more: solid.
- Radius at fit = 14 + 16 x ln(1 + d) / ln(1 + dmax) px (14-30). Unnamed force nodes are drawn at 0.75x and satellites at 6 px.
- A named orphan (in the Index, linked by nothing) is hollow but labelled: an entry nothing links to yet.
- Open page: a concentric double ring 6 px apart. Selected: an 8 px ring, its edges at 5 px, outgoing edges solid and incoming dashed, so direction reads without arrowheads; its label becomes an inverted chip.
- Edges: 2.5 px anti-aliased lines (the row-span canvas_line_aa), plus 1 px per extra link up to 5 px, drawn under white knockout discs (r + 4).
- Labels: named pages in bold 34 px, at most 320 px wide (font_draw_left_name), on a white knockout box.
  - Placed greedily by priority: selected, open page, neighbours, then named pages by degree.
  - 4 candidate spots each, tested against placed labels and dots; a label that collides is skipped until zoomed.
  - 'p. N' labels for unnamed pages appear only at 2x zoom or in Around mode.

LAYOUT: src/graph.c, pure, in CORE_SRC
- SEED: Navi's place_disk. BFS shells grow from each component's top-degree hub, with rings sorted by parent angle and components packed outward. Jitter is deterministic, seeded by a hash of the page id, never its index.
- RELAX: about 300 Barnes-Hut steps (theta 0.9) with Navi's constants: REPULSION 16000, SPRING_K 0.055, SPRING_L 110, GRAVITY 0.02, DAMPING 0.9.
- WHERE IT RUNS:
  - up to 300 force nodes: in-process, with a work_pump callback every 2 steps (about 0.25 s on the Kindle);
  - more, or Tidy up: a niced bgjob child writes graph.ini atomically while the view shows the O(n + e) seed. The result is swapped in with one GL16 only while the map is open and idle (no input for 500 ms). 2000 force nodes with 4000 links take about 3.4 s in the child.
- INCREMENTAL: a new force node goes at its placed neighbours' centroid plus one rest length (or beside its section head), then 40 steps run over its 2-hop neighbourhood with everything else fixed (under 10 ms). A full relayout runs only when more than 10% of the nodes changed, or on Tidy up.
- Nothing moves between visits.
- Floats differ between arm64 and armv7, so positions persist in graph.ini and tests assert invariants, never coordinates.

SCREEN
- Upright header, 190 px:
  - Back (150 x 150);
  - the title 'Index' with Graph | List;
  - an 'All | Around' segment ('Todas | Alrededor', 2 x 300);
  - Fit.
- Bottom row, 170 px:
  - − and + (220 x 140);
  - 'Unlinked: Show / Hide' ('Sin enlaces: Mostrar / Ocultar'), the satellites and the tray;
  - 'Tidy up' / 'Ordenar', shown once positions exist.
- Selecting a dot replaces the bottom row with a 320 px card:
  - the name at 64 px;
  - 'Page 12. Links to 3, linked from 2.' / 'Página 12. Enlaza a 3, enlazada desde 2.';
  - Open, Around it, Rename (Rename uses kbhost over the map).
- Sideways: the same, with the tray on the right.

INTERACTION
- Tap a dot: the nearest within max(r x zoom, 59 px = 5 mm), by the view's own hit test (HitList holds only 128 entries). GL16 of the old and new selection plus the card.
- Tap the selected dot again, or Open: go_to_page (GC16), close the map, and push the origin on the back list.
- Tap empty space: deselect.
- One-finger or pen drag: pan. An offset blit is presented by DU at most every 180 ms; at release, a pumped re-render and one GL16.
- Pinch: zoom 0.25x-6x, with a nearest-neighbour scaled DU preview, then GL16. − and + step by 1.5x. Fit resets.
- Around: a radial ring layout (Navi's positions_radial). The centre page sits in the middle, depth 1 on one ring, depth 2 on an outer ring, angle-sorted by parent; only members are drawn. Instant and deterministic.
- Default view: All, centred on the open page at a zoom that fits its 2-step neighbourhood, or fits everything if that keeps dots at least 10 px.
- The last mode and the Unlinked choice are remembered per notebook in graph.ini.
- Back or Close menu returns to the page; 'pages' swaps to the Pages view.

PERFORMANCE
- Culled to the viewport. Drawing order: edges, knockouts, dots, labels. work_pump every 64 edges.
- About 50-70 ms on the Kindle for 100 nodes. Worst case, 2000 force nodes and 4000 edges at fit: 1-2 s, pumped, shown behind the seed frame.
- If the 4.6 MB offscreen canvas cannot be allocated: 'Not enough memory for the map.' and the List opens instead.

PROBES: editor.map, editor.map.nodes, .edges, .force, .satellites, .tray, .orphans, .selected, .mode, .layout ('seed', 'running', 'done'), .node.PID ('tier r x y visible'), .labels.

ONE REGISTRY
A new, UI-free src/actions.c/.h, beside shortcuts.c, holds per action:

plan.data_and_formats:
THE .qpg FORMAT NEVER CHANGES
No header bump, no tool id >= 10, no ext flag, no chunk holding page coordinates. Snapped shapes are ordinary strokes. Areas, overlays, the bar, the card and the map are never in pages.

links.ini (2.0.0-beta.5, unreleased, so free to change)
  # Grimoire: links on pages
  link.12=0a1b2c3d,p7
  area.12=0a1b2c3d,410,1220,380,140
- link.<pid>=<seed>,<target>: byte for byte today's grammar. The target is index or p<pid>, 1-15 bytes from '!' to '~'.
- area.<pid>=<seed>,<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>: decimal page px at store_notebook_page_size. 0 <= x, y; 1 <= w, h; x + w and y + h <= 6000.
  - The last line for a pid+seed wins.
  - An area line with no matching link line is dropped at the next save and logged.
  - A malformed area line is carried verbatim, and its link falls back to the ink box.
  - After a page-size change an area is clamped; one left empty means no area.
- Links with an area use it; links without one use their ink box (the beta.5 rule).
- Size: a worst-case pair of lines is about 63 B, so 4000 links take about 252 KB plus up to 16 KiB of carried lines. links.ini therefore gets its own cap, NAV_LINKS_FILE_MAX = 512 KiB. nav.ini keeps 256 KiB. NAV_LINKS_MAX 4000 and NAV_LINKS_PER_PAGE 64 are unchanged.
- The device's f9d13f5 build on the new file:
  - it reads every link. line, and ink links keep working there because migration never removes ink;
  - it carries area. lines as unknown lines up to 16 KiB (about 430 links);
  - past that, or past 256 KiB, it refuses the file: links are read-only there and the file is never overwritten.
  - 1.2.0 to beta.4 never read links.ini.
- Writes stay whole and atomic, and an unreadable file is never overwritten.

gestures.ini (new, in root/ beside shortcuts.ini and controller.ini; absorbs the pen plan's unreleased pen.ini)
  # Grimoire: gestures (Settings > Gestures). Built in unless a line says otherwise:
  # touch.2.down=pages, touch.2.up=links, touch.2.left=next-page, touch.2.right=previous-page, pen.Button.triple=clear-page, pen.Button.hold=clear-page
  touch.2.tap=undo
  touch.2.left=nothing
  pen.Button.double=links
- Grammar: shortcuts.ini's. '#' and ';' comments, trimmed key=value, a later duplicate wins, case-insensitive.
- Keys: touch.<1|2|3>.<up|down|left|right|tap> (touch.1.tap is refused) and pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>.
- Values: an action name, nothing, or pan|zoom in a drag slot.
- OVERLAY MODEL: built-in defaults are never written; a line overrides one, and '=nothing' switches one off. Defaults added later still reach the owner. Only slots that were set are written; when none are left the file is removed. Reset deletes it.
- Reads are bounded at 64 KiB through shortcuts.c's factored bounded reader.
  - A malformed line is refused and counted, and toasted when the sheet opens.
  - A well-formed line this version cannot use is kept verbatim, up to 2 KiB, and written back.
  - A file that does not read runs on the built-in defaults, is never overwritten, and the sheet offers Reset.
- It is read in app_init, by the Controller sheet's Reload, and each time the Gestures sheet opens.
- It cannot live in settings.ini: test_probe.c:29-39 and store.c reserve dotted pen. and touch. keys.

graph.ini (new, per notebook folder; a CACHE)
  # Grimoire: the Index map's layout (a cache: deleting it loses nothing)
  gen=5f3a9c21
  mode=all
  unlinked=show
  pos.12=-310,442
- gen is FNV-1a 32 of the sorted force-node and edge sets. pos values are integer world units (1 = 1 px at zoom 1). pin.<pid>=1 is reserved for v2.
- Unknown lines are carried (255 B each, 16 KiB total) under a 256 KiB cap.
- An unreadable file is ignored and not overwritten that session. A gen mismatch updates incrementally or recomputes.
- Older versions never read it. Raw ZIP exports leave it out because it is a cache. nav.ini and links.ini stay in the ZIPs.

settings.ini (undotted numeric keys, append-only; missing means the default, and 1.0.0-beta drops them, so the default returns)
- link_areas 0|1, default 0
- shapes 0|1, default 1 (2 reserved for lines only, 3 for an every-stroke diagram mode)
- shape_hold_ms 300..1500, default 550
- gestures 0|1, default 1
- rotation_lock 0 = follow the follow_rotation setting, 1..4 = locked at rotation 0..3; default 0
- hints: a bitmask, default 0. Bit 0 gestures tip, 1 first link, 2 eye, 3-4 bar hint count, 5 first snap, 6 edge hint.
All go in FORMAT.md's table and the settings.* probes (app.c:1022-1037).

MEMORY ONLY
- History kinds ACT_LINK (link records, n >= 1) and ACT_REPLACE (shape-last).
- The back list: up to 32 page ids per open notebook. It is pushed by link follows, bar commits, Find results, map opens and Pages-view opens, not by next or previous page, and cleared at close.
- Recent targets (4), the area cache (64), the canvas LRU (3), the shape region copy, the map canvas.

NAME SEARCH: store.c's static fold_next and cmp_name are exposed as i18n_fold_next and i18n_name_match: prefix first, then word start, then substring; accent-folded and case-insensitive. No new file.

DOCS
- FORMAT.md: links.ini v2, gestures.ini, graph.ini, the settings keys, and the moving-between-versions rows (area links are inert before beta.5 and partly in f9d13f5; older versions ignore gestures.ini and graph.ini; .qpg is unchanged).
- SHORTCUTS.md: registry, sources, gestures, 'not only with Enable shortcuts', the unassignable list.
- DESIGN.md: new screens and the refresh table; DU corrected from about 120 to 188 ms.
- SIM.md and TESTING.md: commands and probes.
plan.eink_and_performance:
MEASURED WAVEFORMS (24-27 C): DU 188 ms, GL16 271 ms, GC16 341 ms (the whole panel). DU is 294 ms when cold. CPU figures are host times x20.

REFRESH PLAN
- Gesture: nothing is drawn while the fingers move; the action's own refresh is the feedback. Recognition costs under 20 us per frame, and firing on lift adds 13-30 ms.
- Bar open and close: a 1.37 Mpx card. Compose plus copy take about 50-90 ms, then GL16. About 0.35 s, no flash.
- Chip press: an immediate DU invert (app_press_feedback).
- Peek: GL16 of the page area only. A cache hit is about 0.35-0.45 s. A miss adds a pumped load and render, typically 0.1-0.3 s and up to 1.2 s.
- Commit: one GC16, which resets the 30-count. Cancel: GL16, or GC16 after 3 or more peeks. Back: GL16.
- Eye: GL16 of the button, plus the union of the area rects, flushed separately when far apart.
- Link long press: the four border strips by DU, with their own app_flush, then the card by GL16, never one union. On close: GL16 of the card and strips.
- Link mode: strip GL16; lasso DU per batch; on lift, GL16 of the lasso's box union.
- Link to..., Find and every keyboard: kbhost.
- Index map: open and close GC16; selection GL16 of small rects; pan and zoom DU at most every 180 ms, then GL16 at release.
- Smart shapes: preview DU, cancel DU, commit through the normal settle. Never GL16 or a toast while the pen is down (pen_leave's wait).
- Gestures record card: GL16 of its reason line only.

FLASH BUDGET
- The every-30th-UI-refresh promotion (app.c:931) stays, because writing's GL16 settles count toward it, and an area-weighted rule would change ghost cleanup under writing.
- GC16 is used only for deliberate screen changes: commit, go to a page, the Pages view, map open and close, theme, invert.
- Each commit's GC16 resets the counter, so heavy bar use costs at most one surprise flash per roughly ten sessions without a commit. Revisit only after device testing.

KEYBOARD LAG STAYS FIXED (kbhost, step 5; adopt the other lane's helper if it lands first)
- Draw only when the field or a key changed, never on an unchanged move (pagesview.c:344-345 redraws on every move today).
- Present the field, then the key, as separate small DU flushes.
- One GL16 settle 900 ms after typing pauses.
- Toast floor at the keyboard's top. It docks top or bottom, as asked.
- Never hosted inside a full-screen compose: the Pages view redraws everything per call (editor.c:672-675).
- The keyboard.draws probe is asserted in every scenario that types.

NEVER BLOCK THE PEN (its evdev buffer overflows after about 100 ms)
- No MXCFB_WAIT_FOR_UPDATE_SUBMISSION, no second wait on a marker, no new display calls. Screens only app_invalidate; app_flush presents. The only wait stays pen_leave before a non-DU refresh.
- Pumped or split:
  - page renders every 64 rows;
  - page reads (new: store_read_page takes a pump callback every 256 strokes, used by peek, prefetch and idle migration);
  - shape dabs every 8 points;
  - map edges every 64;
  - layout every 2 steps, with big layouts in a bgjob child;
  - prefetch one 160-row band per idle tick;
  - idle migration one page per idle tick.
- A sim probe, main.longest_unpumped_ms, is asserted under 100 ms in the big-notebook, prefetch and migration scenarios.
- input_pump drains touch into touchgest, and frames carry kernel SYN times, so a backlog after a render neither bunches a swipe, nor fakes a hold, nor overflows the touch buffer.
- The device scan's busy flag counts every down contact, so its 330-370 ms block never starts mid-gesture.
- light_get never runs on the input path; light_cached replaces it there.

PRIMITIVES (step 6)
- canvas_line_aa becomes row-span: bit-identical, about 40x faster on long edges (0.02 against 0.82 ms per edge on the host). This is a prerequisite for the map.
- canvas_dash_rect(r, thick, on, off, halo), canvas_dash_poly for the lasso, canvas_disc_pattern(cx, cy, r, level) (4x4 Bayer on 2x2 cells) and canvas_slash.
- Everything new is 1-bit-safe.

MEMORY
- Canvas LRU: at most 3 x 4.6 MB.
- Map canvas: 4.6 MB, only while open.
- Shape region copy: at most 4.6 MB, only during a hold.
- Graph arrays: about 2000 x 32 B.
- Every allocation failure has a slower path that draws the same pixels.

LIVE VIEW: it streams App.screen before the toast and chip (app.c:933), so viewers see the bar, the card, the eye and the map, as they see the panel. Excluding them would need live_push skip rects; this is noted, not done.

owner_questions.question: In the Links bar, does each row stand for an Index entry or for one link?
options: One row per Index entry the page links to. Two links to the same page show once, marked ×2. Holding that row renames the entry, or deletes or retargets all its links on this page in one undoable step. Holding a link on the page acts on that one link only.
One row per link. Two links to the same page are two rows, each numbered like its area.
owner_questions.recommended: One row per Index entry, with ×N
owner_questions.why: Your brief says the bar shows 'the index entries that are linked to in that particular page'. A destination listed once reads like an index. Deleting one particular link stays exact through the long press on the page, and Undo covers the group delete.

owner_questions.question: While you hop between links in the bar, which page's links does it list?
options: The page you started on, until you stay (tap the page) or go back (X, two fingers down, Back)
The page you are looking at, so you can walk a chain
owner_questions.recommended: The page you started on
owner_questions.why: 'Tap outside the hotbar to confirm' means something only if the bar is a look from where you were. You can compare several targets, and the way home is always one tap. To follow a chain, you stay on a page and swipe up again.

owner_questions.question: When you rename from a link, what gets renamed?
options: The target page's name in the Index, everywhere it appears (the Index, the tiles, the map, the PDF outline). On an unnamed page the button reads 'Add page 20 to the Index...', which makes it an entry and a section start.
A separate label for that link only, stored in links.ini; page names stay as they are
owner_questions.recommended: The target page's Index name
owner_questions.why: Your brief treats links as Index entries, and keeping one name per place keeps the bar, the Index, the map and the PDF in agreement. Per-link labels would need UTF-8 in links.ini and would drift away from the Index. The button wording and the toast make the global effect visible.

owner_questions.question: Sideways, or zoomed in, where the page can scroll: what does a two-finger drag do?
options: Mid-screen it scrolls, as today. Navigation swipes start in an edge band: 25 mm at the top and bottom, 15 mm at the sides.
Navigation everywhere. Two-finger scrolling is lost when sideways or zoomed in.
Navigation only from the edge bands, even upright
owner_questions.recommended: Scroll mid-screen, navigate from the edge bands
owner_questions.why: Upright at the fitted view nothing scrolls, so 'two fingers down opens Pages' works anywhere, exactly as you wrote it. Elsewhere this keeps vertical scrolling. A drag that starts at a scroll limit never opens anything by surprise, and a one-time tip teaches the edge.

owner_questions.question: Which gestures should come built in, beyond your two-down (Pages) and two-up (Links)?
options: Also two fingers left and right to turn pages (a gesture never adds a page; at the end, a toast)
Only your two
Also two-finger tap for Undo and three-finger tap for Redo
owner_questions.recommended: Also two-finger left and right page turns
owner_questions.why: Your brief says gestures serve navigation by default. A straight 20 mm two-finger swipe is deliberate, and the panel's arrows are its visible twin. Taps fire too easily from a resting hand, so the sheet suggests them instead of binding them. Three-finger support is unknown until the step-1 log.

owner_questions.question: What does 'record a gesture' mean in Settings > Gestures?
options: Do one gesture from a set Grimoire can tell apart reliably: 1, 2 or 3-finger swipes, 2 or 3-finger taps, and pen-button clicks and holds. Grimoire names what it saw and says why when it refuses.
Draw any shape you like (free-form matching)
owner_questions.recommended: A fixed set, recognised and named
owner_questions.why: On a 75 Hz touch panel with palms and a hovering pen, a free-form matcher always picks something, and its mistakes cannot be explained. A fixed set uses the same thresholds as runtime, so whatever records will also fire. Every refusal has a reason, and all of it can be tested headless.

owner_questions.question: Should the panel get both new buttons?
options: Both: Shapes under the eraser and Links under Next (13 buttons; sideways with 4 pins the panel scales to about 93%)
Only Shapes. Links opens by gesture, a hold on the page chip, or a button in the Pages view
Neither: Shapes only in the tool picker
owner_questions.recommended: Both
owner_questions.why: Every gesture needs a visible twin, and you called links the hook of the app. The worst case is 8 mm buttons sideways with 4 pins, and the panel can still fold. Scenario taps are made symbolic before either button lands, so the tests are safe.

owner_questions.question: Should pen-button gestures be recorded in the same Gestures sheet, instead of the pen plan's separate Pen button sheet?
options: One action-first Gestures sheet for touch and pen; gestures.ini absorbs the planned pen.ini. The held-button cycler stays a Settings row.
Keep a separate, gesture-first Pen button sheet
owner_questions.recommended: One sheet
owner_questions.why: You asked for one place where anything the controller can do is assigned. It is one file and one rule: per action, at most one touch gesture and one pen gesture. Both files are unreleased, so nothing breaks.

risks: Pen near. 'Write, lift, swipe' often starts with the pen still hovering. The first build rejects multi-finger gestures while the pen hovers, so the headline gesture can feel refused. The rate-limited 'Move the pen away' toast keeps it from feeling like a hang, and step 19 relaxes the rule from the device log. The owner must test this in build P2.
The panel's slot count, TOUCH_MAJOR range and palm flagging are unknown. Three-finger gestures and the palm-size guard stay hidden or log-only until the step-1 log is read.
Sideways or zoomed in, navigation needs the edge band, which is harder to teach than 'anywhere'. Mitigations: the one-time tip, the Gestures sheet footer, and the visible Links button and page chip.

How a two-finger drag feels will change: the zoom no longer drifts while panning, swipes no longer move the view, and timing switches to kernel time. k_pinch_gate guards the dead zone but not the feel; the owner tests it.

Peek state could leak into edits. Mitigated by design: a peek is a display state, S->index, S->page, history and hit tests stay on the origin, and every way out commits or cancels explicitly. Scenarios cover autosave, sleep and leaving the editor during a peek.

Peek cost and memory: a cold peek of a dense or PDF page can still take up to 1.2 s; GL16 peeks build up ghosting until the commit's or cancel's GC16; the cache takes up to about 14 MB. Prefetch must stop at the first contact. Kindle RAM headroom is not measured, and every allocation has a slower fallback that draws the same pixels.

Migration is a one-way rewrite of the owner's links.ini. Using the 7 mm grown box, or counting erase strokes, would silently change tappable areas, so fixtures are copies of real device notebooks. If f9d13f5 is ever used again it carries area lines only up to 16 KiB (about 430 links), then goes read-only there and never overwrites the file.

Areas are invisible to every other reader (older versions, the share page, Live view's page layer). Only the PDF carries them, as invisible /Link annotations, so a user may think links were lost. The eye only helps on the device.
Smallest-wins replaces last-drawn-wins, so beta.5 links with overlapping boxes may resolve differently. This is acceptable while beta.5 is unreleased, and test_nav covers it.

ACT_LINK writes a notebook-wide sidecar from inside a page's history. A failed save must drop the step after nav_load restores the file, never leave history pointing at a change that did not happen. Redo after the target page is deleted must do nothing.
Renaming from a link can create a section start, which moves the Index tab's section highlight for later pages. The button wording and the toast name it, but it may still surprise.

Smart shapes: very large or slow handwriting can show a preview and then revert (two DU frames). The corpus is small (47 strokes, read-time stamps). The region-render preview may be slow on dense pages; the tile backup is the planned fallback if the shape-log shows renders over about 300 ms.

The Index map: large layouts run in bgjob's single queue, so a PDF mirror can delay them, and the seed placement must look acceptable meanwhile. Floats differ between arm64 and armv7, so tests use invariants only. The canvas_line_aa rewrite touches every Gothic drawing and must stay bit-identical.
Panel growth to 13 buttons, and the moved Settings bottom row, break raw coordinate taps. Step 4's symbolic taps, and the updated 10 taps plus y_all_screens.qs:631, must land before or with them.
The Buttons sheet becomes parametrized by BindKind, which can regress the Controller flow. v_controller*.qs must stay green at every step.
The pen plan's references are stale and its lane is unimplemented. Folding pen.ini into gestures.ini, and its actions into the registry, requires that lane to adopt this design (P7).
A new keyboard surface that bypasses kbhost brings back the Index keyboard lag. keyboard.draws is asserted in every typing scenario.
Live view streams App.screen, so viewers see the bar, the card, the eye and the map. That may surprise someone streaming their notes.
